WOLBERO, abbot of the monastery of St. Pantaleon, was elected in 1147 in place of Gerard, who had resigned his office, worn out by age. He was distinguished both in eloquence and intellect. Learned in Scripture, he wrote four books on the *Song of Songs* for virgins consecrated to God and of the Order of Saint Benedict. He died in 1167, CXCV, 1001.

WOLF and REINBRAT, with their sisters Osbirin and Meinbirin, gave part of their inheritance to the church of the Holy Savior at Werth, under Emperor Louis the Pious, in 834, XCIX, 804.

WOLFAUD. See SIGEBAUD.

WOLFEO, bishop of Constance, sent a letter to Bernalt, bishop of Strasbourg, on behalf of the cleric Anno, that, after receiving holy orders, he might be able to administer a parish, in 817, CXXIX, 1389.

WOLFHARD, priest of Hasenried and Benedictine monk in the diocese of Eichstätt, flourished about the beginning of the tenth century. He wrote a life of Saint Walpurga, which he dedicated to Erchambald, his bishop, and later added three books on her miracles, 908, CXXIX, 865.

WOLFOALD, or Wolfaud, and his wife Adalsinda bestowed many gifts upon the monastery of St. Michael in the district of Verdun in 709. Whether he is the same man who made certain exchanges with Sigebaud is not certain to us, 1038, LXXXVIII, 1254.

WOLPHELM (Blessed), abbot of Brauweiler near Cologne in the district of Ripuarian Francia. Born of distinguished lineage, while still a boy he studied the liberal arts at Cologne; but soon, having broken the chains of earthly pleasures, he went to St. Maximinus at Trier and became a monk, and not long afterwards was elected abbot of Brauweiler. [Col. 0546] He wrote books *On the Sacrament of the Altar*, 1100, CLIV, 403.

WOLSTAN, monk of Winchester in England. He was a disciple of Æthelwold; he flourished in the tenth century, in 993, and wrote the life of Saint Swithun, bishop of Winchester, and of Æthelwold, CXXXVII, 79.

WRACHARIUS, son of one Brunharius, gave certain lands to Blessed Ludger, abbot of the monastery of Werth; this was done in 799, during the reign of Charlemagne, XCIX, 815.

## X

XYSTUS (Saint). See SIXTUS.

## Z

ZACCHAEUS CHRISTIANUS, monk of the fifth century. It is uncertain whether he was a Gaul or an Italian. Some conjecture that he was African because of the affinity of his style with writers of that region. Three books of *Consultations* by him survive, 420, XX, 1062.

ZACHARIAS (Saint), pope, born at Polychronium Pontinium in Calabria; first a regular canon, then a monk of Saint Benedict, and finally cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church, he succeeded Gregory III in 741. He died in 752. His letters and decrees survive, LXXXIX, 892.

ZACHARIAS, bishop of Chrysopolis. This author, whom people commonly make bishop of Besançon, nevertheless seems never to have left the Premonstratensian state which he had embraced in the abbey of St. Martin at Laon. His commentary on the harmony of the Evangelists survives. He died in 1152, CLXXXVI, 9.

ZACHARIAS, bishop of an uncertain see. No one tells us his origin, native country, or age. Some have called him bishop of Sabina, others bishop of Brescia. A serious, learned, and elegant sermon by him on Saint George survives, CLXXXVI, 619.

ZACHARIAS BENEDICTUS, a Carthusian of Vicenza, concerning whom we have learned nothing, published a poem celebrating the origin of the holy Carthusian Order. He seems to have flourished in the fifteenth or sixteenth century, CLIII, 571.

ZANETO. See ERFO.

ZENO, leader of the Stoics, born in Cyprus, came to Athens and there taught a new system of things under a portico, whence he was called a Stoic. He died in 260 BC. A letter from him to Antigonus, king of Syria, survives in Saint Ambrose, XVII, 1152.

ZENO (Saint), bishop of Verona; the origin of his father is uncertain. It is commonly thought that he was raised to the episcopate in 363, when both pagans and Arians were flourishing at Verona; Saint Zeno won over nearly all of them by examples of his eloquence and virtues. He died near the end of the fourth century. Two books of *Treatises*, or sermons, by him survive, 381, XI, 9.

ZEPHERINUS, or ZEPHYRINUS (Saint), pope and martyr, succeeded Saint Victor and prudently administered the affairs of the Church; but during his pontificate a most cruel persecution raged against Christ’s worshippers. He died in 218. Certain decrees are attributed to him in Isidore Mercator, CXXX, 125.

ZONARAS (John), Greek author of the twelfth century, about 1150, and chief secretary to Emperors John and Manuel. He handed down *Annals*. A preface and fragments on the Councils of Carthage survive from him in Cyprian, published in Greek and Latin, III, 1079, 1083.

ZOSIMUS (Saint), pope. A Greek by nationality, he was elected unanimously in place of Saint Innocent I in 417. He acted extensively against the Pelagian heresy. He issued decrees and letters concerning the governance of the Church. He died in 418 and was buried on the Tiburtine Way beside the body of Saint Lawrence the martyr, XX, 637.

[Col. 0547]

## XIII. ANALYTICAL INDEX, ALPHABETICALLY ARRANGED, OF ALL AUTHORS WHOSE WRITINGS ARE AVAILABLE IN THE *COURSE OF LATIN PATRISTICS*

(The Roman numeral indicates the volume; the Arabic numeral, the column.)

### NOTICE

In this index, as its title indicates, we have arranged all writers alphabetically and, under each individual’s name, gathered together all his works, even minor works, scattered here and there. We indicate the volume and column where they are found, and summarize as briefly as possible what they contain, so that the reader, without even handling the volumes, may know everything written by each author and immediately have the desired material at hand, thus enjoying and benefiting from another’s labor.

[ANALYTICAL INDEX.]

[Col. 0547]

## A

ABAELARD (Peter), abbot of Ruy, 1142.

1. *Apology, or Confession of Faith, of Peter Abaelard.*

2. Twelve letters: to Heloise, to a friend, to Bernard of Clairvaux, to G., bishop of Paris, etc.

3. Thirty-four sermons: to the Virgins established in the oratory of the Paraclete; on the principal feasts of the year; on certain saints; on the dedication of a church; on almsgiving.

4. Exposition of the Lord’s Prayer.

5. Exposition of the Apostles’ Creed.

6. Exposition of faith on the Athanasian Creed.

7. *Ethics*, or the book called *Know Yourself*, treating of sin, repentance, and confession.

8. Forty-two problems of Heloise, with Peter Abaelard’s solutions, concerning certain words of the Gospels, the Epistles of Saint Paul, etc.

9. Exposition on the Hexaemeron.

10. Exposition in five books on Saint Paul’s Epistle to the Romans.

11. *Introduction to Theology*, divided into three books: Catholic faith, hope, charity, the sacraments, the Trinity, testimonies of prophets and philosophers concerning the Trinity, and the perfections of God.

12. *Christian Theology*, five books: distinction of the three persons in God; against the calumnies of unbelievers; on the introduction of philosophical testimonies; invectives against dialecticians and against those who wish even God to be comprehended by human reasoning; answers to objections; the generation of the Word from the Father; the procession of the Spirit; and the basis for believing in one God.

13. *Yes and No*, or 158 questions concerning God, the Trinity, angels, the first parents, the incarnate Son of God, baptism, the Eucharist, marriage, etc., etc.

14. Dialogue between a philosopher, a Jew, and a Christian.

15. Epitome of *Christian Theology*.

16. Hymns and sequences for the whole cycle of the year, for the use of the virgins of the monastery of the Paraclete.

17. Various lamentations, CLXXVIII, 9 ff.

[Col. 0548]

ABBAUD, abbot, 1130. Treatise on the breaking of Christ’s body, CLXVI, 1340.

ABBO (Saint), bishop of Metz, 651. Letter of Saint Abbo to Saint Desiderius, concerning King Dagobert’s gift to the basilicas of Metz and various other matters, LXXXVII, 217, 262.

ABBO, donor, 739. Will of Abbo, by which he bestows very extensive gifts upon the monastery of St. Peter at Novalesa, LXXXVIII, 1290.

ABBO, monk of Saint-Germain, 923.

1. Three books, written in verse, *On the Parisian War against the Normans*.

2. Five sermons: on the Lord’s Supper; to penitents; on the foundation and growth of Christianity, CXXXII, 722 ff.

ABBO (Saint), monk of Fleury, 1004.

1. Thirteen letters: to Pope Gregory V, to Robert king of the Franks, to Odilo of Cluny, to Abbot Bernerius, to the monks of Micy, etc.

2. *Apologeticus* to Hugh and Robert, kings of the Franks, on preserving the Catholic faith, expelling heretical depravity, simony, etc.

3. Collection of canons, fifty-two chapters: on churches, kings, priests, monks, soldiers, etc.

4. Life of Saint Edmund, king and martyr of the English.

5. Acrostic poem to Emperor Otto.

6. Grammatical questions.

7. Epitome on the Lives of the Roman Pontiffs, from Saint Peter to Saint Gregory I.

8. On the Cycle of Victorius, CXXXIX, 420 ff.

ABEDOC, Irish abbot, year uncertain. Selected chapters from an ancient collection of canons compiled in Ireland, about the eighth century, XCVI, 1280.

ABSALON, archbishop of Lund, twelfth century. Will of Absalon, archbishop of Lund, CCIX, 756.

ABSALON, abbot of Springiersbach, 1203. Fifty-one sermons, on the principal feasts of the year, from Advent to the feast of All Saints, CCXI, 12 ff.

ACHARD, abbot and afterwards bishop of Avranches, 1155. Two letters: one to Henry II, king of England; the other to A., bishop of Lisieux, CXCVI, 1381.

ADALARD, abbot of Saint-Bertin, 853. Donations, CXXXVI, 1229, 1273.

ADALBERO, archbishop of Reims, 988.

1. Forty-one letters: to Egbert, archbishop of Trier; to Willigis, archbishop of Mainz; to King Lothair; to Duchess Beatrice; to Empress Theophanu; etc.

2. Introduction of monks into the monastery of Mouzon, CXXXVII, 504.

ADALBERO, bishop of Laon, 1030. A poem to Robert, king of the Franks, composed of 430 hexameter verses: a satirical poem concerning matters of his own time which appeared disorderly to him, CXLI, 767.

ADALBERO, bishop of Liège, 1139. Two diplomas, CLXXXIX, 1055, 1477.

ADALBERT (Saint), bishop of Prague, 997.

1. Homily on the feast of Saint Alexius the Confessor.

2. Profession of the Rule of Saint Benedict by Blessed Adalbert, CXXXVII, 899.

ADALBERT, archbishop of Mainz, 1136. Six letters: to Pope Callixtus, Pope Innocent II, Saint Otto of Bamberg, etc., CLXXII, 1337; CLXIII, 1356; CLXXIX, 657.

ADALBERT, scholastic of Metz, 979. Prologue to his florilegium from the moral works of Lord Gregory, CXXXVI, 1310.

ADALBERT, priest and monk of Nemetum, 1079. Two letters to Bernald, priest, CXLVIII, 1141, 1166.

ADALGER, bishop of an uncertain see, perhaps Augsburg, of the Order of Saint Benedict, 964. *Admonition to Nonsuinda the Recluse*, or *Book on the Pursuit of Virtues*, CXXXIV, 916.

ADALGISEL GRIMO, donor from the diocese of Metz, 634, LXXXVII, 1343.

ADALHARD (Saint), abbot of Corbie in Gaul, 826. Ancient statutes of the abbey of Saint Peter at Corbie, prescribed by Adalhard for his monks, CV, 533; CXX, 1507.

ADALSINDA, abbess of St. Martin at Tournai, 657. Charter by which she gives her monastery to the monastery of Bèze, LXXXVIII, 1166.

ADAMNAN (Saint), Benedictine abbot of Iona, at the beginning of the eighth century.

1. Three books *On the Life of Saint Columba*.

2. Three books *On the Holy Places*, from the report of Arculf, Gallic bishop.

3. Canons of Adamnan, LXXXVIII, 722 ff.

ADAM, canon of Bremen, about 1073–1076.

1. *Deeds of the Bishops of the Church of Hamburg*—*Description of the Islands of the North*.

2. Adam’s epilogue to Bishop Liemar, CXLVI, 458, 620, 660.

ADAM OF SAINT VICTOR, canon of Paris, 1173. Thirty-six sequences: some for particular feasts, others concerning saints, CXCVI, 1424.

ADAM THE SCOT, regular canon of the Premonstratensian Order, 1180.

1. Forty-seven sermons: on the Advent of the Lord; Christmas Day; the day of Saint Stephen; the day of Saint John the Evangelist; the day of the Holy Innocents; and the Epiphany of the Lord.

2. *Book on the Order, Habit, and Profession of Canons of the Premonstratensian Order*, distributed into fourteen sermons.

3. *On the Threefold Tabernacle*, or on the tabernacle of Moses in its literal sense; the tabernacle of Christ, which is in faith; and the tabernacle of the mind, which is in inward thought.

4. *On the Threefold Kind of Contemplation*: God is considered in himself as incomprehensible; God is considered as terrible in the reprobate; and the Lord is considered as lovable and sweet in the elect.

5. Two books of *Soliloquies on the Instruction of the Soul*, CXCVIII, 98 ff.

ADAM, abbot of Perseigne, of the Cistercian Order in the bishopric of Le Mans, 1203.

1. Thirty letters: to Osmund, monk; to Odo, bishop of Paris; to the countess of Perche; to William, bishop of Hélie (*Heliensis*); to the countess of Chartres; to Blanche, countess of Champagne; to certain young men; and to certain virgins.

2. *Mariale*, five sermons on the Blessed Virgin Mary.

3. Seven Marian fragments, CCXI, 584 ff.

ADELA, abbess of Paltiole near Trier, 732. Her will, LXXXVIII, 1286.

ADELA, lady of Medanta, donor, 1066, CLV, 318.

ADELA, queen of the Franks, 1191. On the procuration of the bishop in the church of St. Exuperius at Corbeil, CCV, 912.

ADELAIDE, donor of the valley of Fontevraud, twelfth century, CLXII, 1104.

ADELBERT, bishop of Verdun, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 174.

ADELBOLD, bishop of Utrecht, 1027.

1. Life of Saint Emperor Henry.

2. Life of Saint Walburga.

3. Short treatise to Pope Sylvester II on the method of finding the thickness of a sphere.

4. Charter concerning vassals, or persons bound by fealty, of the Church and the bishop of Utrecht.

5. Music, CXL, 1086.

ADELGORIUS, archbishop of Magdeburg, 1100–1110. Letter of Adelgorius and others to the bishops of Saxony, France, and Lorraine, and to all Christ’s faithful. They seek aid against pagans who were massacring Christians most cruelly, CLVII, 484.

ADELMANN, bishop of Brescia, 1161–? [the printed date is incomplete/uncertain].

1. Letter to Berengar concerning the sacrament of the Eucharist.

2. Alphabetical rhythms on the distinguished men of his time, CXLIII, 1290 ff.

ADEMAR, viscount of Scalas and abbot of Tulle, tenth century. His will, CXXXII, 469.

ADEMAR, monk of the monastery of Saint Cybard at Angoulême, 1029.

1. Three books of *Histories*, from the first king of the Franks to 1027.

2. Commemoration of the abbots of the Basilica of Saint Martial the Apostle at Limoges.

3. Letter on the Apostleship of Saint Martial.

4. Fragment of Ademar’s sermon delivered at the Council of Limoges.

5. Ademar’s acrostic to Rohon, bishop of Angoulême.

6. Three sermons, apparently delivered at the Council of Limoges, CXLI, 9 ff.

ADEMAR, viscount of Limoges, 1062. Donation of the abbey of Saint Martial to Hugh of Cluny, CLIX, 957.

ADEODATUS (Saint), pope, 676.

1. Letter of Pope Adeodatus to all the bishops of Gaul, granting the monastery of St. Martin at Tours immunity from episcopal authority, except in the ordination of priests and the preparation of chrism.

2. Privilege granted by Pope Adeodatus to the monks of the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul at Canterbury, LXXXVII, 1139.

ADO, probably abbot of Reims, 715. Charter for the basilica of St. Remigius, LXXXVIII, 1261.

ADO (Saint), archbishop of Vienne in Gaul, 875.

1. Chronicle, divided into six ages, from the creation of the world to the year of the Lord 815.

2. Martyrology.

3. Passion of Saint Desiderius, bishop of Vienne.

4. Privilege of Ado confirming the church of Vellens to the abbey of St. Eugendus in the Jura.

5. Life of Saint Theuderius, abbot at Vienne in Gaul, CXXIII, 24 ff.

ADOLPH, archbishop of Cologne, twelfth century. Letter to Innocent III, CCXVI, 1003.

ADREVALD, monk of Fleury, 878.

1. History of the translation of Saint Benedict.

2. Miracles of Saint Benedict wrought in Gaul after the translation, down to the middle of the ninth century.

3. *On the Body and Blood of Christ*, against the absurdities of John Scotus.

4. Life of Saint Aigulf, abbot of Lérins and martyr, CXXIV, 500 ff.

ADRIAN I, pope, 797. 1. Fifty-eight letters: to King Pippin, King Charles, Tilpin, Archbishop of Rheims; Constantine and Irene; and Patriarch Tarasius (the latter two written in Greek). 2. Bull of Adrian confirming the division of the diocese of Strasbourg into seven archdeaconries, the separation of the bishop’s revenues from those of the chapter, etc., XCVI, 1168; XCVIII, 261.

ADRIAN II, pope, 872. Forty-one letters and decrees: to the Frankish kings Lothair and Charles the Bald; to Emperor Basil; to Louis, king of Germany; to the archbishops of Vienne, Rheims, and Constantinople; to the synod of Troyes, etc., CXXII, 1260; CXXIX, 1015.

ADRIAN III, pope, 885. 1. Privilege of Adrian III for the monastery of Piacenza. 2. Letter of Adrian III to Sigebod, Archbishop of Narbonne, CXXVI, 972.

ADRIAN IV, pope, 1154–1159. Two hundred and fifty-eight letters and privileges; CLXXXVIII, 1361 ff.

ADROALD, distinguished man, 648. Donation for the construction of a monastery, LXXXVIII, 1155; CXXXVI, 1185.

ADSO, monk of the monastery of Dervus in the district of Perthes in Champagne, 992. 1. Life of Saint Frodobert, first abbot of Celle near Troyes. 2. Life, in two books, of Saint Mansuetus, first bishop of the city of the Leuci. 3. Life of Saint Basolus the Confessor. 4. Short work on the translation and miracles of Saint Basolus the Confessor. 5. Life of Saint Bercharius, first abbot of Hautvillers and Dervus. 6. On the miracles of Saint Waldebert, third abbot of Luxeuil, CXXXVII, 598.

ADVENTIUS, Bishop of Metz, 875. 1. Treatise on Waldrada, in which he attempts to prove that Waldrada, Lothair’s concubine, had already from tender age been joined in marriage by his father, Lothair Augustus. 2. Letter of Adventius to Theutgaud, Bishop of Cologne. 3. Letter of Adventius to Nicholas, sending his profession, in which, clearing himself in the matter of Lothair, he declares that he accepts and obeys the ordinances made by the pontiff at the Roman synod; accordingly, he implores pardon and peace. 4. Privilege of Adventius for Gorze Abbey. 5. Epitaph of Adventius, composed by himself, CXXI, 1142; CXXV, 803.

AEGIDIUS, deacon of Paris, about 1200. 1. Fragments from Peter of Riga’s book entitled *Aurora*, incidentally inserted in various places together with additions by Aegidius of Paris. 2. Verses of Aegidius of Paris on the number of books in each Testament and the manner of reading them. 3. On the punishments of hell, CCXII, 18 ff.

AEGIDIUS, Bishop of Évreux, about 1180. Three letters to Pope Alexander III concerning the king of England, CC, 1409.

ÆLFRIC, Saint, Archbishop of Canterbury, 1006. Thirty-five canons. Letter on the canons to Bishop Wulfin, CXXXIX, 1470.

AELIDIS, Queen of Cyprus, 1234. Letter of the Queen of Cyprus concerning the renunciation of the counties of Champagne and Brie, CCXVI, 988.

AELRED, Blessed, Abbot of Rievaulx in England, about 1167. 1. Twenty-five sermons for the seasons and saints’ days. 2. Thirty-two sermons on burdens, on chapter XIII and following of the prophet Isaiah. 3. Three books of *The Mirror of Charity*. 4. A compendium of *The Mirror of Charity*. 5. Three books on spiritual friendship. 6. Rule, or instruction, for recluses. 7. On the Battle of the Standard in the time of King Stephen. 8. Genealogy of the kings of England. 9. Life of Saint Edward, king and confessor. 10. On the nun of Watton, concerning a certain wondrous miracle, CXCV, 196 ff.; CLXXXIV, 817, 849.

AEMILIANUS, priest and abbot, about 650. Letter to Braulio, Bishop of Saragossa, LXXX, 674, 699.

AENEAS, Bishop of Paris, 870. Book against the Greeks, divided into 209 chapters, CXXI, 682.

AENGELBERT, donor of Trier, 709. Charter by which he confers gifts upon Bishop Willibrord at the place Alfheim in Toxandria, LXXXIX, 542. Another charter by the same, 346.

AETHELSTAN, king of the English, 928. Ecclesiastical laws, CXXXVIII, 461.

AGANO, Bishop of the Church of Autun, 1098. 1. Judgment of Agano against Raginard. 2. Charter of Agano for the foundation of the Church of Saint Germanus and Saint Saturninus of Planesia. 3. Letter of Bishop Agano and the other bishops of the province of Lyons on behalf of Ralph, Archbishop of Tours, CL, 1540 ff.

AGAPETUS I, pope, 546. Seven letters: to Justinian, confirming his statement of faith and exhorting him to defend the Catholic faith, etc.; to the African bishops, congratulating them on having escaped from the hands of heretics; to Caesarius, Bishop of Arles, concerning Bishop Contumeliosus when he had appealed to the Apostolic See, etc., LXVI, 32, 46.

[Col. 0551]

AGAPETUS II, pope, 956. Twenty-two letters and privileges, to various monasteries, CXXXIII, 890.

AGATHO, Saint, pope, 679. Three letters: to the Augusti, expounding the faith of the Catholic Church; to Æthelred, king of the Mercians; to the Augusti concerning the celebration of the Sixth Synod, LXXXVII, 1162.

AGERADUS, Bishop of Chartres, 696. Privilege granted to a certain monastery dedicated to Saint Mary, on the River Loire, LXXXVIII, 1228.

AGILULF, king of the Lombards, twenty-second century [as printed; evidently anomalous]. Privilege concerning the territory of Bobbio, LXX, 321.

AGIO, Archbishop of Narbonne, 927. History of Vabres Abbey, CXXXII, 780.

AGIUS, priest and monk, about 1000. Dialogue on the death of Saint Hathumoda, first abbess of Gandersheim, CXXXVII, 1169.

AGNELLUS, Bishop of Ravenna, 552. Letter to Armenius on the grounds of the faith, LXVIII, 380.

AGNELLUS, also called Andrew, abbot of Saint Mary at Blachernae and of Saint Bartholomew at Ravenna, 842. *Liber Pontificalis*, or lives of forty-six bishops of Ravenna, from Saint Apollinaris to George, a contemporary of Agnellus, CVI, 429, 476.

AGNES, wife of Henry the Black, eleventh century. Letter to Hugh of Cluny, asking him to pray for the deceased emperor, CLIX, 932.

AGOBARD, Saint, Bishop of Lyons, 840. 1. Book against the doctrine of Felix of Urgell, addressed to the pious Emperor Louis. 2. On the insolence of the Jews, addressed to the same emperor. 3. Letter of Saint Agobard and the bishops Bernard and Eaof concerning Jewish superstitions, to the same emperor. 4. Consultation and petition concerning the baptism of Jewish slaves, addressed to the magnates of the palace. 5. Letter on avoiding intercourse and association with Jews, to Nibridius, Bishop of Narbonne. 6. Book against the law of Gundobad and the impious contests conducted under it, addressed to the aforesaid emperor. 7. On the privilege and right of the priesthood, to Bishop Bernard. 8. Against the foolish popular belief concerning hail and thunder. 9. Book against the objections of Abbot Fredegisus. 10. Letter to the magnates of the palace against the impious ordinance concerning the baptism of Jewish slaves. 11. Letter to Bartholomew, Bishop of Narbonne, concerning the deception of certain signs. 12. Lament concerning injustices, to Matfred, a magnate of the palace. 13. On the manner of ecclesiastical governance, to the clergy and monks of Lyons. 14. Book on images of saints. 15. Book on the administration of ecclesiastical property. 16. Book arranged from divine sayings. 17. Sermon on the truth of the faith. 18. Sorrowful letter on the division of the Frankish Empire among the sons of Emperor Louis. 19. Apologetic book for the sons of Emperor Louis against their father. 20. Brief document to Lothair. 21. Letter to Ebbo, Bishop of Rheims, on hope and fear. 22. Book on divine psalmody. 23. Book on the correction of the Antiphonary. 24. Book against Abbot Amalarius. 25. Poems of Saint Agobard: epitaph of Charlemagne; on the translation of the relics of the holy martyrs Cyprian, Speratus, and Pantaleon to the city of Lyons, CIV, 30 ff.

AHYTO, or HETTO, Bishop of Basel, 836. 1. Capitulary of Hetto, or twenty-five articles for the priests of his diocese, showing how they ought to govern themselves and the people entrusted to them chastely and justly, and strengthen them in religion. 2. Short work on the vision and death of Wetin, monk of Reichenau, CV, 762 ff.; CXV, 9.

AIGLIBERT, Bishop of Le Mans, 692–700. Two charters for the monastery of Saint Mary beside the Sarthe, LXXXVIII, 1228, 1240.

AILERAN, Saint, Irish Scot and abbot, 595. 1. Mystical interpretation of Christ’s ancestors. 2. Likewise, a moral explanation of the same names compiled by him, LXXX, 328.

AIMERIC, Patriarch of Antioch, 1187. Three letters: to Louis, king of France, concerning the Turkish victory over Christians; to Henry, king of England, concerning the same; to Hugh Etherian concerning his book against the teaching of the Greek Church, CCI, 1403.

AIMERIC, Count of Auch, 1068. Letter by which he gives Saint Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, the monastery of Saint Orientius to set in order, CLIX, 961.

AIMERIC, King of Jerusalem, twelfth century. Oath of the kings of Jerusalem, CLV, 1238.

AIMO, Abbot of Saint Peter of Dives, 1150. Letter of Aimo to the brethren living at Totesbury in England, CLXXXI, 1708.

AIMOIN, monk of Fleury, 1088. 1. History of the Franks, four books, from the first king of the Franks to Dagobert. 2. Translation of Father Benedict, composed in heroic metre. 3. Two books on the miracles of Saint Benedict. 4. Sermon on Saint Benedict, CXXXIX, 628. 5. Letter of Aimoin to Hervé, treasurer of Saint Martin’s, concerning the life and martyrdom of Saint Abbo, abbot of Fleury Abbey, CXXXIX, 388.

AIMOIN, monk of Saint-Germain, 888. 1. History of the translation of Saint Vincent, Levite and martyr, from Spain to the Castrensian monastery in Gaul. 2. Two books on the miracles of Saint Germanus. 3. Account of the translation of Saint Savinus the martyr. 4. On the translation of the holy martyrs George the monk, Aurelius, and Nathalia from the city of Córdoba to Paris, CXXVI, 1009; CXV, 939.

AISTULF, king of the Lombards, 752. Donation to Lopecinus, Bishop of Modena, etc., LXXXVII, 1384, 1411.

AIVALD, priest, eighth century. Donation to the monastery of Pistoia, LXXXVII, 1430.

ALAN, Abbot of Tewkesbury, about 1164. 1. Fourteen letters: to Philip, king of France; Henry, king of England; Baldwin, Archbishop of Canterbury; John, Archbishop of Lyons; etc. 2. Life of Saint Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury, CXC, 1475, 208.

ALAN, Bishop of Rennes, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1409.

ALAN, Bishop of Auxerre, 1166. 1. Two letters to Louis the Younger, king of the Franks, asking him to protect the Church of Auxerre against the vexations of the Count of Nevers. 2. Three diplomas of Alan: to the monastery of Saint Marcia; to the priory of Saint Amator; and to certain churches. 3. Testament of Alan. 4. Life of Saint Bernard, CCI, 1384 ff.; CLXXXV, 469.

ALAN OF LILLE, most celebrated doctor, surnamed “the Universal,” perhaps identical with the preceding, 1202. 1. Brief elucidation of the *Song of Songs* in praise of the Virgin Mary, Mother of God. 2. On the art of preaching, in which excellent concepts for shaping sermons on nearly every moral subject are suggested, now published for the first time. 3. Eight sermons, now first brought to light, from a most ancient manuscript of the library of Blessed Mary of Alne, of the Cistercian Order, in the diocese of Liège; three other sermons from a very ancient manuscript of the monastery of Blessed Mary of the Dunes. 4. Book of memorable opinions and sayings: on the Nativity of the Lord, Saint Peter the Apostle, and Saint Mary; other sayings commonly called “wonders,” but perhaps better, “memorabilia.” 5. Short work on the six wings of the Cherubim, containing concise and sound teaching on contrition, confession, satisfaction, love of God and neighbor, etc. 6. Penitential book, or method for worthily administering and receiving the sacrament of penance. 7. Four books on the Catholic faith against the heretics of his time, especially the Albigensians. 8. *The Complaint of Nature*, composed partly in prose and partly in verse. 9. *Anticlaudianus*, or nine books on the office of the good and perfect man, in hexameter verse. 10. An exceedingly elegant rhythmical poem on Christ’s Incarnation, in which he most ingeniously sang that this divine work had disregarded all the rules of the liberal arts. 11. Book of parables, composed in alternating hexameter and pentameter verse. 12. Five books on the articles of the Catholic faith. 13. Alan’s rules of sacred theology. 14. Book of distinctions of theological terms, in which the words are arranged alphabetically, CCX, 9 ff.

ALBERIC, deacon, about 535, 543. Sermon on Saint Scholastica, LXVI, 941.

ALBERIC, canon and custodian of the Church of Aix, about 1125. History of the Jerusalem expedition, composed by Alberic concerning the passage of Godfrey of Bouillon and the other princes, in twelve books, CLXVI, 388 ff.

ALBERIC, Bishop of Ostia, 1100. Letter to the monks of the monastery of Saint Orientius at Auch, concerning concord between the Archbishop of the Church of Auch and the monastery of Saint Orientius, CLV, 1632.

ALBERIC, donor of Chartres, 1080. On the junior prebend of the church of Saint Leobinus at Châteaudun, CLV, 337.

ALBERO, Archbishop of Trier, 1147. Letter to Suger, asking what the envoys of the king of France had communicated to him concerning the Jerusalem expedition, CLXXXVI, 1361.

ALBERT, Abbot of Micy, about 1004. 1. Letter to Pope John XVII concerning the antiquity and customary number of monks of Micy Abbey. 2. Charter of Albert, confirming certain estates to the abbey of Jumièges, CXXXIX, 585.

ALBERT, cardinal, twelfth century. Five letters: to Thomas of Canterbury; King Henry; the convent of Canterbury; William, Archbishop of Sens; and Gilbert, Archbishop of Ravenna, CXC, 980 ff.

ALBOIN, priest, about 1080. Two replies of Alboin to the priest Bernald concerning priestly celibacy, CXLVIII, 1083, 1091.

[Col. 0553]

ALBUIN, hermit, about 999. Letter to Heribert, Archbishop of Cologne, CXXXVIII, 185.

ALCHER, monk of Clairvaux, 1169. 1. Book on spirit and soul. 2. Book on loving God, CXCIV, 1896, 1683.

ALCUIN, Blessed, abbot, teacher of King and Emperor Charlemagne, 804. Two hundred and thirty-two letters: to King Æthelred; Charlemagne; Offa, king of the Mercians; Coenwulf, king of the Mercians; Gisela, daughter of Charlemagne; Pope Adrian I; Pope Leo III; Patriarch Paulinus; Arno (Aquila), Archbishop of Salzburg; etc.

Exegetical works:

1. Questions and answers on Genesis.
2. *Enchiridion*, or a devout and brief exposition of the penitential psalms, Psalm CXVIII, and the gradual psalms.
3. Compendium on the *Song of Songs*.
4. Commentaries on Ecclesiastes.
5. Interpretations of the Hebrew names of the ancestors of our Lord Jesus Christ.
6. Commentaries on the Gospel of Saint John.
7. Treatise on three Epistles of Saint Paul: to Titus, Philemon, and the Hebrews.
8. Brief commentary on certain sayings of Saint Paul.
9. Five books of commentary on the Apocalypse.

Dogmatic works:

1. Three books on faith in the Holy and Undivided Trinity, addressed to the glorious Emperor Charlemagne, devoted to God.
2. Short work on the procession of the Holy Spirit, addressed to Charlemagne.
3. Short work of Alcuin, sent to the abbots and monks of Gothia, against the heresy of Felix of Urgell; seven books against the same Felix.
4. Four books against the letter sent to him by Elipand of Toledo.

Liturgical and moral works:

1. Book of Sacraments.
2. Book on the use of the Psalms, with various formulas suited to daily affairs.
3. Offices for weekdays, or Psalms arranged according to the several days of the week on which they are sung in church, with prayers, hymns, confessions, and litanies.
4. On the ceremonies of Baptism.
5. Book on virtues and vices, addressed to Count Wido.
6. Book on the nature of the soul, addressed to the Virgin Eulalia.
7. On confession of sins, addressed to the boys of Saint Martin.

Hagiographical works:

1. Writing on the Life of Saint Martin of Tours.
2. Life of Saint Vedastus, Bishop of Arras.
3. Life of Blessed Richarius the priest.
4. Two books on the life of Saint Willibrord, Bishop of Utrecht.

Poems:

1. Night prayers.
2. Various inscriptions.
3. Verses to various persons.
4. Epigrams and riddles.
5. Poem on the bishops and saints of the Church of York.

Educational works:

1. Grammar.
2. On orthography.
3. Dialogue on rhetoric and the virtues.
4. On dialectic.
5. Disputation of Pippin, royal and most noble youth, with Albinus the schoolmaster.
6. On the course and leap of the moon and the leap year.

Doubtful works: Albinus’s confession of faith; disputation of boys by questions and answers; Alcuin’s propositions for sharpening the minds of youth; *On the Divine Offices*; four homilies attributed to Alcuin, vols. C, CI.

ALDBERT, deacon, 756. Letter to Lull, Archbishop of Mainz, XCVI, 835.

ALDEGUNDIS, having become a nun, 661. Two charters for the Church of Saint Mary at Maubeuge and the sisters established there, LXXXVIII, 1160, 1162.

ALDHELM, Saint, Bishop of Sherborne, 709. 1. Eleven letters. 2. On the praises of virginity, or on the virginity of saints. 3. Letter to Acircius, or book on the number seven and on metres, riddles, and the rules of poetic feet. 4. Poems: *On the Praises of Virgins*, about 2,240 hexameter verses; *On the Eight Principal Vices*, about 472 hexameter verses; *On the Basilica Built by Bugge, Daughter of the King of England*, about 100 verses; poem on the altars dedicated to Blessed Mary and the twelve apostles, about 325 verses; twenty-one verses written in honor of the apostles when the author entered their church at Rome; fragment on the Day of Judgment, about 120 verses, LXXXIX, 64.

ALDRIC, Saint, Archbishop of Sens, 836. Two letters: to the Church of Sens and to Bishop Frotharius, CV, 809 ff.

ALDRIC, Bishop of Le Mans, 856. Life of Aldric written by his disciples, CXV, 29.

ALEXANDER I, Saint, pope, 119. 1. Decrees of Pope Alexander I concerning priests: that they are not to be harassed, nor documents extorted from them through fear or fraud; and concerning the mixing of the Lord’s Passion in the consecration of his body, etc. 2. Two letters concerning the cases or grievances of priests, so that slanders and unjust prosecutions may be avoided, CXXX, 89.

ALEXANDER II, pope, 1073. Letters and diplomas, CLII. Vol. CXLVI, 1280 ff. Diploma concerning the legation of Saint Peter Damian in Gaul, CXLV, 857.

ALEXANDER III, pope, 1181. One thousand five hundred and twenty-one letters and privileges, from 1159 to 1181, CC, 9 ff.

[Col. 0554]

ALEXANDER, canon of Liège, eleventh century. Life of Wazo, Bishop of Liège, CXLII, 725.

ALEXANDER, monk and later abbot of the monastery of Saint Augustine at Canterbury, 1200. Life of Saint Hugh, Bishop of Lincoln in England, of the Carthusian Order, written in five books, CLIII, 937.

ALEXANDER OF MONTAGU, donor of Langres, thirteenth century, CLXXXV, 1429, 1431, 1432.

ALEXANDER, Abbot of Jumièges, about 1200. Letter on the Son of Man, CCV, 920.

ALEXIUS, Emperor of Constantinople, 1094. Letter to Robert, Count of Flanders, and all Christians, asking that they bring him aid against the pagans, CLV, 465.

ALFRED THE GREAT, king of the English, 910. Ecclesiastical laws, CXXXVIII, 447 ff.

ALGER, canon and schoolmaster of Liège, 1140. 1. Three books on the sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood. 2. On the sacrifice of the Mass. 3. Book on mercy and justice. 4. Short work on free will, CLXXX, 728 ff.

ALGRIN, John, Dean of Amiens and cantor of Abbeville, Cardinal of Sabina, 1200. Commentary on the *Song of Songs*, CCVI, 20 ff.

ALIENORA, or Eleanor, Queen of England, 1160. Letters to Pope Alexander III concerning letters sent by the supreme pontiff, CC, 1362. Letters to Celestine III concerning the release of Richard, king of the English, her son, CCVI, 1262 ff.

ALMANNUS, monk of Hautvillers, 868. Reply to Theudoin, provost of Châlons, concerning the writing of the life of Saint Memmius, CXXI, 385.

ALMODIS, Countess of Nîmes, 1066. Donation to the abbey of Saint Giles and its other dependencies, CLIX, 959.

ALOIN, 680. Donation made to the monastery of Saint Gall, LXXXVIII, 1204.

ALPERT, monk of Saint Symphorian at Metz, about 1024. 1. Short work on the bishops of Metz. 2. Two books on the diversity of times, CXL, 444 ff.

ALPHANUS, Saint, Bishop of Benevento, 615. Charter renouncing the rights of the Church of Saint Martin, LXXX, 326.

ALPHANUS, Archbishop of Salerno, 1085. 1. Poems in honor of Saints Sabina, Nicholas, Christina, Benedict, Peter the Apostle, Margaret the Virgin, Catherine, Ursula, Agnes, etc., and several others containing much relevant to sacred history—more than 2,000 verses. 2. Sermon of Alphanus on the Gospel words, “When Jesus was passing through his own city,” etc. 3. Life and Passion of Saint Christina, virgin and martyr, CXLVII, 1220 ff.

ALPHONSUS BONUSHOMO, Spaniard, about 1072. Letter on the Book of Samuel concerning the coming of the Messiah, translated by him from Arabic into Latin, to Master Hugh of the Order of Preachers, CXLIX, 336.

ALPHONSUS VIII, king of Spain, 1157. 1. Letter to Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, concerning the receipt of an annual payment. 2. His testament to Cluny, CLIX, 938, 973.

ALPHONSUS I, king of Portugal, 1185. Letters: to Pope Lucius II, by which he makes his kingdom tributary to the Roman Church, CLXXIX, 935; to Saint Bernard of Clairvaux, CLXXXII, 675. Charter of King Alphonsus, CLXXXV, 981. Privilege of Alphonsus, king of Portugal, granted to the monastery of Saint John, CLXXXVIII, 1675.

PETER ALPHONSI, a Christian converted from Judaism, 1106. 1. Dialogues in which the impious opinions of the Jews are refuted by the clearest arguments both of natural and heavenly philosophy, and certain more obscure passages of the prophets are explained. 2. *Clerical Discipline*, or moral tales, XXIX, CLVII, 536 ff.

ALRED, king of the English, 755. Letter to Lull, Archbishop of Mainz, XCVI, 823.

ALTFRID, Bishop of Münster, date unknown. Acts, or Life, of Saint Liudger, Bishop of Mimigernaford, XCIX, 770 ff.

ALULF, monk of Tournai, seventh century. On the exposition of the New Testament, LXXIX, 1137.

ALVARUS, Paul of Córdoba. See PAUL.

ALWALO, author of unknown date, about 1099. Letter of Alwalo to Pope L., requesting absolution from the excommunication imposed for injuries inflicted upon the provostship of Capua, CLI, 643.

AMALARD, monk of Orbais, 774. Letter to Lull, Archbishop of Mainz, XCVI, 847.

AMALARIUS, Archbishop of Trier, 815. 1. Letter to Emperor Charlemagne concerning the ceremonies of baptism, XCIX, 886. 2. Verses of Marinus, the same Amalarius, CI, 1288.

AMALARIUS, Symphosius, priest of Metz. See SYMPHOSIUS.

AMALASUINTHA, Queen of the Goths, 552. Four letters: to Emperor Justinian, the senate of the city of Rome, and the Empress Theodora, LXIX, 975, 797, 803, 804.

[Col. 0555]

AMALFRID, 685. Charter by which he grants Hunulfocurtis monastery to the monastery of Sithiu, LXXXVIII, 1209; CXXXVI, 1193.

AMALRIC, prior of the Holy Sepulchre and afterward Patriarch of Jerusalem, 1184. Certain privileges, CLV, 1178, 1208, 1221, 1210, 1244, 1266, 1276.

AMANDUS, Saint, Bishop of Maastricht, 679. Two charters of Saint Amandus: for Abbot Andrew, to whom he gives the estate of Barisiacum for constructing a monastery; codicil concerning the burial of his body, LXXXVII, 1268.

AMATUS, Archbishop of Bordeaux, 1100. Two letters, CLV, 1641.

AMBLARD, Abbot of Solignac, date unknown. Letter of Amblard to Hervé, canon of Tours, sending him a book on the life of Saint Eligius, bishop, CXXXVIII, 188.

AMBROSE, Saint, Bishop of Milan and Doctor of the Church, A.D. 397.

1. Six books of *Hexaemeron*.
2. One book on Paradise.
3. Two books on Cain and Abel.
4. One book on Noah and the Ark.
5. Two books on Abraham.
6. Two books on Isaac and the Soul.
7. One book on the Good of Death.
8. One book on Flight from the World.
9. Two books on Jacob and the Blessed Life.
10. One book on Joseph the Patriarch.
11. One book on the Blessings of the Patriarchs.
12. One book on Elijah and Fasting.
13. One book on Naboth the Jezreelite.
14. One book on Tobit.
15. Four books on the interpretation of Job and David.
16. Two apologies for the prophet David.
17. Expositions of twelve Psalms.
18. Exposition of the Gospel according to Luke.
19. Commentary on the *Song of Songs*, collected from the writings of Saint Ambrose.
20. Five books on the destruction of the city of Jerusalem; a summary of the history of Jerusalem’s destruction, that is, a recapitulation of everything said in the preceding books.
21. Three books on duties.
22. Three books on virgins.
23. One book on widows.
24. One book on virginity.
25. One book on the education of a virgin.
26. One book exhorting to virginity.
27. One book on the fall of a consecrated virgin.
28. One book on the mysteries.
29. Six books on the sacraments.
30. Two books on penance.
31. Five books on faith.
32. Three books on the Holy Spirit.
33. One book on the sacrament of the Lord’s Incarnation.
34. Ninety-one letters, divided into two classes.
35. Two books on the death of his brother Satyrus.
36. Consolation on the death of Valentinian.
37. Oration on the death of Theodosius.
38. Certain hymns.
39. On the forty-two stations of the children of Israel.
40. Commentaries on the Epistles of Blessed Paul.
41. Treatise on the Trinity.
42. Treatise on the orthodox faith.
43. Short work on the dignity of the priesthood.
44. Short work to a devout virgin.
45. Sixty-three sermons hitherto ascribed to Saint Ambrose.
46. Letters separated from the body of Ambrosian letters.
47. Two prayers before Mass.
48. Exposition of the seven visions of the Book of Revelation.
49. One book on penance.
50. Short work on the Holy Spirit.
51. On the harmony of Matthew and Luke in Christ’s genealogy.
52. Short work on the dignity of the human condition.
53. Exorcism.
54. Acts of Saint Sebastian.
55. Book on the conflict of vices and virtues.
56. Two books on the calling of the Gentiles; on the customs of the Brahmans.
57. Letters of several philosophers, of which Saint Ambrose is said to be the translator.
58. Explanation of the Creed for catechumens.
59. Hymns attributed to Saint Ambrose, XIV, XV, XVI, XVII.
60. Three sermons ascribed to Saint Ambrose: on perfection, almsgiving, and charity, XVIII, 109.

AMBROSE, Saint, Bishop of Cahors, 779. For writings attributed to him, see among the works of Saint Ambrose of Milan, XVI, LXXXIX, 1197.

AMBROSE AUTPERT, Saint, Abbot of Benevento, 778. 1. Two sermons and one homily: on avarice, on the Gospel reading, and on the Transfiguration of the Lord. 2. Life of Saints Paldus, Taso, and Tato, LXXXIX, 1277 ff.

AMBROSE, priest of Milan, tenth century. Letter to Atto of Vercelli, CXXXIV, 112.

AMBROSE, mayor of the palace of King Liutprand, 713. Privilege, LXXXVII, 1399.

AMADEUS, Blessed, Bishop of Lausanne, 1145–1149. 1. Letter to his sons of the Church of Lausanne. 2. Eight homilies on Mary, the Virgin Mother, CLXXXVIII, 1300, 1304.

AMADEUS, count, 1025. Charter concerning the church of Saint Maurice in the district of Maltacena, CXLII, 1042.

AMELIUS, Abbot of Aurillac, eleventh century. Entrusts to Hugh of Cluny the task of reforming the cell of Curiacum, CLIX, 942.

AMOENUS, author of unknown date. At the end of the fifth century. 1. *Enchiridion of the Old and New Testament*, about 200 hexameter verses, about 1176. 2. An Egyptian invoking the God of Martin escapes the danger of a storm. 3. Acrostic on Leontius, bishop restored to the Church of Bordeaux, LXI, 1076.

AMMONIUS, Alexandrian, date unknown. Gospel harmony, LXVIII, 255.

[Col. 0556]

AMPHILOCHIUS, Saint, Bishop of Iconium, about 378. Life of Saint Basil, Archbishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, LXXIII, 293.

AMULO, Bishop of Lyons, 853. 1. Two letters: to Theobald, Bishop of Langres, and to Gottschalk, on divine predestination and free will. 3. Sayings of Blessed Augustine on predestination and the grace of God, and on human free will, collected by Amulo, Bishop of Lyons. 4. Letter, or book, against the Jews, addressed to King Charles, CXVI, 77.

ANACLETUS, pope, A.D. 104. 1. Decrees on the oppression and accusation of bishops, the ordination of archbishops, primates and patriarchs, and their ministers. 2. Letters on the ordination of archbishops, the remaining bishops, and priests; on faith and other matters, CXXX, 59.

ANACLETUS, antipope, 1130–1137. Fifty-one letters and privileges, CLXXIX, 690.

ANAMODUS, subdeacon of the Church of Regensburg, 899. Two books of Saint Emmeram’s transactions, containing charters concerning gifts, exchanges, boundary arrangements, reciprocal exchanges, and agreements pertaining to the imperial monastery of Saint Emmeram of the Order of Saint Benedict, drawn up in the ninth century of Christ, CXXIX, 900 ff.

ANASTASIA AUGUSTA, 519. Letter to Pope Hormisdas, LXIII, 451.

ANASTASIUS I, Saint, pope, 401. Four letters; the latter two are wrongly attributed to him, XX, 66.

ANASTASIUS III, pope, 913. Two privileges, CXXXI, 1184.

ANASTASIUS IV, pope, 1154. Eighty-seven letters and privileges, CLXXXVIII, 990.

ANASTASIUS, abbot, priest of the Holy Roman Church, and librarian, 888. 1. Lives of the Roman pontiffs from Blessed Peter the Apostle to Nicholas I. 2. Translation of the Eighth General Synod. 3. Translation of the Seventh General Synod. 4. Translation of the chronology of Saint Nicephorus, Bishop of Constantinople. 5. Collections. 6. Headless history of the holy martyrs Cyrus and John, translated by Anastasius. 7. Passion of Saint Demetrius the martyr. 8. Acts of Saint Crispina, virgin and martyr. 9. Sermon of Saint Theodore the Studite on Saint Bartholomew the Apostle, translated by Anastasius. 10. Three letters: to Emperor Charles the Bald, concerning Saint Dionysius the Areopagite, first bishop of Paris, the Areopagitic writings, and John Scotus their translator; and to Ado, Archbishop of Vienne, CXXVII, CXXVIII, CXXIX, LXXX, 491. 11. Letter to Lauduleus concerning the writing of the translation of Saint Stephen, the protomartyr, XLI, 817.

ANASTASIUS, Saint, monk and hermit, 1085. Letter to Abbot Gerald on the truth of the body and blood of Christ the Lord, CXLIX, 424, 434.

ANASTASIUS, emperor, 518. Six letters to Pope Hormisdas concerning the restoration of peace to the Church in the matter of Acacius and his associates. He reproaches Hormisdas for excessive harshness, LXIII, 369, 373, 381, 383, 385, 409.

ANATOLIUS, Bishop of Constantinople, fifth century. Fragment of a letter to Saint Leo concerning his ordination, LIV, 854. Other letters to Saint Leo concerning proceedings at the Council of Chalcedon, etc., LIV, 975, 1082.

ANDREW, Bishop of Praevalitana, sixth century. Letter to Pope Hormisdas, LXIII, 443.

ANDREW. See AGNELLUS.

ANDREW, King of Hungary, 1048. Ecclesiastical constitutions, CLI, 1258.

ANDREW, Lord of Montbarry, twelfth century, CLXXXV, 1467.

ANDREW, priest of Bergamo, 877. Chronicle from 540 to 877, CLI, 1265.

ANDREW, Blessed, Vallombrosan and disciple of Saint Arialdus, 1076. Life of Saint Arialdus the deacon, CXLIII, 1438.

ANDREW, Blessed, Abbot of Struma, date unknown. Life of Saint John Gualbert, abbot and first founder of the Vallombrosan Congregation, CXLVI, 766.

ANDREW, monk of Fontevraud, disciple and confessor of Saint Robert, 1117. Life of Blessed Robert of Arbrissel, or his final manner of life and death, CLXII, 1057.

ANDREW, chancellor of the king of the Danes, 1195. Letter to Cardinal Melior, CCIX, 716.

ANDREW OF CALVINIAC, 1202. Oath of fidelity to the Roman Church, CCXVII, 286.

ANGELOMUS, monk of Luxeuil, 856. 1. Commentary on Genesis. 2. Expositions of the Books of Kings. 3. Expositions of the *Song of Songs*, CXV, 106.

ANGELRAMNUS, Bishop of Metz, 791. 1. Collection of canons presented to Pope Adrian. 2. Certain donations, XCVI, 1034.

ANGELRANNUS, Abbot of the monastery of Saint Richarius at Centula, 1045. Life of Saint Richarius, first Abbot of Centula, described in verse, CXLI, 1421.

ANGILBERT, Saint, Abbot of Centula, 814. 1. On the restoration of the monastery of Centula. 2. Certain statutes in rubric form. 3. About one hundred poems: a poem inscribed inside a certain tower; a poem to Pippin; two epitaphs, XCIX, 842 ff.

ANGILBERT, Abbot of Corbie, 890. Verses to Louis, king of the Franks and brother of Carloman, in a copy of Saint Augustine’s *On Christian Doctrine* sent as a gift to the same king, CXXIX, 784.

ANGILBERT PUSTERLA, Archbishop of Milan, 860. 1. Rescript of consultation, or exhortation, of the bishops to the Lord Emperor Louis. 2. Privilege for the Ambrosian basilica, CLI, 1260 ff.

ANITIUS, Saint, pope, 164. Decrees concerning the ordination of archbishops and the remaining bishops, and appeals from lesser to greater sees or to the Roman Church, CXXX, 116.

ANIANUS, deacon of Celeda, 410–415. 1. Translation of twenty-six homilies of Saint Chrysostom on Saint Matthew. 2. Translation of Chrysostom’s homilies in praise of Saint Paul. 3. Translation of Chrysostom’s sermon to the newly baptized. 4. Books against Saint Jerome’s letter to Ctesiphon (a lost work). See the preceding translations among the works of Saint Chrysostom, XXI, 1173.

ANNAEUS SYLVIUS, Bishop of Octodurus, 450. Calendar of Sylvius, L, 1293; XIII, 676; LIII, 965.

ANNEMUNDUS, Saint, Bishop of Lyons, 656. Charter of Saint Annemundus to the monastery of Saint Peter at Lyons, LXXXVII, 474; LXXXVIII, 1164.

ANNO, Saint, Archbishop of Cologne, 1072. Two diplomas, CXLIII, 1517, 1583.

ANNO, Abbot of Inda, 1147. Letter to Wibald, Abbot of Stavelot, CLXXXIX, 1143.

ANSBALD, monk, 711. Two charters by which he confers gifts upon Willibrord, CLXXXIX, 544, 545.

ANSCHAR, Saint, Bishop of Hamburg, 865. 1. Life of Saint Willehad, first Bishop of Bremen. 2. Letter of Ansgar, CXVIII, 1014 ff.

ANSEBERT, Bishop of Autun, 696. Charter for the Church of Saint Nazarius at Autun, LXXXVIII, 1231.

ANSEGISUS (St), Abbot of Fontenelle, A.D. 833. Constitution of Abbot Ansegisus, CV, 748.

ANSELLUS THE SCHOLAR, year uncertain. Metrical Vision of Ansellus the Scholar, CLI, 644.

ANSELLUS, cantor of the Holy Sepulchre, A.D. 1108. Letter to the Church of Paris, sending a portion of the wood of the Holy Cross, CLXII, 730.

ANSELM, monk of St Remigius at Rheims, about A.D. 1054–1057. History of the dedication of the Church of St Remigius at Rheims, CXLII, 1410.

ANSELM, canon of Liège, A.D. 1058. 1. Deeds of the Bishops of Tongeren, Maastricht, and Liège, CXLIII, 862; CXXXIX, 957, 1065. 2. Life of Wazo, Bishop of Liège, CXLII, 725.

ANSELM (St), Bishop of Lucca, A.D. 1085. 1. Two books Against Guibert the Antipope, in Defence of Gregory VII, the Lawful Roman Pontiff. 2. Collections. 3. Canonical Collection, arranged in thirteen books. 4. Spurious minor works: meditations on the Lord’s Prayer; on the Salutation of the Blessed Virgin Mary; on the *Salve Regina*; on the deeds of Our Lord Jesus Christ; etc., CXLIX, 436, 446 ff.

ANSELM OF RIBEMONT, A.D. 1099. Letter to Manasses, Archbishop of Rheims, concerning the expedition to Jerusalem, CLV, 469.

ANSELM OF GEMBLOUX, A.D. 1112. Chronicle; Continuation of the Chronicle of Sigebert of Gembloux from the year 1112 to the year 1148, CLX, 240.

ANSELM (St), Archbishop of Canterbury, A.D. 1109. Dogmatic works: 1. *Monologion on the Essence of the Divinity*. 2. *Proslogion*, or Discourse on God’s Existence. 3. Apologetic Book against Gaunilo. 4. Book on Faith in the Trinity and on the Incarnation of the Word, against the Blasphemies of Ruzelin or Roscelin. 5. Book on the Procession of the Holy Spirit against the Greeks. 6. Dialogue on the Fall of the Devil. 7. Two Books, *Why God Became Man*. 8. Book on the Virginal Conception and Original Sin. 9. Dialogue on Truth. 10. Book on the Will. 11. Dialogue on Free Will. 12. Treatise on the Harmony of Foreknowledge and Predestination, and also of God’s Grace, with Free Will. 13. On Waleran’s Three Questions, and Especially on Unleavened and Leavened Bread. 14. On the Diversity of the Sacraments, to Bishop Waleran. 15. On Concubinary Priests, or the Stumbling-block of Priests. 16. On Marriages of Kindred. 17. Dialogue on the Grammarian. 18. Book on the Will of God.

Ascetical and paraenetic works: 1. Sixteen homilies on the Gospels of St Matthew, St Luke, and St [Col. 0558] John, etc.; sermon on the Passion of the Lord; exhortation to contempt for temporal things and desire for eternal things. 2. Admonition to a Dying Man Who Is Excessively Afraid Because of His Sins. 3. Poem on Contempt for the World, about 1,000 verses. 4. Book of Meditations and Prayers. 5. Treatise on Peace and Concord. 6. Hymns and Psalter concerning the Holy Virgin Mary. 7. Verses on his predecessor Lanfranc.

Letters: four books of Letters: seventy-seven letters in the first, fifty-three in the second, 188 in the third, and 129 in the fourth, CLVIII, CLIX.

ANSELM, scholar and canon of Laon, A.D. 1117. 1. Expositions on the Song of Songs. 2. Expositions on the Gospel of Matthew. 3. Expositions on the Apocalypse. 4. Letter to H., Abbot of St Lawrence at Liège, CLXII, 1169.

ANSELM, Bishop of Havelberg, A.D. 1154. 1. Book on the Order of Regular Canons. 2. Apologetic Letter for the Order of Regular Canons. 3. Three Books of Dialogues: On the Unity of Faith and the Manifoldness of Living, from Righteous Abel to the Last Elect; On the Procession of the Holy Spirit against the Greeks; On the Different Eucharistic Rite of Greeks and Latins—namely, unleavened and leavened bread—and on the Authority of the Roman Church, CLXXXVIII, 1087; CLXXXIX, 1243.

ANSELM, Archbishop of Milan, A.D. 1000. Two Privileges, CLV, 1655.

ANSOLD, donor at Chartres, A.D. 1088. Grant of the vicarage of Our Lady, CLV, 358.

ANTERUS, pope, A.D. 239. Decrees, CXXX, 145.

ANTONINUS HONORATUS, Bishop of Constantine, A.D. 438. Consolatory Letter to Arcadius, driven into exile by Genseric, King of the Vandals, L, 567.

ANTONINUS OF PIACENZA, year uncertain. Itinerary to the Holy Places, LXXII, 897.

ANTONIUS, disciple of St Simeon Stylites, A.D. 385. Life of St Simeon Stylites, LXXIII, 325.

ANTONIUS, poet, years uncertain, fourth century. Poem Against the Pagans, about 150 verses, V, 261.

ANULINUS, proconsul under Constantine the Great. Letter to Constantine, VIII, 480.

APOLLINARIS, Bishop of Valence, A.D. 492–500. Two Letters to Avitus, Bishop of Vienne, LIX, 231, 273.

ARATOR, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, A.D. 551. 1. Two letters in verse: to Florian concerning his verses; to Pope Vigilius, to whom he presents his poems on Luke. 2. Two books On the Acts of the Apostles, 1,250 hexameter verses. 3. Letter to the patrician Parthenius: at whose urging he sings sacred themes, praises him, and asks that he may graciously deign to receive his poems, LXVIII, 46 ff.

ARCADIUS, emperor, A.D. 407. Two letters to Pope Innocent I, asking him to free himself and Eudoxia from excommunication, XX, 633.

ARCULF (St), bishop, early eighth century. Three Books on the Holy Places, based on the account of Arculf, a Gallic bishop, LXXXVIII, 780, 721.

ARDUICUS, Bishop of Besançon, A.D. 850–869. Letters to Hincmar and to the bishops established in King Louis’s realm, CXXI, 382.

ARDUIN, of Chartres, A.D. 996. Grant concerning the meadows of Teuvas, CLV, 249.

AREDIUS, Bishop of Vaison, A.D. 683. Charter for the monastery of Grasello, LXXXVIII, 1204.

AREFASTUS, monk of Chartres, A.D. 1028. On the things which he gave to the monastery of St Peter at Chartres, CLV, 202.

AREGIUS (St), Abbot of Attane, A.D. 591. Testament of Aregius, LXXII, 774; LXXI, 119, 1143.

ARIALD (St), deacon and martyr, A.D. 1066. Discourses: to the clergy of Milan on priestly continence; to Pope Alexander, asking that Herlembald be made Standard-bearer of the Church, CXLIII, 1516; CXLVIII, 935.

ARIBO, Archbishop of Mainz, A.D. 1031. Council of Seligenstadt, held in the matter of ecclesiastical discipline in the year of our Redeemer 1022, under Aribo’s presidency, CXLI, 1109; CXL, 1058.

ARIBO THE SCHOLAR, A.D. 1090. Aribo’s *Music*, CL, 1308.

ARICHIS, Duke of the Lombards, A.D. 769. Chapter for the Church of St Mary at Benevento. Privilege for the church and monastery of St Sophia, LXXXVII, 1417, 1418.

ARISTOTLE, Athenian philosopher. Philosophical maxims or axioms collected from Aristotle, in the Venerable Bede, XC, 966. Various works of Aristotle annotated, LXIV, 159, 639, 712, 909.

ARIUS, heresiarch and presbyter of Alexandria, A.D. 336. Statement of Faith presented to Emperor Constantine, VIII, 564.

ARMENIUS, monk, year uncertain. On the Canonical Books of the Old and New Testament, together with a Confession of the Catholic Faith, LXXIV, 1243.

ARNALD, prior of the Holy Sepulchre, twelfth century. Privilege, LV, 1219.

[Col. 0559] ARNALD, Abbot of St Peter the Living at Sens, A.D. 1124. Three letters: to Josceran, Bishop of Langres; to Bernard, Abbot of St John at Réome; and to King Louis, CLXIII, 1473.

ARNALD, Abbot of Cîteaux, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Innocent III concerning the victory won against heretics, CCXVI, 137.

ARNO, provost of Reichersberg, A.D. 1175. 1. Shield of the Canons. 2. Fragment from a Book against Folmar, CXCIV, 1490.

ARNOBIUS OF AFRICA, about A.D. 304. Seven Books of Disputations against the Pagans, V, 714.

ARNOBIUS THE YOUNGER, about A.D. 460. 1. Two Books on the Conflict concerning God Three and One, the Two Substances in Christ in Unity of Person, and the Harmony of Grace and Free Will. 2. Commentaries on the Psalms. 3. Notes on Certain Passages of the Gospels, LIII, 238.

ARNOLD, Bishop of Halberstadt, A.D. 1011. Letter to Henry, Bishop of Würzburg, concerning the establishment of the bishopric of Bamberg, CXXXIX, 1494.

ARNOLD, formerly Count of Vohburg, monk and dean of St Emmeram, about A.D. 1040. 1. Two Books on the Miracles and Commemoration of Blessed Emmeram. 2. Homily on the Eight Beatitudes and St Emmeram, CXLI, 985, 1089.

ARNOLD, Archbishop of Cologne, A.D. 1151. Letters and diplomas, CLXXXIX, 1284, 1401, 1404, 1405, 1480, 1482; CXCVII, 163; CC, 9.

ARNOLD, Archbishop of Trier, twelfth century. Letter to St Hildegard, CXCVII, 181.

ARNOLD, Archbishop of Mainz, A.D. 1178. Letter to St Hildegard, CXCVII, 157.

ARNULAUS, hermit, twelfth century. Letter to Peter of Poitiers, CLXXXIX, 360.

ARNULF, Archbishop of Rheims, A.D. 1023. 1. Arnulf’s Oath and the Acts of His Election. 2. Warning against Robbers. 3. Short Book of Arnulf’s Abdication. 4. Arnulf’s letters and privileges, CXXXIX, 1543 ff.

ARNULF, priest of Flanders, A.D. 1147. Letter to Milo, Bishop of Thérouanne, on how Lisbon was captured, CLXXIX, 1813.

ARNULF, cleric of Milan, A.D. 1079. Five Books of the Deeds of the Archbishops of Milan, CXLVII, 280, 286.

ARNULF OF BOERIES, Cistercian monk, A.D. 1149. Mirror of Monks, CLXXX, 1658; CLXXXV, 1175.

ARNULF, chaplain to the Duke of Normandy and afterward Patriarch of Jerusalem, about A.D. 1124. Privilege and letter, CLV, 1115, 469.

ARNULF, Duke of the Burgundians, A.D. 706. Charters for the monastery of the Holy Apostles near Metz and for the monastery of Echternach, LXXXVIII, 1249; LXXXIX, 549.

ARNULF, Bishop of Lisieux, A.D. 1184. 1. One hundred and thirty letters, to Henry II, King of England; St Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury; and others. 2. Four sermons, three delivered at the Council of Tours and the fourth on the Blessed Virgin Mary. 3. Treatise on the schism arising after the death of Pope Honorius II. 4. Poems: on the Nativity of the Lord; on spring renewal; to a beggar-poet; to wanton companions; the epitaph of Empress Matilda; etc., about 300 verses, CCI, 9 ff.

ARTHALD, Archbishop of Rheims, A.D. 961. Letter to the synod assembled at Ingelheim, CXXXIII, 957.

ARTMANN, viscount, A.D. 1082. Charter of the foundation of a monastery below the castle of Brunechild in the district of Cahors, CLIX, 971.

ASCARICUS, bishop, early eighth century, date uncertain. Two Letters, XCIX, 1232.

ATHALARIC, king, A.D. 535. Letters: to Pope John II concerning simoniacs; to the Senate of the city of Rome; etc., LXVI, 11; LXIX, 733; LXXII, 1118.

ATHANASIUS (St), Archbishop of Alexandria, A.D. 354. 1. Reply of St Athanasius to Liberius, Bishop of Rome, VIII, 1397. 2. Two letters to Lucifer, XIII, 1037. 3. Life of Blessed Antony the Abbot, LXXIII, 125. 4. On the Observances of Monks, CIII, 665. 5. Exhortation to the Bride of Christ, ibid., 672.

ATTO, Bishop of Vercelli, A.D. 960. 1. Capitular. 2. Short Book on Ecclesiastical Oppressions. 3. Eleven letters. 4. Exposition on the Epistles of St Paul. 5. Seventeen sermons. 6. Polyptych called the *Perpendiculum*, CXXXIV, 9 ff.

ATTO, Bishop of Pistoia, A.D. 1153. Life of St John Gualbert, CLXXXVIII, 986; CXLVI, 667.

ATTO, Bishop of Troyes, A.D. 1154. Two letters to Peter the Venerable of Cluny, CLXXXIX, 271, 303. Grant, ibid., 1066. Two diplomas, CLXXXV, 1920.

AUDOBERTUS OF TREMOILLE, of Poitiers, twelfth century. Grant of the site at Ville-Salem, CLXII, 1111.

AUDOENUS (St), Bishop of Rouen, A.D. 659. Life of St Eligius, Bishop of Noyon, LXXXVII, 482.

[Col. 0560] AUDOMAR, Bishop of Thérouanne, A.D. 662. Charter of Audomar for the basilica of St Mary, which he established, exempting it from every episcopal jurisdiction, LXXXVIII, 1174.

AUDRAD, chorepiscopus of Sens, A.D. 854. 1. Audrad’s letter to Hincmar, written in verse. 2. Book on the Fountain of Life, written in verse, about 250 lines. 3. Extracts from the Book of Revelations, CXV, 15 ff.

AUGUSTINE (St), Bishop of Hippo, A.D. 387–430. 1. Two Books of Retractions. 2. Thirteen Books of Confessions. 3. Two Books of Soliloquies. 4. Three Books Against the Academics. 5. One Book on the Happy Life. 6. Two Books on Order. 7. One Book on the Immortality of the Soul. 8. One Book on the Greatness of the Soul. 9. Six Books on Music. 10. One Book on the Teacher. 11. Three Books on Free Will. 12. Two Books on the Morals of the Catholic Church and on the Morals of the Manichaeans. 13. Rule for Servants of God, XXXII, 584 ff. 14. Two hundred and seventy letters, XXXIII, 62 ff. 15. Four Books on Christian Doctrine. 16. One Book on True Religion. 17. Two Books on Genesis against the Manichaean. 18. Twelve Books on Genesis according to the Letter. 19. Seven Books of Expressions in Sacred Scripture. 20. Seven Books of Questions on the Pentateuch. 21. One Book of Annotations on Job. 22. Mirror of Sacred Scripture. 23. Five Books on the Harmony of the Evangelists. 24. Two Books on the Lord’s Sermon on the Mount according to Matthew, XXXIV, 15 ff. 25. Two Books of Questions on the Gospels. 26. One Book of Seventeen Questions on the Gospel according to Matthew. 27. Twenty-four Treatises on the Gospel of John. 28. Ten Treatises on John’s Epistle to the Parthians. 29. One Book, Exposition of Certain Propositions from the Epistle to the Romans. 30. Unfinished Exposition of the Epistle to the Romans. 31. One Book, Exposition on Galatians, XXXV, 1322 ff. 32. Expositions on the Psalms, XXXVI–XXXVII. 33. Three hundred and ninety-six sermons; fragments of sermons, XXXVIII–XXXIX. 34. One Book of Eighty-three Diverse Questions. 35. Two Books of Diverse Questions, to Simplicianus. 36. One Book on Dulcitius’s Eight Questions. 37. One Book on Faith in Things Not Seen. 38. One Book on Faith and the Creed. 39. One Book on Faith and Works. 40. One Book, *Enchiridion on Faith, Hope, and Charity*. 41. One Book on the Christian Contest. 42. One Book on Instructing Beginners. 43. One Book on Continence. 44. One Book on the Good of Marriage. 45. One Book on Holy Virginity. 46. One Book on the Good of Widowhood. 47. Two Books on Adulterous Marriages. 48. One Book on Lying. 49. One Book on the Work of Monks. 50. One Book on the Divination of Demons. 51. One Book on Care to Be Taken for the Dead. 52. One Book on Patience. 53. Four Treatises on the Creed for Catechumens. 54. One Treatise on Christian Discipline. 55. One Treatise on the New Song. 56. One Treatise on Wednesday. 57. One Treatise on the Flood. 58. One Treatise on the Time of the Barbarians. 59. One Treatise on the Unity of Fasting. 60. One Treatise on the Destruction of the City, XL, 12 ff. 61. Twenty-two Books, *The City of God against the Pagans*, XLI, 13 ff. 63. One Book on Heresies, to Quodvultdeus. 63. Treatise against the Jews. 64. One Book on the Usefulness of Believing, to Honoratus. 65. One Book on Two Souls against the Manichaeans. 66. One Book, Acts or Disputation against Fortunatus the Manichaean. 67. One Book against Adimantus, Disciple of Mani. 68. One Book against the Letter of Mani called *The Foundation*. 69. Thirty-three Books against Faustus the Manichaean. 70. Two Books on the Proceedings with Felix the Manichaean. 71. One Book on the Nature of the Good against the Manichaeans. 72. One Book against Secundinus the Manichaean. 73. Two Books against the Opponent of the Law and the Prophets. 74. One Book to Orosius, against the Priscillianists and Origenists. 75. One Book against the Sermon of the Arians. 76. Conference with Maximinus, Bishop of the Arians. 77. Two Books against the Same Arian Maximinus. 78. Fifteen Books on the Trinity, XLII, 22 ff. 79. Psalm against the Party of Donatus. 80. Three Books against the Letter of Parmenian. 81. Seven Books on Baptism against the Donatists. 82. Three Books against the Letters of Petilian. 83. Letter to Catholics against the Donatists, commonly called the One Book on the Unity of the Church. 84. Four Books against Cresconius the Donatist Grammarian. 85. On the Only Baptism against Petilian. 86. Brief Account of the Conference with the Donatists. 87. One Book to the Donatists after the Conference. 88. Sermon to the People of the Church of Caesarea. 89. One Book on the Proceedings with Emeritus. 90. Two Books against Gaudentius, Bishop of the Donatists. 91. Sermon on the Subdeacon Rusticianus, XLIII, 24 ff. 92. Three Books on the Merits and Forgiveness of Sins. 93. One Book on the Spirit and the Letter. 94. One Book on Nature and Grace. 95. One Book on the Perfection of Human Righteousness. 96. One Book on the Proceedings against Pelagius. 97. Two Books on the Grace of Christ and Original Sin. 98. Two Books on Marriage and Concupiscence. 99. Four Books on the Soul and Its Origin. 100. Four Books against Two Letters of the Pelagians, to Boniface. 101. Four Books against Julian. 102. One Book on Grace and Free Will. 103. One Book on Rebuke and Grace. 104. On the Predestination of the Saints, XLIV, 109 ff. 105. One Book on the Gift of Perseverance. 106. An Unfinished Work against Julian’s Second Reply, comprising six books, [Col. 0561] XLV, 994. 107. Unpublished Sermons, XLVI, 818 ff.

AUGUSTINE (St), Apostle of the English, A.D. 604. 1. Letters, LXXX, 93. 2. Privilege granted by St Augustine to the Abbey of Canterbury, LXXX, 96.

AUNARIUS (St), Bishop of Auxerre, A.D. 578. 1. Synod held by Aunarius. 2. Letter to Abbot Stephen, exhorting him to compose the life of St Amator, LXXII, 760.

AURELIANUS (St), Bishop of Arles, A.D. 545. 1. Rule for Monks. 2. Rule for Virgins. 3. Extracts from Aurelianus’s letter to King Theudebert, the Elect, LXVIII, 386.

AURELIANUS, monk of Réome, A.D. 851. Letter to Bernard, arch-cantor and future archbishop, prefixed to the book on Music composed by him, CVI, 1521.

AURELIUS (St), Bishop of Carthage, A.D. 420. 1. Letter to all bishops established throughout the provinces of Byzacena and Arzugitana. 2. Synodal Letter of Aurelius, XX, 1008.

AURINANDUS, citizen of Lucca, A.D. 823. Founds the monastery of St Peter at the place called Castellione, LXXXVII, 1368.

AUSONIUS, poet of Bordeaux, A.D. 393. 1. One hundred and eleven epigrams. 2. *Ephemeris*, that is, the business of an entire day. 3. Thirty poems for deceased relatives. 4. Commemoration of the professors of Bordeaux. 5. Epitaphs of heroes. 6. Quatrains. 7. Order of Noble Cities. 8. Play of the Seven Sages. 9. Twenty idylls. 10. Twenty-one eclogues. 11. Twenty-four letters written in verse. 12. Ausonius’s thanksgiving to Emperor Gratian, his pupil, for the consulship. 13. Summaries of Homer’s *Iliad* and *Odyssey*, XIX, 824 ff.

AUSPICIUS (St), Bishop of Toul, A.D. 470. Letter to Arbogast, Count of Trier, written in verse, LXI, 1005.

AUTBERTUS (St), Bishop of Cambrai, A.D. 640. Charter concerning the monastery of Wallers, by which he receives the estate of Wallare into his protection, LXXX, 595.

AUTCONDA OF LUCCA, A.D. 744. Founds a monastery in the city of Verona, LXXXVII, 1374.

AUTPERTUS (St) AMBROSIUS. See AMBROSIUS.

AUTPERTUS, Abbot of Monte Cassino, A.D. 837. Sermon on St Matthias, CXXIX, 1023.

AUXILIUS, Frankish priest, ninth century, date uncertain. 1. On Ordinations Performed by Pope Formosus. 2. Short Book on the Case and Affair of Pope Formosus, CXXIX, 1054.

AVESGOT, Abbot of St Peter of Couture at Le Mans, A.D. 1072. Letter to St Anselm, later Archbishop of Canterbury, CXLIII, 1431.

AVITUS, priest, date uncertain. Letter to Palchonius concerning the relics of St Stephen, etc., XLI, 805.

AVITUS (St), Bishop of Vienne, A.D. 494. 1. Eighty-eight letters. 2. Homily on the Rogations: whence the custom of Rogation Days arose. 3. Fragments of various minor works. 4. Five books of poems on the events of Mosaic History, about 3,000 hexameter verses. 5. On the Consolatory Praise of Chastity, to his sister Fuscina, a virgin consecrated to God. 6. Four letters, supplement to Sirmond’s edition of Avitus. 7. Fragments of a book on the divinity of the Holy Spirit. 8. Conference of bishops, especially Avitus of Vienne, before King Gundobad against the Arians. 9. Sermon for Tuesday in Rogationtide, LIX, 200 ff.; LXIII, 394.

AYMARD (St), third Abbot of Cluny, A.D. 994. Cartulary, CXXXVII, 704.

AZO, donor of Aquileia, A.D. 129, XCIX, 643.

## B

BACHIARIUS, monk, A.D. 420. 1. Bachiarius’s Profession of Faith. 2. Book on the Restoration of One Who Has Fallen, to Januarius, XX, 1016 ff.

BALBULUS NOTKER. See NOTKER.

BALDERIC, year uncertain. Deeds of Archbishop Albero, CLIV, 1307.

BALDERIC, Archbishop of Dol, A.D. 1130. 1. Four Books of Jerusalemite History. 2. History of the Translation of the Head of St Valentin, Martyr, to Jumièges in Gaul. 3. Life of St Hugh, Bishop of Rouen. 4. Baldric’s Itinerary, or Letter to the Monks of Fécamp. 5. Life of Blessed Robert of Arbrissel. 6. Historical Poems. 7. Acts of St Valerian, Martyr. 8. Diploma by which he confirms all the goods of the monastery of St Florentius, CLXVI, 1050 ff.

BALDWIN, Archbishop of Canterbury, A.D. 1188. 1. Various treatises: on the most holy sacrament of the Eucharist; on the corrupt morals of clergy and people; on the love of God; on the twofold resurrection; on heavenly rest; ... on the angelic salutation; on the wound of charity; on the evangelical beatitudes; ... on cenobitic life; on the perfect monk; on the commendation of faith. 2. Book on the Sacrament of the Altar, or Letter to Bartholomew, Bishop of Oxford, CCIV, 404 ff. 3. Letter to Pope Urban III, CCII, 1533.

[Col. 0562] BALDWIN, Count of Flanders, A.D. 1112. Letter to Pontius, Abbot of Cluny, CLXVI, 845.

BALDWIN, Count of Flanders and Emperor of Constantinople, A.D. 1197. Eleven letters and diplomas, CCIX, 914.

BALDWIN, Bishop of Noyon, A.D. 1150. Letters, CLXXX, 1628; CLXXXVI, 1417, 1423, 1425, 1435; CC, 1418.

BALDWIN OF VALENCE, twelfth century. Dialogue against the Jews, CCIX, 423.

BANDINUS, master and theologian, year uncertain in the twelfth century. Four Books of Sentences, in which the whole body of theology and a compendium of our faith are treated purely, simply, and methodically: 1. On the Most Holy Trinity. 2. On the Creation of the World and the Fall of Man. 3. On the Incarnate Word and the Restoration of Man. 4. On Ecclesiastical Sacraments, CXCII, 965 ff.

BARBEDAURUS, dean of the Church of Paris, A.D. 1173. Charter of an agreement between the chapter of the Church of Paris and Henry the Great, etc., CCV, 910.

BARTHOLOMEW (Bl), Abbot of Marmoutier, A.D. 1084. Letter to Ernald, Bishop of Le Mans, CXLIX, 394.

BARTHOLOMEW, Bishop of Laon, A.D. 1121. Pious grants made to St Norbert and the Premonstratensians, CLXX, 136.

BARTHOLOMEW, Bishop of Châlons, A.D. 1151. Letter to Abbot Suger, CLXXXI, 1722.

BARTHOLOMEW OF EXETER, A.D. 1171. Letter to Pope Alexander, CXCIX, 365; CC, 1461.

BASIL (St), Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, A.D. 379. 1. Rule for Monks, CIII, 483. 2. Admonition to a Spiritual Son, CIII, 684, 483.

BASIL, Prior of the Grande Chartreuse, twelfth century. Letter to Peter the Venerable, CLXXXIX, 458.

BASIL, Archbishop of Trnovo, A.D. 1204. Letter to Innocent III, CCXV, 288.

BAUCIO (HUGH DE), A.D. 1153. Letter to Wibald, Abbot, CLXXXIX, 1430.

BAUDONIVIA, nun, sixth century. On the Life of St Radegund, Queen of the Franks, LXXII, 663.

BEATUS (St), priest, A.D. 790. Letter to Elipandus, XCVI, 894.

BEDE THE VENERABLE, Anglo-Saxon priest, A.D. 730.

Didactic works: 1. On Orthography. 2. Book on the Art of Meter, to Wigbert the Levite. 3. Book on the Figures and Tropes of Sacred Scripture. 4. On the Nature of Things. 5. On Times. 6. On the Reckoning of Time. 7. On the Method of Computation. 8. On the Celebration of Easter. 9. On the Ordering of the Days of Easter. 10. On Thunder. 11. Doubtful minor works.

Exegetical works: 1. *Hexaemeron*, four books. 2. Commentaries on the Pentateuch. 3. Three Books on the Tabernacle and Its Vessels, and the Garments of the Priests. 4. Allegorical Exposition on the Prophet Samuel, four books. 5. Questions on the Books of Kings. 6. Book on Solomon’s Temple. 7. Three Books of Exposition on Ezra and Nehemiah. 8. Interpretation of the Book of Tobit. 9. Exposition on the Proverbs of Solomon. 10. Short Book on the Strong Woman. 11. Fragments on the Proverbs of Solomon. 12. Seven Books of Exposition on the Song of Songs. 13. Exposition on the Song of Habakkuk. 14. Exposition on the Gospel of St Matthew. 15. On the Gospel of St Mark. 16. On the Gospel of St Luke. 17. On the Gospel of St John. 18. Exposition on the Catholic Epistles. 19. Explanation of the Apocalypse. 20. On the Creation of the Six Days. 21. Questions on the Pentateuch. 22. Questions on the Book of Joshua. 23. Questions on the Book of Judges. 24. Questions on the Book of Ruth. 25. Questions on the Books of Kings. 26. Various Questions. 27. Exegesis of the Book of Psalms.

Paraenetic and ascetical works: 1. Forty-nine homilies on the feasts of Blessed Mary, the Lord Jesus, and other saints; on Advent, Lent, etc. 2. One hundred and nine spurious homilies. 3. Little Book of Prayers. 4. Little Book on the Offices. 5. Little Book on Meditation upon Christ’s Passion through the Seven Hours of the Day. 6. On Remedies for Sins.

Poems: 1. Metrical Life of St Cuthbert, Bishop of Lindisfarne. 3. Passion of St Justin, Martyr. 4. Poetic Martyrology. 4. Thirteen Hymns. 1. Sixteen letters, to Abbot Albinus, Bishop Ecgbert, Acca, etc.

Historical works: 1. Life of the Five Holy Abbots of the Monastery at Wearmouth and Jarrow—Benedict, Ceolfrith, Easterwine, Sigfrith, and Hwaetberht. 2. Prose Life of St Cuthbert, Bishop of Lindisfarne. 3. Book on the Life and Miracles of St Cuthbert of Lindisfarne. 4. Life of Blessed Felix the Confessor. 5. Martyrologies according to the Cologne and Bollandist exemplars. 6. Ecclesiastical History of the English People, XC, XCV.

BELETH (JOHN), Parisian theologian, A.D. 1182–1190. *Rationale of the Divine Offices*, CCII, 9 ff.

BENEDICT (St), head and protector of all Western monks, [Col. 0563] A.D. 543. 1. Rule of St Benedict, with commentaries, seventy-three chapters. 2. Sermon of St Father Benedict delivered at the departure of St Maurus and his companions. 3. Letter of St Benedict sent to St Maurus. 4. Supposititious writings: Letter to St Remigius, Bishop of Rheims; Sermon on the Death of St Placid; Monastic Order, explaining how brothers ought to live religiously and diligently in the monastery and serve as soldiers of the Lord, LXVI, 125 ff., 936.

BENEDICT I, pope, A.D. 573–577. 1. Fragment of a letter to the Patriarch of Grado on betrothals. 2. Letter to Bishop David, proving from the sacred writings that the supreme Trinity is unity, LXXII, 684.

BENEDICT (St) CRISPUS, Bishop of Milan, A.D. 725. 1. Complaint in a synod concerning Pope Constantine. 2. Medical poem written during his diaconate. 3. Epitaph of Ceadwalla, King of the Anglo-Saxons. 4. Letter to Boniface of Mainz, LXXXIX, 362, 776.

BENEDICT II, pope, A.D. 684. Two letters, to Peter the regional notary and to King Ervig, XCVI, 421.

BENEDICT THE DEACON, year uncertain. Collection of Capitularies, XCVII, 698.

BENEDICT (St), Abbot of Aniane, A.D. 821. 1. Code of Monastic and Canonical Rules collected by St Benedict, Abbot of Aniane. 2. Harmony of Rules, seventy-seven chapters. 3. Letters of St Benedict. 4. Five minor works: on the Incarnation of the Lord; on the Holy Trinity; on the repetition of baptism; Benedict the Levite’s disputation against the Felician impiety; Benedict the Levite’s confession of faith; an extract on the various modes of penances by Abbot Benedict, CIII, 394 ff.

BENEDICT III, pope, A.D. 858. 1. Four letters: to Hincmar, Archbishop of Rheims; to the bishops established in Charles’s kingdom; and to Louis, Abbot of St Denis. 2. Diploma of Benedict III, receiving the monastery of Fulda under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirming its immunities, CXV, 690. 3. Confirmation of Corbie’s privileges, CXXIX, 1002.

BENEDICT IV, pope, A.D. 905. 1. Two letters: to the bishops and princes of Gaul, etc.; and to the clergy and people of Langres. 2. Privilege granted by Pope Benedict to H., Abbot of Fulda, CXXXI, 40.

BENEDICT VI, pope, A.D. 974. Six letters and privileges: to Frederick, Bishop of Salzburg; to Theodoric, Bishop of Trier; to Peter, Abbot of the monastery of St Benedict; privilege for the monastery of Vézelay; for the monastery of St Peter at Rodez; and for the monastery of St Cecilia of Montferrat, CXXXV, 1080.

BENEDICT VII, pope, A.D. 983. Twenty-eight letters and privileges: to Gauls and Germans; concerning the rights of the Archbishopric of Trier; for the monastery of St Benedict at Trier; for the Church of Trier; for the monastery of Monte Cassino; for the monastery of St Peter at Perugia; for the Church of Ausona; for the monastery of Cluny; etc., CXXXVII, 314.

BENEDICT VIII, pope, A.D. 1024. Forty letters and decrees: to Bruno, Bishop of Langres; for the monastery of St Benignus at Dijon; for the Church of Urgell; for the Church of Bamberg; for the abbey of Farfa; to Emperor Henry; for the monastery of Monte Cassino; for the Church of Paderborn; to the bishops of Burgundy and Aquitaine; for the Church of Porto; to Count William; etc., CXXXIX, 1577.

BENEDICT IX, pope, A.D. 1033–1048. Ten letters and diplomas: to Gumbald of Bordeaux; to Roland, provost, and the other canons of the Church of St Florentina; for the Church of Silva Candida; for the monastery of Monte Cassino; to Poppo, Archbishop of Trier; to Adalbert, Archbishop of Hamburg; etc., CXLI, 1344 ff.

BENEDICT, monk of St Andrew’s, A.D. 1001. 1. Chronicle from the year 743 to the year 967. 2. Short Book on Imperial Power in the City of Rome, CXXXIX, 9 ff.

BENEDICT, canon of the Holy Church of St Peter, A.D. 1143. Book on the Ecclesiastical Order of the Entire Year, and especially on Apostolic Dignity and the Whole Curia, CLXXIX, 732.

BENEDICT, Abbot of Peterborough, twelfth century, year uncertain. Life of St Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury and Martyr, CXC, 267.

BERCTINUS, Master of the Knights Templar, twelfth century. Letter to Louis, King of the Franks, CLV, 1281.

BERENGARIUS, Viscount of Narbonne, about A.D. 1057. Berengarius’s complaint against Guifred, Archbishop of Narbonne, CXLIII, 837.
