BERENGARIUS, emperor, A.D. 921. Two diplomas, for the castle of Puzzuolo and for the castle of Savorgnano, XCIX, 638; CLI, 1283.

BERENGARIUS, heresiarch of Angers, A.D. 1088. Profession of faith, CXLVIII, 1455.

[Col. 0564] BERENGARIUS THE SCHOLAR, disciple of Abelard, A.D. 1150. 1. Apology against Blessed Bernard, Abbot of Clairvaux, and others who condemned Peter Abelard. 2. Letters to the Bishop of Mende, against the Carthusians, CLXXVIII, 1857 ff.

BERENGAUDUS, A.D. 890. Exposition on the Seven Visions of the Book of Revelation, CXXIX, 785; XVII, 763.

BERENGOSUS, Abbot of St Maximin at Trier, A.D. 1112. 1. Three books On the Praise and Discovery of the Holy Cross. 2. On the Mystery of the Lord’s Wood and the Visible and Invisible Light by Which the Ancient Fathers Once Deserved to Be Enlightened. 3. Five sermons: on the feast of martyrs; on martyrs; on one confessor; on the dedication of a church; and on the veneration of relics, CLX, 936.

BERNALD, priest, A.D. 1085. 1. Treatise on the Sacraments of Excommunicated Persons according to the teaching of the Holy Fathers. 2. Apology concerning the excommunication of Gregory VII, CXLVIII, 1062, 1067. 3. Apology for the decrees of Gregory VII against simoniacs, 1105. 4. On Avoiding Communion with Excommunicated Persons, ibid., 1181. 5. Apologetic Arguments against the Objections of Schismatics, 1220, etc., etc.

BERNARD, Frankish monk, A.D. 870. Bernard’s itinerary, made to the Holy Places in A.D. 870, CXXI, 569.

BERNARD, Archbishop of Vienne, A.D. 836. Letter to Emperor Louis on Jewish superstitions, CIV, 78.

BERNARD THE SCHOLAR OF ANGERS, about A.D. 1029. Book on the Miracles of St Faith, CXLI, 124.

BERNARD, Count of Auch, A.D. 1070. Grant, CLIX, 962.

BERNARD, Count of Bigorre, A.D. 1064. Grants the monastery of Blessed Felix and St Licerius to the monastery of Cluny, CLIX, 958; another grant, ibid., 963.

BERNARD, Count of Besalú, A.D. 1085. 1. Letter to Bernard, Abbot of Marseilles. 2. Diploma of Bernard, Count of Besalú, by which he subjects the abbey of Ripoll to the monastery of St Victor at Marseilles, CXLIV, 420.

BERNARD, Bishop of Lodève, A.D. 1098. Grant for the Church of St Gregory at Rodez, CL, 1549.

BERNARD OF TOLEDO, A.D. 1100. Four sermons on the antiphon *Salve Regina* (“Hail, Queen”), CLV, 146.

BERNARD, Abbot of St Saviour in Italy, A.D. 1140. Two letters, to Innocent and to Bernard of Clairvaux, CLXXXII, 547–548.

BERNARD OF HILDESHEIM, A.D. 1149. Letters to Abbot Wibald and to the monks of Corvey, CLXXXIX, 1220.

BERNARD, Bishop of Paderborn, A.D. 1149. Letters to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1242, 1419; to Eugenius III, ibid., 1276.

BERNARD OF BOURGES, twelfth century. Grant of a certain house to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, CLV, 1202.

BERNARD, first prior of the Charterhouse of Portes, A.D. 1151. Three letters: to Aymon de Varennes and Aymon de Rohoria on fleeing the world; to the nuns of Lyon, exhorting them to stricter discipline; and to Raynald the recluse, on how one ought to live before the Lord, CLIII, 885; CLXXXI, 1724.

BERNARD (Saint), Abbot of Clairvaux, 1155. 1. Four hundred and eighty-two letters: to his nephew Robert; to Arnold, Abbot of Morimond; to Adam, a monk; to Bruno, Archbishop of Cologne; to Pope Honorius; to Haimeric, Chancellor; to Humbald, Archbishop of Lyons; to Atto, Bishop of Troyes; to Hugh, Archbishop of Rouen; to Stephen, Bishop of Metz; to Hugh, Count of Champagne; to Theobald, Count of Champagne; to Louis, King of the Franks; to Geoffrey, Bishop of Chartres; to Guilencus, Bishop of Langres; to the monks of Flavigny; to Suger, Abbot of Saint-Denis; to certain nuns; to Pope Innocent; to Henry, King of England; to Emperor Lothair; etc. 2. Five books *On Consideration*, addressed to Eugenius III. 3. Treatise *On the Character and Office of Bishops*, or Letter XLII to Henry, Archbishop of Sens. 4. Sermon, or book, *On Conversion*, addressed to clerics. 5. Book *On Precept and Dispensation*. 6. *Apology* addressed to William, Abbot of Saint-Thierry. 7. Book *In Praise of the New Knighthood*, addressed to the Knights Templar. 8. Treatise *On the Degrees of Humility and Pride*. 9. Book, or treatise, *On Loving God*, addressed to Haimeric, Cardinal and Chancellor of the Holy Roman Church. 10. Treatise *On Grace and Free Will*, addressed to William, Abbot of Saint-Thierry. 11. Letter, or treatise, to Hugh of Saint-Victor, concerning baptism and other questions proposed by him. 12. Letter CXC, or treatise, to Pope Innocent II, *Against Certain Articles of Abelard’s Errors*. 13. Book *On the Life and Deeds of Saint Malachy, Bishop of Ireland*. 14. Treatise *On Chant*, or *On the Correction of the Antiphonary*. 15. [Col. 0565] Eighty sermons for the liturgical seasons, thirty-nine on the saints, and one hundred and twenty-five on various subjects. 16. *Sentences.* 17. *Parables* commonly attributed to Saint Bernard. 18. Formula for private confession. 19. Office for Saint Victor the Confessor. 20. Eighty-six sermons on the *Song of Songs*. Doubtful works, CLXXXII, CLXXXV [lacuna].

BERNARD, cardinal, 1153. Two letters: to Pope Eugenius III; to the Bishop of Halberstadt, CLXXX, 1640; CLXXXIX, 1426.

BERNARD, Bishop of Nevers, 1180. Letter to Alexander III, requesting that, in the case of Saint Thomas of Canterbury, he show some indulgence toward the King of England, CC, 1417.

BERNARD, Bishop of Porto, 1164. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 985.

BERNARD, Abbot of Fontis Calidi, of the Premonstratensian Order, 1190. Book against the sect of the Waldensians, CCIV, 793.

BERNARD GUIDO, Bishop of Lodève in France. *Life of Pope Innocent II*, CLXXIX, 28.

BERNELINUS, year unknown. *Music: a swift and true division of the monochord in the diatonic genus*, CLI, 654.

BERNERUS, Abbot of Hamularia, 982. 1. *On the Life of Saint Hunegundis, Virgin of Hamularia.* 2. *On the Translation of the Body of Saint Hunegundis, Virgin, among the people of Vermandois*, CXXXVII, 50.

BERNO, Abbot of Reichenau, 1048. 1. A small book concerning certain matters pertaining to the office of the Mass. 2. Book *On the Celebration of the Lord’s Advent*. 3. Dialogue on how the fasts of the Four Seasons are to be observed on their respective Saturdays. 4. Small works on music, on the varied modulation of psalms and chants, and on the harmonious diversity of tones. 5. Eleven letters: to Gero, Archbishop of Magdeburg; to Emperor Henry II; to H., Abbot of Saint-Saviour; to the monks of Reichenau; to H., a bishop; etc. 6. *Life of Saint Meginrad, Hermit and Martyr among the Swiss.* 7. *Life of Saint Ulrich, Bishop of Augsburg.* 8. Poem on the Trojan War, CXLII, 1047 ff.

BERNOWINUS, Bishop of Clermont, 824. Poems, about 120 verses: an epitaph for the Cross; etc., CV, 445.

BERTARIUS, Abbot of Monte Cassino, 884. 1. Poem on Saint Benedict, CXXVI, 976.

BERTARIUS, priest of Verdun, 915. *Deeds of the Bishops of Verdun*, CXXXII, 502.

BERTHEFREDUS, Bishop of Amiens, 662. Charter by which he grants privileges to the monastery of Corbie, LXXXVIII, 1178.

BERTHOLD, monk, 1054. 1. *Life*, or eulogy, of Hermann the Cripple, monk of Reichenau, CXLIII, 25. 2. Continuation of Hermann’s chronicle from 1054 to 1066, CXLIII, 264.

BERTHOLD, priest of Constance, 1080. Annals from 1055 to 1080, CXLVII, 344. Extracts from the Chronicle of Berthold of Constance, CXLVIII, 104, 209.

BERTHOLD, Abbot of Zwiefalten, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 284.

BERTHWALD of Sumerford, 686. Donation to Aldhelm of the Church of Malmesbury, LXXXIX, 313.

BERTICHRAMNUS (Saint), Bishop of Le Mans, 623. Testament of Saint Bertichramnus, LXXX, 388.

BERTIGISILUS, abbot, 646. Letter to Saint Desiderius, Bishop of Cahors, LXXXVII, 257.

BERTILINDIS, nun, 710. Charter by which she gives Bishop Willibrord all that she possesses from her maternal inheritance in Toxandria, LXXXIX, 343.

BERTOENDUS, Bishop of Châlons, 692. Charter for the monastery of Der, LXXXVIII, 1225.

BERTRADA and her son Charibert, 721. Charter for the monastery of Prüm, LXXXVIII, 1274.

BERTRAND, Count of Tripoli, 1100. Privilege concerning three estates, CLV, 1198.

BERTRAND, Patriarch of Aquileia, 1334. Transfer of the provostship of Saint Odalric to the church of Saint Mary at Udine, XCIX, 655.

BERTRAND DE BLANCESFORT, Master of the Templars, 1168. His letters to Louis the Younger, CXCV, 1000; CLV, 1269, 1272, 1277.

BERTRAND, Bishop of Bordeaux, 1165–1170. Letters to Alexander III concerning the rebellion of the monks of Saint-Macarius, CC, 1368.

BERTRAND, Bishop of Agen, 1182. Letter to Pope Lucius III reporting that Henry, the Young King of England, chose burial in the church of Rouen, CCI, 1377.

BILEHILT, donor, 734. Charter by which he founds and endows a convent outside the walls of Mainz, LXXXVIII, 1289.

BLIDEGISILLUS, deacon, 640. Charter for the monastery of Fossatus, LXXXVIII, 1157.

BOHEMOND, Prince of Antioch, 1111. Two letters: to Pope Urban concerning the siege of Antioch; to [Col. 0566] all Christ’s faithful concerning Christian victories over the Turks, CLV, 390.

BODOLUS, 748. Charter by which he confers gifts on the monastery of Hohenau, LXXXVIII, 1318.

BOETHIUS, Roman senator, 475–525. 1. Five books *On the Consolation of Philosophy*. 2. *On Unity and the One.* 3. Two books *On Arithmetic*. 4. Five books *On Music*. 5. Interpretation of Euclid’s geometry. 6. Commentaries on Porphyry. 7. Commentaries on Aristotle. 8. Commentaries on Cicero. 9. *On the Understanding of Rhetoric.* 10. *Distinction of Rhetorical Topics.* 11. *On the Discipline of Students.* 12. *On the Two Natures and One Person.* 13. *On the Unity of God.* 14. *Whether Father, Son, and Holy Spirit may be affirmed of God.* 15. *Whether everything that exists is good*, or *On the Hebdomads*. 16. Brief summary of the faith, LXIII–LXIV.

BONACURSUS, formerly a heretic, later a Catholic, 1190. Small book against the Cathars, CCIV, 776.

BONIFACE (Saint) I, pope, 419. Eight letters and decrees: to bishops established throughout Gaul concerning Maximus, Bishop of the city of Valence, accused of various crimes; to Rufus, that the Corinthians should receive Perigenes as the bishop they seek; to Emperor Honorius, or a petition that the prince establish that no pontiff should ever be ordained in Rome through canvassing; to Hilary, Bishop of Narbonne, that in every province no one should be ordained bishop in disregard of the metropolitan; to Rufus and the other bishops established throughout Macedonia, Achaia, etc., XX, 746.

BONIFACE II, pope, 530–531. Letters and decrees: to Caesarius of Arles concerning confirmation of the Second Synod of Orange; doubtful letter to Eulalius, Bishop of Alexandria, concerning the reconciliation of the Church of Carthage, LXV, 32, 43.

BONIFACE IV, pope, 607. Roman council under Boniface IV. Letter from the same to Æthelberht, King of the English, concerning the monastery established in the city of Canterbury, LXXX, 104.

BONIFACE V, pope, 625. Three letters: to Justus, Archbishop of Canterbury, to whom he sends the pallium; to Edwin, King of the English, whom he urges to Christian faith; to Æthelburh, wife of King Edwin, whom he congratulates on having received the faith, LXXX, 436.

BONIFACE (Saint), Bishop of Mainz and martyr, 747. 1. Thirty-nine letters: to Bishop Daniel; to Abbess Eadburga; to Archbishop Egbert; to Archbishop Nothhelm; to Pope Zachary; to Æthelbald, King of Mercia; to Cuthbert, his fellow bishop; to religious men in Gaul; to Pope Stephen; to Pippin, King of the Franks; etc. 2. The oath by which Saint Boniface bound himself to Pope Gregory II. 3. Fifteen sermons: on the true faith; on the origin of the human condition; on the twofold operation of righteousness; on the eight evangelical Beatitudes; on faith and works of love; on the Incarnation of the Son of God and the restoration of humankind; on the Lenten fasts; for the day of the Paschal solemnity; etc. 4. *Life and Martyrdom of Saint Livinus, Bishop and Martyr.* 5. Verse riddles concerning the virtues, sent by Saint Boniface to his sister, LXXXIX, 598; LXXXVII, 328.

BONIFACE, Marquis of Montferrat, 1203. Two letters to Pope Innocent III, CCXV, 105, 624.

BONIZO, Bishop of Piacenza, 1089. 1. *Book to a Friend*, or nine books *On the Persecution of the Church*. 2. Small book on the sacraments, sent to Walter, monk and prior of the monastery of León. 3. Fragment of a papal history. 4. *Bonizo’s Decretal*, CL, 782.

BORONUS of Honau, 726. Two charters for the monastery of Honau, LXXXVIII, 1280, 1312.

BOSO, King of Arles, 874. Reply of King-elect Boso to a synod, CXXXVIII, 789.

BOTWINUS, abbot, 756. Letter to Lullus, Bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 836.

BOVO, Abbot of Saint-Bertin, 1065. *On the Discovery and Elevation of the Body of Saint Bertin, Abbot*, CXLIII, 1369; CXLVII, 1141.

BRACILAUS, Duke of Bohemia, 1039. Laws of Bracilaus, enacted at the tomb of Saint Adalbert for the reform of morals, CLI, 1258.

BRAULIO (Saint), Bishop of Saragossa, 646. Thirty-two letters: to Isidore, Bishop of Seville; to Jactatus, priest; to Floridus, archdeacon; to Frunimianus, priest and abbot; to his sister Basilla; to Bishop Wiligild; to Honorius I; to Bishop Valentinus; to Aemilianus, priest and abbot; to King Chindaswinth; to Eugenius, Primate of Toledo; etc. 2. *Life of Saint Aemilianus the Confessor, surnamed Cucullatus.* 3. Acts concerning the martyrs of Saragossa, LXXX, 640.

BREGWINUS, abbot, about 761. Letter to Saint Lullus, Bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 843.

[Col. 0567] BRIDFERTUS, monk of Ramsey, 1008. 1. *Life of Saint Dunstan.* 2. Commentary on Bede’s book *On the Nature of Things*. 3. Commentary on the book *On Speech by Gesture*, CXXXIX, 1423.

BRUNO (Saint), Archbishop of Cologne, 965. Diploma confirming an exchange made between Werinfrid, abbot, and Count Warner, CXXXIV, 988.

BRUNO, Bishop of Langres, 1016. 1. Two letters: to Heldric, Abbot of Saint-Germain at Auxerre; to the clerics of Langres concerning continual confession of sins. 2. Charter conferring certain things upon the monastery of Bèze, CXXXIX, 1533.

BRUNO (Saint), Bishop of Würzburg, 1045. 1. Exposition on the Psalms. 2. Commentary on the Canticles. 3. Commentary on the Lord’s Prayer, the Apostles’ Creed, and the Athanasian faith, CXLII, 9 ff.

BRUNO, cleric of Magdeburg, 1079. *Book on the Saxon War*, CXLVII, 485.

BRUNO EUSEBIUS, Bishop of Angers, 1081. Letter to Master Berengar concerning the sacrament of the Eucharist, CXLVII, 1202.

BRUNO (Saint), founder of the Carthusian Order, in the year of the Lord 1100. 1. Exposition on the Psalms. 2. Exposition on all the Epistles of Paul. 3. Two letters: to Ralph the Green, provost of the Church of Reims; to his sons of the Grande Chartreuse. 4. Sermon on contempt for riches. 5. Confession, CLII–CLIII.

BRUNO, perhaps a monk, 1100. *Gregoriale*, CLV, 146; LXXIX, 681.

BRUNO (Saint) of Asti, Bishop of Segni, 1125. 1. Exposition on Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, and Deuteronomy. 2. On Job. 3. On the Psalms. 4. On Proverbs. 5. On the Canticles. 6. Commentaries on Matthew, Mark, Luke, John, and the Apocalypse. 7. One hundred and forty-three homilies. 8. Three unpublished sermons. 9. Six books of *Sentences*: on the figures of the Church; the ornaments of the Church; all things new; the Holy Trinity; the principal feasts; the praises of the Blessed Virgin Mary; feasts of martyrs, confessors, etc. 10. Various treatises: on the Incarnation of the Lord and his burial; on the unleavened sacrifice; on the sacraments, mysteries, and ecclesiastical rites of the Church. 11. *Life of Saint Pope Leo IX.* 12. Reply concerning the state of the Church. 13. *Life of Saint Peter, Bishop of Anagni.* 14. Four letters: to Peter, Bishop of Porto; to the bishops and cardinals of the Holy Roman Church; to Pope Paschal, CLXIV–CLXV.

BRUNO, Bishop of Hildesheim, 1156. Letter to Wichmann, Archbishop of Magdeburg, concerning the Bishop of Osnabrück, who, detained by illness, is unable to come to him, CLXXXIX, 1445.

BRUNO, Bishop of Strasbourg, 1130. Letter to Gerhoh, provost, CLXVI, 1348.

BUGGA, abbess, about 720. Letter to Saint Boniface of Mainz, LXXXIX, 690.

BULGARANUS, count, 610. Three letters addressed to the Bishop of France, LXXX, 107.

BURCARDUS, Abbot of Balerna, twelfth century. Congratulatory letter to Nicholas of Clairvaux concerning conversion and new love, CXCVI, 1605.

BURCHARD, Bishop of Worms, 1026. 1. Twenty books of decrees drawn from councils, the decrees of orthodox Fathers, and synods of various nations, CXL, 538 ff. 2. Letter to Alpert, ibid., 536.

BURGUNDOFARA, sister of Saint Faro, 632. Testament of Burgundofara for the benefit of the monastery of Eboriacum, LXXXVII, 1137.

## C

CADURCUS, provost of the tower of Bourges and chancellor, about 1150. Letter to Rotrou, Count of Perche, concerning the tower of Bourges, CLXXXVI, 1396.

CAECILIANUS, Bishop of Carthage, 314. Letter to Felix, VIII, 749.

CAESARIUS (Saint), Bishop of Arles, 542. 1. Sixty-nine sermons attributed to Saint Caesarius, found among the works of Saint Augustine. 2. Twenty-four homilies: on Easter; on the Day of Judgment; on almsgiving; on tithes; on performing penance; to monks; etc. 3. Small work *On the Observance of Widowhood*. 4. Rule for monks. 5. Rule for virgins. 6. Sermon to nuns. 7. Three letters: to Abbess Caesaria and her community; to a virgin dedicated to God. 8. Testament of Blessed Caesarius. 9. Second Council of Orange, concerning grace and free will against Faustus of Riez, composed by Saint Caesarius, LXVII, 997 ff.

CAESARIUS, patrician, 621. Three letters to King Sisebut, LXXX, 366, 368, 369.

CAIUS (Saint), pope, 295. 1. On the single decree attributed to [Col. 0568] Caius, concerning those to be ordained. 2. Letter of Pope Caius to Bishop Felix, concerning bishops accused, faith in Christ unto eternal life, etc., V, 180.

CALDONIUS, African confessor, 250. Letter to Cyprian concerning the lapsed, IV, 271. Another letter concerning Felicissimus, who had been excommunicated, IV, 331.

CALIXTUS (Saint), pope, 217. 1. Decrees concerning the fast of the Four Seasons and other matters. 2. Letter to all the bishops of Gaul, that conspiracies and other unlawful acts should not occur, CXXX, 130 ff.

CALIXTUS II, pope, 1124. Two hundred and eighty-one letters and privileges: to Adalbert, Archbishop of Mainz; to Didacus, Bishop of Compostela; to Bernard, Archbishop of Auch; to Frederick, Archbishop of Cologne; to Franco, Abbot of Tournus; privileges and bulls for various monasteries, CLXIII, 1093.

CALOJOANNES, Emperor of the Bulgarians, 1216. His letters to Pope Innocent III, CCXV, 155, 287, 290, 551.

CAMBIUS (P.), Bishop of Paris, 1208. Letter for the solemnity of the Circumcision of the Lord and of Saint Stephen, CCVII, 1168.

CAMENUS (Franciscus), 1115. Hymn to Saint Nicholas the Pilgrim, CLXII, 720.

CANAPARIUS (J.), monk, eleventh century. *Life of Saint Adalbert, Bishop of Prague and Martyr*, CXXXVII, 860.

CANCELLINUS, count, 1072. Donation for the foundation of the abbey and monastery of Mosnac, XCIX, 641.

CANDIDUS, Arian, about 372. 1. Book *On the Divine Generation*, addressed to Marius Victorinus the Rhetor, VIII, 1014. 2. Letter to Marius Victorinus the Rhetor, VIII, 1036.

CANDIDUS, author uncertain. *On the Image of God*, CI, 1359.

CANDIDUS, monk of Fulda, 840. 1. *Life of Saint Eigil, Abbot of Fulda*, CV, 381. 2. Small work on the Passion of the Lord. 3. Letter: whether Christ could have seen God with bodily eyes, CVI, 57.

CANGITHA, abbess, 733. Letter to Boniface, Archbishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 726.

CANUTE, King of the English, 1014–1036. Ecclesiastical laws, CLI, 1172.

CANUTE VI, King of the English, up to 1195. Diploma, CCIX, 754.

CAPPIDUS OF STAVRIA, Frisian priest, 943. *On the Life of Saint Odulph, Priest*, CXXXIII, 858.

CAPREOLUS, Bishop of Carthage, 432. Two letters: to the Council of Ephesus concerning the one person of Christ, God and man, against Nestorius; to Vitalis and Constantius concerning the same matter, LIII, 844.

CARILEFUS (Saint), priest and monk, first Abbot of Anisole, 540. Copy of a testament, LXXIV, 1262.

CARLOMAN, King of Austrasia, 771. Diplomas: for the monastery of Saint-Denis; for the monastery of Saint Gregory; concerning immunity for the Church of Argenteuil; for the monastery of Prüm; for the monastery of Honau; for the monastery of Novy; for the monastery of Grandval, XCVI, 1572 ff.

CARLOMAN, King of Gaul, 882. Capitularies, CXXXVIII, 791.

CHARLES, Mayor of the Palace, 741. Charter by which he gives the estate of Clichy to the basilica of Saint-Denis, LXXXVIII, 1302. Two charters: for the monastery of Maastricht; for the basilica of Saint-Saviour at Utrecht, LXXXIX, 552. Letter to bishops, dukes, etc., 699.

CHARLEMAGNE, emperor, 800–814. 1. Capitularies. 2. Diplomas, foundations, privileges, and pious donations concerning ecclesiastical matters: throughout Gaul, Italy, and Germany. 3. Twenty-four letters: to Offa, King of Mercia; concerning the schools of the Church of Osnabrück; to Baugulf, Abbot of Fulda, concerning literary studies; to his subjects concerning Paul the Deacon’s homiliary; to Queen Fastrada concerning victory over the Avars and the litanies; to Elipand and the other bishops of Spain; to Pope Leo III; to Garibald, Bishop of Liège; to Master Albinus; etc. 4. Four Carolingian Books, concerning images. 5. Nine poems: to Pope Adrian; epitaph of Pope Adrian I; to Alcuin; to Paul, monk of Monte Cassino; verses inscribed in a book of the Gospels; on the death of his Roland, XCVII, XCVIII.

CHARLES, King of Jerusalem and Sicily, 1382. Letter in favor of the Cardinal of Alençon, XCIX, 669.

CHARLES THE BALD, King of the Franks, 877. 1. Nine letters: to Pope Nicholas; to the bishops and counts of Gaul; to Pope Adrian II; to Ado, Archbishop of Vienne. 2. Small book of proclamation against Wenilo, Archbishop of Sens, CXXIV, 861; CXXXVIII, 527, 539.

CARTHUITUS, bishop, year unknown. *Life of Saint Stephen, First King of the Hungarians*, CLI, 1203.

[Col. 0569] CASSIAN (John), Abbot of Marseille, 430. 1. Twelve books *On the Institutes of the Coenobites*: on monks’ clothing; nocturnal prayers; daytime prayers; the institutions of renunciants; the spirit of gluttony; the spirit of fornication; the spirit of avarice; the spirit of anger; the spirit of acedia; the spirit of vainglory; the spirit of pride. 2. Twenty-four Conferences: on a monk’s aim and end; discernment; the three renunciations; the desire of flesh and spirit; the eight principal vices; the death of saints; the mobility of the soul and spiritual wickedness; principalities or powers; prayer; perfection; chastity; God’s protection; spiritual knowledge; divine charisms; friendship; definition; the three kinds of monks; the end of the cenobite and hermit; the end of penitence; the relaxation during the Fifty Days; nocturnal illusions; willing good and doing evil; mortification. 3. Seven books *On the Incarnation of Christ against Nestorius the Heretic*, XLIX–L.

CASSIODORUS AURELIUS SENATOR, Abbot of Vivarium, 560. 1. Twelve books of *Variae*, containing many letters of King Theodoric, King Athalaric, King Theodahad, etc. 2. Twelve books of the ecclesiastical history called the *Tripartite History*, from the three Greek authors Sozomen, Socrates, and Theodoret. 3. Chronicle addressed to King Theodoric. 4. Paschal computation. 5. Exposition on the Psalter. 6. Exposition on the *Song of Songs*. 7. *On the Instruction of Divine Scriptures.* 8. *On the Arts and Disciplines of Liberal Learning.* 9. *On Speech and the Eight Parts of Speech.* 10. *On Orthography.* 11. *On the Soul.* 12. Summaries of the Apostolic Epistles. 13. Summaries of the Acts of the Apostles. 14. Summaries of the Apocalypse, LXIX–LXX; LXVI, 13.

CATULFUS, year unknown. Epistolary Instruction to Blessed King Charles, XCVI, 1364.

CATWALLONUS, Abbot of Redon, 1038. Two letters: to Hildegard, Duchess of Anjou, wife of Fulk Nerra; to Letgarde, Abbess of Saint Mary, concerning charity, CXLI, 1281.

CEADWALLA, Anglo-Saxon king, seventh century. Donation, LXXXIX, 312.

CELERINUS, African confessor, 250. Two letters to Lucianus, III, 673; IV, 274.

CELLANUS, year unknown, eighth century. Letter to Saint Aldhelm, Bishop of Sherborne, LXXXIX, 99.

CELSUS, 308. Celsus’s preface on Jewish unbelief, addressed to Bishop Vigilius, VI, 49.

CENA, or CENE, nun, 733. Letter to Boniface of Mainz, LXXXIX, 733. Letter to Lullus, Bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 841.

CEOLFRIDUS, Anglo-Saxon priest, 709. Letter to King Naitan of the Picts, concerning the catholic Easter and Roman tonsure, LXXXIX, 350.

CEREALIS, Bishop of Castellum, 485. Small book against Maximinus the Arian, LVIII, 757.

CHILDEBERT, King of the Franks, 558. Constitution concerning the abolition of remnants of idolatry and the chaste celebration of holy-day festivals, LXXII, 1122.

CHILDEBERT III, King of the Franks, 695. Eleven diplomas of Childebert III for various monasteries, LXXXVIII, 1089 ff.

CHILDERIC II, King of the Franks, 660–673. Eleven diplomas for various monasteries, LXXXVII, 1286.

CHILDERIC III, King of the Franks, 743. Four diplomas: for the monastery of Saint-Bertin; for the estate of Ardennes; for the monastery of Anisole; for the monasteries of Stavelot and Malmedy, LXXXVIII, 1147 ff.

CHILPERIC II, King of the Franks, 716. Diplomas for the monastery of Saint-Denis; the monastery of Fontenelle; the monastery of Corbie; the monastery of Fossatus; the basilica of Saint Arnulf at Metz; the monastery of Saint-Bertin; etc., LXXXVIII, 1116 ff.

CHINDASWINTH, King of the Visigoths in Spain, 646. Letter to Saint Braulio, Bishop of Saragossa, LXXX, 678.

CHRISTIAN, Archbishop of Mainz, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 158.

CHRISTOPHER, usurper of the Apostolic See, 905. Diplomas of Christopher confirming the privileges of the Abbey of Corbie in the diocese of Amiens, CXXXI, 45.

CHRODEGANG (Saint), Bishop of Metz, 766. 1. Rule of canons. 2. Diploma for the foundation of the monastery of Gorze, LXXXIX, 1054.

CHRODOBERT, Bishop of Tours, 670. Judgment concerning an adulterous woman, LXXXVII, 1131; LIV, 1424.

CHROMATIUS (Saint), Bishop of Aquileia, 407. 1. Surviving treatises on the Gospel of Saint Matthew, XX, 328. 2. Sermon on the eight Beatitudes, ibid., 324.

CICERO, Roman orator, 43 BC. Cicero’s *Topics*, [Col. 0570] LXIV, 1039. Sayings collected from Cicero, XC, 1053.

CLAUDIUS, Bishop of Turin, c. 820. 1. *On the Books of Instruction of Letter and Spirit concerning Leviticus*, addressed to Abbot Theodemir. 2. Thirty questions on the Books of Kings. 3. Exposition on Saint Paul’s Epistle to the Galatians. 4. Exposition of the Epistle to Philemon. 5. Short chronicle, CIV, 610.

CLEMENT (Saint) I, pope, 93. 1. Canons of the Apostles promulgated through Pope Clement. 2. Five letters: to James, brother of the Lord; to the same, concerning consecrated vestments and vessels and the office of priesthood and clerics; to his disciples, who had in some measure gone astray through the persuasions of evil men; to the nations among whom they live; on the common life, CXXX, 16 ff.

CLEMENT II, pope, 1047. Eight letters and privileges: for the Church of Fulda; for the monastery of Fulda; to all the children of the Church; for the Church of Hamburg; to Geoffrey, Count of Anjou, and Agnes, his countess and wife; for the monastery of Tharisis; to John, Archbishop of Salerno; for the Church of Bamberg, CXLII, 574.

CLEMENT III, pope, 1191. 1. One hundred and sixty-one letters and privileges. 2. Fifty-six decrees, CCIX, 1276 ff.

CLEMENTIA, Countess of Flanders, 1109. Letter to Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, inviting him to reform the monastery of Saint-Bertin, CLIX, 939. Letter to Lambert, Bishop of Arras, CLXII, 664.

CLEMENTIANUS FORTUNATUS, Italian priest, fourth century. Verses on Easter, VII, 285.

CLOVIS I, King of the Franks, 511. Ordinance to bishops after the Gothic War, concerning captives, both clerics and laypeople, to be released on the judgment and testimony of bishops, LXXII, 1118.

CLOVIS II, King of the Franks, 656. Three diplomas for the monastery of Saint-Denis, LXXXVII, 681 ff.

CLOVIS III, King of the Franks, AD 691. Seven privileges: for the monastery of Saint-Bertin; for the monastery of Saint-Denis . . . for the monastery of Anisole . . . for the monastery of Grasse; etc., LXXXVIII, 1080 ff.

CLOTHAR I, King of the Franks, 558. General constitution for all officials, that in all cases the standard of ancient law be maintained, LXXII, 1120.

CLOTHAR II, King of the Franks, 628. Ecclesiastical ordinances; decrees concerning slaves and sanctuaries; edict concerning the Synod of Paris; ordinance for the monastery of Saint-Denis; letter to Arnulf, LXXX, 448.

CLOTHAR III, King of the Franks, 660–670. Four diplomas: for the monastery of Saint-Denis, the monastery of Corbie, etc., LXXXVII, 1277.

CELESTINE (Saint) I, pope, 432. Thirteen letters and decrees: to the bishops of Illyricum; to bishops of the provinces of Vienne and Narbonne; to all bishops established throughout Apulia and Calabria; to bishops throughout the East; to Nestorius; to the clergy and people of Constantinople; to Cyril, Bishop of Alexandria; to the Council of Ephesus; to Emperor Theodosius; to the bishops of Gaul; to the Council of Ephesus after Nestorius’s condemnation; etc., L, 407.

CELESTINE II, pope, 1144. Fifty letters and privileges: for the Church of Saint Marianus at Gubbio; to Alvisus, Bishop of Arras; for the Church of Saint John at Monza; for the Church of Cella Superior at Würzburg; for the principal Church of Augsburg; for the monastery of Saint Martin at Ahu; for the monastery of Thenol; for the Premonstratensian monastery; to Arnald, Archbishop of Narbonne; to Hugh, Archbishop of Tours; for the monastery of Rota; for the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem; etc., CLXXIX, 761.

CELESTINE III, pope, 1198. 1. Three hundred and thirty-one letters and privileges. 2. Seventy decrees, CCVI, 868 ff.

CELESTIUS, disciple of Pelagius, 415. 1. Statement of faith presented by Celestius to Pope Zosimus. 2. Summary of a letter to the Roman clerics. 3. Book against original sin. 4. Definitions concerning sinlessness, XXI, 1173; XLVIII, 497, 505, 615, 617.

COELIUS SYMPHOSIUS, year unknown, fourth century. One hundred riddles, VII, 289.

COELIUS SEDULIUS. See SEDULIUS.

COGITOSUS, 591. *Life of Saint Brigid the Virgin*, composed by Cogitosus, LXXII, 776.

COLUMBANUS (Saint), Irish abbot and confessor, 615. 1. Rule for cenobites. 2. Book *On Establishing the Measure of Penances*. 3. Various instructions, commonly called seventeen sermons: on the one and triune God; the mortification of vices; pursuing contempt for the world; labor in the present life; the present life . . . on the Last Judgment; love of God and neighbor; zeal in serving God; etc. 4. [Col. 0571] Six letters to various persons: to Saint Pope Gregory; to the Fathers of a certain Gallican synod concerning the Easter controversy; to Boniface IV; etc. 5. Poems: letter to Hunaldus; single-line maxims; letter to Fedolius; against women; on the vanity and misery of mortal life, LXXX, 202, 210 ff. 6. Document concerning the monastery of Bobbio, LXXX, 322.

COLUMBANUS, Abbot of Saint-Trond, 850. Elegiac poem on the death of King Charlemagne, CVI, 1258.

COMMODIANUS OF GAZA, African, year unknown, fourth century. *Instructions against the gods of the Gentiles for Christian discipline: by the initial letters of the verses*, V, 202 ff.

CONAN, Count and Duke of Brittany, 1118. Conan’s document concerning the restoration and confirmation of Belle-Île, CLXXII, 1327.

CONON, Cardinal-Bishop of Palestrina, 1124. Nine letters: for the monastery of Saint-Quentin-du-Mont near Péronne; concerning the election of a bishop for the Church of Metz; to Theoger, Bishop-elect of Metz; to the Bishop of Langres; to Frederick, Archbishop of Cologne; to H., Bishop of Nevers, CLXIII, 1432 ff.

CONRAD II, called the Salian, Emperor of Germany, 1024–1039. 1. Constitutions: edict concerning the bondsmen of churches; chapters concerning benefices; edict concerning benefices; etc. 2. Thirty-two diplomas: for the monastery of Corbie; for the monastery of Saint Pontianus at Lucca; for the Church of Paderborn; for the New Corbie monastery; to the Bishop of Cremona; for the monastery of Saint Peter at Pavia; for the Church of Bremen; for the Church of Hamburg; etc., CLI, 1040 ff.

CONRAD, Abbot of Paderborn, 1155. Letter to Wibald, Abbot of Stavelot, CLXXXIX, 1439.

CONRAD, monk, 1100. *Life of Blessed Wolphelm, Abbot of Brauweiler near Cologne*, CLIV, 404 ff.

CONRAD III, Emperor of Germany, 1146. Letters: to Pope Eugenius III, CLXXX, 1613, 1616, 1623 ff.; to Wibald, abbot, CLXXXIX, 1132; to the brethren of Stavelot, ibid., 1133. Diplomas, CLXXXIX, 1471, 1485, 1489; CXCVII, 185.

CONRAD, Bishop of Worms, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 173.

CONSTANS, priest, year unknown. Treatise on the passion of Blessed Emmeram, martyr, XCVI, 1368.

CONSTANTIA, 1195. Charter of renunciation made concerning the city of Castellana, CCVI, 1275.

CONSTANTINE I THE GREAT, emperor, 337. 1. Decrees and constitutions. 2. Orations. 3. Thirty-eight letters: to Pope Miltiades; to Caecilianus, Bishop of Carthage; to Chrestus, Bishop of Syracuse; to the Donatist bishops; to Arius; to the Churches; to the Nicomedians; to Helena; to the Antiochenes; to Eusebius; to the Synod of Tyre and the King of Persia; to Athanasius; etc., VIII, 93 ff.; VI, 32.

CONSTANTINE IV, Flavius, emperor, 678. Copy of the letter which Constantine sent to Pope Donus, for the purpose of reconciling the two Churches, namely the Eastern and Western, LXXXVII, 1148. Letter to Pope Leo II, XCVI, 388; to the Roman synod, XCVI, 393.

CONSTANTINE, pope, 715. Two letters to Brithwald, Archbishop of Canterbury, LXXXIX, 336 ff.

CONSTANTINE, antipope, 767. Letter to King Pippin, XCVIII, 233.

CONSTANTINE V, emperor, 775. Sacred imperial decree of the Augusti Constantine and Irene to Blessed Pope Adrian, CXXIX, 200.

CONSTANTINE, Abbot of Saint-Symphorian, 1024. *Life of Adalbero II, Bishop of Metz*, CXXXIX, 1552 ff.

CONSTANTINE THE AFRICAN, monk of Monte Cassino, 1098. Prologue to the book *On Common Topics Necessary for Medical Knowledge*, CL, 1564.

CONSTANTIUS, emperor, 359. Copy of Constantius’s letter to the Italian bishops who had assembled at the Council of Rimini, X, 655. Further letters of the same to Athanasius; to the Alexandrian clergy; to Nestorius; to Eusebius; to the Council of Rimini, XIII, 558 ff.

CONSTANTIUS, Bishop of Albi, 651. Letter of Constantius to Saint Desiderius, LXXXVII, 217, 258.

CORNELIUS (Saint), pope and martyr, 250. Three letters: to Cyprian of Carthage concerning legates sent by Novatian to Carthage, etc.; to Fabius of Antioch concerning Novatian. Other letters attributed to Cornelius, III, 712, 715, 733, 837 ff.

CORONATUS, notary, seventh or eighth century. Sermon on the life of Saint Zeno, Bishop of Verona, XI, 200.

COSMAS JAPYGUS, poet of Matera, 850. Poem in honor of Saints Theopompus and his companions, CXXXIII, 880.

COSMAS, Dean of Prague, 1125. Three books of the *Chronicle of the Bohemians*, from the origin of the Bohemian people to his own time, CLXVI, 9 ff.

[Col. 0572] COTTO (John), around the end of the eleventh century. Treatise on music, CL, 1392.

COXIDA (Elias de), seventh Abbot of the Cistercian monastery of Dunes, 1203. Two sermons: to the rector; on the love of God, CCIX, 992 ff.

CRISCONIUS, African bishop, eighth century, year unknown. *Canonical Abridgment*, or concordance of the canons of the councils listed below and of the Roman bishops: that is, the canons of the Apostles, of Nicaea, Ancyra, Neocaesarea, Gangra, Antioch, Laodicea, Chalcedon, etc.; likewise those of Bishops Siricius, Innocent, Zosimus, Celestine, Leo, and Gelasius, LXXXVIII, 829.

CUMMIANUS (Saint), Irish abbot, 661. 1. Letter to Ségéne, Abbot of Hy, concerning the Easter controversy. 2. Book *On the Measure of Penances*, LXXXVII, 969.

CUTHBERT, disciple of the Venerable Bede, 730. 1. *Life of Bede the Venerable, Priest and Monk of Jarrow*, XC, 36. 2. Letters to Lullus, Bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 828, 838.

CYNEHARDUS, bishop of Winchester, c. 756. Letters to Lullus, bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 831, 837.

CYNEWULF, king of the West Saxons, c. 772. Letter to Lullus, bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 846.

CYPRIAN (St), bishop of Carthage, 258. 1. Approximately seventy letters: to St Cornelius, pope; to Antonianus; to Lucius, pope; to Stephen I, pope; to Jubaianus, on baptizing heretics; to Magnus, on baptizing Novatians; etc., III, 700 ff.; to Donatus; to the presbyters and deacons residing at Rome; to the clergy, on praying to God; to the martyrs and confessors who requested that peace be granted to the lapsed; to the clergy, on the lapsed; to the clergy, on the care of the poor; to the Thibaritans, exhorting them to martyrdom; to Pomponius, on virgins; to Caecilius, on the sacrament of the Lord’s cup; to the clergy and people, on his withdrawal shortly before his passion; etc., IV, 192 ff. 2. Book on the Dress of Virgins. 3. Book on the Lapsed. 4. Book on the Unity of the Church. 5. Book on the Lord’s Prayer. 6. To Demetrianus. 7. On the Vanity of Idols. 8. On Mortality. 9. On Works and Almsgiving. 10. On the Good of Patience. 11. On Zeal and Envy. 12. To Fortunatus, an Exhortation to Martyrdom. 13. To Quirinus: Testimonies against the Jews, three books. 14. Book on Spectacles. 15. Book in Praise of Martyrdom. Doubtful works: Book on Discipline and the Good of Modesty; Book on Gamblers; Computation of Easter, IV, 440 ff.

CYPRIAN of Antioch, date uncertain. Prayer for the martyrs: the prayer which he delivered on the day of his passion, IV, 905.

CYPRIAN, bishop of Toulon, 545. Life of St Caesarius of Arles, LXVIII, 1001, 1253.

CYPRIAN, monk of Monte Cassino, 760. Hymn on St Benedict, LXXXIX, 1051.

CYPRIAN, archpriest of the Church of Córdoba, 928. Eight epigrams, CXXXII, 787; CXXI, 567.

CYRICIUS, bishop of Barcelona, 662. Three letters: to Bishop Tacio; to Hildefonsus, bishop of Toledo, XCVI, 9, 193, 194; LXXX, 729.

CYRIL (St), bishop of Alexandria, 450. 1. Three synodical letters to Nestorius, bishop of the city of Constantinople, XLVIII, 801 ff. 2. St Cyril’s Apology for the Twelve Chapters against the Eastern bishops, ibid., 933. 3. St Cyril’s Apology against Theodoret, or Reply to what Theodoret said against the Anathemas, ibid., 969. 4. Scholastic Notes on the Incarnation of the Only-Begotten, 1005. 5. Fragment of a letter of St Cyril of Alexandria to St Leo concerning Easter, 414, LIV, 598, 607.

CYRIL the Blessed, teacher of the Order of the Holy Spirit of Saxia, c. 1200. On the Rule of the Order of the Holy Spirit of Saxia, addressed to the brethren of that order, CCXVII, 1156.

## D

DADO, bishop of Verdun, 923. Historical fragment on the life of Hatto and Berhard, his predecessors, CXXXII, 778. Letter to Ratbod of Trier on behalf of the priest Adrian, requesting that he may henceforth be permitted to remain and be enrolled in Ratbod’s diocese, CXXIX, 1396.

DAGOBERT I, king of the Franks, 638. Forty ecclesiastical precepts or diplomas: for the Church of St Peter at Trier; for the basilica of Worms; that Bishop Desiderius may assume the bishopric of Cahors; establishing the market of St Denis; concerning the many churches which he built in honour of St Denis; granting the right of asylum to the monastery of St Denis; for the monastery of St Maximinus at Trier; on the foundation of the monastery of Haslach; on the foundation of the church of the Cross of St Audoenus; donations to the monastery of St Denis; fragment of Dagobert’s testament; etc., LXXX, 500 ff.

DAGOBERT II (St), king of the Franks, 675. Four ecclesiastical precepts or diplomas: for the monastery of Weissenburg; on the foundation of the monastery of Horre; [Col. 0573] for the monastery of the church of Strasbourg; for the monasteries of Stavelot and Malmedy, LXXXVII, 1301 ff.

DAGOBERT III, king of the Franks, 712. Four diplomas: for the monastery of Anisole; for the Church of Le Mans and the monasteries subject to that Church, especially for the monastery of Anisole; etc., LXXXVIII, 1111 ff.

DAGULF, abbot of Saint-Denis, 809. Dagulf’s eighteen-line poem, dedicating to Charlemagne his psalter inscribed in golden letters, XCIX, 825.

DAIMBERT, archbishop of Pisa, 1100. Circular letter of Daimbert, Godfrey of Bouillon, and Count Raymond of Saint-Gilles to Pope Paschal concerning victories won by the Christian army in the Holy Land, CLXIII, 448.

DAMASUS (St), pope, 384. 1. Nine letters: to Paulinus, bishop of the city of Antioch, a confession of the Catholic faith; to Acholius and the other bishops of Macedonia; to Jerome; etc. 2. Thirty-seven poems: in praise of David; on Christ; on the name of Jesus; on the surnames of the Saviour; on St Andrew the Apostle; on the Catacombs of the Holy Apostles; on St Stephen, Pope and Martyr; on St Marcellus the Martyr; on Pope St Eusebius; the vow of St Damasus; on St Agnes the Martyr; on St Agatha the Martyr; on his own tomb; etc., XIII, 347 ff.; XXII, 375, 451; LXXIV, 525.

DAMIANI. See PETER.

DAMIAN, bishop of Pavia, 679. Letter to the Emperor Constantine, setting forth the decrees of the ancient Fathers concerning the Catholic faith, LXXX, 1262.

DANIEL, English bishop, 718. Letters: on behalf of a certain devout priest whom he commends to all kings, dukes, bishops, etc.; to Boniface, bishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 687, 703, 707.

DANDINA, William of Grandmont, surnamed of Saint-Savin, 1157. 1. Life of Blessed Hugh of Lacerta, disciple of St Stephen, founder of the Order of Grandmont. 2. Itinerary of the Brothers of Grandmont, or Translation of the relics of the seven holy Virgins, companions of St Ursula, from the diocese of Cologne to the church of Grandmont, CCIV, 1182.

DARMUND, of Noyon, 708. Charter by which he sells estates in the districts of Vermandois and Noyon to the abbot of Saint-Bertin, LXXXVIII, 1251.

DEFENSOR, monk of Lococia, early eighth century. Book of Sparks, or Sentences of the Catholic Fathers, LXXVIII, 596.

DEODUIN, bishop of Liège, 1075. 1. Letters: to King Henry against Bruno and Berengar; to Bishop I., giving thanks for a gift and describing St Remaclus’s triumph over his adversaries. 2. Privilege for the collegiate church of Blessed Mary at Huy; diploma by which he established fifteen canons in the church at Huy or Hoei, CXLVI, 1438 ff.

DERMATIUS, Irishman. Itineraries or exhortations of Dermatius departing for Jerusalem, CLV, 185.

DESIDERIUS (St), bishop of Cahors, 651. 1. Sixteen letters: to Bishop Salustius; to Grimoald, mayor of the palace; to King Sigebert; to King Dagobert; to Bishop Dado; to Bishop Paul; to Sulpicius, bishop of Bourges; to Bishop Caesarius; to Felix, bishop of the city of Narbonne; etc. 2. Fragment of the testament of Desiderius, bishop of Cahors, LXXXVII, 248 ff.

DESIDERIUS, king of the Lombards, 758. Two diplomas: for the monastery of St Michael and St Peter in the city of Brescia; for Theodemar, abbot of the monastery of Monte Cassino, LXXXVII, 1388, 1393.

DEUSDEDIT (St), pope, 617. Letter to Gordian, bishop of Seville: those who receive their own children from the sacred font are to be separated from their wives; and no one is to take his co-mother-in-law (*commater*) as wife, LXXX, 361.

DEUSDEDIT, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church, 109 [incomplete in the source]. 1. Collection of Canons, preface. 2. Fragments on the privileges and authority of the Roman Church and the ecclesiastical order, and against invaders of ecclesiastical property, simoniacs and schismatics, Guibertines and Henricians, CL, 1566 ff.

DEXTER L., of Barcelona, 430. Chronicle of universal history, together with the commentaries of Fr Francisco Bivar, in which the whole ecclesiastical history from Christ’s birth through 430 years is carefully examined, XXXI, 50 ff.

DINOTH, abbot of Bangor, 600. Dinoth’s reply to the monk Augustine, who demanded submission to the Roman Church, LXXX, 21.

DIONYSIUS (St), pope and martyr, 269. One letter, or fragment of Pope Dionysius’s work against the Sabellians, V, 109. Two letters: to Urban, prefect; to Bishop Severus, V, 132, 134.

DIONYSIUS, bishop of Alexandria, 248. Fragment of a letter of Dionysius, bishop of Alexandria, to Pope Stephen, [Col. 0574] III, 1102. Fragments of the first letter of Dionysius to Pope Sixtus, V, 89. Fragments of the second letter of Dionysius to Philemon, presbyter of Sixtus, V, 92. Fragment of the third letter of Dionysius to Dionysius, then presbyter of Xystus and afterwards his successor, V, 93. Fragment of the fourth letter of Dionysius to Pope Sixtus II. Fragments of two letters of Dionysius of Alexandria to Dionysius of Rome, V, 117.

DIONYSIUS (St) the Areopagite, translated, 95. 1. The Celestial Hierarchy, CXXII, 1038. 2. The Ecclesiastical Hierarchy, ibid., 1070. 3. On the Divine Names, ibid., 1214. 4. Letters, ibid., 1178.

DIONYSIUS EXIGUUS, Roman monk, 540. 1. Letter of St Cyril and of the Council of Alexandria against Nestorius, translated into Latin by Dionysius Exiguus. 2. Two letters on the calculation of Easter. 3. Code of the canons of the universal Church. 4. Ancient code of canons of the Roman Church. 5. Collection of decrees of the Roman pontiffs. 6. Book on the creation of man, a supplement to Basil the Great’s *Hexaemeron*, translated by Dionysius Exiguus. 7. Translation, with preface, of the letter of St Proclus of Constantinople to the Armenians. 8. History of the discovery of the head of St John the Baptist, translated into Latin by Dionysius. 9. Paschal cycle, preceded by his own historical account, LXVII, 9 ff. 10. Life of St Pachomius, abbot of Tabennesis, translated by Dionysius Exiguus, LXXIII, 228.

DIOSCORUS, deacon, c. 520. Three letters to Pope Hormisdas, reporting what had taken place at Thessalonica and Constantinople, etc., LXIII, 446, 471, 478.

DODANA, or DUODENA, devout woman, 840. Dodana’s book, *Manual*, directed to her son William, CVI, 109.

DODECHINUS, abbot, 1090. Additions to the Chronicle of Marianus Scotus, CXLVIII, 1441.

DOMINIC, patriarch of Grado and Aquileia in Venetian territory, 1050. Letter to Peter, patriarch of Antioch, CXLI, 1456.

DOMNIZO, priest and monk of Canossa, 1130. Life of Countess Matilda, CLXVI, 1340.

DOMNOLUS (St), bishop of Le Mans, 576. Testament of St Domnolus, LXXII, 650.

DONATUS (St), bishop of Besançon, 651. Rule for Virgins, LXXXVII, 268, 274.

DONUS, pope, 678. Epitaph of Pope Honorius attributed to Pope Donus by Papebroch, LXXXVII, 1154.

DOROTHEUS, bishop of Thessalonica, 529. Letter to Pope Hormisdas concerning condemned heretics, refuting the charge brought against himself, LXIII, 371, 499.

DOTO, abbot of St Peter’s, c. 756. Letter to Lullus, bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 837.

DRACONTIUS, poet, 440. 1. Poem on God, three books, 2,244 hexameter verses. 2. Dracontius’s *Satisfaction*, addressed to Gunthar, king of the Vandals, while he was in chains, 316 verses, LX, 596, 680 ff.

DRAUSCIUS, bishop of Soissons, 666. Charter granting privileges to St Mary’s monastery at Soissons, LXXXVIII, 1183.

DREPANIUS FLORUS, Gallic poet, fifth century. 1. Psalms XXII, XXVI, and XXVII written in metre. 2. Hymns of the three holy youths Ananias, Azariah, and Misael; to Michael the Archangel; on the Paschal candle; to Modoin, bishop of Autun and friend; etc., LXI, 1082, 1084.

DROGO, duke of Burgundy and Aquitaine, 691. Charter for the church of St Arnulf, LXXXVIII, 1221.

DROGO, bishop of Beauvais, 1058. Letter to W., his fellow bishop, CXLIII, 864.

DROGO, cardinal-bishop of Ostia, 1137. 1. Sermon on the Lord’s Passion. 2. Book on the creation and redemption of the first man. 3. Short work on the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. 4. Book on the divine offices, or canonical hours, CLXVI, 1514.

DRUTHMARUS CHRISTIANUS, monk of Corbie, 850. 1. Exposition on Matthew the Evangelist. 2. Brief exposition on Luke the Evangelist. 3. Little exposition on John the Evangelist, CVI, 1261 ff.

DUDO, dean of St Quentin of Vermandois, 1029. Three books on the customs and deeds of the first dukes of Normandy, CXLI, 608 ff.

DULCIDIUS, bishop of Salamanca, date uncertain. Chronicle of Albelda, CXXIX, 1124.

DUNGAL THE RECLUSE, monk, 826. 1. Letter to Charlemagne on the double solar eclipse of 810. 2. Book against Claudius of Turin, addressed to the emperors Louis and Lothair. 3. Eighteen poems: on Charlemagne; to a church; to fountains; to a window; to a door; epitaph of Abbot Folrad; epitaph of Abbot Fardulf; other epitaphs, CV, 448.

DUNSTAN (St), archbishop of Canterbury, 988. 1. Letter to Wulfsige, bishop of Sherborne. 2. Regular Concord of the monks and nuns of the English nation, CXXXVII, 408, 473 ff.

DURAND, abbot of Saint-Martin of Troarn, 1088. 1. Book on the Body and Blood of Christ against Berengar and his followers. 2. Poems: epitaph of Ainard, abbot of Dives; epitaph of Countess Mabilia, wife of Roger of Montgomery, CXLIX, 1373 ff.

DURAND, bishop of Clermont, 1095. Letter to Rodulf, archbishop of Tours, CXXIX, 1397. Letter to Anselm of Canterbury, CL, 1488; CLVLI, 1132.

DYNAMIUS, patrician, 601. 1. Two letters. 2. Life of St Marius. 3. Life of St Maximus, LXXX, 24 ff.

## E

EADMER, monk of Canterbury, of the Order of St Benedict, 1121. 1. *History of Recent Events*, seven books, from Dunstan, archbishop of Canterbury, and Edward, king of the English, in 988, to 1121. 2. Book on the Excellence of the Virgin Mary. 3. On the Four Virtues of Blessed Mary and her Sublimity. 4. On the Blessedness of the Heavenly Country. 5. Book on the Similitudes of St Anselm. 6. Life of St Wilfrid, bishop of York. 7. Life of Blessed Bregwine, archbishop of Canterbury. 8. Life of St Oswald, bishop of Worcester and archbishop of York. 9. Life of St Dunstan, archbishop of Canterbury. 10. Life of St Odo, archbishop of Canterbury. 11. Life of St Anselm of Canterbury. 12. Two letters: to the people of Glastonbury, who claimed to possess the body of St Dunstan; to the monks of Worcester, concerning the election of a bishop, CLIX, 346 ff.; CLVIII, 49.

EARDULF, bishop of the Church of Rochester, c. 756. Letter to Lullus, bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 833.

EBALUS, archbishop of Reims, 1032. Charter for the monastery of Mouzon, CXLI, 1112.

EBBO or EBO, bishop of Reims, 850. 1. Ebbo’s Confession. 2. Apology. 3. Short poems: inscription for the church of St Peter; epitaph of Ebbo’s mother, CXVI, 9 ff.

EBERHARD, abbot of Tegernsee, 1027. Eleven letters: to his brother; to Count Udalric; to Duke Henry of Bavaria; to Count Theomo; to Engelbert, bishop of Freising; to King Henry, CXLI, 1308.

EBERHARD, bishop of Bamberg, 1147. Letters to Pope Eugenius III, CLXXX, 1615. To the provosts of Salzburg and Chiemsee concerning the death of Eberhard, archbishop of Salzburg, CXCIII, 495. To Eberhard, archbishop of Salzburg, against Gerhoh concerning the Real Presence, ibid., 500. Against the same Gerhoh concerning the glory and honour of the Son of Man, ibid., 514. To Hildegard, proposing to her a subtle question concerning the three divine persons, CXCVII, 167.

EBERHARD, archbishop of Salzburg, 1159. Letter to Henry on behalf of Pope Alexander, CXCVI, 1569.

EBERHARD, archbishop of Juvavum, 1178. Letter to Hildegard, commending himself to her prayers, CXCVII, 164. Letter to Alexander III, elect of Aquileia, commending himself, CC, 1374. (Perhaps the same person as the preceding.)

EBERWIN, abbot of St Martin’s, Trier, eleventh century. 1. On the abbey of St Martin, from the Life of St Magericus. 2. From the Miracles of St Symeon, CLIV, 1244 ff.

EBRARD, regular canon of the monastery of Watin, 1089. Chronicle of the monastery of Guatin, CXLIX, 1513.

EBROIN, archbishop of Bourges, 810. Letter to Magno, archbishop of Sens, on behalf of the priest Dodobert, requesting that he may remain in Magno’s parish with Hercambald, CXXIX, 1389.

EBROIN, count, 721. Charter for the basilica of St Peter at the place called Rinharim, LXXXVIII, 1277.

EBWALD, king of the East Angles, 733. Letter to Boniface, archbishop of Mainz: he gives thanks for the prayers offered on behalf of his lowliness, LXXXIX, 724.

ECKBERT, abbot of Schönau, 1165. 1. Thirteen sermons against the Cathars: on the heresies against which the dispute is directed; on the growth and manifestation of the Catholic faith; on faith; concerning the first heresy; on marriage; against the second heresy; on eating meat; against the fourth heresy; on infant baptism; on baptism with water; on the souls of the dead; against the eighth heresy; on the Body and Blood of the Lord; etc. 2. Extract on the Manichaeans from St Augustine. 3. Short work in praise of the Cross. 4. Soliloquy, or eighteen meditations. 5. Spur of Love. 6. On St Elisabeth the Virgin, mistress of the Sisters of the Order of St Benedict at Schönau in the diocese of Trier, CXCV, 9 ff.

EDGAR, king of the English, 974. Ecclesiastical laws; three charters: concerning the expulsion of married clerics; for the new monastery at Winchester called Hyde; for the monastery of Malmesbury; concerning the same matters; etc., CXXXVIII, 482 ff.

EDMUND, king of the English, 944. Ecclesiastical laws, CXXXVIII, 479.

[Col. 0576] EDWARD THE ELDER, king of the English, 906. Ecclesiastical laws, CXXXVIII, 459.

EDWARD (St) III, king of the English and confessor, 1041–1066. 1. Ecclesiastical laws drawn from his secular laws. 2. Other laws of King Edward written in the Norman language, CLI, 1190.

EDWARD GRIM, monk, 1164. Life of St Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury and martyr, CXC, 2 ff.

EGBERT (St), archbishop of York, 729. 1. Extracts from the sayings and canons of the Holy Fathers. 2. Penitential of St Egbert, four books. 3. Dialogue on Catholic Instruction. 4. Canons on remedies for sins, LXXXIX, 378.

EGILMAR, bishop of Osnabrück, 891. Complaint to Pope Stephen V, CXXIX, 808.

EGINARD, or EINHARD, abbot of German race and secretary of Charlemagne, 840. 1. Life of the Emperor Charles, XCVII, 28 ff. 2. Annals of Abbot Eginhard, collated with those of Lorsch, from 741 to 829, CIV, 368. 3. Sixty-three letters: to Ansegisus; to Abbot Gozbert; to Otgar, archbishop; to Count Poppo; to Geboin, count of the palace; to Count Hatto; to Lothair, co-ruler of the empire; to the empress; to a friend; etc., ibid., 509. 4. History of the Translation of the Blessed Martyrs of Christ Marcellinus and Peter, ibid., 537. 5. Six charters: for the monastery of Lorsch; description of the places and boundaries of the estate of Michelstadt; to Meginfrid, abbot of the monastery of St Servatius; for the monastery of Blandin; etc., 601 ff.

EGINO, abbot of St Ulrich’s, 1135. Letter, CLXX, 855.

EIGIL (St), abbot of Fulda, 822. Life of St Sturmi, first abbot of Fulda, CV, 421.

EKKEHARD, bishop of Urach, 1100. 1. Chronicle of Würzburg, from Augustus, Roman emperor, to Henry, German emperor, 1057. 2. Universal Chronicle, containing much concerning the origin of the Franks, the Goths, Amazons, Huns, Lombards, deeds of Charlemagne, and origin of the Saxons. 3. *Hierosolymita*, on the oppression, liberation, and restoration of the holy Church of Jerusalem. 4. Letter to Erkembert, CLIV, 433, 460 ff.

ELDEFONSUS, Spanish bishop, 845. Short work on the Eucharistic bread; a revelation made to him in the Holy Spirit in the seventh month, CVI, 881 ff.

ELEUTHERIUS (St), bishop of Tournai, 525. Six sermons: on the Holy Trinity; on the Incarnation of the Lord; for the feast of the Annunciation; prayer of Blessed Eleutherius, at the point of death, to God for the faith and Church of Tournai, LXV, 84.

ELEUTHERIUS, pope, 177. Decrees of Pope Eleutherius, CXXX, 119.

ELEUTHERIUS, bishop of Winchester, 675. Eleven charters, to Aldhelm, bishop of Sherborne, LXXXIX, 309.

ELFREDA, date uncertain. Letter to St Boniface of Mainz, LXXXIX, 803.

ELIAS (of Coxida). See COXIDA.

ELIGIUS (St), bishop of Noyon, 659. 1. Sixteen homilies: on the Nativity of the Lord, concerning the preservation of peace and almsgiving; on the day of the Purification of St Mary, concerning the Gospel and the use of lights; in Lent, on the praises of fasting; on Maundy Thursday, concerning the washing of the apostles’ feet and the reconciliation of penitents; on Maundy Thursday, on not delaying the doing of penance; to public penitents, that they may repent earnestly; on Maundy Thursday to clergy, people, and public penitents; on Maundy Thursday, to the people, on true charity; on Maundy Thursday, on the prodigal son and the penitent; etc. 2. Letter to St Desiderius, bishop of Cahors. 3. Charter for the church which he founded in the district of Solignac, LXXXVII, 473, 593 ff.

ELIPANDUS, bishop of Toledo, 790. Five letters: to Migetius the heretic; to Abbot Fidelis; to Charlemagne; to Albinus; to Felix, recently converted, XCVI, 860.

ELISABETH, queen of Hungary, 1383. Letter to the citizens of Udine, XCIX, 670.

ELLINGER, abbot of Tegernsee, c. 1030. Seven letters: to Fromund, monk of Tegernsee, concerning his excellent disposition toward him and the order of priesthood; to Egilbert, bishop of Freising; etc., CXLI, 1317.

ELPIS, wife of Boethius, 525. Two hymns in honour of the holy apostles Peter and Paul, LXIII, 537.

EMBRICO, bishop of Würzburg, 1135. Sermon at the funeral of St Otto, bishop of Bamberg, CLXXIII, 1361.

EMMA, queen of the English, 1045. Letter to her sons Edward and Alfred, CXLI, 1374, 1398.

EMMO, bishop of Sens, 659. 1. Precept concerning the subjection of the monks of St Columba to their abbot, [Col. 0577] the election of an abbot, and his authority over the monks and the property of the monastery. 2. Charter for the monastery of St Peter at Sens, LXXXVIII, 1168 ff.

ENCHERIADES, date uncertain. Monochord, CLI, 693.

ENGELBERT, prior of the Valley of St Peter, 1181. Two letters concerning St Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, to Pope Alexander III, CC, 1436 ff.

ENGELMODUS, bishop, date uncertain. Verses to Abbot Radbert, CXX, 25.

ENNODIUS, Magnus Felix, bishop of Pavia, 521. 1. Nine books of letters: to Faustus, John, Agapitus, … Apollinaris, Pope Symmachus, Avitus, Boethius, Messala the orator, Arator, etc. 2. Ten miscellaneous short works: Panegyric delivered to King Theodoric; little book against those who dared to write against the synod; Life of Blessed Epiphanius, bishop of Pavia; On the Life of Blessed Antony, monk of Lérins; *Eucharisticum* on his own life; Didactic Exhortation to Ambrose and Beatus; decree issued when all bishops were ordered to have cell-bearers; petition by which Gerontius, the boy of Agapitus, was absolved; blessing of the candle. 3. Twenty-eight speeches: on the feast-day of Laurentius, bishop of Milan; speech sent to Honoratus, bishop of Novara, for the dedication of the basilica of the Apostles, where a temple of idols had stood; etc.; on heretics and the synod … At the dedication of the auditorium when the transfer to the forum took place. Preface when Arator entered the auditorium. Grammatical thanksgiving when Parthenius recited well, … Speech delivered when the son of Eusebius was entrusted for study … Speech given to Arator when he advanced to praise … When Paterius and Severus were entrusted for study; etc. 4. Twenty-one poems: itinerary of the castle of Briançon … epithalamium delivered for Maximus, a man of senatorial rank … itinerary of the Po; to Faustus concerning his poems; to Olybrius concerning his eloquence … evening hymn … hymn on Pentecost … hymn on the Ascension of the Lord … hymn on St Ambrose; hymn on St Mary; hymn on St Martin; hymn on St Dionysius; etc.—Epigrams, CLI; LXIII, 13 ff.

EODEBERT, 704. Charter by which he sells all his property at Rumeliacum to Rigobert, abbot of Saint-Bertin, LXXXVIII, 1248; CXXXVI, 1198.

EPHIBIUS, abbot, 696. Testament of Ephibius concerning gifts bestowed on the Church of Vienne, LXXXVIII, 1234.

EPHRAEM (St), deacon, sixth century. 1. Life of St Abraham the Hermit, LXXIII, 281. 2. Life of St Mary the Harlot, niece of Abraham the Hermit, LXXIII, 631.

EPIPHANIUS, bishop of Salamis in Cyprus, 403. Letter to John, bishop of Jerusalem. He excuses himself for having ordained Paulinianus priest without consulting John, and then warns him to refrain from the errors of Origen, XXII, 517.

EPIPHANIUS, bishop of Constantinople, sixth century. Four letters to Pope Hormisdas: concerning his election; the Catholic faith which he professes together with the Roman Church; the emperor and his marriage; showing eagerness for the union of the Churches; stating that he had sent to the emperor prayers offered by the Easterners; etc., LXIII, 494, 497, 506, 523.

ERACLIUS, bishop of Liège, 971. 1. Letter to Bishop Ratherius. 2. Account of a miracle of St Martin. In his own hand he describes his miraculous healing, as also a second vision, CXXXV, 945.

ERACLIUS, bishop of the Church of Bigorre, 1064. Donation to the monastery of Cluny, CLIX, 958.

ERCHAMBERT, bishop of Freising, 853. 1. Letter to his people concerning the body of St Bartholomew the Apostle, reportedly brought into Bavaria. 2. Fragment from the Brief History of the Kings of the Franks and Mayors of the Palace, CXVI, 32.

ERCHEMBERT, monk of Monte Cassino, 890. History of the Lombards, CXXIX, 745.

ERINGIUS, king of the Spanish Goths, 719. Eringius’s address to the Council of Toledo, CXXX, 549, 563.

ERKEMBALD, bishop of Strasbourg, 991. 1. Erkembald’s Sigh, or soliloquy and prayer to God which he used whenever he heard singing in churches. 2. Short poems: epigram, tetrastich. 3. Municipal laws given by Erkembald to the city of Strasbourg, CXXXVII, 582.

ERMANRIC, monk of Reichenau, 850. Fragments from Ermanric’s book on Grammar addressed to Grimoald, archchaplain, containing much concerning the distinguished men of St Gall, CXVI, 24.

ERMENGAUD, c. 1192. Short work against the Waldensian heretics, who say and believe that this world and all visible things were made not by God but by the devil, CCIV, 1236.

ERMENOARA, nun of Dijon, 715. Charter for the monastery of St Benignus at Dijon, LXXXVIII, 1259.

ERMINETHRUDIS, illustrious matron, 700. Fragment [Col. 0578] of her testament, in which she records very many legacies to churches and persons, LXXXVIII, 1243.

ERMOLDUS NIGELLUS, 826. Elegiac poem on the deeds of Louis the Pious, from 781 to 826, four books, about 2,500 verses, CV, 570.

ERNALD, abbot of Bonneval in the diocese of Chartres, 1156. 1. On the Works of the Six Days. 2. Commentary on Psalm CXXXII. 3. Short book on the gifts of the Holy Spirit. 4. Book on the principal works of Christ up to his ascent to the Father, addressed to Pope Adrian IV, CLXXXIX, 1509. 5. On the Seven Words of the Lord on the Cross. 6. Short book on the praises of Blessed Mary the Virgin. 7. Meditations. 8. On the Life of St Bernard, CLXXXIX, 1514 ff.

ERNISIUS, abbot and R. prior of St Victor’s, Paris, 1164. Letters to Robert of Hereford, CXC, 687; CXCVI, 1225.

ERNULF, bishop of Rochester, 1124. 1. Collections concerning the affairs of the Church of Rochester from the foundation of the see to his own time. 2. Letter on incestuous marriages, CLXIII, 1441.

ERPO, dean of Halberstadt, 1136. Letter to Pope Innocent II concerning the election of Gerard, provost of St John’s, as bishop of Halberstadt, CLXXIX, 666.

ETHELBERT, king of the English, 616. 1. Donations to various churches. 2. Decree that the property of God and of the Church is not to be taken away, LXXX, 342.

ETHELRED, king of the English, 871. Two donations: to Abbot Aldhelm and to the monastery of Maldon, LXXXIX, 311.

ETHELRED II, king of the English, 979–1016. Ecclesiastical laws, CLI, 1165.

ETHELWOLD, bishop of Winchester, 983, CXXXVII, 77.

ETHELVOLF, Irish abbot, date uncertain, eighth century. 1. Canons selected from an ancient collection. 2. Irish canons. 3. Poem on the abbots and devout men of the monastery of St Peter on the island of Lindisfarne, about 800 verses, XCVI, 1280 ff.

EUCHERIUS (St), bishop of Lyons, 449. 1. Letter or short book in praise of the desert, to Hilary, priest of Lérins. 2. Exhortatory letter to his kinsman Valerianus on contempt for the world and secular philosophy. 3. One book of Forms of Spiritual Understanding, to Uranius. 4. Two books of Instructions, to Salonius. 5. Passion of St Maurice and his Companions. 6. Twelve homilies to monks. 7. Exhortation to monks. 8. Two books of Epitomes of Cassian’s Works, to Castor of Apt. 9. Doubtful works: Commentaries on Genesis and the Books of Kings, L, 685.

EUCLID of Megara, 400 BC. Two books of Geometry translated by Boethius, CXIII, 1307.

EUDOXIA LICINIA AUGUSTA, wife of Valentinian III. See LICINIA.

EUGENIUS (St), bishop of Carthage, 485. 1. Profession of faith of the Catholic bishops of Africa. 2. Letter to his fellow citizens on preserving the Catholic faith, LVIII, 768.

EUGENIUS (St), bishop of Toledo, 637. 1. Miscellanies, about 500 verses. 2. Dracontius’s *Hexaemeron*, corrected by St Eugenius at the king’s command, about 700 verses. 3. Four letters: to Braulio; to Eugenius; to Protasius of Tarragona, LXXXVII, 348 ff.

EUGENIUS II, pope, 824–827. 1. Diploma of Pope Eugenius II. 2. Letter to Bernard, archbishop of Vienne. 3. Decrees of Pope Eugenius II, from the Council of Reims, CV, 640. Privileges: for the Church of St Peter at Rouen; for the monastery of Lorsch, CXXIX, 985 ff. Rite of proof by cold water instituted by Pope Eugenius II; collection of imperial decrees, ibid.

EUGENIUS III, pope, 1145. Five hundred and thirty-nine letters and privileges, CLXXX, 1003.

EUGYPPIUS, African abbot, date uncertain. 1. Treasury drawn from the works of St Augustine, 352 chapters. 2. Life of St Severinus, apostle of Noricum, LXII, 1168, 561 ff.

EULOGIUS (St), archbishop of Toledo and martyr, 859. 1. Three books of Memorials of the Saints. 2. Martyrial Document. 3. On the Life and Passion of the Holy Virgins Flora and Mary. 4. Three letters: to Alvarus on the martyrdom of the virgins Flora and Mary; to Baldegothon on the same matter; to Wiliesind, bishop of Pamplona. 5. Apologetic Book of the Martyrs, CXV, 704.

EUMENIUS, schoolmaster of Autun, 310. 1. Panegyric to Constantine Augustus, VIII, 619. 2. Thanksgiving to Constantine Augustus, ibid., 641.

EUPHEMIA, Augusta, 520. Letter to Pope Hormisdas, LXIII, 487.

EUPHRONIUS (St), bishop of Autun, 479. Letter to Bishop Talasius of Angers concerning solemnities, [Col. 0579] bigamous clerics, and those who, being married, are admitted, LVIII, 66.

EUREMARUS, patriarch of Jerusalem, 1115–1117. Letter to Lamberius, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 677.

EUSEBIUS (St), pope, fourth century. Three letters: to all the bishops of Gaul; to the Egyptians; to the bishops of Tuscany and Campania, VII, 1101 ff.

EUSEBIUS PAMPHILUS, bishop of Caesarea, 338. On the Life of the Blessed Emperor Constantine, VIII, 9 ff.

EUSEBIUS, bishop of the Eastern Church, 340. Letter to Pope Julius I, VIII, 977.

EUSEBIUS (St), bishop of Vercelli, 350–384. 1. The Gospel collated with various copies of the Old Latin version. 2. Three letters: to the Emperor Constantius; to the presbyters and people of Italy; to Gregory, bishop of Spain. 3. Confession concerning the Holy Trinity, XII, 9, 947 ff.

EUSEBIUS of Cremona, date uncertain. Life of St Jerome, XXII, 235, 239.

EUSEBIUS, bishop of Milan, 454. Synodical letter to Pope St Leo concerning the Eutychians and his letter to Flavian, which was read and approved in the Synod of Milan, LIV, 945.

EUSTATHIUS, bishop and legate of the Synod of Lampsacus, 366. Letter to Pope Liberius, VIII, 1377.

EUSTATHIUS, 450. Latin paraphrase of St Basil’s *Hexaemeron*, nine books, LIII, 865.

EUSTOCHIUM, consecrated virgin, 430. Letter on the holy places, to Marcella, XXII, 483.

EUSTOCHIUS of Tours, 460. Letter to the bishops established within the Third Province, LIII, 1013.

EUTHERIUS, heretic of Tyana, 430. 1. Fragment from a sermon against Cyril, XLVII, 1085. 2. Letter to Pope Xystus, L, 593.

EUTRANDUS, deacon of Pavia, 640. Chronicle, from 600 to 630, LXXX, 633.

EUTROPIUS (St), abbot and bishop, AD 600. 1. Letter to Pope Peter on the eight vices. 2. Letter to Pope Peter on the strict discipline of monks and the ruin of monasteries, LXXX, 9 ff.

EUTROPIUS, Lombard priest, 900. On the rights and privileges of emperors in the Roman Empire, CXXIX, 961.

EUTYCHES, heretic and abbot of Constantinople, 451. Letter of Eutyches to Pope St Leo, in which he denies that there are two natures in Christ, namely divinity and humanity, LIV, 713.

EUTYCHIANUS (St), pope, 283. 1. Exhortation to presbyters from an ancient Vatican manuscript. 2. Two letters: to John and to all bishops of the province of Baetica, on faith in the Lord’s incarnation; to bishops established throughout Sicily, on clerics. 3. Decrees, V, 156.

EVAGRIUS, monk, 420. 1. Disputation between Theophilus the Christian and Simon the Jew. 2. Sentences: to brothers dwelling in monasteries and hospices; to virgins, XX, 1062.

EVAGRIUS, presbyter of Antioch, 273. Translation of the Life of Blessed Antony the Abbot, by St Athanasius, LXXIII, 125.

EVANTIUS, abbot, early eighth century. Letter against those who judge the blood of animals to be unclean and say that flesh is clean, LXXXVIII, 720.

EVARISTUS, pope, A.D. 110. 1. Decrees concerning the ordination of deacons and lawful marriage, and concerning the faith and the prohibition against injuring or maligning bishops, CXXX, 82. 2. Letter that Christ is the head and bridegroom of the Church, and how priests ought to love their own churches and those churches ought to love them, CXXX, 81.

EVODIUS, bishop of Uppsala, A.D. 428. 1. Book on the Faith, against the Manichaeans, XXII, 1233. 2. Letters to Augustine, concerning the soul separated from the body; reason and God; and the soul of Christ, XXXIII, 693, 701, 702, 708.

EVREMARUS, bishop of Caesarea, A.D. 1129. Privilege, CLV, 1168.

EZELO, monk of Cluny, date unknown. Epitome of the Life of St. Hugh, abbot of Cluny, CLIX, 909.

F

FABIANUS, pope, A.D. 250. Decrees and three letters, CXXX, 151 ff.

FACUNDUS, bishop of Hermiane, A.D. 547. 1. Twelve books in Defence of the Three Chapters of the Council of Chalcedon, addressed to Emperor Justinian. 2. Book against Mocianus the Scholar. 3. Letter on the Catholic Faith in Defence of the Three Chapters, LXVII, 521 ff.

FALCO, archbishop of Lyons, A.D. 1140. Gives the house of Portes to the Carthusian monks, CLIII, 1125.

[Col. 0580] FALCO of Benevento, A.D. 1139. Chronicle, from the year 1103 to the year 1140, CLXXIII, 1149.

FALTONIA PROBA, a most distinguished woman, A.D. 400. Virgilian Centos, as testimony to the Old and New Testaments, about 700 verses, XIX, 801.

FARDULFUS, abbot of Saint-Denis, A.D. 809. Three poems: verses inscribed on the building of St. Denis, and other verses by Fardulfus, XCIX, 824.

FARICIUS, date unknown. Life of St. Aldhelm, bishop of Sherborne, LXXXIX, 64.

FARO (St.), bishop of Meaux, A.D. 670. Two charters: for the monastery of Eboriacum and for the monastery of Rebais, LXXXVII, 1133.

FAROALDUS, duke of Spoleto, eighth century. Letter to Pope John VI, CL, 1306.

FASTIDIOSUS, Arian priest, A.D. 533. Sermon of Fastidiosus the Arian, LXV, 375.

FASTIDIUS, bishop of the Britons, A.D. 430. One book on the Christian Life, L, 380.

FASTREDUS, third abbot of Clairvaux, A.D. 1157. Two letters: to a certain abbot of his order, concerning the observance of regular discipline; to Omnibonus, bishop of Verona, concerning the Council of Toulouse, at which Pope Alexander was recognized, and concerning the assembly at Pavia, CLXXXVIII, 1657; CLXXXII, 764; CC, 1363.

FAUSTINUS, priest, A.D. 368. 1. On the Trinity, addressed to Galla Placidia, or On the Faith against the Arians. 2. The Faith of Faustinus, presented to Emperor Theodosius. 3. Petitionary booklet addressed to the emperors Valentinian, Theodosius, and Arcadius, XIII, 29, 1050.

FAUSTINUS (St.), fifth century. Homily on the Passion of the Lord, LIX, 408.

FAUSTUS, Manichaean, of Milevum in Africa, A.D. 401. Book against the Catholic Faith, XX, 80.

FAUSTUS (St.), bishop of Riez, A.D. 485. 1. Two books on the Grace of God and Free Will. 2. Nineteen letters: Faustus’s profession of faith; to Lucidus, a Predestinarian priest, that he may retract his errors; a letter against the Arians and Macedonians; to Benedictus Paulinus, on faith unto salvation; on repentance; to Felix, pope, and Patricius; to Ruricius, bishop of Limoges, on the divine persons; and on various matters, etc. 3. Eight sermons addressed to monks, LVIII, 776 ff.; LIII, 681.

FELIX (St.), pope and martyr, A.D. 272. Four doubtful letters: to Bishop Paternus, concerning judgments, accusations, and defenses involving the sacred orders; concerning the authority of the judge of the Apostolic See and accused bishops; to Bishop Benignus, concerning those in error about the Son of Man; to Bishop Maximus and the clergy of Alexandria, concerning Christ’s divinity and humanity, V, 145 ff.

FELIX, African confessor, third century. Two letters to Cyprian, IV, 420, 423.

FELIX (St.), Pope II, A.D. 355. Two letters and decrees: to the bishops gathered in the Alexandrian synod, concerning the cases of bishops; to the same and to the remaining priests of the Lord, concerning the patient endurance of persecutions and tribulations, XIII, 10 ff.

FELIX III (St.), pope, A.D. 483. Fifteen letters and decrees: to Acacius of Constantinople, concerning actions taken against the Catholic faith; to Emperor Zeno, on behalf of the Church of Alexandria; to Peter the Fuller, that he may come to his senses; to all bishops, concerning those rebaptized; to the clergy and people of Constantinople, concerning Acacius’s excommunication; to the monks of the city of Constantinople and Bithynia, concerning the same matter; to Flavitas, bishop of Constantinople, concerning the same matter; to Thalasius, archimandrite of Constantinople, that he should not communicate with the Church of Constantinople; etc. Decree of Pope Felix III: in ecclesiastical causes the royal will must be subordinated to priests, LVIII, 890, 977.

FELIX, Pope IV, A.D. 526. Letters and decrees: to Caesarius of Arles, concerning laymen not being promoted to the priesthood before probation; a constitution concerning the Church of Ravenna; to all bishops, concerning the celebration of Mass; to Sabina, concerning her devotion to the Church; etc., LXV, 9 ff.

FELIX, bishop of Messina, A.D. 590. Letter to Pope St. Gregory, concerning degrees of consanguinity, LXXVII, 1320.

FELIX, bishop of Limoges, A.D. 650. Letter to St. Desiderius, bishop of Cahors, LXXXVI, 213, 266.

FELIX, bishop of Lucca, A.D. 685. Diploma for the monastery of St. Frigdianus, LXXXIII, 147.

FELIX, bishop of Toledo, about A.D. 700. Life, or eulogy, of St. Julian, bishop of Toledo, XCVI, 444.

FELIX, bishop of Ravenna, A.D. 717. Prologue to the sermons of St. Peter Chrysologus, LXXXIX, 359.

FELIX, bishop of Urgell, A.D. 790. Felix’s confession of faith, XCVI, 882.

FELIX, priest, A.D. 745. Two charters for the monastery of Saint-Bertin, LXXXVIII, 1304.

[Col. 0581] FERMUS, cleric of Pistoia, eighth century. Donation, LXXXVIII, 1437.

FERNANDUS, king of Spain, A.D. 1172. Two privileges for the Roman Church, CC, 1369.

FERRANDUS FULGENTIUS, deacon of the Church of Carthage, A.D. 547. 1. Seven letters: to Bishop Fulgentius, concerning the salvation of an Ethiopian catechumen; to Anatolius, deacon of the city of Rome, concerning Christ’s two natures; to Eugyppius, priest, concerning the essence of the Trinity and Christ’s two natures; to Severus, scholar of Constantinople, that Christ is one of the holy and indivisible Trinity; to Pelagius and Anatolius, deacons of the city of Rome, against the Acephali; to Count Reginus, on what a religious commander ought to be in military actions, or On the Seven Rules of Innocence. 2. Abridgment of the Canons. 3. Life of St. Fulgentius, bishop of Ruspe, LXVII, 878; LXV, 378, 392; LXXXVIII, 818.

FERREOLUS (St.), bishop of Uzès, about A.D. 558. Rule for monks, LXVI, 960.

FESTUS, S. P., fourth century. Fragment On the Meaning of Words, XCV, 1605.

FIDIS, countess of Narbonne, A.D. 1077. Charter concerning the gift of the church of St. Peter of Sermur, made to Hugh of Cluny and Unaldus, abbot of Moissac, CLIX, 967.

FIRMATUS, canon of St. Leobinus of Chartres, A.D. 1049. Donation, CLV, 322.

FIRMILIANUS, bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, about A.D. 258. Letter to Cyprian against Stephen’s letter concerning the baptism of heretics, III, 1153.

FIRMINUS, bishop of Uzès, A.D. 545. Life of St. Caesarius, bishop of Arles, LXVII, 1001, 1253.

FLAVIANUS, bishop of Constantinople, A.D. 449. Two letters to Pope Leo concerning the heresy of Eutyches, LIV, 723, 743, 749, 1259.

FLODOARDUS, canon of Rheims, A.D. 966. 1. Four books of the History of the Church of Rheims. 2. Annals from the year 919 to the year 966. 3. Metrical works: Three books On the Triumphs of Christ and the Saints in Palestine, about 2,600 verses; Two books On the Triumphs of Christ Accomplished at Antioch, about 2,200 verses; Fourteen books On Christ’s Triumphs in Italy, about 13,600 verses, CXXXV, 24.

FLORENTIUS, master of offices, A.D. 359. Letter to Lucifer, bishop of Cagliari, XII, 935.

FLORENTIUS of Worcester, eleventh century. Chronicle, CXLVII, 796.

FLORIANUS, abbot of a Roman monastery, date unknown. Letter to St. Nicetius, bishop-elect, asking him to pray to God for him through Ennodius of Pavia, Caesarius of Arles, and his own abbot Theodatus, already crowned in heaven, whom he adorns with praises, LXXII, 918.

FLORUS, deacon of Lyons, A.D. 860. 1. Book on the Election of Bishops, compiled from the sayings of the Fathers. 2. Short work on the exposition of the Mass. 3. Short works against Amalarius. 4. Martyrology. 5. Sermon on predestination. 6. Book against John Scotus. 7. Various poems: Lament over the division of the empire after the death of Louis the Pious; to Moduinus, bishop of Autun, concerning the unjust persecution of the Church of Lyons; hymn for the feast of SS. John and Paul; inscription of the booklet offered at the altar of St. Stephen; on the Gospel of Matthew; on the Gospel of John; prayer with a commemoration of the ancient miracles of Christ our God; epigram of the book of homilies for the whole year; etc., about 1,500 verses. 8. Exposition of the Epistles of St. Paul, compiled from the works of St. Augustine, CXIX, 9 ff.

FOLBERTUS, of Thérouanne in Campania, A.D. 811. Donation to the monastery of Sithiu, CXXXVI, 1219.

FOLCARDUS, abbot of Lobbes, A.D. 1107. Letter to Emperor Henry, CLVII, 481.

FOLCARDUS, monk of Saint-Bertin among the Atrebates, about A.D. 1080. 1. Life of St. Bertin, abbot of Saint-Bertin in the Morini country. 2. Life of St. John, archbishop of York. 3. Folcardus’s poem on St. Vigor. 4. Life of St. Audomar, bishop of Thérouanne, CXLVII, 1084.

FOLCUINUS, abbot of Lobbes, A.D. 990. 1. Life of St. Folcuin, bishop of Thérouanne in Gaul. 2. On the Deeds of the Abbots of Lobbes, CXXXVII, 529.

FOLIOT, Gilbert, bishop of London, A.D. 1187. 1. Three hundred and twenty-nine letters: to Henry, bishop of Winchester; to Pope Celestine; to Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury; to Prior B. and the brethren of Malvern; to Jocelin, bishop of Salisbury; to Pope Eugenius III; to Robert, bishop of Lincoln; to Empress Matilda; etc., etc. 2. Exposition of the Song of Songs, CCII, 1145; CXC, 747 ff.

FOLQUINUS, monk of Saint-Bertin, A.D. 975. Cartulary, CXXXVI, 1181.

[Col. 0582] FORMOSUS, pope, A.D. 896. Eight letters and privileges: to the monks of St. Theuderic; to Stylinnus, bishop of Neocaesarea in the province of Euphratesia; to Herimannus, archbishop of Cologne; bull for the Church of Girona; to Adalgarius, archbishop of Hamburg; to Herimannus, archbishop of Cologne; etc., CXXIX, 821.

FORTUNATUS VENANTIUS, bishop of Poitiers, A.D. 700. 1.
