Eleven books of Miscellanies: to Vitalis, bishop of Ravenna; On the Basilica of St. Martin; On the Basilica of St. Vincent beside the Garonne; On the Basilica of Lord Denis; hymn concerning Bishop Leontius; On Prémillac, an estate near Bordeaux, in honor of the holy cross; to the clergy of Paris; on St. Hilary and St. Medard; to Euphronius, bishop of Tours; to Bishop Felix; to Villicus, bishop of Metz; various epitaphs; to the citizens of Tours concerning Gregory, bishop of Tours; on Bishop Gregory’s birthday; on the marriage of King Sigebert and Queen Brunhild; on Queen Theodechild; on Galeswintha; on the garden of Queen Ultrogotha; to Gogo; on Duke Bodegisel; hymns on the Nativity of the Lord; on St. Mary; etc., etc., about 7,200 verses. 2. Four books On the Life of St. Martin, about 2,900 verses. 3. Individual booklets on the devastation of Thuringia, spoken in the person of Radegund. 4. Life of St. Hilary, bishop of Poitiers. 5. Life of St. Germanus, bishop of Paris. 6. Life of St. Albinus, bishop of Angers. 7. Life of St. Paternus, bishop of Avranches. 8. Life of St. Radegund, queen. 9. Life of St. Amantius, bishop of Rodez. 10. Life of St. Remigius, bishop of Rheims. 11. Life of St. Medard, bishop of Noyon and Tournai. 12. Life of St. Marcellus, bishop of Paris. 13. Life of St. Leobinus, bishop of Chartres. 14. Life of St. Mauritius, bishop of Angers. 14. Passion of the Holy Martyrs Denis, Rusticus, and Eleutherius. 16. Fortunatus’s Exposition of the Catholic Faith. 17. Verses unknown to earlier editors: to Radegund and Agnes; epigram concerning Teudichild, LXXXVIII, 64 ff.

FRANCISCUS CARREUS, monk of the abbey of Bec, date unknown. Addition to the Chronicle of Bec, CL, 691.

FRANCISCUS A PUTEO, prior of the Grande Chartreuse, date unknown. Life of St. Bruno, founder of the Carthusians, CLII, 491.

FRANCO, scholar of Liège, A.D. 1005. Specimen from the work On the Squaring of the Circle, CXLIII, 1374.

FRANCO, abbot of Affligem, A.D. 1125. 1. Twelve books On the Grace of God. 2. Letter that a monk who has cast off the habit cannot be saved. 3. By the same author, [a letter] to the nuns and sisters at Bigard, and a consolatory letter to Forest, CLXVI, 716.

FRECULPHUS, bishop of Lisieux, A.D. 850. Two volumes of Chronicles: the first contains history from the beginning of the world to the time of Caesar Octavian and the birth of our Savior Jesus Christ; the second, from that point onward to the kingdoms of the Franks and Lombards, CVI, 917 ff.

FREDEGARIUS, scholar, A.D. 660. 1. Epitomized History of the Franks. 2. Chronicle, from the year 583 to the year 641. 3. Selected fragments from other excerpts of Fredegarius which concern the history of the Franks, LXXI, 573, 609, 697.

FREDEGISUS, abbot of the monastery of St. Martin of Tours, A.D. 834. Letter on nothing and darkness to the great men of the Palace, CV, 751.

FREDERICUS, provost of Val-Dieu near Liège, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 306.

FREDERICUS, count of Toul, A.D. 1142. Ratifies the grant of the right to receive salt at the village, which had been given to the monastery of Tart by Matthew, duke of Lorraine, CLXXXV, 1412.

FRETELLUS, archdeacon, about 1120. Book of the Holy Places of the Land of Jerusalem, CLV, 1038.

FRIDEGODUS, Benedictine monk, about A.D. 963. Metrical Life of St. Wilfrid, bishop of York, about 1,400 verses, CXXXIII, 980.

FRIDERICUS, archbishop of Cologne, A.D. 1131. Six letters and diplomas: to the clergy of Liège; for New Corbie; for the monastery of Grofschaft; to the Milanese; to the Church of Liège; etc., CLXVI, 1348. Diploma concerning the subjection of the monastery of Malmedy and the superiority of Stavelot over it, CLXXXIX, 1457.

FRIDERICUS I, emperor, A.D. 1153. Ten letters: agreement with Pope Eugenius III; he informs Eugenius, as pontiff, concerning his election and coronation, CLXXX, 1636. Frederick’s rescript to the bishops of Germany, CLXXXVIII, 1641. To Pope Adrian, for confirmation of the bishop-elect of Ravenna, ibid., 1642. Charter concerning the monastery of Balma, CLXXXIX, 1070. Letter to Abbot Wibald, promising to avenge the latter’s injuries, ibid., 1409; to the monks of Corbie; to the citizens of Höxter, ibid., 1410. Letter [Col. 0583] to King Henry, CXC, 1058. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 186.

FRIDERICUS II, emperor, A.D. 1212. Three letters to Pope Innocent III: cession of the county of Fondi to Innocent III; promise to Pope Innocent III; promise that the crown of Sicily will be separated from the Empire, CCXVII, 301, 305.

FROLLANDUS, bishop of Senlis, A.D. 1065. Letter to Berengar, CXLIII, 1369.

FROTHARIUS, bishop of Toul, A.D. 844. Twenty-four letters: to Hilduin; to Gerungus, chief doorkeeper of the sacred Palace; to Emperor Louis; to Empress Judith; to Drogo, bishop of Metz; to Einhard; etc., CVI, 864.

FROUMUNDUS, monk of Tegernsee, A.D. 1011. Fourteen letters: to Gozpertus, abbot of Tegernsee; to Ruotker, abbot of Würzburg; to the monk Pabo, concerning clothing with which to defend himself from the cold; to the monk Reginald, whom he urges to persevere in the monastic state; to the same, asking him to send an example of the poet Horace; to the same, requesting that poems of Statius be sent to him; etc., etc. 2. Twenty-seven short poems: on an image of the Crucified One; to Pabo; against those who pressed Froumundus to accept priestly orders; on Gerhard cruelly striking a boy with a stone; on the arrival of Henry, duke of Bavaria; to the same, praying for a fortunate journey and return; on the twelve apostles of the Lord; defense of the school of Würzburg and its master against a certain slanderer; etc., CXLI, 1283 ff.

FROWINUS, abbot of the monastery of Mount of the Angels among the Swiss, after A.D. 1131. 1. Prologue to an explanation of the Lord’s Prayer. 2. Eight books On Free Will, addressed to the monk Adelbert, CLXXIX, 1801.

FRUCTUOSUS (St.), bishop of Braga, A.D. 670. 1. Rule for Monks. 2. Common Monastic Rule. 3. Letter to Braulio, bishop of Saragossa. 4. Poems ascribed to Fructuosus by some persons, LXXXVII, 1088 ff.

FULBERTUS (St.), bishop of Chartres, A.D. 1029. 1. One hundred and five letters: to Archbishop Bonibert; to Abbo; to Einhard; to Bishop Adalbero; to Adeodatus; to Archbishop Leuthericus, his metropolitan; to King Robert and Queen Constance; to Ebalo, archbishop of Rheims; to William, duke of Aquitaine; to Arnulf, archbishop of Tours; to Hildegarius; etc. 2. Treatise on verse 1 of chapter XII of Acts of the Apostles. 3. Treatise against the Jews. 4. Nine sermons to the people: on the Purification of Blessed Mary; on the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary; on God one in Trinity; on the Annunciation of the Lord. 5. Twenty-seven hymns and ecclesiastical poems. 6. Verses on the ounce and its parts, and on the scruple. 7. Proclamation before they say “The peace of the Lord.” 8. Two diplomas: for the monks of Marmoutier at Tours; concerning Jeranivillare, granted by precaria to the knight Gradulf; etc. 9. Life of St. Autbert, bishop of Cambrai, CXLI, 164 ff.

FULCHERIUS, priest of Chartres, A.D. 1127. Three books of the History of Jerusalem, CLV, 825.

FULCHERIUS, procurator of the houses of the Knights Templar, twelfth century. Letter to Louis, king of the Franks, CLV, 1273.

FULCO, count of Anjou, about A.D. 1022. Letter to King Robert, CXLI, 938.

FULCO, count of Anjou, A.D. 1096. Three pious donations: to the Church of St. Maurice of Angers; for the monastery of St. Nicholas, CLV, 480. Other donations, CLXII, 1097.

FULCO III, king of Jerusalem, A.D. 1137. Privileges, CLV, 1123, 1181.

FULCO, archbishop of Rheims, A.D. 900. Two letters: to Stephen V, supreme pontiff; to Emperor Charles the Bald, CXXXI, 12.

FULCO, abbot of Corbie, A.D. 1090. Letter to Pope Alexander II concerning Corbie’s liberty, oppressed by the bishop of Amiens, CL, 1431.

FULCOIUS, subdeacon of the Church of Meaux, A.D. 1098. 1. Letter to Hugh, abbot of Cluny, written in verse. 2. Fragments enumerating the saints of the diocese of Meaux, thirty-six hexameter verses. 3. Epitaph of Otger and Benedict, soldiers who in the time of Charlemagne took the monastic habit in the monastery of St. Faro, CL, 1552.

FULGENTIUS (St.), bishop of Ruspe, A.D. 533. 1. Three books to Monimus: on God’s twofold predestination, one of the good to glory and the other of the evil to punishment; on the offering of sacrifice; on the sending of the Holy Spirit; on St. Paul’s supererogation; on the true exposition of that evangelical saying, “And the Word was with God.” 2. One book against the Arians. 3. Three books to King Thrasamund of the Vandals: on the mystery of Christ the Mediator, who retains two natures in one person; on the immensity of the divinity of the Son of God; on the [Col. 0584] sacrament of the Lord’s Passion. 4. Thirteen letters: concerning the marital duty and the vow of continence made by spouses; to the widow Galla, on consolation after her husband’s death and the condition of widows; to Proba, on virginity and humility; to Proba, on prayer to God and compunction of heart; to Abbot Eugyppius, on charity; to Senator Theodore, on conversion from the world; to Venancia, on right repentance and future recompense; to Donatus, on the orthodox faith and the various errors of heretics; to Ferrandus, concerning the salvation of a dying Ethiopian; etc. 5. One book On the Trinity, addressed to Felix the notary. 6. One book against the Sermon of Fastidiosus the Arian, addressed to Victor. 7. Two books On the Forgiveness of Sins, addressed to Euthymius. 8. One book On the Incarnation of the Son of God and the Creator of Lowly Animals, addressed to Scarilus. 9. On the Truth of Predestination and the Grace of God, addressed to John and Venerius. 10. One book On the Faith, or On the Rule of True Faith, addressed to Peter. 11. One book For the Catholic Faith, against Pinta, an Arian bishop. 12. Ten sermons: on the Lord’s dispensations; on Christ’s twofold Nativity; on St. Stephen the protomartyr; on the Epiphany; on love of God and neighbor; on St. Cyprian the martyr; on the thief crucified with Christ; on the holy day of Pentecost; etc. 13. Thirty-nine fragments against Fabianus. 14. Two sermons hitherto unpublished: on the Circumcision of the Lord; on the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary, LXV, 104 ff.

FULGENTIUS, abbot of Affligem, A.D. 1125. Letter to the monk Franco, CLXVI, 717.

G

GAIDOALDUS, physician, eighth century. Donation for the monastery of St. Bartholomew at Pistoia, LXXXVII, 1432.

GALBERTUS of Bruges, A.D. 1127. On the Life and Martyrdom of Blessed Charles the Good, count of Flanders. A second Life, by Galbertus the notary, CLXVI, 873, 944.

GALERIUS M., Roman emperor, A.D. 311. Edict of Galerius, VII, 249.

GALLUS (St.), abbot and confessor, A.D. 646. Sermon delivered at Constance, on God’s benefits from creation to the incarnation of the Son of God, LXXXVII, 13.

GALLUS (St.), bishop of Clermont, A.D. 650. Letter to St. Desiderius of Cahors, LXXXVII, 212, 265.

GALO, bishop of Paris, A.D. 1125. 1. Letter to Lambert, bishop of Arras. 2. Diploma by which, after expelling the nuns, he grants the church of St. Eligius to the monks of Fosses, CLXII, 725.

GALTERIUS, surnamed Saveyr, bishop of Meaux, A.D. 1082. Letter to Bartholomew, archbishop of Tours, concerning the cell of Creden, adjudged to the monks of Vendôme at the Roman council under Pope Nicholas, CXLVII, 1212.

GALTERIUS, date unknown. Life of St. Anastasius, monk and hermit, CXLIX, 424.

GALTERIUS, Frankish chancellor, A.D. 1100. The Wars of Antioch, CLV, 993.

GALTERIUS, lord of Caesarea, about A.D. 1140. Privilege concerning the gift and grant of the hamlet of Fraisse, CLV, 1169.

GALTERUS, bishop of Langres, A.D. 1179. Three testimonies, CLXXXV, 1436.

GALTERUS of Lille, bishop of Maguelonne, A.D. 1110. 1. Letter to Robert, provost of Lille, concerning the Flowers of the Psalms collected by Liethert. 2. Diploma for the monastery of Gellone, CLVII, 714.

GAMMO, illustrious man, A.D. 697. Charter for the monastery of Limoges founded by him, LXXXVIII, 1235.

GARCIAS, monk of St. Michael of Cuxa, A.D. 1045. Letter to Oliba, bishop of Ausona, concerning the beginnings of the monastery of Cuxa and the sacred relics preserved there, CXLI, 1441.

GARLANDIA (J. de), A.D. 1040. 1. Work of Synonyms, about 650 hexameter verses. 2. Fragment from the book On Equivocal Terms. 3. Fragment from the book On the Mysteries of the Church. 4. Fragment of a book On Orthography, CL, 1592.

GARNERIUS, abbot, date unknown, eighth century. Embassy to King Aistulf, XCVI, 1369.

GARNERIUS, priest of the Society of Jesus, date unknown. Daily Book, CV, 9 ff.

GARNERIUS, bishop of Langres, A.D. 1198. Forty sermons: in Advent; on the Nativity of the Lord; on the Epiphany of the Lord; on the Purification of Blessed Mary; on Septuagesima Sunday; in Lent; on the Lord’s Supper; on holy Easter Day; on the Ascension of the Lord; on holy Pentecost Day; on the feast of the most holy Trinity; on the Nativity of St. John the Baptist; on the Assumption of Blessed Mary; on the Nativity of Blessed Mary; in the General Chapter; on the feast of All Saints; on the Dedication of a Church; on the Spiritual Ark; etc., CCV, 556.

GARNERIUS of Fontaines, A.D. 1210. Donations, CLXXXV, 1424 ff.

[Col. 0585] GARNERUS, regular canon of St. Victor of Paris, A.D. 1166. *Gregorianum*, sixteen books; that is, allegorical explanations of almost all matters contained in the Bible, drawn from all the writings of Pope St. Gregory, CXCIII, 9 ff.

GASTO of Béarn, A.D. 1212. Profession of Gaston of Béarn, CCXVI, 848.

GAUCHERIUS, monk, twelfth century. Letter to a certain Knight Templar concerning spiritual friendship, CXCVI, 1616.

GAUDENTIUS (St.), bishop of Brescia, A.D. 420. 1. Twenty-one sermons or treatises: seven on readings from Exodus; fourteen on Gospel readings and various chapters. 2. Sapphic pentameter poem in praise of Blessed Philastrius, bishop, XX, 792, 828.

GAUFREDUS of Rancon, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, declaring that the king had entrusted the land of Poitou to him, CLXXXVI, 1384.

GAUFREDUS MALATERRA, Benedictine monk, A.D. 1099. Book on the acquisition of the kingdom of Sicily, Calabria, Apulia, and the island of Sicily by the glorious prince Robert Guiscard and his brothers who came from Normandy, CXLIX, 1088.

GAUFREDUS, duke of the Normans and count of Anjou, A.D. 1150. Three letters to Suger: concerning a meeting to be held with him at Beaugency; that he is well and ready to serve the king; giving thanks because Suger is working for the restoration of peace between the king and himself, CLXXXVI, 1351, 1364, 1427.

GAUFREDUS, archbishop of Bordeaux, about A.D. 1148. Five letters to Suger: asks that nothing be changed in the territory of Bordeaux until he learns the condition of the territory; reports the condition of his territory and the king’s invasion of it through the viscount of Gavaret; asks what he wishes done concerning the then-vacant provostship of the city of Bordeaux; that he cannot attend the council at Chartres, CLXXXVI, 1359, 1369, 1392, 1412, 1421.

GAUFRIDUS, bishop of Chartres, about A.D. 1142. Three letters to Stephen, bishop of Paris: informs him that he chooses St. Bernard of Clairvaux as arbiter of his case; excuses himself for being unable to attend the meeting; etc., CLXXIII, 1412 ff. Letter to Suger, complaining of the provost of Hienville, who had risen against him, CLXXXVI, 1399.

GAUFRIDUS, knight, brother of St. Hugh of Cluny, A.D. 1180. Charter concerning Martigniacum in the district of Autun, CLIV, 969.

GAUFRIDUS, bishop of Châlons, A.D. 1142. Seven letters and diplomas: to Peter the Venerable, abbot of Cluny; to Stephen, bishop of Paris; charter of the foundation of an abbey monastery in Argonne; confirmation of the principal donations made to the monastery of Trois-Fontaines; privilege for the monastery of St. Peter; foundation of his anniversary observance in the church of St. Martin-des-Champs, Paris; foundation in the abbey of Montier-en-Der, CLXXIII, 1393 ff.

GAUFRIDUS GROSSUS, monk of Tiron, A.D. 1137. Life of Blessed Bernard, founder of the congregation of Tiron in Gaul, CLXXII, 1362.

GAUFRIDUS, abbot of Clairvaux, A.D. 1166. 1. Declamations on Simon’s dialogue with Jesus, collected from the sermons of St. Bernard and addressed to Henry, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, CLXXXIV, 436. 2. Life of St. Bernard of Clairvaux, CLXXXV, 321, 395, 523. 3. Sermon on the anniversary of St. Bernard’s death, CXXXV, 573.

GAUFRIDUS, mayor of the community of St. Riquier, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1363.

GAUFRIDUS, subprior of the regular canons at St. Barbara in Neustria, about the end of the twelfth century. Forty-three letters: to John, abbot of Baugé, concerning the pastoral burden imposed upon him; to the monks of Baugé; to Abbot John, concerning the vigorous cutting away of vices in the monastery and on various matters; to his friend Peter, concerning continual reading of Holy Scripture; to W., former prior of St. Stephen of Caen, concerning contemplation; to a young hermit, giving him salutary counsels; to Hugh, prior of St. Martin of Laigle, concerning preparation for the feast of the Lord’s Resurrection; to R., priest, concerning the significance in the Mass of the priest’s standing at the right, and concerning certain other rites; etc., CCV, 828 ff.

GAUNILO, monk of Marmoutier, A.D. 1109. Book on Behalf of the Fool against St. Anselm’s argument in the *Proslogion*, CLVIII, 241.

GAUSLINUS, archbishop of the Church of Bourges, A.D. 1027. 1. Two letters of Gauslinus: to King Robert, concerning the causes of a rain of blood; to Oliba, bishop of Ausona, concerning the death of Bernard, count of Besalú, Oliba’s brother. 2. Sermon on St. Martial, CXLI, 765 ff.

GAUSSELMUS, abbot of St. Victor of Marseille, A.D. 1130. Letter to A., prior of St. Victor of Marseille: he rebukes the brethren of Marseille because they exhumed a dead man, and complains that they do not show him the reverence due to him, [Col. 0586] CLXVI, 1335.

GAUTERIUS, bishop of Autun, A.D. 1191. Testimony, CLXXXV, 1472.

GEBHARDUS (St.), archbishop of Salzburg, A.D. 1085. Letter to Hermann, bishop of Metz, on behalf of Pope Gregory VII against the schismatics of that time, CXLVIII, 848.

GEBUINUS, archbishop of Lyons, A.D. 1082. Letter to Rodulphus of Tours, that provision be made for the election of the abbot of the monastery of Savigny, CXLVII, 1209.

GELASIUS I (St.), pope, A.D. 492. 1. Fifteen letters and decrees: to Euphemius, that he anathematize Acacius; to Laurentius, bishop of Lignido, concerning the formula of faith which all bishops are bound to profess; to the bishops of Dardania, informing them that he has been elected pope and exhorting them not to communicate with the Eutychians; to Faustus, master carrying out the office of legate at Constantinople, concerning Acacius’s just condemnation by the Apostolic See; to Honorius, bishop of Dalmatia, concerning the Pelagian heresy; to all bishops throughout Picenum, concerning the same Pelagian heresy, of which he refutes three principal heads; to Emperor Anastasius, concerning restoring peace to the Churches; to the bishops of Lucania, setting forth certain ecclesiastical regulations; to Oeonius, bishop of Arles, concerning the origins of his episcopate; etc., LIX, 9 ff. 2. Canons ascribed to Gelasius, LIX, 142. 3. The Gelasian Sacramentary, or Book of the Sacraments of the Roman Church, LXXIV, 1049.

GELASIUS II, pope, A.D. 1119. Twenty-eight letters and privileges: to A., prior of the church of St. Frigdianus at Lucca and his brethren; to the Roman clergy and people, concerning the intruded antipope; to Jordan, archbishop of Milan, concerning the restoration of Landulf; to the Gauls, concerning Maurice the antipope; to Bernard, bishop of Toledo, concerning Maurice’s intrusion into the see; to Pontius, abbot of Cluny, on behalf of the monastery of Cluny; to Gualterus, archbishop of Ravenna; to the canons of Lucca, whose customs he approves and renews. Bull listing the possessions at Nobiliacum; to the army of Christians besieging the city of Saragossa. Privilege for the monastery of St. Andrew of Avignon; etc., CLXIII, 473 ff.

GEMMULUS, deacon of the Apostolic See, A.D. 744. Two letters to St. Boniface, archbishop of Mainz: sends him gifts and requests his prayers, LXXXIX, 753, 754.

GENNADIUS, priest of Marseille, A.D. 492. 1. Book on Ecclesiastical Doctrines. 2. Book on Ecclesiastical Writers, LVIII, 980 ff.

GERALDUS (St.), first abbot and founder of La Sauve-Majeure, A.D. 1080. 1. Life of St. Adalard, abbot of Corbie. 2. Miracles of St. Adalard. 3. Charter concerning prayers to be offered for the brethren of his congregation and others allied with him, CXLVII, 1004, 1045, 1064, 1078.

GERALDUS, bishop of Ostia, A.D. 1073. Notice concerning the monastery of Mont-Saint-Michel, CLIX, 963.

GERALDUS of Terrazzo, abbot of Solignac, A.D. 1149. Letter to Wibald, abbot of Stavelot, CL, 1267.

GERALDUS, bishop of Cahors, about A.D. 1200. Letter to Emperor Frederick, asking the emperor to order his release from prison, where soldiers were holding him, CCV, 923.

GERARDUS, priest, A.D. 973. Life of St. Ulrich, bishop of Augsburg, CXXXV, 1001.

GERARDUS, dean of St. Medard at Soissons, tenth century. Prologue to the Life of St. Romanus, CXXXVIII, 171.

GERARDUS I, bishop of Cambrai, A.D. 1051. 1. Acts of the Synod of Arras against the Manichaeans; Gerard’s letter. 2. Six letters: to the archdeacons of Liège, concerning conduct toward excommunicated persons; to Adalbero, elected to the see of Laon; to Ebalo, archbishop of Rheims, concerning Adalbero’s election; to Leduinus, abbot of St. Vedast, concerning the fire in the cathedral church of Arras; etc., CXLII, 1268 ff.

GERARDUS II, bishop of Cambrai, A.D. 1092. Charter concerning the foundation of Anchin, CL, 1380.

GERARDUS, abbot of Clairvaux, A.D. 1161. On the Life of St. Bernard, CLXXXV, 385, 390.

GERARDUS, priest, A.D. 1134. *Historia Compostellana*, three books, CLXX, 876.

GERARDUS, bishop of Angoulême, A.D. 1136. 1. The Council of Laon concerning the state of the Church, convened by Gerard in A.D. 1109. 2. Fifteen letters and diplomas concerning the case of Belle-Île. 3. Charter by which he settles the controversy concerning the place called Amanzenas between Bernard, viscount of Comborn, and the abbot of Uzerche, CLXXII, 1312.

GERARDUS ITHERII, seventh prior of Grandmont, [Col. 0587] about A.D. 1188. Life of St. Stephen of Muret, CCIV, 1180.

GERBERTUS. See SYLVESTER II, pope.

GERHOH (Venerable), provost of Reichersberg, 1169.—1. Fourteen letters: to Master A., to whom he sends and commends his work against the errors of the Greeks; to Henry, Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, to whom he offers and commends his exposition of Psalm 64; to Otto, bishop of Freising, concerning his exposition of the Psalms; … to Adam, abbot of Ebrach, against the errors of Folmar, provost of Triefenstein; to the abbot of Windberg, concerning the disputed opinion on Christ’s glory and honour; to Pope Alexander III, to whom he dedicates his exposition of Psalm 131, denounces Peter Lombard, and commends the reform of the Church; etc. CXCIII, 489. 2. Commentary on the Psalms, CXCIII, 462 ff. 3. Exposition of the Canticle of Isaiah, CXCIV, 998. 4. Exposition of the Canticle of Hezekiah, ibid., 1001. 5. Exposition of the Canticle of Hannah, ibid., 1009. 6. Exposition of the First Canticle of Moses, 1017. 7. Exposition of the Canticle of Habakkuk, 1027. 8. Exposition of the Second Canticle of Moses, 1045. 9. Letter to Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, concerning the Son of Man, 1065. 10. Exposition of Psalm 64, or Book on the Corrupted State of the Church, 1074. 11. Little work on the glory and honour of the Son of Man, ibid. 12. Book against Two Heresies, 1162. 13. Book on the Building of God, or on the Study and Care of Ecclesiastical Discipline, 1188. 14. Treatise against Simoniacs, 1335. 15. Book of Letters, or Dialogue addressed to Pope Innocent II, concerning secular and regular clergy, 1376. 16. Lives of the Blessed Berengar and Wirnto, abbots of Formbach, of the Order of St Benedict, 1425. 17. Compendium on the State of the Church under Emperors Henry IV and V, Pope Gregory VII, and certain subsequent pontiffs, 1444. 18. Preface to the Book on the Investigation of Antichrist, 1480, CXCIII, CXCIV.

GERMANUS (St), bishop of Paris, 576. 1. Letter to Queen Brunhild concerning the war of Sigebert with his brother. 2. Charter of the Parisian basilica of Holy Cross and St Vincent. 3. Brief exposition of the ancient Gallican liturgy, arranged in two letters, LXXII, 77 ff.

GERMANUS, bishop and papal legate, 519. Four letters to Pope Hormisdas: concerning Acacius and the other followers; what had been done at Thessalonica by Dorotheus against Bishop John; that Dorotheus had been taken to Heraclea, and that the emperor had not allowed him to be led to Rome; and concerning the Eastern Church’s agreement with the Roman Church on the day of Easter, LXIII, 445, 468, 473, 481.

GERMINIUS, Semi-Arian bishop, 366. Three letters against the Arians, X, 717, 719; XIII, 573.

GERVASIUS, archbishop of Reims, 1067. 1. Letters to Popes Nicholas II and Alexander II. 2. Documents of Gervasius: charter of the establishment or restoration of twelve canons in the church of Saints Timothy and Apollinaris; for the foundation of the abbey of St Denis at Reims, CXLIII, 1400.

GERWIN, bishop of Amiens, 1119. Two letters to Lambert, bishop of Arras: concerning a certain shrine for depositing the relics of Blessed Fuscian; and concerning certain clerics to be ordained, CLXII, 647, 658.

GEZO, abbot of Tortona, 984. Book on the Body and Blood of Christ, CXXXVII, 370.

GIBERT, master of the hospital, 1100. Two letters to Louis VII, king of France, concerning the hospital for the poor at Jerusalem, CLV, 1264, 1270.

GILBERT, bishop of Lune in Ireland, 1110. 1. On ecclesiastical usage, or canonical custom, in learning the hours and performing the office of the whole ecclesiastical order, addressed to the bishops of Ireland. 2. Book on the State of the Church. 3. Letter to St Anselm, archbishop of Canterbury, CLIX, 996.

GILBERT OF HOILAND, Cistercian abbot, 1153. 1. Forty-eight sermons on the Song of Solomon, from the point at which St Bernard, overtaken by death, had stopped. 2. Seven ascetic treatises: on the contemplation of heavenly things; on seeking Christ; on the contemplation of wayfarers and of the blessed; on how unlike are the joys of the way and of the homeland; on conversation and meditation concerning divine things; on the mysteries of human redemption; etc. 3. Sermon on the seed of God’s Word. 4. Four letters: to Brother Richard, whom he commends; to Adam, whom he urges toward the religious state; etc., CLXXXIV, 12 ff.

GILBERT FOLIOT. See FOLIOT.

GILDAS THE WISE, 556. Lamentable Book on the Ruin of Britain, LXIX, 330.

GILDUIN, abbot of St Victor at Paris, 1155. Letter to the bishop of Beauvais, commending a priest to him; another letter concerning the church of St Peter of Mont-Lhery, CXCVI, 1380.

GILLEBERT, monk of Elnone, 1090. History [Col. 0588] of the miracles of St Amand while his body was being carried through France, CL, 1434.

GILO OF PARIS, bishop of Tusculum, 1142. 1. Letter on the life of Blessed Hugh, abbot of Cluny. 2. Abridgment of the Life of St Hugh of Cluny. 3. History of the journey to Jerusalem. 4. A most vehement disputation against the patriarch of Antioch, because he refuses to concede primacy to the Roman pope, scorns the pope’s letters, subjects papal legates to disgrace, etc., CLXXIII, 1385; CLIX, 909; CLV, 941.

GIRARD, associate of Didacus, bishop of Compostela in Spain, twelfth century. From the history of the church of St James of Compostela, CLI, 267.

GIRARD PUCELLE, twelfth century. Oath of Master Girard and others returning from schism, CXC, 392.

GIRARD OF LE PUY-BRUNEL, 1117. Gift of Long Meadow, CLXII, 1110.

GIRARD OF PÉRONNE, monk, 1180. Letter to one of his men, concerning ingratitude, CXCVI, 1608.

GIRARD OF AVANTAN, abbot of Preuilly, 1213. On the kinship between Erard and Philippa, daughter of Count Henry, CCXVI, 981.

GISLEBERT CRISPIN, abbot of Westminster, 1117. 1. Disputation of a Jew with a Christian concerning the Christian faith, CLIX, 1006. 2. Life of St Herluin, founder of the monastery of Bec, CL, 697.

GISLEBERT, archbishop of Tours, about 1120. Letter to Count Conan, CLXXII, 1325.

GISLEBERT PORRETANUS, bishop of Poitiers, 1154. 1. Letter to Matthew, abbot of St Florent at Saumur, concerning how a priest who offers sacrifice with bread alone and without wine should be punished, and concerning certain other questions. 2. Commentaries on Boethius. 3. Book on the Six Principles, CLXXXVIII, 1248 ff.

GISULF, king of the Lombards, 768. Donation for the monastery of Monte Cassino, LXXXVII, 1392.

GLABER. See RODULPHUS.

GLYCERIUS, emperor, fifth century. Edict against simoniacal ordinations, LXXII, 1112; LVI, 896.

GODEFRED, monk of Stavelot, 1080. Triumph of St Remaclus of the monastery of Malmedy, CXLIX, 288.

GODEFRID, duke of Alemannia, 691. Charter for the church of Blessed Arnulf of Metz; fragment of a conveyance made to the monastery of St Gall, LXXXVIII, 1253, 1222.

GODEFRID OF LUCCA, 723. Diploma by which he founds the monastery of St Peter at the place called Castellione, together with Aurinandus, for his sons, LXXXVII, 1368.

GODEFRID OF BOUILLON, duke of Lorraine, first king of Jerusalem, 1100. 1. Four letters: to Bohemond, prince of Antioch, concerning Greek cunning and deceits; to Pope Urban, concerning the siege and capture of Antioch; to all Christ’s faithful, concerning the peace made with the emperor of Constantinople and the victories won over the Turks by the Christian army; to Pope Paschal, concerning those same victories. 2. Address to Christian soldiers, urging them, mindful of their former valour, to persist in the siege of Antioch. 3. Three documents: for the cell of Sathanac; for the small monastery or priory of St Peter in the town of Bouillon; for the church of St Dagobert situated at Sathanac, a town of Lorraine, CLV, 369, 390 ff.

GODEFRID (St), bishop of Amiens, 1115. 1. Seven letters and documents. Diploma for the monastery of Lihons. Grant of the priory of Saints Vitus and Modestus of Ligniac, on the river Canche, in the territory of Arras. Foundation of St Fuscian of the Wood, addressed to Baldwin, bishop of Noyon. Diploma for the church of Crespy. Diploma for Marmoutier. Diploma for the church of Compiègne. 2. Original clauses of the charter of the commune of Amiens, CLXII, 732.

GODEFRID, Venerable abbot of Admont, 1142. 1. Fifty-eight Sunday homilies. 2. Ninety-two summer Sunday homilies. 3. Eighty-five homilies for the feasts of the entire year. 4. Sixteen homilies on various passages of Scripture. 5. Little work on the blessings of the patriarch Jacob at Genesis chapter 49. 6. Book on the ten burdens of Isaiah. 7. Letter to O., formerly his monk, asking him to send books of Josephus and other authors to be copied for him, CLXXIV, 22 ff.

GODEFRID, bishop of Langres, 1158. Confirmation concerning donations made by Warner of Soberne and his brother Bartholomew, CLXXXV, 1409, 1476.

GODEFRID, superior of St Victor at Paris, 1175. Fragments, CXCVI, 1417.

GODEFRID, abbot, author of uncertain date. 1. Life of St Hildegard, abbess, CXCVII, 92. 2. Letter to Hildegard concerning a demoniac woman, 278.

GODEFRID, bishop of Utrecht, 1178. Letter [Col. 0589] to Hildegard, declaring his affection for her, CXCVII, 176.

GODEFRID, priest of Viterbo, 1190. *Pantheon*, or Memory of the Ages, from the origin of the world to the year 1186, CXCVIII, 872 ff.

GODEFRID, monk of Clairvaux, 1256. Account of his visitation at the abbey of Porto, CLXXXV, 1769.

GODEFRID, abbot of St Eucharius, 1208. Letter to Guibert, abbot of Gembloux, promising him, as to one of his own, the prayers of suffrage, CCXI, 1305.

GODEHARD (St), bishop of Hildesheim, 1038. Five letters: to the monks of Niederaltaich, informing them how he was received by those of Tegernsee; to Bishop Theodulus, concerning how he came to the government of Tegernsee monastery; to Azelin, abbot of Lune-lac, that he should present himself as soon as possible before the bishop of Passau; etc., CXLI, 1160, 1229 ff.

GODESCHALC, author of uncertain date. Continuation of the Deeds of the Abbots of Gembloux, CLX, 628.

GODESCHALC, 1039—whether the same as the foregoing I do not know. Five sequences: on the conversion of St Paul the apostle; on Blessed Mary Magdalene; on the beheading of St John the Baptist; on the division of the apostles; on a virgin, CXLI, 1324.

GOFFRID, abbot of Vendôme and cardinal of St Prisca, 1107. 1. One hundred and eighty-four letters, in five books: to Popes Urban II and Paschal II; to legates of the Holy See, concerning the privileges and possessions of his order, which he defends against wicked men; to Ivo, bishop of Chartres, and Goffrid, bishop of Chartres, concerning the same matters; to various bishops—Goffrid, bishop of Angers, Rainald, bishop of Angers, Ulger, bishop of Angers, Hildebert, bishop of Le Mans, Ranulf, bishop of Saintes; to various abbots—Henry, abbot of Saint-Jean-d’Angély, William, abbot of St Florent, Hamelin, abbot of St Albin, Bernard, abbot of St Laumer, etc. 2. Eighteen minor works: treatise on the body and blood of the Lord Jesus Christ; on the ordination of bishops and lay investiture; on simony and lay investiture; on the investiture of ecclesiastical possessions, which is conceded to kings; addressed to Pope Calixtus, on how dispensations ought to be made in the Church; on the Ark of the Covenant; on the Sacraments; on those who cry out disorderly in chapter; God’s invective against the sinner; etc.; on the three things which pastors ought to possess; etc. 3. Eleven sermons: on the Nativity of the Lord, the Resurrection of the Lord, the Ascension of the Lord, the Purification of St Mary, every feast of Blessed Mary Mother of the Lord, etc. 4. Treatise on the ordination of bishops and lay investiture, CLVII, 9 ff.

GOIBERT, 828. Charter concerning the endowment of the basilica of the Lord Saviour at Steneland, CXXXVI, 1272.

GONDEMAR, king of the Goths, 612. Decree concerning the Church of Toledo, LXXX, 181.

GONTER, bishop of Speyer, 1160. Letter to Hildegard, commending himself to her prayers, CXCVII, 171.

GOSBERT, uncertain date. Acrostic poem to William, count of Blois, CXXIX, 1147.

GOSCELIN, monk of Canterbury, 1100. 1. Longer Life of St Augustine, apostle of the English. 2. His shorter Life. History of the translation of St Augustine, bishop and apostle of the English, and of other saints who rested in his monastery at Canterbury. 4. Life of St Swithun, bishop and confessor, at Winchester in England. 5. Life of St Ivo, Persian bishop. 6. Life of St Werburga, virgin and daughter of the king of the Mercians. 7. Life of St Eadgith, or Edith, daughter of Edgar, king of the English, and nun of Winchester, CLV, 9 ff.; LXXX, 44.

GOSCELIN, dean of Beauvais, 1120. Letter to Ralph, archbishop of Reims, concerning the houses of canons not being possessed by secular persons, CLXIII, 1421.

GOSLEN, bishop of Chartres, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, excusing himself that, though summoned by him, he cannot attend the solemnity of St Denis, CLXXXVI, 1399.

GOSLEN, or JOSLEN, bishop of Soissons, 1152. 1. Exposition of the Creed. 2. Exposition of the Lord’s Prayer. 3. Charter for the monastery of La Sauve-Majeure. 4. Two letters to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1475, 1480, 1437, 1438.

GOTHER, dean of Tournai, twelfth century. Letter to Lambert of Arras, CLXII, 697.

GOTTESCHALC, monk of Orbais, 868. 1. Confession of the monk Gotteschalc after his heresy had been condemned. 2. Longer confession. 3. Fragments of the little book on predestination offered by Gotteschalc to Rabanus, archbishop of Mainz, at the assembly held at Mainz in 848. 4. Letter to Ratramnus, written in verse, about 150 lines, CXXI, 345 ff.; CXXV, 618.

GOYLA, donor, 734. Charter by which she confers gifts upon the basilica of St Benignus at Dijon, to be possessed after her own death and that of her husband, LXXXVIII, 1287.

[Col. 0590] GOZECHIN, schoolmaster, about 1059. Letter to Walcher, likewise a schoolmaster and formerly his pupil. After an introductory defence of his withdrawal to Mainz from the teaching chair of Laon, he laments the evils of his age, resulting chiefly from Berengar’s perverse doctrine, CXLIII, 885.

GOZPERT, abbot of Tegernsee, 995. Sixteen letters: to Romuald, abbot of St Emmeram; to Count Arnold, concerning the death of Empress Adelaide; to the same, concerning the boys whom he had hitherto maintained in the monastery for the sake of study; to Count Meginhelm, asking that hounds be sent to him and his brethren; to Gebhard, bishop of Augsburg, whose piety he praises and to whom he promises shortly to come; etc., CXXXIX, 365.

GRADONIC, patriarch of Aquileia, 1029. Gift of a pastoral staff to the chapter of Udine, XCIX, 682.

GRATIAN, monk of St Felix at Bologna, 1151. 1. *Concordance of Discordant Canons*, beginning with the law of divine and human enactment. 2. Second part of the *Decree*, Causes 33. 3. Third part of the *Decree*, on consecration, CLXXXVII, 28, 477, 1704.

GRATIAN, emperor, 377. 1. Constitution against those who rebaptize, addressed to Flavian, vicar of Africa, XI, 1181. 2. Rescript of the Emperor Gratian to Aquilinus, vicar of the city, by which almost all that was requested in the preceding letter is granted, XIII, 583. 3. Letter to Ambrose, inviting him to confirm him in the faith concerning the divinity of the Son and the Holy Spirit, XVI, 875.

GRATIAN, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church and papal notary, twelfth century. Letter to Gaufred Ridel and others, CXC, 985.

GREGORY (St), bishop of Tours, 595. 1. Ten books of the Histories of the Franks. 2. Two books of Miracles. 3. Book on the Glory of the Confessors. 4. Four books on the Miracles of St Martin, bishop. 5. Lives of the Fathers, or Book on the Lives of Certain Saints. 6. Fragments of a commentary on the Psalms. 7. On the Miracles of St Andrew. 8. History of the Seven Sleepers. 9. Book on the Life of St Julian. 10. Life of St Aridius. 11. Antiphon concerning Saints Medard and Gildard, LXXI, 9, 162, 705 ff.

GREGORY (St), Pope I, surnamed the Great, 595. 1. Thirty-five books of *Morals*, or an exposition of the Book of Job. 2. Two books of homilies on the prophet Ezekiel. 3. Two books containing forty homilies on the Gospels. 4. Address to the people concerning mortality. 5. Book of Pastoral Rule. 6. Four books of Dialogues. 7. Letters, fourteen books. 8. Book of Sacraments. 9. Antiphonary. 10. Responsorial. 11. Commentaries on the First Book of Kings. 12. Exposition on the Song of Songs. 13. Exposition of the penitential Psalms. 14. Harmony of certain testimonies of Holy Scripture, LXXV, LXXVI, LXXVII, LXXVIII, LXXIX.

GREGORY II (St), pope, 731. 1. Nineteen letters: to Boniface the priest, granting him authority to proclaim the mystery of faith to unbelieving peoples; to Charles, duke and mayor of the royal household of the Franks, commending Boniface to him; to bishops and others of every rank, clerical as well as lay, concerning Boniface; to the nobles of Thuringia, that they should obey Boniface; to Bishop Boniface, congratulating him on the conversion of the unbelievers; … to Emperor Leo the Isaurian concerning sacred images; etc. 2. Penitential canons. 3. Capitular issued to Bishop Martinian, the priest George, and others sent to Bavaria, LXXXIX, 453, 496 ff.

GREGORY (St) III, pope, 741. 1. Nine letters: to Archbishop Boniface, sending him the archiepiscopal pallium and instructing him how it should be used; to all bishops, priests, and abbots, commending Boniface and asking them to assist him; to the nobles and people of the provinces of Germany, that they should obey Boniface; to the bishops of Bavaria and Alemannia concerning the same; to Charles Martel, mayor of the royal household of Francia, that he should defend the Roman Church against the Lombard kings; etc. 2. Extract concerning various crimes and their remedies, from the sayings of the Fathers and the judgments of the canons, LXXXIX, 558, 576 ff.; XCVIII, 64.

GREGORY IV, pope, 844. Four letters: to Abbot Rabanus; a bull for the monastery of St Justina at Passau; to bishops and other faithful of God throughout Gaul, concerning the dignity and privileges of the monastery of Fleury; to Otgar, archbishop of Mainz, CXXIX, 992. Four other letters of Gregory IV, CVI, 853.

GREGORY V, pope, 999. Twenty-two letters and privileges: to Abbot Winigo; privilege for the church of Cambrai; bull for the monastery of St Martin at Tours; privilege for the church of Ravenna; to Emperor Otto; to Willigis, archbishop of Mainz; to John, archbishop of Ravenna; privilege for the monastery of St Genesius in the diocese of Besançon; letter to Constance, queen of France; etc., CXXXVII, 900 ff.

[Col. 0591] GREGORY VI, pope, 1046. Four letters and privileges: bull for the abbey of Farfa and its abbot Almeric; letter to all Christians; letter to Roland, provost of the church of Florence; bull issued in a Roman council for the monastery of St Quentin of the Mount, CXLII, 573.

GREGORY (St) VII, pope, 1085. 1. Register, eleven books, approximately 330 letters. 2. Eighty letters circulating outside the register. 3. Ten Roman councils, for reforming the state of the Church; against King Henry of Germany; against Berengar; against Guibert, antipope and heresiarch. 4. Commentary on the seven penitential Psalms. 5. Fragment of an exposition on Matthew, CXLVIII, 9, 284 ff.

GREGORY VIII, pope, 1187. Twenty-seven letters and privileges: to the German clergy, whom he exhorts to devote themselves to an expedition for the recovery of Palestine; to all Christ’s faithful concerning the disaster at Jerusalem; for the monastery of Lucelle; for the monastery of La Charité at Foulaines; for the Order of Calatrava, whose possessions he confirms; to Emperor Frederick; etc., CCII, 1535.

GREGORY IX, pope, 1238. Letter on the canonization of St Bruno, CXLII, 34.

GREGORY OF CATINO, monk of Farfa, ninth century. 1. Chronicle compiled from the diplomas of Roman pontiffs, emperors, Lombard kings, dukes, counts, and other public documents, in which the succession of Roman pontiffs, emperors, kings, dukes, etc., appears, as also that of the abbots of the same monastery, etc., CXXVII, 333. 2. Prefaces by Gregory the monk to the Cartulary of Farfa, CL, 1300.

GREGORY, Roman priest, 1119. Collection of canons, CLXIII, 748, 752.

GREGORY, patriarch of Aquileia, 1263. Rights of the archdeaconry of Aquileia, XCIX, 647.

GREGORY, legate of the Holy Roman Church, 1125. Two letters: to Angerannus, bishop of Amiens; to A., abbot of Anchin, CLXVI, 851.

GRIMALD, abbot of St Gall, 872. 1. Book of Sacraments, excerpted from the works of the Holy Fathers. 2. Letter to Reginbert, master of the school of the monastery of St Gall, CXXI, 796.

GRIMOALD, 650. Charter for the monasteries of Stavelot and Malmedy, LXXXVII, 325.

GRIMLAIC, priest, 898. Rule for Solitaries, CIII, 574; CXXIX, 863.

GUAIFER, monk of Monte Cassino, 1084. 1. Six poems: in praise of the Psalter; on the miracle of the man who killed himself; on the conversion of certain Salernitans; hymn concerning St Secundinus; in praise of St Martin, bishop; about 250 verses. 2. Life of St Secundinus, bishop of Troy. 3. Life of St Lucius, pope and martyr, CXLVII, 1282 ff.

GUALBERT (St) JOHN, first founder of the Vallombrosan congregation, 1073. 1. Prayers of St John Gualbert. 2. Letter to the brethren, CXLVI, 668, 970 ff.

GUALFRED, citizen of Pisa, 754. Foundation of the monastery of St Peter at Palatiolo, in the territory of Lucca, LXXXVII, 1384.

GUALTER, prior of St Victor at Paris, 1181. Extracts against the Four Labyrinths of France, CXCIX, 1127.

GUALTER, canon of the church of Thérouanne, 1127. On the life and martyrdom of Blessed Charles the Good, count of Flanders, CLXVI, 874.

GUALTER, archbishop of Ravenna, 1130. Letter to N., archbishop of Naples or Magdeburg, CLXXIX, 38.

GUALTER, provost of Lille, 1119. Letter to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 647.

GUALTER, monk of Cluny, 1141. On the Miracles of the Blessed Virgin Mary, CLXXIII, 1380.

GUALTER OF CHÂTILLON, master at Tournai, 1202. 1. Treatise against the Jews, three books. 2. *Alexandreis*, or the Deeds of Alexander the Great, comprised in ten books, about 550 hexameter verses, CCIX, 420 ff.

GUARIN, abbot of St Victor, 1180. Letter to Alexander III, CC, 1373. Letter to Celestine III, CCVI, 1261. Other letters of Abbot Guarin: to John, cardinal of Naples; to Philip, king of France, that he should put an end to the dissension among the Grandmontines, CXCVI, 1388.

GUARIN, count of Rosnay, 1082. Document concerning the church of St Margaret, given to the monastery of Cluny, CLIX, 970.

GUARIN, bishop of Amiens, 1138. On the grant of two altars in the diocese of Amiens, CLXXXIX, 1065.

GUDIN OF LUXEUIL, uncertain date. Rhythmic lament on the death of Constantius, monk of Luxeuil, CLI, 636.

[Col. 0592] GUERRIC, schoolmaster of Trier, 1054. Letter under the assumed name of Ulric to Pope Nicholas II, concerning clerical continence, CXLIII, 1361.

GUERRIC, abbot of Igny and disciple of St Bernard, 1153. Approximately fifty sermons for the year: on the Advent of the Lord; the Nativity of the Lord; Epiphany; the Purification of Blessed Mary; Lent; the feast of St Benedict; the Annunciation of the Lord; Palm Sunday; the Resurrection of the Lord; etc., down to the feast of Blessed Mary Magdalene, CLXXXV, 9.

GUIBERT, of the Order of Friars Minor, uncertain date. Life of St Eleutherius, bishop of Tournai, LXV, 59.

GUIBERT, Venerable abbot of St Mary at Nogent, 1104. 1. Book on the proper method of delivering a sermon. 2. Ten books of Moral Reflections on Genesis. 3. Tropological interpretations of Hosea, Amos, and Jeremiah. 4. Treatise on the Incarnation against the Jews. 5. Letter concerning the morsel given to Judas and the truth of the Lord’s body. 6. Book in praise of St Mary. 7. Little work on virginity. 8. Dedicatory letter on the pledges of the saints. 9. *The Deeds of God through the Franks*, or *History of Jerusalem*, eight books. 10. On His Own Life, or three books of *Monodies*, CLVI, 9 ff.

GUIBERT, abbot of Gembloux, 1208. 1. Twenty-six letters: to Philip, archbishop of Cologne, concerning the conduct of evil shepherds; to Abbot Hervaeus and the brethren of Marmoutier; to the brethren of Gembloux; to the abbot of St Eucharius; etc. Letters to St Hildegard. 2. On the burning of the monastery of Gembloux, CCXI, 1281, 1288 ff.

GUICHARD, archbishop of Lyons, 1180. Ancient statutes of the Church of Lyons, renewed by Archbishop Guichard, CXCIX, 1092.

GUIDO II, bishop of Le Puy, 996. 1. Statutes promulgated for establishing peace among Christians. 2. Charter written when the abbot was administering the monastery of St Paul of Cormery; he restores what had been taken away from monasteries, CXXXVII, 852.

GUIDO OF AREZZO, abbot of Holy Cross at Fonte Avellana, 1034. 1. Guido’s *Micrologus on the Discipline of the Art of Music*. 2. Verses explaining music. 3. Likewise, other rules of Guido on unfamiliar chant. 4. Guido’s letter to the monk Michael on unfamiliar chant. 5. Corrective treatise on many errors made in Gregorian chant in many places. 6. How music proceeds from arithmetic, CXLI, 376 ff.

GUIDO OF CHÂTILLON, archbishop of Reims, 1053. Five letters and documents, CXLII, 1401.

GUIDO, bishop of Amiens, 1077. 1. Letter to Fulk, abbot of Corbie, that he should attend the synod soon to be held. 2. Charter granted to the abbey of Corbie. 3. Epitaph of Angerannus, abbot of Centula, CXLVI, 1507.

GUIDO, abbot of Farfa, 1090. The Discipline of Farfa and of the monastery of St Paul at Rome, CL, 1191.

GUIDO OF SOBERNON, 1149. Donation, CLXXXV, 1419.

GUIDO, abbot of Chaalis, 1150. Treatise on correcting the chant of the Cistercian Order, CLXXXI, 1720.

GUIDO, abbot of Pontigny, 1150. Letter to Suger, commending to him the cause of the treasurer of Auxerre, CLXXXVI, 1413.

GUIDO, archbishop of Sens, 1187. Letter to Pope Gregory: the bishop of Laon is cleared of the crimes imputed to him, CCII, 1565.

GUIDO, bishop of Chalon, 1265. Testimony, CLXXXV, 1454.

GUIDO OF SAUZ, 1197. Foundation of the collegiate church of Sauz, CLXXXV, 1437.

GUIDO, Cistercian abbot, later archbishop of Reims, 1202. Testimony, CLXXXV, 1413.

GUIGO I, prior general of the Grande Chartreuse, 1137. 1. Six letters: to the brethren of Durbon concerning spurious letters of Blessed Jerome; to Peter the Venerable, abbot of Cluny; to Aimeric, cardinal and chancellor; to Hugh, prior of the Holy Militia; to Pope Innocent II, whom he consoles amid the troubles of schism; etc. 2. Twenty Meditations. 3. Customs. 4. Life of St Hugh, bishop of Grenoble, CLIII, 582 ff.; CLXXIX, 658; CLXXXV, 219.

GUIGO II, prior general of the Carthusians, 1188. 1. *The Ladder of Paradise*, or Treatise on the Manner of Prayer and the Contemplative Life. 2. Book on the Fourfold Exercise of the Cell, CLIII, 785.

GUILENC, bishop of Langres, 1114. Documents concerning the foundation of the abbey of Morimond, CLXXXV, 1441.

WILLIAM, monk of Chalon, 966. On the lightning strike that struck the monastery of St Peter at Chalon, CXXXIV, 1017.

WILLIAM V, duke of Aquitaine, 1030. 1. Six letters [Col. 0593]: to Margrave Maginfred and his wife; to Leo, bishop of Vercelli; to Duke William; to Fulbert, bishop of Chartres; to Abbot Aribert; to Hildegarius. 2. Diploma by which he grants the village of St Macarius to the church of Holy Cross at Bordeaux, CXLI, 832.

WILLIAM (Blessed) I, abbot of St-Germain-des-Prés, 1031. Letters, or charter, to the brethren of the monastery of St-Germain-des-Prés, CXLI, 834.

WILLIAM (St), abbot of St Benignus at Dijon, 1031. Two letters to Pope John XIX. Letter to Odilo, abbot of Cluny, concerning the death of William, count of Burgundy; the death of Richard, count of the Normans; and matters especially concerning the monastery of Vézelay. Privilege for the monastery of Fruttuaria, CXLI, 836 ff.

WILLIAM OF APULIA, before 1099. Historical poem on the deeds of the Normans in Sicily, Apulia, and Calabria, down to the death of Duke Robert Guiscard, addressed to Roger the son; about 2,800 hexameter verses, CXLIX, 1020.

WILLIAM, abbot of St Arnulf at Metz, 1090. 1. Seven letters: to Pope Gregory VII, congratulating him on his election; to Manasses, archbishop of Reims, resigning to him the leadership of the monastery of Saint-Remi; … to a certain monk, whom he exhorts to seek the one God; etc. 2. Prayer to be said in commemoration of St Augustine before the consecration of the Mass, CL, 872.

WILLIAM, archbishop of Rouen, 1117. Letter to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 650, 683.

WILLIAM OF HAUTEPIERRE, archbishop of Besançon, 1120. Charter, CLXVI, 847.

WILLIAM OF BIRON, about 1117. Charter granting the valley of Seguin in the forest of Cadouin to Lord Robert of Arbrissel, CLXII, 1110.

WILLIAM OF CHAMPEAUX, bishop of Châlons, 1121. 1. Fragment on the sacrament of the altar. 2. Charter of William of Champeaux. 3. On the origin of the soul. 4. Dialogue between a Christian and a Jew concerning the Catholic faith, CLXIII, 1037.

WILLIAM, abbot of St Thierry near Reims, about 1150. 1. Letter to the brethren of Mont-Dieu concerning the solitary life. 2. Meditative prayers. 3. Book on contemplating God. 4. On the nature and dignity of divine love. 5. Disputation against Peter Abelard, addressed to Geoffrey of Chartres and Bernard. 6. On the errors of William of Conches, addressed to St Bernard. 7. Book on the sacrament of the altar. 8. Letter to a certain monk who had written concerning the body and blood of the Lord. 9. Mirror of Faith. 10. Enigma of Faith. 11. Commentary on the Song of Songs. 12. Exposition of the Epistle to the Romans. 13. Two books on the nature of body and soul, CLXXX, 186; CLXXXIV, 365; CLXXXV, 221, 225.

WILLIAM, monk of Saint-Denis and disciple of Suger, 1152. 1. Life of Abbot Suger, CLXXXVI, 1193. 2. Verses on the death of Abbot Suger, ibid., 1211. 3. Letter to certain of his fellow monks, ibid., 1472.

WILLIAM THE FLEMING, twelfth century. On the Life of St Bernard, CLXXXV, 1403.

WILLIAM OF TRAHINAC, sixth prior of Grandmont, about 1180. Two letters: to Peter Bernard of Grandmont, concerning the death of St Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury; and to Henry II, king of England, concerning the same, CCIV, 1177.

WILLIAM DANDINA OF GRANDMONT, surnamed of St Savin, about 1157. Life of Blessed Hugh of Lacerta, disciple of St Stephen, founder of the Order of Grandmont, CCIV, 1181.

WILLIAM, archbishop of Tyre, 1190. History of Deeds Done in the Regions Beyond the Sea, from the time of the successors of Muhammad to the year of the Lord 1184, CCI, 209.

WILLIAM, lord of Salins, 1285. Donation to the canons of Salins, CLXXXV, 1439.

GUILLEMANS (J.), regular canon, uncertain date. Life of Blessed Ida, countess of Boulogne, mother of King Godfrey, CLV, 448.

WILLIAM OF MONTEACUTO, 1255. Two charters: for the brethren of Buxières; for the church of Buxières, CLXXXV, 1428.

GUITMUND, archbishop of Aversa, 1089. 1. Three books on the truth of Christ’s body and blood in the Eucharist. 2. Guitmund’s confession concerning the Holy Trinity, Christ’s humanity, and the truth of the body and blood of our Lord. 3. Guitmund’s letter to Erfastus. 4. Guitmund’s address to William I, king of England, when he declined the episcopate, CXLIX, 1425.

[Col. 0594] GUMPOLD, bishop of Mantua, between 967 and 985. Life of Wenceslaus, duke of Bohemia, CXXXV, 920.

GUNDECHAR, bishop of Eichstätt, about 1073. Pontifical Book of Eichstätt, CXLVI, 985.

GUNDOBAD, king, about 500. Letter to Avitus of Vienne, consulting him concerning certain words of Isaiah, LIX, 236.

GUNDULF, bishop of Rochester, 1108. Two letters: to the monks of Bec, that they should not grieve at the loss of their abbot Anselm; and to Anselm, living at Lyons, that by his presence he should relieve the church of Canterbury, afflicted by many tribulations, CLIX, 836.

GUNTHAR, bishop of Cologne, 768. 1. Gunthar’s diabolical chapters against Pope Nicholas. 2. Gunthar’s recantation. 3. Letter to Hincmar; another letter to the bishops established in King Louis’s realm, CXXI, 377.

GUNTHER, Cistercian monk, 1212. 1. Thirteen books on prayer, fasting, and almsgiving. 2. History of Constantinople captured by the Latins under Baldwin. 3. *Ligurinus*, or ten books on the deeds of Emperor Frederick Augustus, surnamed Redbeard (*Aenobarbus*), CCXII, 96.

GUNZO THE GRAMMARIAN, deacon of Novara, 967. Two letters: to Atto, bishop of Vercelli; and to the brethren of Reichenau, against a monk of St Gall who had held him in contempt because he had made a grammatical error, CXXXVI, 1280.

GURHEDEN, monk of Kemperlé, 1118. Account, or report, of the aforesaid controversy, CLXXII, 1327.

GUTHRUM, king of the Danes in East Anglia, 966. Ecclesiastical laws, CXXXVIII, 455, 459.

## H

HACQUEVILLE, Nicholas, president of the Paris Senate, uncertain date. On the praises of St Bernard and the location of Clairvaux, CLXXXV, 565.

HADELHEID, abbess of Gandersheim, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 317.

HADOIND (St), bishop of Le Mans, 638. Testament of Hadoind, bishop of Le Mans, LXXX, 568.

HAICHO OF HONAU, 723. Charter for the monastery of Honau, LXXXVIII, 1279.

HAIMIN, monk of St Vaast at Arras, 834. 1. Sermon on the feast of St Vaast, concerning the eleven little children healed through his merits. 2. Letter to Milo, priest, CV, 756.

HAYTO. See AHYTO.

HALDOIN, abbot, 849. Verses for the tomb of St Remigius, CXXIX, 1033.

HALINARD, Archbishop of Lyons, 1052. Three letters: to Pope John XIX; to Eiquoc, wardrobe-keeper of the Sacred Palace; and to the canons of Lyons, CXLII, 1333.

HALITGARIUS, Bishop of Cambrai, 831. Five books on vices and virtues and on the order of penitents, CV, 649.

HARIULF, Abbot of Aldenburg, 1142. 1. Chronicle of Centula, four books. 2. Life of Saint Arnulf, Bishop of Soissons, three books. 3. Life of Saint Madelgisil, confessor and hermit in Ponthieu, CLXXIV, 1211.

HARMOTUS, Abbot of Saint Gall, 884. 1. Inscriptions in the church of Saint Othmar. 2. Epitaph of Grimald, CXXVI, 990.

HARTMANN, monk of Saint Gall, 850. Poems; verses to be sung before the Gospel; for the Nativity of the Innocents, for the procession; litanies for processions on Sundays . . . verses for receiving the king, etc., CXVI, 23; LXXXVII, 30 ff.

HATTO, Archbishop of Mainz, 912. Letter to Pope John IX, concerning the death of Emperor Arnulf; his seven-year-old son Louis, hailed as king of Germany; and the archbishopric established among the Moravians, CXXXI, 1180.

HATTO, Bishop of Troyes. See ATTO.

HAYMO, Bishop of Halberstadt, 853. 1. Explanation of the Psalms. 2. Commentaries on certain Canticles. 3. Three books of commentaries on Isaiah. 4. Exposition of the twelve Minor Prophets. 5. Exposition of the Song of Songs. 6. On the Epistles of Saint Paul. 7. On the Apocalypse. 8. Homilies: on the seasons, CXLI; thirteen homilies on the saints; five homilies on certain Epistles of Paul. 9. Miscellanies: on the body and blood of the Lord. 10. Epitome of sacred history, or Ten Books for the Remembrance of Christian Matters. 11. Three books on the variety of books, or on love for the heavenly homeland, CXVI, CXVII, CXVIII.

HAYMO of Asirey, of Dijon, 1237. Testimony, CLXXXV, 1456.

[Col. 0595] HEBERNUS, Archbishop of Tours, 855. Miracles of Blessed Martin, CXXIX, 1036.

HEDDO, Bishop of Strasbourg, 748. Charter for the monastery of Arnulf, LXXXVIII, 1314.

HEDEN, illustrious man, 704. Charter by which he grants gifts to Bishop Willibrord, LXXXIX, 535.

HEDILO, Bishop of Noyon, 868. Letter to Dido of Laon on behalf of the priest Arnegis, requesting permission for him to move into Dido’s parish and be subject to him, CXXIX, 1394.

HEIMO, monk of Bamberg, 1135. Annals of Bamberg, CLXXIII, 1363.

HELDERIC, provost of Saint Simeon at Trier, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard: he praises God’s wondrous gifts in her and commends himself to her prayers, CXCVII, 312.

HELENA, Empress, 325. Letter to Constantine, VIII, 529.

HELENGER, Abbot of Saint Disibod, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard: he accuses himself and complains about the poor observance of monastic discipline in his monastery, CXCVII, 204.

HELGAUD, monk of Fleury, A.D. 1051. Life of Robert, King of the Franks, CXLII, 1264.

HELINAND, monk of Froidmont, 1212. 1. Twenty-eight sermons, for Advent, the Nativity of the Lord, the Epiphany of the Lord, the Purification of Blessed Mary, Palm Sunday, Easter, the Ascension of the Lord, Pentecost, etc. 2. *Flowers* collected by Vincent of Beauvais: On Self-Knowledge; On the Good Government of a Prince. 3. Letter to Walter the cleric, entitled *Book on the Restoration of One Who Has Fallen*. 4. Passion of Saints Gereon, Victor, Cassius, and Florentius, Theban martyrs. 5. Chronicle from the year of Christ 634 to 1204. 6. Extracts from Helinand’s poem, composed in the French language, entitled *On Death*, CCXII, 477.

HELLADIUS, Bishop of Tarsus, 433. Letter to Pope Sixtus, L, 594.

HELOISE, Abbess of the Paraclete, A.D. 1142. Letters to Peter Abelard, CLXXVIII, 182, 191, 212. Problems with the solutions of Father Abelard, ibid., 677.

HELPERIC, monk of Saint Gall, 980. Book on computation, CXXXVII, 18.

HELPIDIUS, Rusticus, illustrious man of senatorial rank and former quaestor, 520. 1. Poems on the history of the Old and New Testament. 2. Poem on the benefits of Christ Jesus, LXII, 544.

HEMMING, monk and priest of Worcester, 1095. 1. Life of Wulfstan, Bishop of Worcester. 2. Book on the Growth of the Church of Worcester, CL, 1489.

HENRY I, Emperor of Germany, 919. Copy of the privilege of Emperor Henry concerning the regalian rights granted to Saint Peter, XCVIII, 625.

HENRY II (Saint), Emperor of Germany, 1024. 1. Ecclesiastical diplomas, CXXXIX. 2. Address delivered at the Council of Frankfurt, held in 1006 for the establishment of the bishopric of Bamberg, CXL, 9 ff.

HENRY III, Emperor of Germany, 1056. 1. Three enactments, concerning the oath against calumny, enactment concerning marriages, etc. 2. Fifteen diplomas, CLI, 1081. 3. Letter to Saint Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, CLIX, 931.

HENRY IV, Emperor, 1106. Sixteen enactments, CLI, 1126.

HENRY I, King of the Franks, 1060. Twelve diplomas, CLI, 1025.

HENRY, Bishop of Parma, 1015. Sermon on the Pascha of the Lord, CXXXIX, 1529.

HENRY, cleric of Pomposa, 1092. Letter to Stephen, CL, 1345.

HENRY, Count of Portugal, twelfth century. Letter to Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, concerning a treaty of friendship with Raymond, Count of Galicia, CLIX, 944.

HENRY, monk of Stavelot, 1147. Letters to Abbot Wibald: he gives an account of his dealings with the pope for confirmation of his election as abbot of Corbie, CLXXXIX, 1145; gives thanks for his goodwill, etc., ibid., 1203; writes that the elect has given his assent to his election, ibid., 1210; asks that the best of fathers not abandon his obedient sons, ibid., 1369.

HENRY, Count of Namur, 1148. Letter to Pope Eugenius III, CLXXXIX, 1172.

HENRY, King of the Romans, 1148. Letter to Pope Eugenius III concerning the Archbishop of Mainz, whom he excuses for not having attended the Council of Reims, CLXXX, 1618. Two letters to Abbot Wibald of Stavelot, CLXXXIX, 1186.

HENRY, junior king, 1150. Two letters: to Emperor Manuel, informing him of the victory he had gained over Welf; and to the empress, informing her of the victory he had gained over Welf, CLXXXIX, 1286, 1287.

[Col. 0596] HENRY, Duke of Saxony, A.D. 1148. Letter to Pope Eugenius III concerning Wibald, Abbot of Stavelot, whose merits he extols, CLXXX, 1621. Letter to Abbot Wibald, asking him to be present with him before the king at the court of Regensburg, CLXXXIX, 1362. Letter to Emperor Frederick concerning the pardon granted to Widikind of Swalemberg and the penance imposed upon him, ibid., 1449.

HENRY of Salterey, about 1150. Treatise on the Purgatory of Saint Patrick, Apostle of the Irish, CLXXX, 972.

HENRY, Archbishop of Mainz, 1149. Letter to Abbot Wibald of Stavelot, giving an account of what he had done at the Council of Erfurt, CLXXXIX, 1214. Letter to Hildegard concerning a certain nun elected abbess, CXCVII, 156.

HENRY, Bishop of Minden, 1149. Letter to Abbot Wibald concerning the dispute between the Bishops of Paderborn and Münster, CLXXXIX, 1219. Letter to Wibald clearing himself of the charges previously made against him by Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1328. Letter to Bernard, Bishop of Paderborn, concerning the case pending between Bernard and the Abbot of Corbie, CLXXXIX, 1330. Letter to Abbot Wibald concerning Godebold, whose innocence he defends, ibid., 1343.

HENRY, notary of the royal court, 1150. Three letters to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1296, 1335, 1411.

HENRY, Bishop of Liège, 1151. Letter to Eugenius concerning Arnold, Archbishop of Cologne, requesting confirmation of his election, CLXXX, 1631. Letter to Abbot Wibald, expressing his wish to enjoy Wibald’s presence for correcting defects of conduct, CLXXXIX, 1158. To Wibald, complaining about Henry, Count of the Rock, and the Count of Namur, ibid., 1353 ff.

HENRY, Count of Salm, 1153. Letter to Abbot Wibald, leaving all his disputes to be settled by Wibald’s judgment, CLXXXIX, 1434.

HENRY, Bishop of Troyes, 1153. Letter to Saint Bernard concerning the abbey of Boulancourt, CLXXXII, 693.

HENRY, Archdeacon of Huntingdon, twelfth century. 1. Eight books of the *History of the English*. 2. Letter to Warin concerning the kings of the Britons. 3. Letter to Walter on contempt for the world, or on the bishops and illustrious men of his own time, CXCV, 797.

HENRY, Abbot of Crowland, year uncertain. Life of Saint Thomas, Archbishop and Martyr of Canterbury, CXC, 257.

HENRY, Archdeacon of Salzburg, 1174. History of the Calamities of the Church of Salzburg, addressed to Archbishop Adalbert, CXCVI, 1540.

HENRY I, brother of King Louis VII, Archbishop of Reims, 1175. 1. Twenty letters: to Bernard of Clairvaux on behalf of the Bishop of Alais; to Suger, Abbot of Saint-Denis; to Peter the Venerable, Abbot of Cluny; to Saint Hildegard, to whose prayers he commends himself; to King Louis, against the antipope Victor, etc. 2. Four diplomas: for the Church of Saint-Just; charter concerning fairs established at Reims for the benefit of lepers; concerning non-resident canons; concerning Sampigny, purchased by the Archbishop of Reims, CXCVI, 1581; CLXXXII, 680.

HENRY, Abbot of Stratford, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Alexander III, CXC, 686. To the same pope on behalf of Gilbert, Bishop of London, CC, 1441.

HENRY, Bishop of Bayeux, twelfth century. Letter of Henry, Bishop of Bayeux, concerning the gift made to the chapter of Bayeux of the house of Conan the treasurer, CCVII, 1157.

HENRY, Dean of London, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Alexander III concerning Bishop Gilbert, traveling to Rome, CC, 1412.

HENRY, son of Count Theobald, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1385.

HENRY, Bishop of Winchester, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1432.

HENRY, Bishop of Beauvais, twelfth century. Letter to Peter the Venerable, CLXXXIX, 399.

HENRY of Château-Marsi, Abbot of Clairvaux, later Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and Bishop of Albano, 1188. 1. Thirty-two letters: to Pope Alexander III concerning the holy war; to the King of England; to the Black Abbots of Flanders, etc. 2. Treatise on the Pilgrim City of God, CCIV, 212 ff.

HENRY II, King of England, 1189. 1. Confirmation concerning Labdecombe, CLXXXIX, 1063. 2. Revocation of the articles which King Henry II wished the English Church to observe, CXC, 405. 3. Letters to Reginald, the schismatic of Cologne, concerning Saint Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 1046; to the bishops of England concerning the same, 1045; to William of Sens concerning the same, etc., following. 4. Charters of Henry: for the Abbey of Le Val in Normandy; for the Abbey of Baugé, commonly called Baugerais, of the Cistercian order; [Col. 0597] gift of the church of Fontevraud at Ponts-de-Cé; confirmation of the foundation of Savigny Abbey, etc., CCVII, 1160 ff.

HENRY of Septimello, 1191. Elegy on the vicissitudes of fortune and the consolation of philosophy, four books, CCIV, 841.

HENRY, Bishop of Autun, twelfth century. Two testimonies, CLXXXV, 1467, 1469.

HENRY, King of Hungary, 1204. Letter to Innocent III against certain persons who had not accepted enactments promulgated by the legate of the Apostolic See, CCXVII, 289.

HENRY, brother of the Emperor of Constantinople, 1205. Letter to Innocent III, notifying him that Emperor Baldwin had been captured by the Bulgars and sending envoys, CCXV, 706.

HENRY, Abbot of Saint-Denis, 1207. Disputation with Odo, Bishop of Paris, concerning the church of Argenteuil, CCXII, 88.

HERACLIDES, Alexandrian hermit, year uncertain. *Paradise*, or *Lives of the Fathers*, LXXIV, 244.

HERACLIUS, illustrious man, 494. Letter to Avitus of Vienne, LIX, 288.

HERARD, Archbishop of Tours, 871. 1. Chapters collected from the capitularies of the Frankish kings. 2. Memorandum to Venilo, Archbishop of Sens. 3. Proclamation of King Charles the Bald and of the Third Synod of Soissons, issued by command, explaining why it should not be surprising that a case already decided should again be reconsidered in this synod, and why the king should at last request the bishops to bless his wife the queen, CXXI, 761.

HERBERT, Abbot of Mores, later Archbishop of Torres in Sardinia, 1164. 1. Account of the book of Saint Bernard’s miracles, preserved through a remarkable miracle, CLXXXV, 369. 2. Fragments from books concerning the miracles of Cistercian monks, ibid., 453. 3. Three books on miracles, ibid., 1273.

HERBERT, Abbot of the monastery of Saints Joseph and Habakkuk, 1160. Privilege concerning the exchange of Bethel, CLV, 1162.

HERBERT OF BOSEHAM, 1180. 1. Life of Saint Thomas, Archbishop and Martyr, with dedicatory letter, CXC, 1069. 2. *Book of Apples*. 3. Homily for the feast of Saint Thomas. 4. The Cause of the Exile and Martyrdom of Blessed Thomas, Martyr and Bishop of Canterbury. 5. About forty letters written in the person of Saint Thomas of Canterbury and of others. 6. Gloss on the Psalter, CXC, 1069.

HERIBERT, Bishop of Eichstätt, 1042. Six hymns: on the Holy Cross, Saint Willibald, Saint Walburga, Saint Lawrence, All Saints, and the finding of Saint Stephen, CXLI, 1369.

HERIBERT, monk, about 1150. Letter concerning the heretics of Périgord, CLXXXI, 1720.

HERIC, monk of Auxerre, 881. 1. Preface to his sixty-four homilies on the seasons and saints. 2. Verses to Hildebold, Bishop of Auxerre, in his collections. 3. Seven books, in verse, of the Life of Saint Germanus, Bishop of Auxerre. 4. Miracles of Saint Germanus of Auxerre. 5. Sermon to be recited on the solemnity of Saint Germanus, CXXIV, 1129 ff.

HERIGER, Abbot of Lobbes, 1008. 1. Deeds of the Bishops of Tongeren, Maastricht, and Liège. 2. Life of Saint Berlinda, virgin of Meerbeke in Belgium. 3. Life of Saint Landoald, written at the command of Notger, Bishop of Liège. 4. Metrical Life of Saint Ursmar, abbot. 5. Letter to a certain Abbot Hugh concerning questions proposed to him by Hugh about the discrepancy found between Dionysius and Bede, CXXXIX, 956.

HERIMANN, Bishop of Metz, 1090. 1. On the translation of Saint Clement, or charter for the Abbey of Saint Clement, issued on the day of the translation of that body, 3 May 1090. 2. Charter of Herimann confirming for Walo, Abbot of Saint Arnulf at Metz, the right to an annual market, wrongfully taken away through the action of certain persons, CL, 1177.

HERIMANN, Count of Wincenburg, 1148. Two letters to Pope Eugenius III, bearing witness to the election of Wibald as Abbot of Corbie, CLXXXIX, 1141, 1166.

HERMANN THE LAME, monk of Reichenau, 1054. 1. Chronicle from A.D. 1 to 1054. 2. Two books on the uses of the astrolabe. 3. Short musical works. 4. Sequence concerning Blessed Mary the Virgin. 5. Poem on the conflict between the sheep and flax, CXLIII, 56 ff.

HERMANN, Christian convert from Judaism, 1134. Short work on his conversion, CLXX, 803.

HERMANN, Abbot of Saint Martin at Tournai, 1147. 1. Treatise on the Incarnation of Our Lord Jesus Christ. 2. Three books on the miracles of Saint Mary of Laon and the deeds of Bishop Bartholomew and Saint Norbert. 3. Account of the restoration of the Abbey of Saint Martin at Tournai, [Col. 0598] CLXXX, 9 ff.

HERMANN, Bishop of Constance, 1150. Letter to Abbot Wibald, asking him to obtain, through imperial authority, the liberation of his kinsman Henry, who was held by Welf, CLXXXIX, 1281.

HERRAD, Abbess of Hohenburg, 1169. Dithyrambs for virgins, CXCIV, 1537.

HERTWIG, Archbishop of Bremen, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, announcing the death of his sister, Abbess Richardis, CXCVII, 161.

HERVARD, Archdeacon of Liège, 1208. Letter to G., canon of Laon, CCXI, 1284.

HERVAEUS, Archbishop of Reims, 922. 1. Letter to Wito, Archbishop of Rouen, concerning what penance ought to be imposed on unbaptized pagans and on the baptized, etc. 2. Council of Reims, presided over by Hervaeus, at which an anathema was pronounced against those who had killed Archbishop Fulk, on 6 July, A.D. 900, CXXXII, 660.

HERVEIUS of Sombernon, 1220. Testimonies, CLXXXV, 1424, 1427, 1432.

HERVEUS, venerable monk of Bourg-Dieu, 1150. 1. Eight books of commentaries on Isaiah. 2. Commentaries on the Epistles of Saint Paul, CLXXXI, 9 ff.

HERVEUS, cleric of Saint Thomas of Canterbury, twelfth century. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 694.

HESYCHIUS, African bishop, 419. Letter to Augustine concerning the Day of Judgment, XXXIII, 901.

HESSO, schoolmaster, 1119. Short commentary on the negotiation of peace between Pope Calixtus II and Emperor Henry V in the year of the Redemption 1119, and on the Council of Reims, CLXIII, 1081.

HETERIUS, Bishop of Osma, 790. Letter to Elipandus, XCVI, 893.

HEYMO, monk of Hirsau, 1091. Life of Blessed William, Abbot of Hirsau, CL, 889.

HIERONYMUS (Saint Jerome), priest of Stridon, 420. 1. One hundred and fifty letters, distributed into four classes according to chronological order, XXII, 9 ff. 2. Life of Saint Paul, the first hermit. 3. Life of Saint Hilarion, hermit. 4. Life of Malchus, captive monk. 5. Latin translation of the Rule of Saint Pachomius. 6. Translation of Didymus’s book on the Holy Spirit. 7. Dialogue against the Luciferians. 8. On the Perpetual Virginity of Blessed Mary against Helvidius. 9. Two books against Jovinian. 10. Book against Vigilantius. 11. Book against John of Jerusalem, addressed to Pammachius. 12. Apology against the books of Rufinus, sent to Pammachius and Marcella. 13. Dialogue against the Pelagians, three books. 13*. Fragments of Theodore, Bishop of Mopsuestia. 14. Book on Illustrious Men, addressed to Dextrus, praetorian prefect, with the ancient Greek translation added, which Erasmus published under the name of Sophronius. 15. On the Lives of the Apostles. 16. Letter on the Twelve Doctors, to Desiderius. 17. Book on Hebrew Names. 18. Book on the Site and Names of Hebrew Places. 19. Book of Hebrew Questions on Genesis. 20. Commentary on Ecclesiastes. 21. Translation of two homilies of Origen on the Song of Songs. 22. Greek fragments, *Book of Hebrew Names*. 23. Book of Greek Names from the Acts. 24. On the Blessings of Jacob the Patriarch. 25. On the Ten Temptations of the People of Israel in the Wilderness. 26. Commentary on the Song of Deborah. 27. Hebrew Questions on the Books of Kings and Chronicles. 28. Interlinear exposition of the Book of Job, XXIII, 171 ff. 29. Eighteen books of commentaries on Isaiah. 30. Six books of commentaries on Jeremiah. 31. Translation of nine homilies of Origen on the visions of Isaiah. 32. Abridgment on Isaiah, XXIV, 18 ff. 33. Commentaries on Ezekiel. 34. Commentaries on Daniel. 35. Translation of Origen’s homilies on Jeremiah and Ezekiel. 36. Treatise on the Lamentations of Jeremiah. 37. Commentaries on Hosea. 38. Commentaries on Joel. 39. Commentaries on Amos. 40. Commentaries on Obadiah. 41. Commentaries on Jonah. 42. Commentaries on Micah. 43. Commentaries on Nahum. 44. Commentaries on Habakkuk. 45. Commentaries on Zephaniah. 46. Commentaries on Haggai. 47. Commentaries on Zechariah. 48. Commentaries on Malachi, XXV, 15 ff. 49. Commentaries on the Gospel of Matthew. 50. Translation of Origen’s homilies on Luke. 51. Commentaries on the Epistle to the Galatians. 52. Commentaries on the Epistle to the Ephesians. 53. Commentaries on the Epistle to Titus. 54. Commentaries on the Book of Job. 55. Breviary on the Psalms, XXVI, 9 ff. 56. Translation of the Chronicle of Eusebius Pamphilus. 57. Chronicle of Saint Jerome, XXVII, 34 ff. 58. Divine Library, or the Books of the Old and New Testament, XXVIII, 163 ff.; XXIX, 25 ff.

Spurious works. 1. Fifty-three letters: to Demetrias, on despising inheritance; to Marcella, that she may endure adversity; to a virgin sent into exile; to a sick friend; on the divine [Col. 0599] law; on the Assumption of Blessed Mary; on the seven orders of the Church; praise of virginity; etc., etc. 2. Rule for Nuns. 3. Penitential canons. 4. Martyrology. 5. Book of the Companion (*Comes*), or Lectionary for the cycle of the year. 6. Commentaries on the Gospels and also on the Epistles of Blessed Paul, XXX, 14 ff.

HILARIANUS J., 397. 1. Chronology, or short book on the duration of the world. 2. Exposition on the day of Easter and the month, XIII, 1094 ff.

HILARY (Saint), Bishop of Poitiers, 368. 1. Treatise on the Psalms. 2. Commentary on the Gospel of Matthew. 3. Twelve books on the Trinity. 4. Book on the Synods, or on the Faith of the Easterners. 5. Apologetic replies to critics of the books on the Synods. 6. Letter to his daughter Abra. 7. Hymn sent to his daughter Abra. 8. Three books addressed to Emperor Constantius. 9. One book against Emperor Constantius. 10. One book against the Arians, or Auxentius of Milan. 11. Fragments from the historical work. 12. Fragments from other works of Saint Hilary. 13. Letter, or short book, of Saint Hilary. 13. Sermon on the dedication of a church. 14. Book on the unity of Father and Son. 15. Book on the essence of Father and Son, IX–X, 232 ff.

HILARY, deacon, 398. 1. Commentary on the twelve Epistles of Blessed Paul attributed to Hilary. 2. Questions on the Old and New Testament attributed to Hilary, XVIII, 65 ff.

HILARY (Saint), Bishop of Arles, 449. 1. Sermon on the life of Saint Honoratus, Bishop of Arles. 2. Doubtful works: sermon or account concerning the miracle of Saint Genesius, Martyr of Arles; verses for the feast of the Maccabean martyrs; poem on Genesis addressed to Pope Leo, L, 1213 ff.

HILARY, disciple of Abelard, twelfth century. Elegy in which Hilary laments his teacher’s departure from the Paraclete, CLXXVIII, 1855.

HILARY (Saint), Pope, 461. 1. Eleven letters: to the Empress Pulcheria concerning the assembly at Ephesus, the factions of Dioscorus, etc.; to the bishops of Tarragona, concerning a synodal decree and bishops, etc.; to Leontius, Bishop of Arles, concerning the beginnings of his episcopate; to bishops of various provinces in Gaul, concerning councils to be held every year and the rights of bishops, etc.; to the bishops who had heard the case of Mamertus in synod. 2. Two decrees: concerning the body of Christ and contentious persons, LVIII, 12 ff.

HILDEBERT, venerable Bishop of Le Mans, 1135. 1. One hundred and seventeen letters: to Master William of Champeaux; to Countess Adela; to Matilda, Queen of England; to monks unwilling to receive the Bishop of Chartres . . . to King Henry of England . . . letter of consolation to a friend . . . to the Archbishop of Tours, advising him not to consecrate a young man not canonically elected . . . to the Archbishop of Rouen concerning marriage between blood-relations and relations by marriage . . . to the Bishop of Angers concerning a priest who, for want of unleavened bread, had consecrated using ordinary bread; concerning Pope Paschal II, seized by force and fraud; against a heretic attacking the invocation of saints; etc. 2. Thirteen diplomas: for the benefit of the monastery of Saint Albinus at Angers; for the Church of Saint Ouen near Le Mans . . . for the benefit of Marmoutier; for the Church of Lupiniac . . . confirmation of all the rights and possessions of the monastery of Saint Vincent at Le Mans, etc. 3. One hundred and forty-four sermons: fifty-four on the seasons, thirty-three on the saints, fifty-six on various subjects. 4. Life of Saint Radegund, queen. 5. Life of Saint Hugh, Abbot of Cluny. 6. Book on the Conflict of Flesh and Soul. 7. Moral Philosophy on the Honourable and the Useful. 8. Short book on the four virtues of the honorable life, written in verse. 9. Theological treatise. 10. Treatise on the sacrament of the altar. 11. Book on the exposition of the Mass. 12. Verses on the mystery of the Mass. 13. Book on the Holy Eucharist, written in verse. 14. *Physiologus*. 15. On the order of the world. 16. On the adornment of the world. 17. Poem on the Books of Kings. 18. Moral application of passages of Scripture from the Old Testament. 19. Short book of Christian inscriptions. 20. Verses on Saint Susanna. 21. Verses on the Maccabees. 22. Verses on Saint Vincent. 23. Passion of Saint Agnes, virgin and martyr. 24. On the finding of the Holy Cross. 25. Metrical Life of Blessed Mary of Egypt. 26. Lament of the sinful soul. 27. History of Muhammad, written in verse. 28. Book called *Mathematicus*. 29. Miscellaneous poems, about 3,700 verses, CLXXI, 17; CLIX, 857.
