HILDEBRAND THE YOUNGER, 1150. Short book on contemplation, CLXXXI, 1692.

HILDEFONSUS (Saint), Bishop of Toledo, 669. 1. Book on the Perpetual Virginity of Saint Mary against Three Unbelievers. 2. Book on the Understanding of Baptism. 3. Book on the Journey through the Desert, Which Is Made after Baptism. 4. Two letters to Quiricus, Bishop of Barcelona. 5. Book on Illustrious Men. Doubtful works: thirteen sermons; works attributed to Saint Hildefonsus; short book on the Crown of the Virgin; continuation of the chronicles of Blessed Isidore; twelve epigrams, XCVI, 9.

[Col. 0600] HILDEGARD (Saint), abbess, 1178. 1. One hundred and forty-five letters: to the supreme pontiffs Eugenius, Anastasius, Adrian, and Alexander; to the Archbishops of Mainz, Bremen, Cologne, and Trier; to the Bishops of Bamberg, Speyer, Worms, Constance, Verdun, Liège, Maastricht, and Prague; to Emperors Conrad and Frederick; to many abbots and many abbesses. 2. Three books of visions and revelations. 3. Book of Divine Works of a Simple Person. 4. Solutions to thirty-eight questions: concerning creation, the first parents, the bodies of angels, the ark, Christ after the resurrection, Blessed Paul caught up into the third heaven, the knowledge of the saints in heaven and the wicked in hell, etc., etc. 5. Explanation of the Rule of Saint Benedict. 6. Explanation of the Creed of Saint Athanasius for the community of her sisters. 7. Life of Saint Rupert, Duke of Bingen in the Diocese of Mainz. 8. Life of Saint Disibod, bishop and confessor, at Disibodenberg in the territory of Mainz in Germany. 9. *Physica*: on plants, elements, trees, stones, fish, birds, animals, reptiles, and metals, CXCVII, 145 ff.

HILDEGARIUS, distinguished man, eleventh century. Four letters to Saint Fulbert of Chartres, CXLI, 211, 266 ff.

HILDEMAR, monk, 843. Letter to Ursus, Bishop of Benevento, concerning the correct method of reading, CVI, 393.

HILDEPRAND, King of the Lombards, 768. Decree for the Church of Piacenza, LXXXVII, 1398.

HILDERIC, Abbot of Monte Cassino, 834. Metrical letter on God, CV, 760.

HILDIRAD, German donor, 807. Conveyance at Wenaswalda, XCIX, 807.

HILDUIN, Abbot of Saint-Denis, 840. *Areopagitica*, or Life of Saint Dionysius, CVI, 14 ff.

HILLIN, Archbishop of Trier, eleventh century. Letter to Hildegard, asking her to deign to let a few drops from the king’s wine-cellar drip down to him in writing, CXCVII, 166.

HINCMAR, Bishop of Laon, 878. Short works and ten letters. Letter to the Archbishop of Reims, clearing Nivinus and himself in Nivinus’s affair and censuring Hincmar of Reims; to the same, concerning Hadulf, to whom, in Hincmar’s favor, he permits the site of his former residence, while not yet granting him communion; to the same, concerning the ordination of the cleric Senatus, his own imprisonment, and his appeal to the Apostolic See. Hincmar’s collection from the letters of the Roman pontiffs to Hincmar of Reims. Memorandum presented to the bishops and through them to the king. Satisfaction sent to King Charles through Bishop Odo. Letter to the Archbishop of Reims; to the same, concerning the consent required for an excommunication pronounced by him. Hincmar’s protest, CXXIV, 968 ff.; CXXVI, 280 ff.

HINCMAR, Archbishop of Reims, 882. 1. Letter to King Charles prefixed to the earlier dissertation against the Predestinarians (lost). 2. Later dissertation on God’s predestination and free will, against Gottschalk and the other Predestinarians. 3. Collection from Holy Scripture and sayings of the orthodox, concerning the one and not threefold Deity—that is, the unity of the holy and inseparable Trinity—for repelling Gottschalk’s blasphemies and refuting his trifles. 4. On the divorce of King Lothair and Queen Theutberga. 5. Synodal chapters. 6. Royal coronations: of Charles the Bald, Louis II, Judith daughter of Charles, and Queen Ermentrude. 7. Explanation of Solomon’s Table. 8. On the person of the king and royal ministry, addressed to King Charles the Bald. 9. On avoiding vices and practicing virtues, addressed to King Charles the Bald. 10. On the diverse and manifold nature of the soul, addressed to King Charles the Bald. 11. On restraining the plundering of soldiers, addressed to King Charles the Bald. 12. On the words of the Psalm: “The house of the heron is their leader.” 13. To the bishops and nobles of the Province of Reims, concerning fidelity to be maintained toward King Charles. 14. To King Louis the Stammerer: instruction for the new king in the proper administration of the kingdom. 15. To Emperor Charles III, that he should appoint suitable educators and counselors for the sons of his cousin Louis the Stammerer, kings. 16. To the nobles of the kingdom, concerning the education of King Carloman and the ordering of the palace. 17. A second admonition to the bishops of the realm on behalf of King Carloman, delivered at Épernay. 18. In the common name of the bishops, to the king, concerning the restraint and eradication of the abduction of widows, girls, and nuns. 19. In defense of the liberties of the Church. 20. Synodal chapters. 21. On the duties of bishops. 22. On criminal priests. 23. On the case of the priest Teutfrid. 24. On the vision of the priest Bernold. 25. Advice concerning the penance of King Pippin. 26. On the estate of Noviliac. 27. Oath of Hincmar at Ponthion. 28. Life of Saint Remigius, Archbishop of Reims. 29. Encomium of the same Saint Remigius. 30. Reply to certain [Col. 0601] questions as to why he had used the phrase “mystical Nicene synod” in a certain writing of his humility. 31. Profession of faith sent to the Roman Pontiff. 32. Eight poems. 33. Annals doubtfully attributed to Hincmar, from 861 to 882, CXXV, 50 ff. 34. Fifty-five letters. Short works and letters concerning the case of Hincmar of Laon, CXXVI, 9 ff., 280 ff.

HLVDWIN, donor, 798. Conveyance to Werethinas, XCIX, 797.

HOWEL THE GOOD, King of all Wales, 940. Ecclesiastical laws, CXXXVIII, 472.

HONESTIS (Peter de). See PETER.

HONORATUS (Antoninus). See ANTONINUS.

HONORIUS, monk, sixth century. On the canonical books of the Old and New Testament, and confession of faith, LXXIV, 1244.

HONORIUS I, Pope, 638. 1. Sixteen letters: to Isaac, Exarch of Ravenna, concerning Adalwald, King of the Lombards; to the bishops of Venetia and Istria, concerning the deposition of Fortunatus, Patriarch of Grado; to Sergius, Bishop of Constantinople, concerning Christ’s two wills . . . to Edwin, King of England, that he may persevere in the faith; to Honorius, Bishop of Canterbury, to whom he sends the pallium; to Honorius, Archbishop of Canterbury, to whom he grants primacy over all the churches of Britain, etc. 2. Epigram on the Apostles, astonished at Christ’s Ascension into heaven. 3. Privilege granted to Bobbio monastery, LXXX, 464 ff.

HONORIUS II, Pope, 1130. One hundred and twelve letters and privileges, CLXVI, 1216.

HONORIUS of Autun, 1136. 1. Four books on the philosophy of the world. 2. Book on the affections of the sun. 3. Three books of the Image of the World. 4. Summary of the Whole of Universal History. 5. Four short books on the luminaries of the Church, or ecclesiastical writers. 6. Book on Heresies. 7. Catalogue of Roman pontiffs. 8. Commentary on Plato’s *Timaeus*. 9. *Hexaemeron*. 10. On the ten plagues of Egypt in their spiritual sense. 11. Exposition of selected Psalms. 12. Questions and answers on Proverbs and Ecclesiastes. 13. Exposition on the Song of Songs. 14. Seal of Blessed Mary. 15. Jewel of the Soul, or on the divine offices and ancient rite of the Masses, and on the canonical hours and solemnities of the entire year. 16. *Sacramentary*, or book on the causes and mystical meaning of the rites of the divine office in the Church. 17. Mirror of the Church. 18. *Elucidarium*, or dialogue on the sum of all Christian theology. 19. Book of Twelve Questions, chiefly asking whether the holy Archangel Michael precedes Blessed Peter the Apostle, or Peter precedes Michael. 20. Short book of eight questions on angels and man. 21. *The Inevitable*, or dialogue on predestination and free will. 22. Greater Ladder of Heaven, or dialogue on the order of knowing God in creatures. 23. Lesser Ladder of Heaven, or short work on the degrees of charity. 24. On the soul’s exile and homeland. 25. On cloistered life. 26. *Eucharistion*, or book on the body and blood of the Lord. 27. *Summa Gloria*, or book on the Apostolic See and the Emperor, concerning the precedence of priesthood over kingship, CLXXII, 40 ff.

HONORIUS, Emperor, 398. 1. Laws of Honorius: law against those invading churches; law concerning the rescript which the Donatists had obtained from Julian. Laws against rebaptizers, XI, 1192, 1194, 1204, 1206, 1208. Laws of Honorius renewing penalties enacted against Donatists and other heretics, ibid., 1216. Law imposing financial penalties on Donatists, ibid., 1420. 2. Letters to Symmachus, prefect of the city, XVIII, 398, 401, 402, 405; rescript to Pope Boniface in which the emperor decrees that, if two bishops should again be ordained at Rome, both are to be expelled from the city, XX, 765; two letters to Arcadius, ruler of the East, concerning what had been done at Constantinople and concerning the calling of a synod at Thessalonica, XX, 507, 512.

HORMISDAS, pope, A.D. 514. Eighty-one letters and decrees. To Saint Remigius, bishop of Rheims, to whom he delegates vicarial authority in Gaul; to the emperor Anastasius, whom he praises for his concern for the peace of the Church; to John, bishop of Nicopolis, concerning the condemnation of Nestorius and Eutyches; to the synod of Old Epirus on the same matters; to Avitus, bishop of Vienne; to Timothy, bishop of Constantinople, urging efforts for the unity of the Church; to the orthodox eastern bishops, whose steadfastness in faith he praises; to the people and monks of Constantinople, instructing them to abstain from association with heretics; etc., LXIII, 363, 525. Decretal concerning the divine Scriptures, LXII, 538. Letter to Caesarius of Arles, in which he confirms various enactments made by Caesarius, LXVII, 1286.

HROTSVITH, virgin and nun of Gandersheim in Germany, of the Order of Saint Benedict, A.D. 999.

1. Six comedies: *Gallicanus*, *Dulcitius*, *Callimachus*, *Abraham*, *Paphnutius*, *Sapientia*.
2. A history in verse of the birth and praiseworthy [Col. 0602] life of the inviolate Mother of God.
3. A history in verse of the Ascension of the Lord.
4. The Passion of Saint Gangolf, martyr.
5. The Passion of Saint Pelagius, most precious martyr.
6. The Fall and Conversion of Theophilus the Vicedominus.
7. A history of the conversion of Proterius.
8. A history of the passion of Saint Dionysius, eminent martyr.
9. A history of the passion of Saint Agnes, virgin and martyr.
10. A poem on the beginnings of the convent of Gandersheim.
11. A poem on the deeds of Emperor Otto I, CXXXVII, 940, 976 ff.

HUBERT, archbishop of Canterbury, A.D. 1200. Letter to the dean and chapter of Salisbury concerning a certain canon, whom he teaches may be exempted from the law of residence, CCVII, 403.

HUCBALD, monk of Saint-Amand, A.D. 930.

1. Letter concerning Saint Theodoric.
2. Hymn concerning Saint Theodoric.
3. Life of Saint Rictrudis, abbess of Marchiennes.
4. Passion of Saints Quiricus and Julitta, martyrs.
5. Life of Saint Aldegundis, virgin.
6. Life of Saint Lebwin, priest and confessor.
7. Historical commentary on Saint Jonatus, confessor and first abbot of Marchiennes in Belgium, *Miscellanea*.
8. Book on harmonic instruction.
9. *Musica Eucheriadis*.
10. Brief memorandum concerning tones and the chanting of psalms.
11. Eclogue in praise of Calvitius.
12. Metrical letter to Emperor Charles the Bald. He sends him the poems of his master Milo in praise of frugality.
13. Epitaph of Milo, monk of Saint-Amand, CXXXII, 816.

HUGH, priest of Metz, son of Drogo, 715. Charter by which he bestows gifts upon the basilica of the Holy Apostles at Metz, LXXXVIII, 1262.

HUGH of Honau, A.D. 748. Charter by which he bestows gifts upon the monastery of Honau, LXXXVIII, 1313, 1318.

HUGH CAPET, king of the Franks, A.D. 996. Diploma concerning the election of abbots and the church of Saint Leodegar at Campellis, CXLI, 945.

HUGH, bishop of the church of Langres, A.D. 1051. Treatise on the Body and Blood of Christ against Berengar, CXLII, 1322 ff.

HUGH II, bishop of the church of Nevers, A.D. 1065. Letter to Bartholomew, archbishop of Tours, concerning the cell of Credon, adjudged to the monks of Vendôme at the Roman council under Pope Nicholas, CXLIII, 1366.

HUGH I, bishop of Troyes, A.D. 1074. Letter to Bartholomew, archbishop of Tours, concerning the cell of Credon, adjudged to the monks of Vendôme, CXLVI, 1435.

HUGH, count of Troyes, A.D. 1121. Donations, CLXXXV, 1459, 1460, 1475, 1535, 1444.

HUGH, bishop of Senlis, about A.D. 1095. Letters concerning the abbey of Crépy, CLIX, 974.

HUGH, archbishop of Besançon, A.D. 1066. Charter for the restoration of the chapter of Saint Stephen, LXXX, 421.

HUGH, priest of Saint-Étienne, A.D. 1077. Charter concerning a donation made to Hugh of Cluny, CLIX, 968.

HUGH, abbot of Flavigny, about A.D. 1100. Chronicle from the Incarnation of Christ to the year 1102, CLIV, 9 ff.

HUGH (Saint), bishop of Lincoln in England, of the Carthusian Order, A.D. 1200.

1. Letters of enactments issued during visitation.
2. Seven diplomas: a charter confirming the grants of donors; a charter concerning two portions of the church of Corby; for the monastery of Saint Oswald of Bardney; for the church of Saint Andrew at Northampton; concerning the church of Walden; etc., CLIII, 936, 1114 ff.

HUGH, archbishop of Edessa, twelfth century. Letter to R., archbishop of Rheims, and to the canons of the Holy Apostles and Blessed Symphorian. He sends relics of Saint Thaddaeus and of King Abgar, CLV, 478.

HUGH, bishop of Die, A.D. 1075. Four letters to the archbishop of Tours, CLVII, 507.

HUGH, archbishop of Lyons, A.D. 1106. Thirty-one letters and privileges: to Rodulf, archbishop of Tours, concerning his legation; another to the same, inviting him to the council of Dijon; another to the same, inviting him to the council of Clermont; another to the same, inviting him to the council of Autun; concerning the church of Saint Faith at Chastellet, granted to the monastery of Conques; to Pope Gregory VII, concerning the council of Autun; to Countess Matilda, concerning the election of Pope Victor III; concerning the church of Saint Desiderius at Brescia, which he grants to the Cluniacs; to the bishops of Arras, Chartres, Autun, etc., CLVII, 488 ff.

HUGH (Saint), abbot of Cluny, A.D. 1109.

1. Eight letters: to William I, king of the English; to the brethren of Moissac; to Anastasius the hermit, that he may return to the monastery; to Pope Urban II, against Robert, abbot of Saint-Remigius; to King Philip, that, having renounced his kingdom, he may embrace monastic life.
2. Statutes of Saint Hugh for Alfonso, king of Spain, concerning the reception of Lambert, abbot of Saint-Bertin, as though he were a monk properly belonging to Cluny.
3. Exhortation to the nuns serving God at Marcigny.
4. Memorandum for his successors concerning [Col. 0603] the nuns of Marcigny.
5. Imprecation of Blessed Abbot Hugh.
6. What Blessed Hugh related in chapter on the Vigil of the Nativity of the Lord, CLIX, 845, 928, 946 ff.

HUGH OF SAINTE-MARIE, monk of Fleury, A.D. 1119.

1. *Ecclesiastical History*, arranged in four books; a second edition arranged in six books, from the origin of the world to Charlemagne.
2. History of the Franks of the region of Sens.
3. Fragments of the history of Fossatus.
4. Deeds of the Kings of the Franks.
5. Treatise on royal power and priestly dignity.
6. Letter to Ivo, bishop of Chartres.
7. Life of Saint Sacerdos, bishop of Limoges, CLXIII, 792, 821 ff.

HUGH OF CLERIES, Angevin knight, A.D. 1130. Commentary on the Mayoralty and Seneschalship of France, formerly hereditary in the counts of Anjou, CLXIII, 1034.

HUGH, bishop of Soissons, twelfth century. Five letters, to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 657, 659, 671.

HUGH OF RIBEMONT, A.D. 1125. Letter to G., of Anjou. He answers the question put to him: whether the soul of the first man was made from nothing, and how sin is contracted, CLXVI, 832.

HUGH (Saint), bishop of Grenoble, A.D. 1132.

1. Extracts from the cartulary of the church of Grenoble.
2. Two letters and diplomas; a charter forbidding women to approach the Charterhouse; concerning the fief of the episcopal cellarer, CLXVI, 1564.

HUGH, bishop of Porto in Galicia, A.D. 1134. *Compostelan History*, three books, CLXX, 876 ff.

HUGH OF DOUAI, archbishop of Sens, A.D. 1142. Letter to B., dean, and the other canons of the Church of Paris, offering consolation concerning the death of the bishop of Paris, CLXXIII, 1427. Two letters to Suger, asking him to receive the church of Blessed Columba of Sens under his protection; concerning the return of King Louis, CLXXXVI, 1397, 1402.

HUGH OF SAINT-VICTOR, regular canon of Saint-Victor at Paris, A.D. 1142.

*Exegetical Part.*

1. Preliminary notes on the sacred Scriptures and their writers.
2. Explanatory annotations on the Pentateuch.
3. Explanatory notes on the Book of Judges.
4. Explanatory annotations on the Books of Kings.
5. Nineteen homilies on Solomon’s *Ecclesiastes*.
6. Explanatory notes on the Lamentations of Jeremiah.
7. Explanatory notes on the prophet Joel.
8. Moral exposition on Obadiah.
9. Explanation of the Canticle of Blessed Mary.
10. Questions and determinations on the epistles of Blessed Paul. Exegetical doubts. Allegories on the Old Testament; allegories on the New Testament.
11. Exposition of the celestial hierarchy of Saint Dionysius the Areopagite, according to the translation of John Scotus, addressed to Louis, king of France, son of Louis the Fat; ten books, CLXXV, 9 ff.

*Dogmatic Part.*

1. Instructions on the Decalogue of the Lord’s Law.
2. Dialogue on the sacraments of the natural and written law.
3. *Sum of Sentences*, divided into seven treatises.
4. On the sacraments of the Christian faith.
5. Four books on Noah’s Ark in its moral sense.
6. On Noah’s Ark in its mystical sense.
7. Four books on the vanity of the world and the use of transitory things.
8. Seven books of didactic instruction.
9. Little book on which is greater, the power or the will of God.
10. On the four wills in Christ.
11. On the wisdom of Christ’s soul.
12. On the Virginity of Blessed Mary.
13. On the manner of speaking and meditating.

*Mystical Treatises.*

1. Exposition of the Rule of Saint Augustine.
2. On the instruction of novices.
3. Soliloquy on the pledge of the soul.
4. On the praise of charity.
5. On the manner of praying.
6. On the love of the Bridegroom for the Bride.
7. A golden little work on meditation, or the art of meditating.
8. On the fruits of flesh and spirit. Three letters: to Ranulf of Mauriac, on charity; to the same, on the resolution of four questions proposed by Ranulf of Mauriac; to John, archbishop of Seville, on the Christian faith, CLXXVI, 9 ff.

HUGH FARSITUS, canon of Soissons, A.D. 1143. Little book on the miracles of the Blessed Virgin Mary in the city of Soissons, CLXXIX, 1778.

HUGH, first abbot of Pontigny of Mâcon, afterwards bishop of Auxerre, A.D. 1151.

1. Two letters, to Suger.
2. Charter concerning the property possessed by Hugh of Tilly, CLXXXI, 1740; CLXXXVI, 1393, 1406.

HUGH OF LIZINIAC, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1352.

HUGH METELLUS, regular canon, about A.D. 1157. Four letters: to Saint Bernard, before whom he attempts to clear himself and his associates of accusation; to Abbot William, written in the person of his own abbot; to Gerland, concerning the sacrament of the Holy Eucharist, CLXXXVIII, 1269; CLXXXII, 687, 688.

HUGH, bishop of Ostia, A.D. 1140. Letter to the Cistercian chapter concerning the death of Pope Eugenius III, CLXXXII, 694.

HUGH OF BAUX, A.D. 1153. Letter to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1430.

HUGH, of Amiens, archbishop of Rouen, A.D. 1164.

1. Fifteen letters: to Louis, king of the Franks, concerning the establishment of a market [Col. 0604] at Gozengres; concerning the liberty of the church of Saint Martin of Pontoise; to Suger, abbot of Saint-Denis; to Pope Innocent II, concerning the death of Henry I, king of the English; to Eugenius III concerning the monastery of Vézelay; to all the faithful concerning the seamless cloak.
2. Seven books of theological questions, or dialogues.
3. Treatise on the Hexaemeron.
4. Three books against the heretics of his time, or on the Church and its ministers.
5. Treatise on memory.
6. On the Catholic faith and the Lord’s Prayer.
7. Life of Saint Adjutor, monk of Tiron, CXCII, 1112 ff.; CLXXXVI, 1399, 1430 ff.; CLXXIX, 970.

HUGH OF FOUILLOY, A.D. 1174.

1. Four books on the cloister of the soul.
2. On the medicine of the soul, CLXXVI, 1018, 1184.
3. Two books on beasts and other things, CLXXVII, 9 ff.; CXCVI, 1553.

HUGH OF POITIERS, notary of William, abbot of Vézelay, A.D. 1167. History of the monastery of Vézelay, four books, CXCIV, 1560.

HUGH, cleric of Saint Thomas of Canterbury, 1175. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 698.

HUGH, bishop of Langres, A.D. 1220. Testimonial, CLXXXV, 1469.

HUGH OF CHAMPFLEURY, bishop of Soissons and chancellor of King Louis VII, A.D. 1175. Eight letters: to the lord bishop of Porto; to King Louis, concerning a conference with the Normans; concerning the lifting of the interdict upon the Church of Soissons; etc., CXCVI, 1583.

HUGH, king of Cyprus, twelfth century. Privilege concerning Lacridon in Cyprus, CLV, 1253.

HUGH, abbot of Saint Mary at Adrianople and prior of Saint John at Constantinople, twelfth century. Letter to Louis, king of France, CLV, 1276. Letter to Pope Alexander III, in which he recounts what he did among the eastern peoples for the stability of the Roman Church during Emperor Frederick’s expedition, CC, 1375.

HUGH, lord of Caesarea in Palestine, twelfth century. Privilege of the village of Feniculus concerning the liberty and boundaries of the land, CLV, 1238.

HUGH ETHERIANUS, A.D. 1177–1180.

1. Book on the soul already stripped of the body, or on the return of souls from the lower world.
2. Three books on the heresies of the Greeks, CCII, 165.

HUGH V, seventeenth abbot of Cluny. Statutes of the monastery of Cluny, CCIX, 881 ff.

HUGH, dean of Saint Mary at Paris, A.D. 1208. Foundation of Bishop Odo for the performance of the mandate on Maundy Thursday, CCXII, 90.

HUGH, bishop of Riez, A.D. 1209. Letter to Innocent III concerning the affair of the count of Toulouse, CCXVI, 126.

HUMBALD, bishop of Ostia, twelfth century. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 986.

HUMBERT, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, bishop of Silva Candida, A.D. 1061.

1. Against the calumnies of the Greeks.
2. Reply against Nicetas, monk of the monastery of Stoudios.
3. Brief and concise account of the actions undertaken by the envoys of the Holy Roman and Apostolic See in the imperial city.
4. Three books against the Simoniacs, CXLIII, 912 ff.

HUMBERT, archbishop of Besançon, A.D. 1155. Proof concerning the complaint, CLXXXV, 1456.

HUMBERT, abbot of the monastery of Charroux, A.D. 1164. Charter concerning land granted on lease by the chapter to the monks of Charroux at Épehy, CCV, 907.

HUNALD, nobleman, A.D. 677. Donation of Hunald and his wife to Berarius, bishop of Le Mans, of what they possessed in the estate of Gaviriac, LXXXVIII, 1198.

HUNALD, monk of Bonne-Espérance, twelfth century. Letter to the provost concerning the sayings of Blessed Hilary in the book *On the Trinity*, CCIII, 174.

HUNTBERT, abbot, A.D. 671. Charter for the monastery of Murbach, LXXXVIII, 1197.

HYACINTH, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, twelfth century. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 987. Letter to Gerhoh, teaching that Alexander is regarded as the legitimate pontiff by the whole Church, with few exceptions, CXCIII, 586.

HYGINUS, date uncertain. Life of Saint Macarius the Roman, LXXIII, 416.

## I

IBBO, bishop of Tours, A.D. 720. Charter for the monastery of Saint Martin at Tours, LXXXVIII, 1264.

IDA (Blessed), countess of Boulogne, mother of King Godfrey, about A.D. 1100. Ecclesiastical donations, CLV, 460.

IDALIUS, bishop of Barcelona, A.D. 690. Two letters: to Julian, bishop of the first see of Toledo; to Zuntfred, bishop of the first see of Narbonne, XCVI, 427, 816 ff.

IDATIUS, bishop of Aquae Flaviae, A.D. 460.

1. A brief chronicle from Theodosius to his own time.
2. A list of consuls from their first appointment, LI, 869, 874 ff.; LXXIV, 703.

IGINIUS, pope, A.D. 164.

1. Decrees concerning faith and other [Col. 0605] matters.
2. Letter to the Athenians, CXXX, 108 ff.

IMBERT, monk of Grandmont, A.D. 1174. Letter concerning the translation of the relics of the holy seven virgins, companions of Saint Ursula, from the diocese of Cologne to the Church of Grandmont, CCIV, 1222.

INGEBORG, queen of the Franks, A.D. 1196. Letter to Celestine: although she herself has been neglected, the king has attached himself to the daughter of the duke of Merania, CCVI, 1277.

INGOARA, nun of Sens, A.D. 711. Charter for the monastery of Saint Peter at Sens, LXXXVIII, 1258.

INNOCENT (Saint), pope, A.D. 417. Forty-three letters and decrees: to Anysius, bishop of Thessalonica, whose authority over the churches of Illyricum he confirms; to Victricius, bishop of Rouen, concerning clerics, virgins, married persons, the baptized, etc.; to all bishops assembled in the council of Toledo, concerning dissension and the corrupt discipline of the churches of Spain; to Theophilus, bishop of Alexandria, concerning John of Constantinople; to Exsuperius, bishop of Toulouse, concerning the continence of priests or levites, final penance, administrators, books received in the canon, etc.; to the clergy and people of Constantinople concerning the convening of an ecumenical council; to John Chrysostom, bishop of Constantinople, whom he consoles; to Aurelius, concerning the reckoning of Easter; to Alexander, bishop of Antioch, concerning peace; to Decentius, bishop of Gubbio, concerning certain ecclesiastical rites; etc., etc., XX, 458 ff.; XXXIII, 779, 783, 786, 788.

INNOCENT II, pope, A.D. 1143.

1. Five hundred and ninety-eight letters and privileges.
2. Council of Rheims of Pope Innocent II, in which the antipope Anacletus is excommunicated and Louis the Younger, his father being present, is crowned king of France by the pope himself in the year 1131, CLXXIX, 21, 54 ff.

INNOCENT III, pope, A.D. 1216.

1. Letters, or Registers, in sixteen books.
2. Twenty-nine sermons for the seasons; thirty-two sermons on saints; twelve sermons, called common, for the birthdays and feasts of the holy apostles, martyrs, confessors, and virgins.
3. Little book on almsgiving.
4. Encomium of charity.
5. Six books on the mysteries of the Gospel Law and the sacrament of the Eucharist.
6. Encomium of the Blessed Virgin Mary and her Son Jesus Christ.
7. Three prayers on the life and passion of our Lord Jesus Christ.
8. Three prayers concerning all saints, for the defense and tranquility of the Catholic and orthodox Church.
9. Hymn concerning Christ and the Blessed Virgin Mary, his most worthy mother.
10. Book on the fourfold kind of marriage, CCXIV, CCXV, CCXVI, CCXVII.

IRENE, empress, A.D. 775. Imperial rescript to the Most Holy and Blessed Pope Adrian, CXXIX, 199.

IRMINA, abbess in Germany, A.D. 704. Charter by which she grants Bishop Willibrord all that she possesses in the estate of Stancheim, LXXXIX, 537.

ISAAC, Cistercian abbot of l’Étoile, A.D. 1169.

1. Fifty-three sermons, on the principal feasts from All Saints’ Day to the Assumption of Blessed Mary.
2. Letter on the soul to a certain intimate friend.
3. Letter on the office of the Mass to John, bishop of Poitiers, CXCIV, 1684 ff.

ISAAC, bishop of Langres, A.D. 880. Canons, ten titles, CXXIV, 1073.

ISAIAH, Syrian abbot, fourth century. Rule for monks, CIII, 427.

ISARN, bishop of Toulouse, about A.D. 1100. Charter of the donation of the church of Saint Saturninus of Toulouse to the monastery of Cluny, CLIX, 981.

ISEMBERT, priest of Poitiers, eleventh century, to Saint A., bishop of Angers, CXLI, 270.

ISIDORE (Saint), bishop of Seville, A.D. 636.

1. Twenty books of *Etymologies*.
2. Two books of *Differences*, or On the Properties of Words.
3. Certain allegories of sacred Scripture.
4. On the birth and death of the Fathers praised in Scripture.
5. Prefaces to the books of the Old and New Testaments.
6. Book of numbers occurring in Holy Scripture.
7. Questions on the Old and New Testaments.
8. Questions on the Old Testament.
9. On the Catholic Faith from the Old and New Testaments, against the Jews, addressed to his sister Florentina.
10. Three books of *Sentences*.
11. Two books on ecclesiastical offices.
12. *Synonyma*, on the lamentation of the sinful soul.
13. Rule of monks.
14. Eleven letters.
15. Book on the order of created things.
16. Book on the nature of things.
17. Chronicle, from Adam to Heraclius, A.D. 620.
18. History of the kings of the Goths, Vandals, and Suebi.
19. Book on illustrious men.
20. Collection of Canons ascribed to Saint Isidore of Seville. Councils. Decretal letters, LXXX–LXXXI.

ISIDORE OF PACENSIS, eighth century. Epitome of emperors, or *Annals of the Arabs*, together with a chronography of Spain, collected in one volume, from the Era 649 to the year 788, XCVI, 1245.

ISIDORE MERCATOR, ninth century. Collection of decretals, [Col. 0606] or ecclesiastical rules established by the holy Fathers, CXXX, 2 ff.

ISO, monk of Saint Gall, A.D. 771.

1. Two books on the miracles of Saint Othmar.
2. Formulae of Iso, CXXI, 780.

IVO (Saint), bishop of Chartres, A.D. 1115.

1. *Decretum*, divided into seventeen parts: concerning faith and baptism, etc.; concerning the Body and Blood of the Lord, etc.; concerning the Church, etc.; concerning feasts and fasts, etc.; concerning the primacy of the Roman Church, etc.; concerning clerics, monks, marriages, homicides, etc.
2. *Panormia*, eight books: concerning faith, various heresies, baptism, etc.; concerning the constitution of churches and the offerings of the faithful; concerning the election of the supreme pontiff; concerning the primacy of the Roman Church and the law of metropolitans and bishops, etc.; concerning clerics accused solely on grounds of infamy and without witnesses; concerning weddings and marriages, etc.
3. Two hundred and eighty-eight letters.
4. Twenty-five sermons on ecclesiastical sacraments and offices and the principal annual feasts. Doubtful works: six sermons to the people; *Micrologus* on ecclesiastical observances; chronicle of the kings of the Franks, CLXI–CLXII.

## J

JAMES, deacon, date uncertain. Life of Saint Pelagia, harlot, LXXIII, 664.

JAPYGUS. See COSMAS.

JEREMIAH, archbishop of Sens, A.D. 827. Two letters, to Amalarius and to Frotharius, bishop of Toul, CV, 730.

JESSE, bishop of Amiens, A.D. 834. Letter on baptism, CV, 780.

JOHN, bishop of Antioch, A.D. 433. Letter to Pope Sixtus, L, 591.

JOHN, deacon, A.D. 496. Letter to the illustrious man Senarius, concerning various rites pertaining to baptism and other observances worthy of notice, LIX, 397.

JOHN, deacon, date uncertain. Life of Saint Gregory the Great, four books, LXXV, 60.

JOHN, bishop of Constantinople, A.D. 519.

1. Copy of the document in which he professes the Catholic faith and rejects all heretics, especially Acacius, LXIII, 443.
2. Copy of his report to Hormisdas, announcing that the peace of the Church has been established, etc., ibid., 449, 480.

JOHN, bishop of Nicopolis, A.D. 529. Letter to Hormisdas, in which he professes the Catholic faith and asks to be instructed concerning what must be avoided and what must be observed, LXIII, 387.

JOHN II, pope, A.D. 535. Five letters: to Justinian, asking him to use every effort to bring back those whom he knew to be straying from the right path of Catholic faith; to the senators concerning the Sleepless monks, followers of Nestorius, warning them that they must be avoided; to the bishops of Gaul concerning Bishop Contumeliosus, whom he confined in a monastery for penance; etc., LXVI, 12 ff.

JOHN III, pope, A.D. 572. Two letters: to the bishops of Germany and Gaul, concerning certain chorepiscopi who were arrogating excessive authority to themselves in the laying on of hands; he then shows that Clement ruled the Apostolic See after Blessed Peter; etc.; to Eraldus, bishop of Vienne, concerning the Mass offices which are variously performed in different churches; he grants him the use of the pallium, LXXII, 9 ff.

JOHN, bishop of Arles, A.D. 595. Letter to the virgins of the monastery of Saint Mary, LXXII, 860.

JOHN (Saint) OF DAMASCUS, A.D. 754. Life of Saint Barlaam, hermit, and Josaphat, king of India, LXXIII, 444.

JOHN, abbot of Biclar, A.D. 595. Chronicle, continuing where Victor ends, that is, from the year 566 to the year 590, LXXII, 860.

JOHN, bishop of Ravenna, A.D. 604. Letter to Pope Gregory, in which he defends the privileges of his church by custom, etc., LXXVII, 654.

JOHN IV, pope, A.D. 642. Four letters: to the bishops and priests of Scotland, concerning the celebration of Easter according to Catholic custom and the revival of the Pelagian heresy; to Emperor Constantine, son of Heraclius, an apology for Pope Honorius concerning the one will in Christ; to Bulcred, king of the Saxons; etc., LXXX, 597.

JOHN, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, translator. *Sayings of the Elders*, LXXIII, 992.

JOHN VII, pope, A.D. 707. Two letters: to Æthelred, king of the Mercians, and to Alfrid, king of the Deirans; he admonishes Berhtwald, archbishop of Canterbury, to summon a synod and make Wilfrid and his opponents either meet together or hasten to Rome. To the bishops of Britain, LXXXIX, 53 ff.

JOHN, bishop of Pistoia, A.D. 715. Profession made to Balsarius, bishop of Lucca, LXXXVII, 1350.

JOHN, archbishop of Constantinople, A.D. 715. Letter to Pope Constantine, LXXXIX, 341.

JOHN SCOTUS. See SCOTUS.

JOHN VIII, pope, A.D. 883. Three hundred and eighty-two letters and decrees, CXXVI, 648.

JOHN IX, pope, A.D. 905.

1. Four letters: to Hervey, archbishop of Rheims; to Styllianus, bishop of Neocaesarea; to the clergy and people of Langres; to Charles the Simple, king of the Franks.
2. Canon concerning the election of a pope.
3. Prefatory address at the Council of Ravenna, CXXXI, 28 ff.

JOHN X, pope, A.D. 928. Fifteen letters and privileges: to the bishops of the province of Narbonne; for the church of Autun; for the monastery of Saint Gall; to the archbishops of Ravenna, Cologne, and Narbonne; to King Charles III; etc., CXXXII, 798.

JOHN XI, pope, A.D. 936. Five letters and privileges: for the monastery of Cluny; for the monastery of Vézelay; to the clergy and people of Autun; for the monastery of Saint Mary and Saint Martin at Poitiers, CXXXII, 1056.

JOHN, monk and disciple of Saint Odo, A.D. 954.

1. Life of Saint Odo, second abbot of Cluny, CXXXIII, 44.
2. Prologue to his book on miracles, CXXXIII, 884.

JOHN XII, pope, 963. Twenty letters and privileges: to William, archbishop of Mainz; for the monastery of Saint Mary of Humolaria; to Berengar, bishop of Verdun; to Landulf, bishop of Benevento; to Henry, archbishop of Trier; to Saint Dunstan, bishop of Canterbury, concerning the grant of the pallium; for the monastery of Saint Saviour at Fulda; etc., CXXXIII, 1013 ff.

JOHN, abbot of Saint Arnulf at Metz, A.D. 983.

1. Life of Saint Glodesindis, abbess of Metz, CXXXVII, 212; history of the translation of Saint Glodesindis, abbess of Metz, ibid., 217.
2. Life of John, abbot of Gorze, ibid., 239.

JOHN XIII, pope, A.D. 973. Thirty-three letters and decrees. Bull for the establishment of the archbishopric of Magdeburg. Diploma concerning the excommunication of Herold, archbishop of Salzburg. Privilege for the church of Ferrara. Bulls for the monastery of Saint Maximin at Trier, the monastery of Déols in the diocese of Bourges, the monastery of Fulda, and the monastery of Saint Vincent at Metz. Letters concerning the establishment of the bishopric of Prague, for the church of Arles, etc., CXXXV, 949.

JOHN XIV, pope, A.D. 984. Letter to Alo, archbishop of Benevento, CXXXVII, 357.

JOHN XV, pope, A.D. 1016. Seventeen letters and privileges: for the monastery of Ciel d’Oro at Pavia; for the monastery of Saint Maximin; for the church of Noyon; to all the faithful concerning the monks of Corbie; for the monastery of Aniane; for the church of Hamburg; for the monastery of Saint Peter of Roda; for the monastery of Fulda; etc., CXXXVII, 826.

JOHN, Venetian deacon, A.D. 1008. Chronicle of Venice and Grado, CXXXIX, 876 ff.

JOHN XVIII, pope, A.D. 1009. Fourteen letters and diplomas: for the monastery of Saint Florentius at Saumur; for the church of Saint Mary at Isergia; for the church of Saints Cosmas and Damian at the Golden Mica; for the church of Paderborn; for the monastery of Saint Benignus at Dijon; for the monastery of Belleloc; etc., CXXXIX, 1477.

JOHN XIX, pope, A.D. 1033. Twenty-two letters and diplomas: for the church of Porto; to all kings, bishops, dukes, counts, etc.; for the church of Silva Candida; to Poppo, patriarch of Aquileia; to Robert, king of France, concerning the immunity of the monastery of Cluny; to Gauslin, bishop of Mâcon, concerning the immunity of the same monastery; etc., CXLI, 1114.

JOHN, bishop of Sabina, A.D. 1059. Complaint against the monks of Farfa at the Roman synod of the year 1151, CXLIII, 908.

JOHN, monk and disciple of Saint Peter Damian, A.D. 1072. Life of Blessed Peter Damian, CXLIV, 113.

JOHN GUALBERT. See GUALBERT.

JOHN, bishop of Avranches, afterwards archbishop of Rouen, A.D. 1079.

1. Book on ecclesiastical offices.
2. Two charters for the priory of Saint Victor at Calais, concerning the right of institution, removal, provision, correction, etc., which the bishop of Avranches fully retained in the monastery of Saint Michael, its abbot, and twelve canons.
3. Council of Rouen celebrated by John in the basilica of Saint Mary at Rouen, CXLVII, 9 ff.

JOHN, abbot of Fécamp, A.D. 1079.

1. Little book of prayers collected from Scriptures and the words of the Fathers.
2. Another little book on divine contemplation.
3. Seven letters: to William, king of England; to Vitalis, abbot of Bernay; to Warinus, abbot of the monastery of Saint Arnulf at Metz; to disorderly monks; to William, king of the English, CXLVII, 444.

JOHN SMERA POLOVECIUS. See SMERA.

JOHN, priest of Würzburg, date uncertain. Description of the Holy Land, CLV, 1054.

JOHN, monk of the Charterhouse of Portes, A.D. 1140. Five letters: to Stephen, his brother in flesh and spirit, concerning flight from the world; to Letold, concerning the manner of praying; to Hugh, concerning the manner of praying and especially thanksgiving; to Berard, concerning the guarding of the heart; to his nephew Bernard, who was considering transferring from the Carthusian Order to another order, concerning steadfastness in his resolution, CLIII, 900.

JOHN, bishop of Acre, A.D. 1138. Privilege concerning permission to build a church in the city of Acre and the gift of the church situated in the territory of Casalis, CLV, 1170.

JOHN, monk of Bèze, A.D. 1115. Chronicle of Bèze, CLXII, 862, 753.

JOHN OF CONSTANCE, A.D. 1137. Letter to Geoffrey, abbot, Richard, prior, and the monks of the monastery of Savigny; or preface to the book on ecclesiastical computation, CLXIII, 1480.

JOHN, deacon and monk of Saint-Ouen, A.D. 1117. Four sermons, CLXII, 1151.

JOHN OF MICHAELSBERG, A.D. 1128. Rule of the Templars, CLXVI, 854.

JOHN, monk, about A.D. 1132. Letter to Albero, archbishop of Trier, concerning the three Masses to be celebrated at the Nativity of the Lord and the feasts to be observed within its octave, CLXVI, 1510.

JOHN, abbot of Sponheim, date uncertain. Oration in praise and commendation of Rupert, formerly abbot of Deutz, CLXVII, 12.

JOHN, monk of Saint Lawrence at Liège, A.D. 1147. Vision of the state of souls after death and miracle of Saint Lawrence, martyr, CLXXX, 177.

JOHN CIRITA, abbot of Tarouca in Spain, A.D. 1159. Rule of the military Order of Avis, CLXXXVIII, 1669.

JOHN, abbot of Casa-Marii, A.D. 1002. Letter to Abbot Bernard concerning the unhappy outcome of the expedition to the Holy Land, CLXXXII, 590.

JOHN, bishop of Alet, A.D. 1153. Letter to Saint Bernard, CLXXXII, 680.

JOHN, monk of Cornwall, date uncertain.

1. Apology concerning the Incarnate Word, CLXXXVII, 296.
2. Little book on the canon of the mystical offering and its orders, CLXXVII, 457.
3. Eulogy addressed to Pope Alexander III, asserting that Christ is a certain man, CXCIX, 1041.

JOHN, cardinal of Santa Maria Nuova, date uncertain. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1411.

JOHN THE HERMIT, A.D. 1180. Life of Saint Bernard, abbot, CLXXXV, 532, 1255.

JOHN, abbot of Frithesel, A.D. 1150. Letter to Abbot Wibald, writing that he will go to the king, CLXXXIX, 1292.

JOHN, notary, A.D. 1151. Letter to R., prince and count of Ric., concerning the alliance of Welf with the Sicilian king, CLXXXIX, 1323.

JOHN, prior of Saint Swithun at Winchester, A.D. 1164. Letter to Alan, CXC, 1483.

JOHN OF NAPLES, date uncertain. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 988. Letter to Abbot Guarin and the brethren of Saint-Victor, CXCVI, 1394.

JOHN, priest of Poitiers, A.D. 1164. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 1022.

JOHN OF SALISBURY, bishop of Chartres, A.D. 1180.

1. Three hundred and twenty-nine letters.
2. *Polycraticus*, or *On the Trifles of Courtiers and the Footprints of Philosophers*, eight books.
3. *Metalogicon*, four books.
4. On the seven groups of seven.
5. *Entheticus on the Doctrine of Philosophers*, 1,850 verses.
6. Life of Saint Anselm, archbishop of Canterbury.
7. Life of Saint Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, CXCIX, 9 ff.

JOHN, twelfth century. Letter to Philip of Harvengt, abbot of Bonne-Espérance, CCIII, 170.

JOHN, abbot of Baugé, about 1200. Letter to Abbot Geoffrey, lamenting the pastoral burden imposed upon him, CCV, 827.

JOHN DE BELMEIS, archbishop of Lyons. Nine letters: to Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury; to Gilbert, bishop of London; to the rectors of churches; to G., bishop of Glasgow, CCIX, 877.

JOHN OF THIELRODE, monk of Saint Bavo, A.D. 1294. Genealogy of the counts of Flanders, CCIX, 987.

JOHN, master of the schools of Orléans, A.D. 1202. Letter concerning peace between Bishop Odo and the Church of Paris, CCXIV, 1190.

JOHN, abbot of Saint Geneviève, 1202. Letter concerning the parochial right of Saint Geneviève and the bishop’s procurations upon the church of Saint Geneviève, CCXIV, 1185.

JOHN, bishop of Cambrai, about A.D. 1203. Letter to the lord of Tournai, CCXI, 504.

[Col. 0609] JOHN WILLIAM, A.D. 1208. Letter to Guibert, abbot of Gembloux, CCXI, 1302.

JOHN, humble catholicos of the Armenians, A.D. 1205. Letter to Pope Innocent III, CCXV, 692.

JOHN, king of England, A.D. 1213. Three letters approving the conditions of absolution, CCXVI, 876. Two letters to Innocent III: concerning the agreement between the king himself and Queen Berengaria, formerly wife of King Richard; he recounts the barons’ disobedience and also that, because of this matter, he cannot undertake a journey to the Holy Land, CCXVII, 303, 306.

JOBIANUS, subdeacon, A.D. 767. Letters to Anselperga, abbess of the monastery of Saint Saviour at Brescia, in which he grants her fisheries situated in the territory of Feronianum, LXXXVII, 1389.

JOCERANNUS, bishop of the Church of Lyons, A.D. 1136. Letter to the bishop of Angoulême, CLXXII, 1326.

JOCERANNUS, bishop of Langres, A.D. 1120. Letter concerning the church at Fontenay of Saint Martin of the Meadow, CLXXXV, 1451.

JONAS, abbot of Elnone, seventh century. 1. Life of St. Columbanus, abbot. 2. Second Life of St. Eustace, abbot of Luxeuil. 3. Second Life of St. Attala, abbot of Bobbio. 4. Third Life of St. Bertulf, abbot of Bobbio. 5. First Life of St. Burgundofara, abbess of York. 6. Book of the Miracles of St. John, abbot of Reomay, LXXXVII, 1009.

JONAS, bishop of Orléans, 842. 1. On the Instruction of Laypeople, three books. 2. A Short Work on Royal Instruction, addressed to King Pippin. 3. On the Veneration of Images, three books, which, at the command of Emperor Louis, he published against the blasphemies of Claudius, bishop of the Church of Turin. 4. History of the Translation of St. Hubert, bishop of Tongeren, to the monastery of Andage, CVI, 118.

JONAS, canon of St. Victor, 1173. Letter to Ervisius, abbot of St. Victor, CXCVI, 1388.

JORDAN, bishop of Limoges, 1052. 1. Letter to Benedict VIII, Roman pontiff, CXLII, 1348. 2. Two charters for the chapter of Limoges, concerning the agreement between himself and William, count of Poitiers, ibid., 1351. 3. Acts of the Second Council of Limoges, 1354.

JOSCELIN, bishop of Salisbury in England, 1148. Letter to Suger, from whom he requests relics of St. Denis, CLXXXVI, 1363. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 1038.

JOSCELIN, archbishop of Tours, 1174. Six letters, CXCVI, 1536.

JOSEPH, disciple of Alcuin, 804. Joseph’s poem addressed to St. Ludger, XCIX, 821. Other verses in an epitome of Isaiah, ibid.

JOSEPH, priest, in the year of the Lord 846. History of the Translation of the Bodies of Saints Ragnobert and Zeno, CVI, 889.

JOTSALD, Cluniac monk, 1050. Prologue addressed to Pope Stephen on the life and virtues of St. Odilo, abbot, CXLII, 898.

JULIAN, emperor, 362. Rescript of Emperor Julian in favor of the Donatists, XI, 1179.

JULIAN POMERIUS, fifth century. Three books on the Contemplative Life, LIX, 416.

JULIAN, Pelagian bishop of Eclanum, in the year of the Lord 415. 1. A statement of faith sent to the Apostolic See in the name of eighteen bishops refusing to subscribe to the condemnation of Pelagius and Celestius. 2. Letters to Zosimus and Rufus. 3. Four books to Bishop Turbantius against the first book of St. Augustine on concupiscence. 4. Eight books to Florus against the second book of St. Augustine on marriage. 5. Book on Love. 6. Book on the Good of Constancy against the perfidy of a Manichaean. 7. Interpretation of Rufinianus’s booklet, XXI, 1172.

JULIAN (St.), bishop of Toledo, 690. 1. Foreknowledge of the World to Come, three books. 2. Apologetic book on the Three Chapters. 3. Three books on the Demonstration of the Sixth Age. 4. *Antikeimenōn*—that is, “of passages in the two Testaments that appear contradictory”—two books. 5. Commentary on the prophet Nahum. 6. Life of St. Ildefonsus. 7. Prayers composed by St. Julian and found in the Mozarabic Missal. 8. History of Paul’s Rebellion against Wamba, king of the Goths, XCVI, 428 ff.

JULIUS (St.), Pope Julius I, 352. 1. Two letters, to the Antiochenes and to the Alexandrians, written in Greek. 2. Ten decrees according to Gratian and Ivo. 3. Two letters of rebuke to Eastern bishops concerning the case of Athanasius and offenses against the Roman Church, etc., VIII, 858 ff.

JULIUS, abbot of the Isle of Mont-Christ, 719. Complaint concerning various usurpers of the rights of his monastery, LXXXVII, 1364.

JUNILIUS, African bishop, 550. Two books on the Parts of the Divine Law, LXVIII, 15.

JUSTINIAN, *vir illustris* (“illustrious man”), 565. Eight letters to Pope Hormisdas: on peace and unity in the Eastern Church, [Col. 0610] LXIII, 430, 450; to the same pope concerning dissensions stirred up by the Scythian monks and to be restrained by him, LXIII, 475 ff.; that, Acacius having been condemned, peace prevails at Constantinople; on the most holy Trinity, ibid., 496; urging him to labor for the union of the Churches, LXIII, 507; that Christ the Lord is correctly called “one in the Trinity,” as distinct from “one from the Trinity,” LXIII, 508, etc.

JUSTINIAN, emperor, 565. 1. Novels concerning religion, LXXII, 922. 2. Letters: to Pope John II, to whom he presents a profession of his faith; to Pope Agapetus I, to whom, newly elected, he presents a profession of faith in the manner of his forefathers. Justinian’s first confession of faith to Pope Agapetus; his second confession of faith to Agapetus, LXVI, 14, 35, 41, 42. Letter to Blessed John, metropolitan bishop, LXIX, 119; to Cosmas, bishop of Mopsuestia, LXIX, 119. Decree of Emperor Justinian, ibid., 30. 3. Book against Origen, written in Greek, LXIX, 178. 4. Letter against certain persons who defend in writing the impious Theodore and his unjust doctrines, the letter called that of Ibas, and Theodore’s books against the Catholic faith, LXIX, 274.

JUSTINIAN II, emperor, 686. Copy of the imperial command sent to John, pope of the city of Rome, confirming the Sixth Council of Constantinople, XCVI, 425.

JUSTIN, emperor, 527. Seven letters to Pope Hormisdas: on restoring peace to the Eastern Church, on Acacius, on Dioscorus, etc., LXIII, 426, 427, 448, 479, 486, 499, 501, 521.

JUSTUS (St.), bishop of Urgell, 540. 1. Letter to Pope Sergius concerning his little book on the Song of Songs, offering it to him and asking that, should anything in it require correction, he freely admonish him. 2. Exposition of the Song of Songs, LXVII, 961 ff.

JUVENCUS, Spanish priest, in the year of the Lord 329. 1. Gospel History, four books, about 3,226 verses. 2. Book on Genesis, 1,441 verses. 3. Poem on the Praises of the Lord. 4. Heroic Triumph of Christ, XIX, 9 ff.

## K

KENRED, king of the English, 709. Charter concerning lands in which the Blessed Virgin Mary is said to have appeared to Bishop Egwin, together with many others granted to the monastery of Evesham in the Lateran church, Pope Constantine confirming everything, LXXXIX, 336.

KENULF, king of the Mercians, ninth century. Letter to Pope Leo III concerning the abolition of the archbishopric of Lichfield and the restoration of the dignity of the Church of Canterbury, etc., CII, 1024.

KERVYN DE LETTENHOVE, 1853. On the controversy between Boniface and Philip the Fair, CLXXXV, 1833.

## L

LABORANS, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, 1191. Critical investigation into the compilation of the Decretals, CCIV, 870.

LACTANTIUS LUCIUS CAECILIUS FIRMIANUS, Latin rhetorician, 325. 1. Seven books of the Divine Institutes: On False Religion; On the Origin of Error; On the False Wisdom of the Philosopher; On True Wisdom and Religion; On Justice; On True Worship; On the Blessed Life. 2. Epitome of the Divine Institutes, addressed to Pentadius, VI, 112, 1018 ff. 3. Book on the Workmanship of God, or the Formation of Man. 4. Book on the Wrath of God. 5. Book on the Deaths of the Persecutors, addressed to Donatus the Confessor. 6. Fragments of Lactantius. 7. The *Phoenix*, attributed to Lactantius, eighty verses, VII, 9 ff.

LAMBERT, monk of Pultaria, 843. Letter to Abbot Alberic on the correct method of reading, CVI, 398.

LAMBERT, bishop of Le Mans, date uncertain. Letter to Hildebrand, bishop of Sées, CXXXII, 467.

LAMBERT, emperor, 898. Synodal chapters, CXXXVIII, 809.

LAMBERT OF ASCHAFFENBURG, 1040. Annals, from Adam to the year 994, CXLI, 444.

LAMBERT OF HERSFELD, 1076. Annals from the year 1040 to the year 1077, CXLVI, 1028 ff.

LAMBERT, master and prior of the Carthusians of Squillace in Calabria, 1125. Statutes, CLIII, 1149.

LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, 1119. 1. On the Primacy of the See of Arras. 2. Letters of Lambert and others to him, CXLIV. 3. Fourteen privileges for various monasteries and churches. 4. Canons of the Council of Clermont, in the year of the Incarnation 1095, collected by Lambert, CLXII, 615 ff.; CLXIII, 454 ff.

LAMBERT OF SAINT-OMER, 1130. 1. *Liber Floridus*, CLXIII, 1004. 2. Genealogy of the Kings of France and Counts of Flanders, CCIX, 938 ff.

LAMBERT OF LIÈGE, about 1150. From the Discovery and Miracles of St. Matthias, CLIV, 1280.

[Col. 0611] LANDERIC (St.), bishop of Paris, 651. Charter for the monastery of St. Denis, LXXXVII, 298.

LANDULF THE SAGACIOUS, date uncertain. Supplement to the *Historia Miscella*, XCV, 1143.

LANDULF THE ELDER, cleric of Milan, 1100. History of Milan, three books, CXLVII, 804.

LANDULF THE YOUNGER, or of St. Paul, 1137. History of Milan, CLXXIII, 1430.

LANFRANC, archbishop of Canterbury and primate of England, 1089. 1. Commentaries on all the epistles of Paul, with an inserted brief gloss. 2. Book on the Body and Blood of the Lord against Berengar of Tours. 3. Decrees for the Order of St. Benedict; that is, regulations which monks ought to observe in monasteries and likewise in cathedral churches. 4. Sixty-three letters of Lanfranc and others to him. 5. Address delivered by Blessed Lanfranc at the council held in A.D. 1072 on the primacy of the Church of Canterbury, against Thomas of York. 6. Short work on concealing confession, CL, 102 ff.; CLVIII, 1087.

LATRO, P., 1193. Instrument of renunciation made by Peter Latro and Nepos to Pope Celestine III, CCVI, 1272.

LAURENTIUS (St.), bishop of Novara, 540. Two homilies: On Repentance; On Almsgiving, LXVI, 88.

LAURENTIUS, first a monk of Monte Cassino and afterwards bishop of an uncertain see, in the year of the Lord 950. Sermon for the Vigil of St. Father Benedict, CXXXIII, 885.

LAURENTIUS, Pisan deacon of Verona, 1119. Seven books on the Balearic War, or on the Pisans’ deeds in Majorca and their triumph celebrated at Pisa in the year of salvation 1115, CLXIII, 513.

LAURENTIUS OF LIÈGE, 1201. Deeds of the Bishops of Verdun and the Abbots of St. Vitonus, CCIV, 916.

LAURENTIUS, abbot of Westin, 1173. Letter to Ernest, abbot of St. Victor, CXCVI, 1385.

LAURENTIUS, abbot of Westminster, twelfth century. Letter to Alexander III on behalf of Gilbert, bishop of London, CC, 1452.

LEANDER (St.), bishop of Seville, 591. 1. Rule, or Book on the Instruction of Virgins and Contempt for the World, addressed to his sister Florentina. 2. Homily in Praise of the Church, issued upon the conversion of the people after a council and the confirmation of the canons, LXXII, 870.

LEDUIN, abbot of St. Vaast at Arras, 1040. Constitution concerning the general assembly, CXLI, 1333.

LEIDRAD, bishop of Lyons, 816. 1. Book on the Sacrament of Baptism, addressed to Emperor Charlemagne. 2. Three letters, to Emperor Charlemagne and to his sister, XCIX, 854.

LEO, bishop of Bourges, 460. Letter to the bishops established within the Third Province, LIII, 1013.

LEO (St.) THE GREAT, pope, 440. 1. Ninety-six sermons delivered to the Roman people on the principal feasts of the whole year. 2. One hundred and seventy-three letters. 3. Fragments attributed to St. Leo the Great, LIV, 137. 4. The most ancient book of sacraments of the Roman Church, commonly attributed to Pope St. Leo. 5. Letter to the sacred virgin Demetrias, or Treatise on Humility, attributed to Leo the Great by Quesnel, LV, 21 ff.

LEO (St.), bishop of Sens, 548. Letter to Childebert, king of the Franks, who was seeking his presence or consent for the ordination of a bishop of Meaux, LXVIII, 9.

LEO II, pope, 683. Six letters written in Greek, to Emperor Constantine, to the bishops of Spain, to Count Simplicius, to Ervig, king of Spain, and to the bishops and king of Dalmatia, XCVI, 384.

LEO III (St.), pope, 818. 1. Sixteen letters: to Kenulf, king of the Mercians; to Charlemagne; to Riculf, bishop of Mainz; the Creed of Pope Leo; to Athelard, archbishop of Canterbury. 2. Three privileges: for the Benedictine nunnery of Horres near Trier; for transferring the episcopal see of Regensburg from the monastery of St. Emmeram to the church of St. Stephen; and for the monastery of St. Benedict at Cupersano, CII, 993.

LEO IV, pope, 855. 1. Thirty-three letters and decrees: to the Frankish army; to Emperor Lothair; excommunication of the priest Anastasius; to the bishops of Britain; to Emperor Louis; to Charles the Bald; to Prudentius, bishop of Troyes; to Hincmar, archbishop; etc. 2. Homily of Pope Leo IV, CXV, 629 ff.

LEO VI, pope, 939. Letter to the bishops of Dalmatia, CXXXII, 813.

LEO VII, pope, 939. Fifteen letters and privileges: for the monastery of Fulda; for the monastery of Subiaco; for the monastery of Cluny; to Gerard, archbishop of Lorch; to Hugh, king of the Franks and abbot of the monastery of St. Martin of Tours; for the monastery of Cluny; for the monastery of St. Benedict at Fleury; to Guy of Lyons; to the Gauls and Germans; etc., CXXXII, 1065.

LEO VIII, antipope, 965. Four privileges and constitutions: letter to Rodoald, patriarch of Aquileia; privilege concerning investitures; for the monastery of St. Peter of Montmajour; cession of the donations of the Roman Church, CXXXIV, 990.

LEO IX (St.), pope, 1054. 1. Short work on the Conflict of Vices and Virtues. 2. Address to Count Adelbert concerning the restoration of the monastery of Hirsau. 3. One hundred and eleven charters issued while he was still serving as bishop of Toul, CXLIII, 458.

LEO, bishop of Atina, 1062. 1. On the Discovery of the Body of Blessed Mark, martyr and pontiff. 2. Solemn donation made to the canons and clerics of the Church of Atina. 3. Sermon on the Passion of Blessed Mark. Sermon on the octave of St. Mark, bishop and martyr, CXLIII, 1416 ff.

LEO, abbot and legate, tenth century. Letter to Kings Hugh and Robert, CXXXIX, 338.

LEO OF MARSICA, monk of Monte Cassino and later cardinal-bishop of Ostia, 1138. Chronicle of the monastery of Monte Cassino, CLXXIII, 440.

LEO, king of the Armenians, 1205. Letter to Pope Innocent III concerning peace between himself and the Templars and certain other matters, CCXV, 687.

LEODEBOD, abbot of St. Aignan, 667. Charter for the monasteries of St. Aignan and St. Peter of Fleury, LXXXVIII, 1186.

LEODEGAR (St.), bishop of Autun, 678. 1. Letter of consolation to his mother at the convent of nuns at Soissons. 2. Several canons of synods held by St. Leodegar. 3. Testament of St. Leodegar, XCVI, 429.

LEODEGAR, archbishop of the Church of Vienne, 1044. Three charters: he grants the church of St. Ferreolus to St. Victor in full synod; gives the church of St. Symphorianus to the monastery of St. Ferreolus; concerning debased coinage at Vienne, CXLIII, 1404.

LEODEGAR, archbishop of Bourges, about 1125. Address on Blessed Robert of Arbrissel, CLXII, 1118.

LEODEGAR OF CLARIAC, 1128. Charters of *guirpilio* [renunciation] made by Leodegar of Clariac and others to Hugh, bishop of Grenoble, concerning all the land at Fabriis, CLXVI, 1572.

LEONTIUS, bishop of Naples in Cyprus, 620. Life of St. John the Almsgiver, LXXIII, 338.

LEONTIUS, bishop of Arles, 462. Letter to Pope Hilary asking him to protect the rights of the Church of Arles, LVIII, 22.

LEOTALD, count of Mâcon, tenth century. Donation made by Leotald to the monastery of Cluny, CXXXIII, 842.

LEOVIGILD, priest of Córdoba, date uncertain. Book on the Dress of Clerics, CXXI, 568.

LEPORIUS, monk and priest, 426. Booklet of amendment, or satisfaction, containing a confession of the Catholic faith concerning the mystery of Christ’s Incarnation, together with a repudiation of his former error, addressed to the bishops of Gaul, XXXI, 1216, 1222.

LETALD, Benedictine monk of Micy near Orléans, about 996. 1. Life of St. Julian, first bishop of Le Mans. 2. Book of the Miracles of St. Maximin, abbot of Micy. 3. Translation of the body of St. Junian to the Synod of Carrofes, CXXXVII, 782.

LEUTHERIC, archbishop of Sens, about 1027. Letter to the clergy of Paris, CXLI, 247.

LIBERATUS, deacon of Carthage, 556. Brief Account of the Case of the Nestorians and Eutychians, compiled by Liberatus, LXVIII, 964.

LIBERIUS, pope, 363. Eighteen letters: to Hosius, bishop of Córdoba, concerning the embassy and lapse of Vincent, bishop of Capua; to Eusebius, bishop of Vercelli, concerning the embassy of Lucifer, bishop of Cagliari, to Emperor Constantius …; to Eusebius, Dionysius, and Lucifer in exile; Dialogue of Liberius and Emperor Constantius, held three days before Liberius was carried into exile; to the Easterners; to Arsacius; to the Catholic bishops of Italy; to all the orthodox bishops of the East; to Athanasius and the bishops of Egypt; etc., VIII, 1332 ff.; X, 678 ff.

LIBERIUS, poet, date uncertain. Acrostic on Sedulius, XIX, 784.

LICINIA EUDOXIA, empress, 450. Letter to Theodosius concerning the disturbance of the Catholic Church, LIV, 861.

LICINIANUS, bishop of Carthage, 584. Three letters: to Pope Gregory, concerning his book of Rules, which he says he has read, and requesting from him his other moral works; [Col. 0613] to Epiphanius, deacon—a letter showing that angels and rational souls are spirits; to Vincent, bishop of the island of Ibiza, against those who believed that letters had fallen from heaven at Rome in memory of St. Peter, LXXII, 688.

LIETBERT (St.), bishop of Cambrai, 1076. Charter of Lietbert concerning the establishment of regular canons in the church of St. Autbert at Cambrai, CXLVI, 1448.

LIETBERT, abbot of St. Rufus, 1110. Two letters: to Ogerius, provost of the congregation of Ferranica, to whom he commends the canonical order; to a friend, dissuading clerics from frequent access to women, CLVII, 708.

LIETHARD, bishop of Soissons, 1119. Letters to Lambert, CLXII, 692.

LIODOALD OF BRESCIA, 761. Charter of Valerian and Liodoald, granting to Anselperga, abbess of the Brescian monastery of Saints Savior and Julia, the right to a channel for bringing water into that monastery, LXXXVII, 1390.

LISIARD, cleric of Tours, twelfth century. History of Jerusalem, CLXXIV, 1590.

LIUTAD, bishop of Vence, 868. Letter of Liutad, bishop of Vence, to Wenilo, archbishop of Rouen, concerning the deacon Wlfad, CXXIX, 1392.

LIUTPRAND, king of the Lombards, 743. 1. Decree establishing the dues to be paid by the people of Comacchio when bringing salt through the ports of Lombardy. 2. Decree by which he himself confirms in favor of the Church of Arezzo a dispute concerning certain parishes between the bishops of Arezzo and Luni, examined and settled by certain bishops and royal envoys. 3. Donation for the monastery of St. Evasius, LXXXVII, 1358, 1401, 1353.

LIUTPRAND, bishop of Cremona, 974. 1. History of the Deeds of Kings and Emperors, or *Antapodosis*, six books. 2. Book on the Deeds of Emperor Otto the Great. 3. Report on the Embassy to Constantinople. 4. Chronicle, CXXXVI, 769.

LIVINUS (St.), bishop of Metz and martyr, 654. Metrical letter to Florbert, abbot of Ghent, LXXXVII, 345.

LOMBARD. See PETER LOMBARD.

LONEGISIL, first abbot of Bussières, 625. Two charters for Hadoind, bishop of Le Mans, and his church, LXXX, 455, 458.

LONGINIANUS, pagan philosopher, about 427. Letter to St. Augustine, XXXIII, 1030.

LOTHAIR I, emperor, 816. Capitularies of Louis I and Lothair, XCVII, 371, 590 ff. Assembly of Lothair I at Ingelheim, CXXXVIII, 526. Assemblies of Lothair, Louis, and Charles at Marsna, ibid., 553, 575. Three letters, to Pope Nicholas and to Pope Adrian II, CXXI, 372 ff.

LOTHAIR II, king of France, 960. Charter concerning the Cluniac monastery of St. Amand, during the abbacy of Maiolus, CXXXVII, 779.

LOTHAIR III, emperor, 1133. 1. Judgment against Pope Anacletus. 2. Oath of Lothair, CLXXIX, 47, 50. 3. Letter to Pope Innocent II concerning the disputed election of the bishop of Halberstadt, ibid., 668. 4. Three charters granted to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1460 ff.

LUCIAN, confessor, 250. Letter to Celerinus concerning the lapsed, III, 674; IV, 279.

LUCIAN, priest near Jerusalem, date uncertain. Letter to the whole Church concerning the revelation of the body of St. Stephen, XLI, 807.

LUCIFER, bishop of Cagliari, 371. 1. Letter to Eusebius, bishop of Vercelli. 2. One book, To Emperor Constantius, on Not Associating with Heretics. 3. One book, To Emperor Constantius, on Apostate Kings. 4. Two books, To Emperor Constantius, for St. Athanasius. 5. Letter to Florentius. 6. One book, To Emperor Constantius, on Not Sparing Those Who Sin against God. 7. One book, To Emperor Constantius, that One Must Die for the Son of God, XIII, 692 ff. 8. The Faith of Lucifer, XIII, 1049.

LUCIUS (St.), pope and martyr, 253. Letter to the bishops of Gaul and Spain. Decrees of Pope Lucius taken from Gratian, III, 976.

LUCIUS, African bishop, 258. Letter to Cyprian, IV, 422.

LUCIUS II, pope, 1145. Ninety-five letters and privileges, CLXXIX, 820.

LUCIUS III, pope, 1185. Two hundred and fifty-two letters and privileges. Two decrees, CCI, 1068 ff.

LUCULENTUS, sixth century. Commentaries on certain portions of the New Testament, LXXII, 804.

LUDGER (St.), bishop of Mimigernaford, 809. 1. Life of St. Gregory, abbot and rector of the Church of Utrecht on the Rhine, XCIX, 750.

[Col. 0614] LOUIS I, emperor, 840. Capitularies, XCVII, 371. Pact of Emperor Louis I with Pope Paschal, XCVII, 679. Privilege of Emperor Louis concerning the regalia to be confirmed for Pope Paschal, XCVIII, 579. Charters for the monastery of St. Michael, CII, 975 ff. Precepts for the monastery of Aniane, CIII, 1421 ff. Ecclesiastical charters of Louis and his sons down to the division of the Empire, 840. Fifteen letters, CIV, 928 ff.

LOUIS II, emperor, 842. Pact of Strasbourg, CXXXVIII, 528. Chapter of Louis II, king of Italy, CXXXVIII, 545. Second Assembly of Pavia, ibid., 610. Third Assembly of Pavia, ibid., 618; constitutions, 622; ecclesiastical chapters, 624; constitution of Emperor Louis II concerning the dispatch of an army against Benevento, 726 ff.

LOUIS IV, king of France, 954. Precept of Louis, king of the Franks, concerning Salustrac, Chavigny, fishing in the Oise, Cambrai, Savigny, and Ambert, CXXXIII, 840.

LOUIS VI, king of the Franks, 1121. Letter to Calixtus, CLXIII, 1339. Eighteen letters to Abbot Suger, 1348 ff. Privileges granted to St. Denis, CLXXXVI, 1461. Two charters, CLXXXIX, 1060 ff.

LOUIS VII, king of France, 1180. Letters to Pope Alexander, to Thomas of Canterbury, to Emperor Manuel, to William, king of Sicily, CXC, 1055 ff.; to John of Salisbury, bishop-elect of Chartres, CXCIX, 374.

LUIDBERT, archbishop of Mainz, 889. Letter to King Louis, CXXIX, 1052.

LUL, 733. Letter to Abbess Kanebada, LXXXIX, 734.

LULLUS (St.), bishop of Mainz, 787. Eight letters, XCVI, 820 ff.

LUPUS (St.) OF TROYES, 479. Two letters: to Sidonius, concerning the character required of one made a priest; to Thalasius, bishop of Angers, concerning liturgical solemnities, bigamous clerics, and those admitted while married, LVIII, 62 ff.

LUPUS, Blessed Servatus, abbot of Ferrières, 862. 1. Letters of Blessed Lupus and others to him, CXXX. 2. Canons issued at the Council of Verneuil. 3. Book on Three Questions. 4. Collection on Three Questions. 5. Life of St. Maximin, bishop of Trier. 6. Life of St. Wigbert, abbot of Fritzlar. 7. Two homilies for the feast of St. Wigbert. 8. Two hymns for the feast of St. Wigbert, CXIX, 424.

LUPUS, Protospatharius, 1100. Chronicle from 860 to 1102, CLV, 120.

## M

MACARIUS (St.), Alexandrian abbot of Nitria, 390. Rule for monks, CIII, 446.

MACCABAEUS, king of the Scots, about 1050. Ecclesiastical laws, CLI, 1190.

MACEDONIUS, 414. Two letters to Augustine, XXXIII, 652, 665.

MACROBIUS, Donatist, about 340. Passion of the Donatists Maximian and Isaac, VIII, 767; on the passion of the Donatists Maximian and Isaac, addressed to the people of Carthage, VIII, 778.

MAGINGOZ, bishop, 755. Letters to Lullus, bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 824, 825, 840.

MASTER, unknown author, seventh century. Rule for monks, LXXXVIII, 944.

MAGNES, priest of Jerusalem, about 280. Fragment on the Eucharist, V, 344 ff.

MAGNUS, archbishop of Sens, 818. 1. Short work on the Mystery of Baptism, issued by command of Charlemagne. 2. Legal notes collected by Magnon, CII, 980.

MAIOLUS (St.), fourth abbot of Cluny, 994. Cartulary of St. Maiolus, CXXXVII, 780.

MAMERTINUS, consul, 362. Thanksgiving for his consulship, addressed to Julian Augustus, XVIII, 408.

MAMERTUS CLAUDIANUS, priest of Vienne, 470. 1. Three books on the State of the Soul. 2. Two letters, to Sidonius and to the rhetorician Sapaudus. 3. Hymn on the Passion of the Lord. 4. Poems of doubtful authorship: Against Vain Poets; Easter Poem; Praise of Christ; Miracles of Christ, LIII, 693.

MANASSES, archdeacon and subsequently archbishop of Reims, 1119. Letters to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 650, 652, 653, 654, 655, 660, 663, 666, 668, 669 ff.

MANASSES, bishop of Orléans, 1148. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1352.

MANEGALD, priest, 1100. 1. Short work against Wolfelm of Cologne, CLV, 148. 2. Letter [Col. 0615] to Abbot Wibald concerning knowledge of the liberal arts, CLXXXIX, 1248.

MANIGUNDIS, Lombard woman, 768. Testament of Manigundis for the establishment of a convent at Cairate, LXXXVII, 1397.

MANSUETUS (St.), bishop of Milan, 680. Letter to Emperor Constantine, LXXXVII, 1276.

MANTIO, bishop of Châlons, 902. Letter to Fulk, bishop of Reims, CXXXI, 24.

MANUEL, emperor, 1154. Letter to Abbot Wibald concerning the marriage of Emperor Frederick, CLXXXIX, 1438.

MAPPINIUS, bishop of Rheims, 550. Two letters: to St. Nicetius, bishop of Trier, concerning the Council of Toul held in 549; to Villicus, bishop of Metz, concerning the purchase of pigs, LXVIII, 44.

MARBOD, bishop of Rennes, 1128. 1. Six letters: to Rainald, bishop of Angers; to Ingilger, a solitary, that the unworthiness of a minister does not prevent the truth of the sacrament; to the priest Ingunger, concerning evil priests; to Vitalis concerning the admission of a girl into a monastery; etc. 2. Book on Three Enemies: On Women, On Avarice, On Ambition. 3. Life of St. Licinius, bishop of Angers. 4. Life of St. Robert, abbot of La Chaise-Dieu. 5. Life of St. Magnobodus, bishop of Angers. 6. Life of St. Walter, or Gautier, abbot and canon of Stirpensis in the Limousin diocese of Gaul. 7. Sermon on the Life of St. Florentius, priest and confessor, at Mont-Glonne in Gaul. 8. Metrical Life of Theophilus. Poems on the Seven Maccabean Brothers. 10. Verses on St. Lawrence. 11. Passion of St. Victor, martyr. 12. Passion of St. Maurice and his companions. 13. Life of St. Thaïs. 14. Passion of the holy martyrs Felix and Adauctus. 15. Life of Blessed Maurilius, bishop and confessor. 16. Sixty miscellaneous poems. 17. Book on the Ornaments of Speech. 18. Book of Ten Chapters. 19. Forty-five miscellaneous poems. 20. Book on Gems. 21. Three charters, CLXXI, 1458 ff.

MARCELLINUS (St.), pope, 304. Two letters: to Bishop Solomon; to the Eastern bishops, that it is not lawful for a layperson to accuse a cleric, VII, 1085; VI, 9 ff.

MARCELLINUS, priest, 384. 1. Book on the Trinity, or on Faith, against the Arians. 2. Petition addressed to Emperors Valentinian, Theodosius, and Arcadius against Damasus, XIII, 30.

MARCELLINUS, tribune and notary, 411. His statements at the Conference of Carthage, XI, 1259 ff.

MARCELLINUS, count, 567. Chronicle from 379 to 566, LI, 914 ff.; LXV, 975.

MARCELLUS (St.), pope, 310. 1. Two letters: to the bishops of the province of Antioch concerning the primacy and authority of the Roman Church; to the tyrant Maxentius, that he cease raging against Christians. 2. Decree concerning those relegated, VII, 1092; VI, 20 ff.

MARCELLUS, bishop of Ancyra, 342. Letter to Pope Julius I concerning the faith of the Arians and his own faith, VIII, 916.

MARCELLUS, bishop of Memorialis, about 411. Preface to the Acts of the Conference of Carthage, XI, 1232.

MARCIAN, African bishop, about 311. Judgment of Marcian at the Council of Carthage, VIII, 746.

MARCIAN, emperor, 457. Three letters to Pope Leo I: concerning the holding of a council; rejoicing that the faith confirmed at Chalcedon and peace in the Church have been restored; requesting from the pontiff, as necessary, confirmation of the Council of Chalcedon, LIV, 903, 970, 1017.

MARCULF, monk, 660. Two books of formularies: on royal charters and on local charters, LXXXVII, 692 ff.

MARC (St.), pope, 334. 1. Decree attributed to him, concerning the bishop of Ostia’s use of the pallium. 2. Rescript of Pope Mark to Athanasius and all the bishops of Egypt concerning the chapters of the Council of Nicaea, VIII, 850 ff.

MARC, disciple of St. Benedict at Monte Cassino, 612. Poem on St. Benedict, LXXX, 184.

MARC, bishop of Otranto, eighth century. Hymn for Holy Saturday, XCVI, 1346.

MARCUS VALERIUS PROBUS. See VALERIUS.

MARGARET, countess of Burgundy, 1200. Donation for the abbey of Balerne, CLXXXV, 1458.

MARIANUS, priest and archimandrite, 536. Petition of monks presented to Pope Agapetus against Anthimus, Severus, etc., LXVI, 50.

MARIANUS SCOTUS, about 1080. Chronicle from the year of the Incarnation 1 to the year 1104, CXLVII, 601.

MARINUS I, pope, 884. Two privileges, for the monastery of Solignac and for the monastery of Savigny; letter to the monks of St. Giles, CXXVI, 966 ff.

MARINUS II, pope, 946. Seven letters and privileges: for the monastery of Vézelay; for the monastery of St. Boniface at Fulda; for the church of Benevento; for Monte Cassino; [Col. 0616] for the monastery of St. Vincent on the Volturno; for the church of Sabina; etc., CXXXIII, 864.

MARIUS VICTORINUS, African rhetorician, 372. 1. Book to Justinus the Manichaean against the two principles of the Manichaeans and on the true flesh of Christ. 2. On the words of Scripture: “And there was evening and there was morning, one day.” 3. Book on the Generation of the Divine Word, addressed to Candidus the Arian. 4. Four books Against Arius. 5. Hymns on the Trinity. 6. Commentaries on the Epistles of Paul: to the Galatians, Philippians, and Ephesians. 7. Book on Physical Matters, VIII, 994, 1000 ff.

MARIUS VICTOR, or VICTORINUS. See VICTOR.

MARIUS, bishop of Avenches, 795. Chronicle, from 455 to about 580; consuls rather than years are indicated, LXXII, 792.

LEO OF MARSICA. See LEO.

MARTINIAN, monk, 906. Prologue to the Moral Books, CXXXI, 24 ff.

MARTIN (St.), bishop of Tours, 399. Confession of the threefold unity and the one Trinity, XVIII, 9 ff.

MARTIN (St.), bishop of Dume in Braga, 572. 1. Formula of an Honorable Life, addressed to Miro, king of Galicia. 2. Short work on Morals. 3. Short work for Repelling Boastfulness. 4. Short work on Pride. 5. Exhortation to Humility. 6. Short work on Anger. 7. Short work on Easter. 8. Various verses, LXXII, 18 ff.

MARTIN (St.), pope, 649. 1. Seventeen letters: encyclical to all Christ’s faithful concerning the two natures and wills in Christ; to Amandus, bishop of Maastricht, that he not resign the episcopate; etc.; to Emperor Constans concerning the heresy of the Monothelites; to the Church of Carthage concerning the Monothelites; to John, bishop of Philadelphia, concerning the election of Macedonius and Peter made by heretics; to Theodore, bishop of Esbous, that he obey John, bishop of Philadelphia; to Antony, bishop of Bacatha, that he obey the bishop of Philadelphia; to George, archimandrite of the monastery of St. Theodosius, that he obey the bishop of Philadelphia; to Pantaleon; to Peter, an illustrious man, that he support his vicar; to the Churches of Jerusalem and Antioch concerning the Monothelites; to the Church of Thessalonica concerning Paul’s condemnation; etc. 2. Three privileges: for the monastery of Rebais; for the monastery of Blandin; for the monastery of Elnone, LXXXVII, 106 ff.

MARTIN (St.), priest of León, 1201. 1. Book of thirty-four sermons for the temporal cycle and feasts of the year, nine sermons on saints, and eleven sermons on miscellaneous subjects. 2. Exposition of the Epistle of Blessed James. 3. Exposition of the First Epistle of Blessed Peter the Apostle. 4. Exposition of the First Epistle of Blessed John. 5. Exposition of the Book of Revelation, CCVIII–CCIX.

MATERNUS JULIUS FIRMICUS, 353. On the Error of Profane Religions, XII, 972 ff.

MATHILDA (St.), queen, 968. Unpublished letter of Mathilda of Swabia, sister of Empress Gisela and grandmother of Mathilda of Tuscany, to Mieszko II, king of Poland, CLI, 1328; CXXXV, 885.

MATHILDA, countess, 1115. Charter of Countess Mathilda concerning her grant of her possessions to the Roman Church, CXLVIII, 1036; CLVII, 1294; XCVIII, 632, 660.

MATHILDA, queen of the English, 1118. Two letters to Anselm of Canterbury, CLIX, 239, 240. Letter to Pope Paschal, thanking him for the exhortatory letters sent to her husband, CLXIII, 466.

MATHILDA, empress, 1170. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 1054.

MATHILDA, countess of Grignon, 1196. Donations for the church of Fontenay, CLXXXV, 1470, 1471.

MATTHEW, cardinal-bishop of Albano, 1139. Seven letters and charters: concerning the agreement between Henry, archbishop of Sens, and the canons of Étampes; concerning the settlement made between Stephen, bishop of Paris, and Theobald, archdeacon; concerning the election of Odo, abbot of St. Peter of Chartres; concerning the monastery of Argenteuil restored to the abbey of St. Denis; for the church of St. Martin-des-Champs; etc., CLXXIII, 1262.

MATTHEW, duke of Lorraine, 1142. Privilege for the monastery of Tart, CLXXXV, 1411.

MATTHEW, bishop of Troyes, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Alexander III on behalf of St Thomas of Canterbury, CC, 1422.

MATTHEW, treasurer of Sens, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Alexander III, in support of Thomas of Canterbury against King Henry, CC, 1434.

MATTHEW of Vendôme, c. 1200. 1. A metrical paraphrase of the Book of Tobit, about 2,300 verses. 2. Miscellaneous poems: a eulogy of the pope, a eulogy of a knight, a satire upon a fool, a description of the times, a description of a place, CCV, 926.

[Col. 0617] MAURICE of SULLY, bishop of Paris, 1196. 1. Letters to Pope Alexander III in the cause of St Thomas of Canterbury, CCV, 898; CC, 1419. 2. Fifteen charters: concerning a tithe at Campellis; concerning what the knight Ledemallus sold near the village of Saint-Cloud; concerning what William of Macy sold near Saint-Victor; concerning the foundation of Hérivaux; concerning various sales; etc., CCV, 888.

BLESSED MAURILIUS, archbishop of Rouen, 1067. 1. Letter to the bishop of Évreux, because, without consulting the abbot, he had fined a monk for breaking the truce. 2. Profession of faith concerning the sacrament of Christ’s body and blood. 3. Epitaphs of Rollo and William Longsword, dukes of Normandy, CXLIII, 1376 ff.

MAURUS, archbishop of Ravenna, 648. A single letter to Pope Martin of Rome against the heresy of the Monothelites, LXXXVII, 104.

MAURUS, abbot of the Temple of the Lord, twelfth century. Concerning the obedience which he rendered to the church of the Holy Sepulchre, CLV, 1113.

MAXENTIUS, patriarch of Aquileia, 840. 1. Letter to Emperor Charlemagne on the meaning of the rites of baptism. 2. Collection concerning ancient baptismal rites, CVI, 50.

MAXIMUS, African confessor, 250. Letters to Cyprian concerning the lapsed, IV, 290, 342; III, 675.

MAXIMUS, emperor, 385. Two letters: to Pope Siricius, concerning the crimes of the Manichaeans or Priscillianists and the Catholic faith which he promises to defend; to the Emperor Valentinian, urging him to refrain from inflicting violence upon churches and priests, XIII, 590 ff.

MAXIMUS, grammarian of Madaura in Africa, 399. Letter to St Augustine: he excuses the pagans for worshipping one God under various names, and rebukes Christians because they venerated the tombs of martyrs, XXXIII, 81; XVIII, 406.

ST MAXIMUS of Turin, 466. 1. One hundred and eighteen homilies: fifty-three for the liturgical seasons, nineteen for saints, and thirty-six on various subjects. 2. One hundred and sixteen sermons: fifty-five for the seasons, thirty-eight for saints, and twenty-three on various subjects. 3. Six treatises: on baptism, against pagans, and against Jews. Expositions on passages from the Gospels, LVII, 9 ff. Thirty-one doubtful and spurious sermons, three homilies, and two letters, LVII, 844 ff.

MAXIMUS, bishop of Saragossa, 644. 1. Letter to Argebatus, bishop of Portugal, concerning his Chronicle. 2. Chronicle from the year 430 to the year 644, LXXX, 610, 618.
