ST MAXIMUS, confessor and monk of Constantinople, 662. 1. Extract from St Maximus’s letter to the priest Marinus, which, among other matters, offers a defence of Honorius, LXXX, 483; CXXIX, 568. 2. Extract from St Maximus’s letter to the illustrious Peter, concerning Pyrrhus, St Sophronius, bishop of Jerusalem, and Pope Honorius, LXXX, 483; CXXIX, 574. 3. Extract from St Maximus’s letter to the priest Marinus, concerning the procession of the Holy Spirit, CXXIX, 578. 4. Account, taken from St Maximus’s letter to Abbot Thalassius, of what the Roman legates did at Constantinople, CXXIX, 584. 5. The *Ambigua* of St Maximus, CXXII, 1194 ff.

MEFFRID, prior at Eberbach, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 259.

MEGINFRED, master and provost of Magdeburg, c. 1033. One book on the life of Blessed Emmeram, CXLI, 970.

MEGINHARD, 845. Donations for the church of St Saviour in the district of Riporum, XCIX, 809.

ST MELCHIADES, pope, 313. Letter to all the bishops of Spain concerning episcopal judgments, the greater sacrament, fasting on Sunday and Thursday, VII, 1115; VI, 30 ff.

MEROBAUDES, scholar, 427. Poem concerning Christ, LXI, 971.

MARIUS MERCATOR, 456. 1. Writings concerning the Pelagian—or rather the Caelestian—heresy: a memorandum under the name of Caelestius; a book of annotations upon the words of Julian; translations of various treatises written in Greek in the Pelagian controversy. 2. Writings concerning the Nestorian heresy: Marius Mercator’s preface to various sermons of the impious Nestorius on the Incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ; translation of thirteen sermons of Nestorius; four collections of extracts from Nestorius, translated by Marius Mercator; twelve chapters of Nestorius’s blasphemies, with Marius Mercator’s refutations; the apologetic work of St Cyril, bishop of Alexandria, for the twelve chapters against the Eastern bishops, translated by Marius Mercator; St Cyril, bishop of Alexandria’s apology against Theodoret, translated by Marius Mercator; translation of the scholia of St Cyril, bishop of Alexandria, on the Incarnation of the Only-begotten; extracts made by Marius Mercator from the books of Theodore of Mopsuestia, [Col. 0618] Theodoret, bishop of Cyrrhus, and Eutherius, bishop of Tyana, of the Nestorian party, XLVIII, 62 ff.

MESSIANUS, priest of Arles, 545. On the life of St Caesarius, bishop of Arles, LXVII, 1025.

MICHAEL, dean of Paris, 1191. Authentic instrument of the chapter of Paris concerning the bishop’s procuration in the church of St Exuperius at Corbeil, CCV, 913.

MELISENDE, queen of Jerusalem, 1152. Privilege concerning the exchange of John the Patrician, CLV, 1137.

MILO, monk of Saint-Amand, 872. 1. Metrical life of St Amand, about 2,000 verses. 2. Sermon on the translation of St Amand. 3. Poem on the conflict of spring and winter. 4. Epitaph of Pippin and Drogo, sons of Charles the Bald, who, having been entrusted to Milo for their education, died while still boys, CXXI, 925 ff.

MILO, cardinal and monk of St Albinus of Angers, date unknown. Metrical praise of Pope Paschal II, CLXIII, 28.

MILO, count of Bar, 1145. Foundation records of the nunnery of Jully, CLXXXV, 1408.

MILO, bishop of Thérouanne, c. 1160. Letter to Pope Alexander III against Gilbert, bishop of London, CC, 1416.

MILO, master, 1209. Letter to Pope Innocent III concerning the affair of the faith in Provence, CCXVI, 124.

MILRED, bishop, c. 756. Letter to St Lull, bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 834.

MINUCIUS FELIX (III), third century. *Octavius*, or a dialogue between a pagan and a Christian, III, 232 ff.

MONTANUS, bishop of Toledo, 527. Two letters to the priests of the territory of Palencia, whom he rebukes because they prepared the holy chrism, foreign bishops were admitted to the consecration of basilicas, and because some held the sect of the Priscillianists in honour; letter to Thuribius, whom he praises for his preaching against idolatry, LXV, 48.

JOHN MOSCHUS, Greek author, sixth century. Book X on the lives of the Fathers, or the *Spiritual Meadow of the Fathers*, LXXIV, 120.

MOSES, confessor of the African Church, 250. Letter to Cyprian, with the Roman confessors, concerning the consolations received from his letters, the lapsed, etc., IV, 290.

MUNIO, bishop of Mondoñedo, 1134. *Compostelan History*, three books, from 920 to 1139, CLXX, 876 ff.

## N

NALGOD, monk of Cluny, twelfth century. Life of St Odo, abbot of Cluny, CXXXIII, 85.

NANTHELM, bishop of Belley, 1164. Proof concerning a donation made to the brethren of Majeurev, CLIII, 935.

NAZARIUS, rhetorician, 321. Panegyric delivered to Constantine Augustus, VIII, 582.

NEBRIDIUS, c. 395. Two letters to St Augustine, XXXIII, 67.

NECTARIUS, pagan, c. 400. Two letters to St Augustine, requesting mercy for the citizens of Calama, who had injured Christians and violated the emperor’s most recent edict forbidding the celebration of sacred rites to idols, XXXIII, 313, 380.

NEMESIANUS, third century. Reply to Cyprian: he thanks him for literary consolation and for aid sent, etc., IV, 420.

NESTORIUS, patriarch of Constantinople, 439. 1. Thirteen sermons on the Incarnation of Our Lord Jesus Christ, translated from Greek, XLVIII, 757. 2. Three letters to Pope Celestine, XLVIII, 841 ff.; L, 438, 442, 499.

NICEPHORUS, bishop of Constantinople, 828. Chronology, CXXIX, 511.

ST NICETAS, bishop of Aquileia, 458. 1. On the rule of faith. 2. On the power of the Holy Spirit. 3. On the various names appropriate to Our Lord Jesus Christ. 4. Explanation of the Creed delivered to candidates for baptism. 5. Six fragments, LII, 838.

NICETAS, priest and monk of the monastery of Stoudios, eleventh century. Treatise against the Latins, found at Constantinople by the representatives of the Apostolic See, CXLIII, 973.

ST NICETIUS, bishop of Trier, 551. 1. Treatise on the vigils of God’s servants. 2. On the benefit of psalmody. 3. Two letters: to Chlodoswintha, queen of the Lombards, concerning her husband Alboin and the maintenance of faith in the true God; to the Emperor Justinian, recalling him from error after he had fallen into heresy, LXVIII, 361 ff.; LXXI, 1166.

POPE NICHOLAS I, 867. One hundred and fifty-nine letters and decrees, arranged chronologically: to the Emperor Michael; to Photius; to King Charles; to King Lothair; to Emperor Louis II; to the bishops of Gaul and Germany concerning the church of Beauvais; to Hincmar, archbishop of Reims; to all bishops and princes of Gaul; to Queen Ermentrude; to the bishops or archbishops of Sens, [Col. 0619] Metz, Bourges, Tongeren, Reims, etc., CXIX, 753.

POPE NICHOLAS II, 1061. Forty letters and charters: for the monastery of St Peter at Perugia; for the monastery of St Vincent at the Vulturnus; for Monte Cassino; for the establishment of the chapter of the Blessed Virgin Mary *ad Gradus* at Cologne; to the bishops of Gaul, Aquitaine, and Gascony; to Cervasius, archbishop of Reims; to Lanfranc; for the monastery of Saint-Denis; etc., CXLIII, 1300.

NICHOLAS, prior of Worcester monastery, 1120. Letter to Eadmer concerning the primacy of the see of York in Scotland, CLIX, 810.

NICHOLAS, canon of Liège, 1140. Eulogy of Alger, scholastic of Liège, CLXXX, 737.

NICHOLAS, counsellor of the Roman curia, 1150. Letter to Emperor Conrad, CLXXXIX, 1303.

NICHOLAS, abbot of Corbie, c. 1150. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1416.

NICHOLAS of Mont-Rouen, c. 1170. Four letters to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 679 ff.

NICHOLAS, monk of Clairvaux, c. 1175. 1. Sermons on the Nativity of the Lord, CLXXXIV, 828; sermon on the feast of St Andrew, CLXXXIV, 1049; sermon on the feast of Blessed Mary Magdalene, CLXXXV, 214; CXCVI, 1654. 2. Letters of Nicholas and of others to him, LVII: to the brothers Gerard and Henry; to Atto, bishop of Troyes; to Peter, dean of Troyes; to the priors and elders of Clairvaux concerning his reception; to Peter, abbot of La Celle; to Henry, bishop of Troyes; to Amadeus, bishop of Lausanne; to Henry, count of Champagne; etc., CXCVI, 1589; CLXXXII, 671; CLXXXIII, 26.

NICHOLAS, abbot of Heilsbronn, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, from whom he requests letters of consolation, CXCVII, 291.

NICHOLAS, monk of St Albans, c. 1187. Letter to Peter of La Celle, CCII, 622.

NICHOLAS of Amiens, c. 1203. Supplement to the chronicle of Sigebert of Gembloux, CLX, 409.

NICOSTRATUS, confessor, 250. Letter to Cyprian, IV, 290; III, 674.

NIGELLUS. See ERMOLDUS.

NITHARD, abbot of St Riquier, 853. Four books on the dissensions of the sons of Louis the Pious, down to the year 843, addressed to Charles the Bald, king of the Franks, CXVI, 36.

NIVARD, bishop of Reims, c. 662. Fragment of a charter for the monastery of Hautvillers, LXXXVIII, 1181.

NIVELO, bishop of Soissons, c. 1200. Letter to the bishop of Tournai, to whom he most willingly grants the requested authorization, CCXI, 473.

NIZEZIUS, 680. Charter by which Nizezius and his wife Ermintrude convey numerous properties to the monastery of Moissac by right of sale, LXXXVIII, 1202.

ST NORBERT, founder of the Premonstratensian Order and archbishop of Magdeburg, 1134. 1. Two sermons to the people. 2. Three charters: for the church of St Mary at Magdeburg; for the Premonstratensian brethren; donation of a hospital house for the benefit of hospitality to the poor, CLXX, 1357.

NOTGER, bishop of Liège, 1008. 1. Life of St Hadelin, confessor and founder of the monastery of Celles near Dinant on the Meuse. 2. Preface to the life of St Landuald. 3. Life of St Remaclus, bishop of Maastricht, CXXXIX, 1136.

BLESSED NOTKER BALBULUS, monk of St Gall, 911. 1. Book on interpreters of the divine Scriptures. 2. Book of sequences. 3. Poems of Blessed Notker. 4. Martyrology through the course of the year. 5. Letter to Ruodpert, in which he clears himself of the charge of detraction. 6. Formulae, or various conveyances. 7. On music, CXXXI, 984; LXXXVII, 40 ff.

NOVATIAN, Roman priest, c. 250–270. 1. Book on the Trinity. 2. Letter on Jewish foods; letter written in the name of the Roman clergy to St Cyprian, III, 862, 885 ff.

NOVATUS, Catholic, date unknown. Novatus’s saying on humility and obedience and on trampling down pride, XVIII, 68.

NUMERIANUS, archbishop, 667. Charter for a monastery within the place called Galilee, LXXXVIII, 1191.

## O

OCEANUS, 417. Several letters, XX, 457; XXII, 743.

ODALRIC, archbishop of Reims, 963. Judgment against sacrilegious thieves, CXXXIII, 964.

ODALRIC, provost of Reims, c. 1100. Testament of Odalric, CL, 1546.

ODDO, abbot of St Remigius at Reims, 1136. 1. Letter to Count Thomas concerning a certain miracle of St Thomas [Col. 0620] the Apostle. 2. Charter concerning the foundation of the Charterhouse of Mont-Dieu in the diocese of Reims, CLXXII, 1332.

ODDO, Benedictine monk of Asti, 1125. Exposition of the Psalms composed contemplatively, addressed to Bruno, bishop of Segni, CLXV, 1141.

ODILO, monk of St Medard at Soissons, 920. 1. Book on the translation of the relics of St Sebastian, martyr, and Pope Gregory to the monastery of St Medard at Soissons. 2. Letter to Hucbald, monk of St Amand. 3. Three sermons on St Medard, CXXXII, 576.

ST ODILO, fifth abbot of Cluny, 1049. 1. Four letters: to Fulbert, bishop of Chartres; to Abbot Paternus; to Lord Garsea; to Lady B. 2. Short work on the life of Blessed Abbot Maiolus. 3. Four hymns for the vigil of Blessed Maiolus. 4. Epitaph of Empress Adelaide. 5. Fourteen sermons: on the Nativity of the Lord, Epiphany, Purification of Blessed Mary, Resurrection of the Lord, Ascension of the Lord, Day of Pentecost, etc. 6. The *Credulity* of St Odilo. 7. Sacred poems and prayers. 8. Statute of St Odilo concerning the dead, CXLII, 832.

ODILUS of Le Mans, 721. Charter acknowledging rents from the district of Arduno payable to Herlemand, bishop of Le Mans, LXXXVIII, 1276.

ODO, abbot, date unknown. Life of St Gregory, bishop of Tours, LXXI, 116.

ODO, bishop of Beauvais, 880. 1. Sermon on St Lucian. 2. Canons of Odo issued at the synod of Ponthion. 3. Odo’s ordinance concerning the goods assigned to the congregation of St Peter and concerning the number of fifty canons therein, CXXIV, 1109.

ST ODO, abbot of Cluny, 942. 1. Thirty-five books of *Moralia on Job*. 2. Twelve antiphons on Blessed Martin. 3. Four hymns: on the sacrament of the Lord’s body and blood; on Blessed Mary Magdalene; on St Martin, archbishop of Tours. 4. Three books of *Conferences*. 5. Four books on the life of St Gerald, count of Aurillac. 6. Life of St Gregory, bishop of Tours. 7. Five sermons: on the Chair of St Peter; in veneration of St Mary Magdalene; on St Benedict the abbot; on the burning of the basilica of St Martin; on the feast of St Martin. 8. Short works on music, CXXXIII, 9 ff.

ST ODO, archbishop of Canterbury, 861. 1. Letter appended to the life of Wilfrid, archbishop of York. 2. Constitutions. 3. Synodal letter to his suffragan bishops, CXXXIII, 932 ff.

ODO, deacon of Auch, 983. Letter to Garcia, archbishop of Auch, concerning the church of St Venuntia, which Count William of Astarac gave to the church of Auch, CXXXVII, 312.

ODO, count, 1024. Letter to King Robert, CXLI, 938.

ODO, monk of Saint-Maur-des-Fossés, 1058. Life of Count Burchard, who flourished under King Hugh Capet and his son Robert, CXLIII, 846.

ODO, bishop of Bayeux, 1096. Charter by which he grants the monastery of St Vigor at Bayeux to Jarento, abbot of St Benignus at Dijon, CLV, 476.

BLESSED ODO, bishop of Cambrai, 1113. 1. Exposition of the Canon of the Mass. 2. Three books on original sin. 3. Disputation against a Jew named Leo concerning the coming of Christ, the Son of God. 4. On blasphemy against the Holy Spirit. 5. On the Gospel canons. 6. Homily on the steward of unrighteousness. 7. Eight charters of Blessed Odo, CLX, 1040 ff.

ODO, abbot of Morimond, 1156. Five sermons: for the first Sunday of Advent; on the Nativity of the Lord; on Septuagesima Sunday; on the three births and the same number of virtues of Blessed John and of the Lord the Saviour; on the feast of St Benedict, CLXXXVIII, 1644.

ODO, prior of St Victor and afterwards abbot of St Geneviève at Paris, 1166. Five letters on duly observing the canonical profession, CXCVI, 1398 ff.

ODO OF DEUIL, abbot of Saint-Denis, 1168. Work in seven books on the journey to the East of Louis VII, king of the Franks, surnamed the Younger, in which he himself took part, CXCV, 992; CLXXXV, 1201.

ODO, cardinal and legate of the Apostolic See, twelfth century. Letter to Ervisius, abbot of St Victor, commending to him a maidservant and affairs entrusted to him, CXCVI, 1388.

ODO, bishop of Toul, 1198. Synodal statutes issued in 1192, CCV, 916.

ODO, prior of Canterbury, twelfth century. Two letters to Pope Alexander III, CC, 1396, 1464; CXC, 1003.

ODO of Champagne, 1202. Donation to the church of St Stephen at Besançon, CLXXXV, 1459.

ODO, duke of Burgundy, 1206. Letter to Pope Lucius III [Col. 0621] concerning Henry, the younger king of England, who chose burial in the church at Rouen, CCI, 1378.

ODO OF SULLY, bishop of Paris, 1208. 1. Synodal constitutions. 2. Twenty-six statutes and pious donations: for the church of St Victor at Paris; for abolishing the Feast of Fools; concerning the solemnity of the Circumcision of the Lord and St Stephen; concerning the settlement of the boundaries between the dioceses of Beauvais and Paris; for instituting the feast of St Bernard in the church of Paris; etc. 3. Account of a remarkable miracle, wrought through the merits of Blessed Geneviève in the time of Odo, bishop of Paris, during the flooding of the Seine, which threatened the city of Paris with destruction, CCXII, 48 ff.

ODORANNUS, monk of Saint-Pierre-le-Vif at Sens, 1048. 1. Chronicle from the year of the Lord 675 to 1032. 2. History of the translation of the holy martyrs Savinian, Potentian, and their companions to the monastery of St Peter at Sens. 3. Thirteen short works. 4. Hymn to St Savinian and his companions. 5. Epitaphs of Sens collected by Odorannus, CXLII, 766.

OFFA, king of the Anglo-Saxons, 709. Donation of lands in which the Blessed Virgin Mary is said to have appeared to Bishop Egwin, LXXXIX, 536.

OGERIUS, abbot of Lucedio in the diocese of Vercelli, 1149. Fifteen sermons on the Lord’s discourse to the disciples at the Last Supper, CLXXXIV, 880; CLXXX, 1658.

ST OLLEGARIUS, archbishop of Tarragona, 1137. 1. Two letters: to Pope Innocent II; to Raymond, bishop of Vic and his suffragan, concerning a boy who, while playing, injured another so that his head was fractured, and whether he should be considered irregular. 2. Charter by which he gives beds and the garments of deceased clerics to the poor, CLXXII, 1358.

OLIVA, bishop of Vic or Ausona, 1047. 1. Sermon on the feast of St Narcissus, bishop, confessor, and martyr of Christ. 2. Conversion of Blessed Afra in the province of Raetia, at the city of Augsburg. 3. Three letters: to Gaucelin, archbishop of Bourges; to the monks of Ripoll; to Sancho, king of Navarre. 4. Consecration of the church of Vic. 5. Synodal decree of the Council of Narbonne against invaders of sacred property, held under Oliva, bishop of Ausona, CXLII, 590.

ONUPHRIUS PANVINUS, date unknown. Life of Pope St Gregory VII, CXLVIII, 150.

OODHELM, 799. Conveyance to Withmund, XCIX, 798.

OPTATIANUS PORPHYRIUS, fourth century. 1. Panegyric delivered to Constantine Augustus, whose verses form various figures, such as an altar, a hydraulic organ, etc., XIX, 396. 2. Letter to Constantine, ibid., 392.

OPTATUS, bishop of Milevis, 374. Seven books on the schism of the Donatists against Parmenian, XI, 884.

ORDERIC VITALIS, English-born monk of the monastery of Saint-Évroult, 1147. *Ecclesiastical History*, divided into three parts. In the first part, events from the Incarnation of the Saviour to 1140 are briefly described in the succession of emperors, kings, and Roman pontiffs. In the second, the military achievements of the Normans in France, England, and Apulia; the foundations of monasteries; the succession and deeds of the bishops and abbots of almost all Neustria; and many other memorable matters are set forth in detail under Duke William II. In the third, much is related concerning the death of King William and his three sons; and the journey to Jerusalem and the various events that occurred in those times are added, CLXXXVIII, 17 ff.

ST ORIENTIUS, bishop of Auch, 450. *Commonitorium*, or two books on the means of attaining eternal life, about 900 verses, LXI, 973.

ORIGEN, priest of Alexandria, 253. 1. St Jerome’s translation of nine homilies of Origen Adamantius on the visions of Isaiah, XXIV, 901. 2. St Jerome’s translation, addressed to the priest Vincentius, of Origen’s homilies on Jeremiah and Ezekiel, XXV, 584. 3. St Jerome’s translation, addressed to Paula and Eustochium, of thirty-nine homilies of Origen on the Gospel of Luke, XXVI, 219.

PAULUS OROSIUS, Spanish priest, fifth century. 1. Seven books of *Histories*, from the origin of the world to his own time, a work dedicated to Aurelius Augustine. 2. *Apologetic Book against Pelagius on Freedom of the Will*. 3. Orosius’s consultation, or memorandum, to Augustine concerning the error of the Priscillianists and Origenists, XXXI, 635, 664; XLVIII, 566; XLII, 665.

ST ORSIESIUS, abbot of Tabennesi, 365. Teaching on the formation of monks, CIII, 452.

OSBERN, monk and precentor of the Church of Canterbury, 1085. 1. Life of St Dunstan, archbishop of Canterbury. 2. Life of St Ælfheah, archbishop of Canterbury and martyr. 3. Translation of the same St Ælfheah, CXLIX, [Col. 0622] 368. 4. Life of St Odo, archbishop of Canterbury, CXXXIII, 932.

OSIUS, bishop of Cordoba, 357. 1. Canons of Hosius and of the holy Fathers assembled at the Synod of Sardica. 2. Letter to Constantius Augustus, VIII, 1310.

OSMUND, bishop of Astorga, 1057. Letter to Blessed Ida, countess of Boulogne and mother of King Godfrey, CLV, 460.

OTHELBOLD, abbot of the monastery of St Bavo at Ghent, 1040. Letter to Otgiva, countess of Flanders, enumerating the saints and possessions of the monastery of St Bavo, CXLI, 1338.

OTLOH, priest and monk of the monastery of St Emmeram at Regensburg, 1073. 1. Short work on his temptations, changing fortunes, and writings. 2. Dialogue on three questions: recognition of divine mercy, the diversity of divine judgments, and the varied capacity for doing good. 3. Letter on the causes of God’s permitting good and evil. 4. Book on the spiritual course. 5. Otloh’s account of a miracle which recently happened to a certain layman. 6. Manual, a short work of admonition for clerics and laypeople. 7. Metrical book on spiritual teaching, together with poems of various kinds, about 1,700 verses. 8. Book of Proverbs. 9. Sermon on the feast of the Apostles. 10. Book of Visions. 11. Fragment of an account of the translation of St Dionysius from France to Germany, to the monastery of St Emmeram. 12. Life of St Wolfgang, bishop of Regensburg. 13. Life of St Boniface, bishop of Mainz. 14. Prayer in German, CXLVI, 9, 27 ff.; LXXXIX, 634.

OTKER, monk of Regensburg, date unknown. Measure of the Quadripartite Figure, CLI, 692.

OTTO I THE GREAT, 948. Ecclesiastical constitutions, CXXXVIII, 821, 841, 849; CXXXVI, 600.

OTTO II, emperor, 983. Ecclesiastical constitutions, CXXXVIII, 848, 851.

OTTO III, emperor, 1002. Ecclesiastical constitutions, CXXXVIII, 854.

ST OTTO, bishop of Bamberg, 1134. 1. Forty-four letters and charters of Otto and others to him: to Paschal II concerning his election; to Paschal II for his consecration; foundation charter for the monastery of Michelsfeld; concerning his apostolate in Pomerania; concerning the restoration of the monastery of Banz; foundation charter of Heilsbronn monastery; etc. 2. Sermon which St Otto delivered at his first church, founded in 1124, delivered at Pyritz in Pomerania when he was returning to Bamberg from it for the first time, CLXXIII, 1313, 1267; CLXIII, 464.

OTTO, bishop of Freising, 1152. Letter to Wibald, abbot of Corbie, explaining a certain verse of a Psalm, CLXXXIX, 1398.

OTTO, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, twelfth century. Letter on behalf of Gilbert, bishop of London, CC, 1392.

OWEN, king of the Welsh, twelfth century. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 1055.

## P

PACATUS DREPANIUS, proconsul and Gaul by nationality, 394. Panegyric of Emperor Theodosius, XIII, 472, 478 ff.

ST PACHOMIUS, abbot of Tabennesi, 348. 1. Rule for monks, XXIII, 66. 2. Seven letters, mystical words, XXIII, 88; CIII, 452.

ST PACIAN, bishop of Barcelona, 397. 1. Three letters to Sympronianus the Novatian: on the Catholic name, on Sympronianus’s letter, against the treatises of the Novatians. 2. *Paraenesis*, or exhortatory book on repentance. 3. Sermon on baptism, XIII, 1052.

PAGANUS of Miribello, twelfth century. Two donations, CLXII, 1112, 113.

PALLADIUS, bishop of Helenopolis, 417. On the lives of the Fathers, or the *Lausiac History*, LXXII, 1065.

ST PALLADIUS, bishop of Auxerre, 651. Letter to St Desiderius, bishop of Cahors, LXXXVII, 264, 216.

PAMMACHIUS, 417. Several letters, XX, 457; XXII, 743.

PANDULPH of Anagni, associate of Gelasius II, 1119. Life of Pope Gelasius II, CLXIII, 473.

PANVINUS ONUPHRIUS. See ONUPHRIUS.

PAPHNUTIUS, Egyptian abbot, fourth century. 1. Life of St Onuphrius the hermit, LXXIII, 211. 2. Rule for monks, CIII, 434.

PASCENTIUS, 400. Letter to St Augustine, XXXIII, 1051.

POPE PASCHAL I. Seven letters: concerning the discovery of the relics of St Cecilia; to Bernard, archbishop of Vienne; to Emperor Louis; to Petronax, archbishop of Ravenna; to the people of Milan, [Col. 0623] CII, 1076; CVI, 831. Bull for the monastery of Farfa, CXXIX, 977; bull for the monastery of St Vincent at the Vulturnus; letter to all Christians in the northern regions; letter to Stephen, bishop of Cahors, CXXIX, 984.

POPE PASCHAL II, 1118. Four hundred and thirty-eight letters and privileges, CLXIII, 32.

PASCHASINUS, bishop of Lilybaeum, 450. Letter to Pope Leo concerning Easter of the year 444, L, 1294; LIV, 606.

PASCHASIUS, deacon, 512. 1. Two books on the Holy Spirit. 2. Letter to Eugyppius: regarding the life of Blessed Severinus written by Eugyppius, he judges that nothing should be added to its author’s work, LXII, 9 ff.

ST PASCHASIUS RADBERTUS, abbot of Corbie, 865. 1. Exposition on Matthew. 2. Exposition on Psalm 44. 3. Exposition on the Lamentations of Jeremiah. 4. Book on the Body and Blood of the Lord. 5. Letter on the Body and Blood of the Lord to Frudegard. 6. Short work on the Virgin’s childbirth. 7. Three books on faith, hope, and charity. 8. On the passion of Saints Rufinus and Valerius. 9. Life of St Adalhard, abbot of Corbie. 10. Epitaph of Arsenius, or Life of the Venerable Wala, abbot of Corbie in Gaul, written in two books in dialogue form, CXX, 9 ff.

ST PATERIUS, disciple of Pope St Gregory, sixth century. Book on the exposition of the Old and New Testaments, compiled from various books of St Gregory the Great, LXXIX, 684.

ST PATRICK, apostle of the Irish, 450. 1. Confession of St Patrick, explained in a letter to the Irish. 2. Letter of St Patrick to Coroticus. 3. Synod of St Patrick. 4. Various canons attributed to St Patrick. 5. Certain proverbs of St Patrick. 6. Charter of St Patrick. 7. Book on the three dwelling-places. 8. Book on the twelve abuses of the age, LIII, 790.

ST PAULA, 415. Letter to Marcella concerning the Holy Places, XXII, 483.

PAULINUS, deacon of Milan, 418. 1. Life of St Ambrose, bishop of Milan. 2. Short work against Caelestius, presented to Pope Zosimus. 3. Short work on the blessings of the patriarchs, XX, 703.

ST PAULINUS, bishop of Nola, 431. 1. Thirty-five poems: he sends birds to Gestidius while he himself was still living in the world; he sends oysters to the same Gestidius; shortly after his own conversion from the world, he asks God for upright morals; he enumerates various attributes of God; on St John the Baptist, Christ’s Forerunner; paraphrases of certain Psalms; on St Felix; etc., about 10,000 verses, LXI, 438 ff. 2. Four letters: to Sulpicius Severus, priest in Aquitaine, urging him not to abandon his resolve for perfection; to St Amand, then a priest and later bishop of Bordeaux, concerning his unwilling ordination as priest; to Bishop Alypius concerning Augustine’s books which he had received; to Augustine, whom he praises for his five books against the Manichaeans; to Licentius, urging him to dedicate himself to Christ; to Delphinus, bishop of Bordeaux; to Pammachius, a man of consular rank; to Jovius, a most distinguished man who attributed much to fate and fortune; to Victricius, bishop of Rouen; to Severus, to whom he sends a portion of the Most Holy Cross; etc., LXI, 9 ff.

PAULINUS of Périgueux, 490. 1. Six books on the life of St Martin, about 3,200 verses. 2. Letter to Bishop Perpetuus. 3. On the visitation of his little nephew, LXI, 1008.

ST PAULINUS, patriarch of Aquileia, 804. 1. Book of exhortation, commonly called *On Saving Precepts*, written to Henry, count or duke of Friuli. 2. Council of Friuli on the most holy Trinity and the Incarnation of the divine Word. 3. Three books against Felix, bishop of Urgell. 4. Poem on the rule of faith; hymns and rhythmic compositions. 5. Five letters: to Emperor Charles; to Pope Leo III; to Charlemagne concerning proceedings at the synod held at Altino in 803. 6. Sacred compendium against Elipandus, sent to the provinces of Spain by decree of the Council of Frankfurt, 794. 7. Letter to Heistulf, who killed his wife for adultery on the testimony of one person, XCIX, 152.

PAULULUS ROBERTUS, date unknown. On ecclesiastical ceremonies, sacraments, offices, and observances, CLXXVII, 382.

PAULUS OROSIUS. See OROSIUS.

ST PAUL, abbot, date unknown. Rule for monks, LXVI, 949.

PAUL OF MÉRIDA, deacon, 610. On the Lives of the Fathers of Mérida, LXXX, 116.

PAUL, deacon and monk of Monte Cassino, date unknown. Life of St Gregory the Great, LXXV, 42.

PAUL, deacon of the Church of Naples, date unknown. Translation of the life of St Mary of Egypt, the harlot, LXXIII, 671.

[Col. 0624] PAUL, bishop of Constantinople, 647. Letter to St Theodore, Roman pontiff: exposition of his faith, LXXXVII, 92.

ST PAUL, bishop of Verdun, 650. Two letters to St Desiderius, bishop of Cahors, LXXXVII, 214, 260 ff.

PAUL THE PERFIDIOUS, king of the East, 699. Letter to Wamba, great prince of Toledo, XCVI, 762.

ST POPE PAUL I, 767. Thirty-three letters: to King Pippin; to Kings Charles and Carloman, sons of King Pippin; to all the Franks; etc., LXXXIX, 1136.

PAULUS WINFRIDUS, deacon of Friuli, 784. 1. Six books on the deeds of the Lombards. 2. Life of St Gregory the Great. 3. Short book on the succession of the bishops of Metz. 4. Passion of St Cyprian attributed to Paul the Deacon. 5. Life and miracles of St Arnold, bishop, written by Paul the Deacon according to Surius. 6. *Historia Miscella*, twenty-four books. 7. Homilies: two hundred and two for the liturgical seasons, ninety-six for saints. 8. Four letters: to King Charles; to Adalhard, abbot of Corbie; to Theudemar, abbot. 9. Poems: life of St Benedict the abbot; hymn on the miracles of St Benedict; on St Scholastica; life of St Maurus the abbot; on St John the Baptist; to Peter of Pisa; epitaph of Rothaid, daughter of King Pippin; epitaph of Queen Hildegard, wife of Charlemagne; etc., XCV, 413.

PAULUS ALVARUS of Córdoba, 869. 1. Confession of Alvarus of Córdoba. 2. Twenty letters of Alvarus and others to him. 3. *Indiculus luminosus* (“Little Book of Light”). 4. Ten poems: the poem of Philomela; distichs on the rooster; verses of praise or prayer; verses, *Ephemerides* of his own illness; his own metrical lament; verses in the library of Leovigild; verses in praise of the cross; in praise of Blessed Jerome, CXXI, 388; CXV, 705.

PAUL of Bernried, regular canon, c. 1099. Life of St Gregory VII, CXLVIII, 39.

PAUL, monk of St Peter at Chartres, 1100. 1. *Old Agano*, or the cartulary of Agano, eight books. 2. Epitaph of Abbot Landric, CLV, 176.

PELAGIUS, a Briton, A.D. 415. 1. Expositions of the Epistles of St. Paul. 2. Booklet on the Faith, addressed to Innocent I. 3. Letter to Demetrias. 4. Works of which only fragments survive: Prayers from Scripture; *On Nature*; *To a Widow*; Letter to a Friend; Letter to Innocent I; Letter, or Certificate of Vindication, to St. Augustine; books *On Free Will*, XXI, 1164; XX, 608.

PELAGIUS, Pope I, A.D. 560. 1. Fifteen letters: to Narses concerning bishops who were disturbing the Church; to the same, that he should restrain the schismatics; to Narses the patrician, that he should suppress the schismatics; … to the bishops of Tuscany, whom he rebukes for schism; … to all God’s people concerning the Catholic faith; … to Sapaudus, bishop of Arles, whose praises he modestly rejects; to King Childebert … concerning heretics; to Sapaudus, to whom he grants the use of the pallium and to whom he delegates his authority in Gaul; etc. 2. The Faith of Pope Pelagius, LXIX, 392.

PELAGIUS, Pope II, A.D. 590. Sixteen letters and decrees: to Gregory the deacon, that he may obtain from the emperor assistance against the Lombards; to Aunacharius, bishop of Auxerre, that the Frankish kings may not make an alliance with the Lombards; to Elias and the bishops of Istria, that through them the Church of God may no longer be divided; to John, bishop of Constantinople, who was claiming for himself the title of universal bishop, for which reason he had convened a general synod; etc., LXXII, 701 ff.

PEREGRINUS, presbyter of the church of Mustis, A.D. 395. Supplicatory booklet, XI, 1191.

PEREGRINUS, patriarch of Aquileia, A.D. 1134. Document concerning an exchange of the rights of advocacy of Aquileia, XCIX, 644.

PEREGRINUS, abbot of St. Mary of the Latins, about A.D. 1240. Privilege of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, CLV, 1111.

PERINGERUS, abbot of Tegernsee, A.D. 1040. Twelve letters: to Count Diemo … to King Henry … to Gotschalk, bishop of Freising … to Egilbert, bishop of Freising … to Count Udalric, CXLI, 1315.

PERPETUA (St.), A.D. 252. The Passion of the Martyrdom of St. Perpetua, III, 18 ff.

PERPETUUS, bishop of Tours, A.D. 482. Testament of Bishop Perpetuus, LVIII, 752; LXXI, 1149.

PERTUALDUS, citizen of Lucca, A.D. 721. Diploma for the monastery of St. Michael, LXXXVII, 1365.

PETRUINUS, bishop of Vaison. See AREDIUS.

PETER (St.) CHRYSOLOGUS, archbishop of Ravenna, A.D. 450. 1. One hundred and eighty-five sermons: on the two sons, the prodigal and the thrifty; … on hypocrisy and almsgiving; … on fasting and almsgiving; … on bringing unbelievers to baptism; … on fasting and Christ’s temptations; … on the fruits of almsgiving; … on the [Col. 0625] two demoniacs; … on the calming of the storm at sea; … on the watchful servant and the blessedness of the kingdom of God; … on the faithful steward; … on removing scandal; … on Christ eating with tax collectors; … on him who had a withered hand; … on various miracles reported in the Gospel; etc.; on the Apostles’ Creed; … on the Lord’s Prayer; … on Christ’s resurrection; … on the announcement and conception of St. John the Baptist; … on the conversion of the Magdalene; … on various parables; … on certain saints; etc., LII, 184. 2. Letter to the presbyter Eutyches, that he should obediently heed the writings of the Roman Pontiff, LIV, 740.

PETER, deacon, A.D. 513. Book on the Incarnation and Grace of Our Lord Jesus Christ, addressed to Fulgentius and the other bishops of Africa, LXII, 84; LXV, 442.

PETER, Librarian, A.D. 892. Abridged History of the Franks, CLI, 1280.

PETER, archdeacon, date uncertain. Questions on the Prophet Daniel, XCVI, 1348.

PETER, monk and abbot of St. Apollinaris in Classe, A.D. 998. Oath made to Gerbert, archbishop of Ravenna, CXXXIX, 269.

PETER (St.) DAMIAN, bishop of Ostia and cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, A.D. 1072. 1. Sixty shorter works: *On the Catholic Faith*; *Antilogus against the Jews*; Dialogue between a Jew and a Christian; Synodal Disputation; Milanese Proceedings, on the privilege of the Roman Church; the book called *Gratissimus*; the *Book of Gomorrah*; *On Degrees of Kinship*; *On Almsgiving*; *On the Canonical Hours*; the book called *The Lord Be with You*; *On Contempt for the World*; *On the Perfection of Monks*; *On the Order of Hermits*; … *On the Celibacy of Priests*; *Against Intemperate Clerics*; … *On the Flight from Ecclesiastical Dignities*; … *On the Brevity of the Lives of Roman Pontiffs and Divine Providence*; … *On the Dignity of the Priesthood*; *Against the Ignorance of Clerics*; … *On the Common Life of Canons*; *On the Mean Clothing of Churchmen*; … *On Sacraments Administered by the Wicked*; … *Against Avarice*; … *On Various Miraculous Narratives*; … *On Images of the Chief Apostles*; … *On Divine Omnipotence*; … *On Various Sacred Questions*; etc. 2. Proceedings of a synod held in Gaul by Blessed Peter Damian. 3. Hymn on the glory of Paradise. 4. On Blessed Peter Damian’s journey to Gaul and his journey beyond the Alps. 5. Exposition of the Canon of the Mass according to Peter Damian. 6. Collections from the New Testament. 7. Two hundred and twenty-seven sacred poems and prayers. 8. Collections on the Old Testament. 9. Eight books of letters: Book I, twenty-one letters to the chief pastors of the Christian commonwealth and to Cadalous the antipope; Book II, twenty-one letters to cardinal-bishops of the Holy Roman Church; Book III, ten letters to Patriarch L. and to archbishops; Book IV, seventeen letters to bishops; Book V, nineteen letters to archpriests, archdeacons, presbyters, and clerics; Book VI, thirty-six letters to abbots and monks; Book VII, nineteen letters to secular rulers; Book VIII, fifteen letters to distinguished men and other private persons. 10. Seventy-four sermons arranged according to the order of the months. 11. Life of St. Odilo, abbot of Cluny and confessor, of the Order of St. Benedict. 12. Life of St. Maurus, bishop of Cesena and confessor, chosen from the Order of St. Benedict. 13. Life of St. Romuald, abbot and confessor, founder of the Camaldolese congregation of the Order of St. Benedict. 14. Life of St. Rodulf, bishop of Gubbio, and of St. Dominic Loricatus. 15. Passion of the holy virgins Flora and Lucilla. 16. Exposition of the visions of the holy martyrs Marianus and James, CXLIV–CXLV.

PETER, monk of Maillezais, of the Order of St. Benedict, A.D. 1073. Two books on the antiquity and improvement of the island of Maillezais and on the translation of the body of St. Rigomer; or, how the monastery of Maillezais was built and the body of St. Rigomer translated, CXLVI, 1248.

PETER TUDEBODUS. See TUDEBODUS.

PETER ALPHONSI. See ALPHONSI.

PETER, bishop of Poitiers, A.D. 1112. Five privileges for the order and congregation of Fontevraud, CLXII, 1090.

PETER CHRYSOLANUS, archbishop of Milan, A.D. 1117. Oration on the Holy Spirit addressed to Emperor Alexius Comnenus, CLXII, 1005.

PETER PISANUS, cardinal, date uncertain. Life of Pope Paschal II, CLXIII, 13. Letter to Alexander III against disobedient bishops, CC, 1365.

PETER DE HONESTIS, cleric of Ravenna, A.D. 1119. 1. Rule of Clerics, three books. 2. Letter to Paschal, pontiff of the supreme see, in which he sends him the Rule of Clerics for correction, CLXIII, 689, 461.

PETER BERNARD, otherwise called de Corilo, fifth prior of Grandmont, A.D. 1172. Six letters of Peter Bernard and others to him: to King Henry of England, informing him of [Col. 0626] his election; to William, prior of Grandmont, announcing to him the murder of St. Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury; to Henry II, king of England, concerning the murder of St. Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, CCIV, 1464.

PETER, bishop of Bourges, A.D. 1120. Donation to Cluny, by which he grants and confirms the church of Carandigna, CLXVI, 845.

PETER LEONIS, A.D. 1125. Two letters: to Engelrannus, bishop of Amiens, that he should see to the restoration to St. Vedastus of Arras of the altar at Campanioles; to A., abbot of Anchin, concerning guests granted by Baldwin’s widow to the Church of Blessed Mary, CLXVI, 852.

PETER, deacon and monk of Monte Cassino, A.D. 1138. 1. Chronicle of the monastery of Monte Cassino. 2. Short work on the distinguished men of Monte Cassino. 3. Book on the birth and death of the righteous men of the monastery of Monte Cassino. 4. Book on the Holy Places. 5. Prologue to the Register of Monte Cassino, addressed to Abbot Seniorectus. 6. Discipline of Monte Cassino. 7. Three letters: to Richiza, empress of the Romans, concerning the death of Emperor Lothair and of Henry, duke of Bavaria, her son-in-law; to Emperor Conrad II, that he should govern the Roman Empire as a Christian and protect the monastery of Monte Cassino. 8. Rhythmical poem on the Last Days, CLXXIII, 440, 763, 1004 ff.

PETER, prior of the Holy Sepulchre, A.D. 1144. Three privileges, CLV, 1176, 1177, 1189.

PETER, bishop of Bourges, A.D. 1149. Six letters to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1389, 1390, 1391, 1395, 1402, 1429.

PETER, monk of Dive, A.D. 1150. Deeds of Seven Abbots of Bec, written in verse, about 500 lines, CLXXXI, 1709, 1703.

PETER THE VENERABLE, ninth abbot of Cluny, A.D. 1158. 1. Six books of letters: to Pope Innocent; to Matthew, bishop of Albano; to Hugh, archbishop of Rouen; to Ato, bishop of Troyes; to William, archbishop of Embrun; to Odo, abbot of Cluny; to Guigo, prior of the Carthusians; to Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux; to Aimeric, cardinal and chancellor of the Apostolic Sublimity; to the monks of the monastery of Cluny; to Albero, bishop of the church of Liège; to Roger, king of Sicily; to Geoffrey, archbishop of Bordeaux; to Suger, abbot of St. Denis; to Louis, king of the Franks; to Pope Eugenius; etc. 2. Four diplomas: charter of Ambrières; charter concerning the church of St. Denis of Carcere; concerning the church of Morsalimes; etc. 3. Letter to Peter de John against those who say that Christ never openly called himself God in the Gospels. 4. Treatise against the Jews. 5. Letter on the translation of the Qur’an (*Alcoran*). 6. Eleven books against the sect of the Saracens. 7. Treatise against the Petrobrusian heretics. 8. Two books on miracles. 9. Four sermons: on the Transfiguration of the Lord; in praise of the Lord’s tomb; on St. Marcellus, pope and martyr; in veneration of any relics whatsoever. 10. Rhythms, prose pieces, verses, and hymns. 11. Statutes of the Cluniac congregation. 12. Arrangement of the household affairs of Cluny, CLXXXIX, 61 ff.

PETER, archbishop of Tyre, A.D. 1162. Privilege concerning the tithe of the hamlet of Derina, CLV, 1167. Another privilege, ibid.

PETER LOMBARD, bishop of Paris, A.D. 1164. 1. Commentaries on the Psalms. 2. Commentaries on the Epistles of St. Paul. 3. Four books of *Sentences*: on the mystery of the Trinity; on the creation and formation of bodily and spiritual things and many other matters relevant thereto; on the Incarnation of the Word; on sacraments and sacramental signs, CXCI, CXCII.

PETER DE ROYA, monk of Clairvaux, A.D. 1169. Letter to C., provost of Noyon: he enumerates the errors of his former life and highly praises the rule of Clairvaux, CLXXXII, 706; CXCIV, 1895.

PETER, bishop of Pavia, twelfth century. Letter to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 1021.

PETER COMESTOR, A.D. 1179. 1. Scholastic History, briefly comprising a large part of Holy Scripture, which had often been widely dispersed both in the sequence of the text and in glosses. 2. Fifty-one sermons: for Advent; on the feast of St. Nicholas; on the Nativity of the Lord; on the Epiphany; on St. Vincent; on the Purification of the Blessed Virgin; on Ash Wednesday; in Lent; on Palm Sunday; on the Lord’s Supper; on the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin; on the Ascension of the Lord; on the Holy Trinity; etc., CXCVIII, 1045.

PETER, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, of the title of St. Chrysogonus, about A.D. 1182. Four letters: to Ervisius of St. Victor’s, Paris; to Garinus, abbot of the same monastery; to all the faithful concerning the excommunication of the Albigensian heretics; to Philip, dean, and the chapter of St. Martin of Tours, CXCIX, 1120; CC, 1370.

[Col. 0627] PETER PISANUS, dean of the church of Blessed Anianus at Orléans, A.D. 1162. Letter to Pope Alexander III, CC, 1365.

PETER, eighth abbot of Clairvaux, A.D. 1186. Nineteen letters: to Pope Alexander III; to the archbishop of Mainz; to the Cistercian abbot; to the convent of Trois-Fontaines; to Simon of Montaigu; to the bishop of Vienne; to the abbot of Vaux; to Queen Theresa; to the king of Portugal; to religious persons established in Germany; etc., CCI, 1392; CC, 1381.

PETER OF CELLES, later abbot of St. Remigius at Reims and finally bishop of Chartres, A.D. 1187. 1. Two books of letters: the first contains seventy-six letters written while he was abbot of Celles; the second contains one hundred letters written by Peter after he had assumed the abbacy of St. Remigius at Reims. 2. Ninety-five sermons: for Advent; on the Nativity of the Lord; on the Purification of St. Mary; on the Sunday in Lent; on the feast of St. Benedict, abbot; on the Lord’s Annunciation; on the Passion of the Lord; on the Lord’s Supper; on the Resurrection of the Lord; on the Ascension of the Lord; on Pentecost; on the Nativity of St. John the Baptist; on the feast of St. Mary Magdalene; on the Transfiguration of the Lord; on the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary; on St. Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux; synodal sermons. 3. Book on Breads. 4. Mystical and moral exposition of the Mosaic tabernacle. 5. Book on Conscience, addressed to Alcher, monk of Clairvaux. 6. Treatise on Cloistered Discipline, addressed to Henry I, count of Champagne, CCII, 397, 405 ff.

PETER, cantor of the Church of Paris, A.D. 1197. *The Word Made Brief*: a moral work most useful to all theologians, pastors, confessors, preachers, jurists, and persons of every condition, CCV, 21.

PETER, bishop of Roskilde, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Celestine, CCIX, 678.

PETER OF BLOIS, about A.D. 1200. 1. Two hundred and forty-three letters. 2. Sixty-five sermons. 3. Short work on the Transfiguration of the Lord. 4. Compendium on Job, addressed to Henry II, most illustrious king of England. 5. Against the Perfidy of the Jews. 6. Twofold treatise on Christian friendship and on the love of God and neighbor. 7. Passion of Reginald, formerly prince of Antioch. 8. Dialogue between King Henry II and the abbot of Bonneval. 9. On the Twelve Benefits of Tribulation. 10. Various treatises. 11. On the division and writers of the sacred books. 12. On hastening the Jerusalem pilgrimage. 13. Instruction in the Catholic faith. 14. On sacramental confession. 15. On penance to be imposed by the priest. 16. Treatise on the appointment of a bishop. 17. Invective against a corrupter of the works of Peter of Blois. 18. Fragment of a letter on maintaining silence. 19. Booklet on the art of letter-writing. 20. Seven poems: Song on the struggle of flesh and spirit; against clerics devoted to pleasure; treatise on the mysteries of the most holy venerable sacrament of the Eucharist; verses in praise of wine; response to someone against beer; etc., CCVII, 2 ff.

PETER OF POITIERS, chancellor of the University of Paris, A.D. 1205. Five books of *Sentences*: on God; on the angels and the first man; on grace; on confession; on charity; on hope; etc.; on Christ; on the sacraments, CCXI, 780.

PETER CAMBIUS, bishop of Paris, about A.D. 1200. Letter concerning the solemnity of the Circumcision of the Lord and St. Stephen, CCVII, 1168.

PETER DE RIGA, about A.D. 1212. Fragments from the *Aurora*, inserted incidentally in various places, CCXII, 18 ff.

PETER, monk of Vaux-de-Cernay, A.D. 1218. History of the Albigensians and of the holy war undertaken against them in 1209, under the leadership and command of Simon de Montfort, CCXIII, 542.

PETER DE NEMOURS, bishop of Paris, A.D. 1212. Letter to Hugh, dean, and the chapter of Paris, by which he confirms Odo’s donations, CCXII, 91.

PETER III, king of Aragon, A.D. 1250. Privilege concerning Palafrugell and Turicella of Monte Raso, CLV, 1255.

PHILASTRIUS (St.), bishop of Brescia, A.D. 387. Book on Heresies, XII, 1112.

PHILIP, presbyter, A.D. 455. Commentary on Job, LIII, 1012.

PHILIP I, king of the Franks, A.D. 1108. 1. Three letters: to Bernard, abbot of Marmoutier, that he should reform the utterly depraved morals of the nunnery of Faremoutiers; to the same, that he should restore the monastery of St. Magloire at Paris to a better condition; to St. Anselm, exiled at Lyons, that he might deign to visit Gaul. 2. Oath of Philip, king of the Franks. 3. Two diplomas: for the cell of St. Germanus at Laie; concerning the goods of deceased bishops of Chartres, CLIX, 837.

PHILIP, bishop of Châlons, about A.D. 1118. [Col. 0628] Two letters to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 665, 667.

PHILIP OF CLAIRVAUX, A.D. 1161. Book of the Miracles of St. Bernard, CLXXXV, 370.

PHILIP, archbishop of Cologne, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 183.

PHILIP, count of Flanders, seventh century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 187. Letter to Pope Alexander on behalf of Thomas of Canterbury, CC, 1392.

PHILIP, dean of Cologne, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 243.

PHILIP, abbot of Park, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 276.

PHILIP OF HARVENG, abbot of Bonne-Espérance, A.D. 1186. 1. Twenty-five letters of Philip of Harveng and others to him: to Wederic, on the works of the six days; to Hervard, on one reading the Holy Scriptures; to Hervald, on reading pagan and sacred books; to John, on the books of Blessed Hilary *On the Trinity*; to Bernard, concerning a Premonstratensian received by the Cistercians against the will of the Premonstratensians; to Pope Eugenius III, from whom he seeks aid against his persecutors; to Richer, that literary studies are necessary for churchmen; etc. 2. Six books of commentaries on the Song of Songs. 3. Moral interpretations of the Song of Songs. 4. On King Nebuchadnezzar’s Dream. 5. Answer concerning the salvation of the first man. 6. Answer concerning the condemnation of Solomon. 7. Six treatises on the formation of clerics: on the dignity, learning, justice, continence, obedience, and silence of clerics. 8. Life of Blessed Augustine, bishop of Hippo. 9. Life of St. Amandus, bishop of Maastricht; on the miracles of St. Amandus performed throughout Gaul. 10. Passion of Saints Cyricus and Julitta. 11. Passion of St. Salvius, martyr. 12. Life of St. Foillan, martyr. 13. Life of St. Gislenus, confessor. 14. Life of St. Landelinus, confessor. 15. Life of Blessed Oda, virgin. 16. Life of St. Waltrude. 17. Passion of St. Agnes. 18. Various poems, CCIII, 2 ff.

PHILIP, bishop of Beauvais, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Celestine concerning his capture, CCVI, 1278. Letters concerning the settlement of the boundaries of the bishoprics of Beauvais and Paris, CCVII, 1178.

PHILIP, king of the Romans, about A.D. 1205. Letters to Innocent III, CCXVII, 295.

PHILIP, king of the Franks, A.D. 1223. Letters to Pope Lucius III: that he should give full credence to Stephen, whom he sends to Rome on business entrusted to him for negotiation; that he should protect the cause of the archbishop of Tours against the bishop of Dol, who was claiming for himself the title of archbishop, CCXI, 391, 395. Letter to Innocent III concerning Count Theobald, CCXVI, 976. Other letters to Innocent III, CCXVI, 1007; CCXVII, 299.

PHILOCALUS DIONYSIUS, A.D. 354. Two ancient calendars, XIII, 671.

PHILOTHEUS, monk, date uncertain. Encomiastic poem on the life and character of St. Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, CLXXXV, 551.

PHOEBADIUS (St.), bishop of Agen, A.D. 400. 1. Book against the Arians. 2. On the Orthodox Faith against the Arians, otherwise *On the Divinity and Consubstantiality of the Son*. 3. Booklet on the Faith, XX, 9.

PIBO, bishop of Toul, A.D. 1107. Fourteen diplomas: for the monastery of St. Aper; for the priory of Asmantia; for the church of St. Deodatus; for the church of Munz; for the cell of Asmantia; for the monastery of St. Leo of Toul; foundation of the priory of St. Theobald; foundation of the priory of St. James at Chastel-Neuf; for the abbey of St. Mansuetus of Toul; foundation of the priory of Laudecourt; for the church of St. Gengulf, CLVII, 414. Letter to Pope Paschal on behalf of the monks of Chaumousey, CLXIII, 447.

PIPPIN, duke of Austrasia, and Plectrude his wife, A.D. 687. Five charters: donation of the fortress of Amblève, in the Ardennes, to Beregisus, that a cell and church may be established there; transfer of the estate of Nugerêt to the basilica of the Holy Apostles near Metz; charter for the church of St. Vedastus, LXXXVIII, 1215, 1219, 1246; donation of the monastery of Susteren to Bishop Willibrord, LXXXIX, 547.

PIPPIN THE ELDER, A.D. 691. Three charters: for the monastery of Lobbes; for the church of St. Peter at Cambrai, LXXXVIII, 1223, 1224, 1238.

PIPPIN, king of the Franks, A.D. 755. 1. Two letters: to Boniface, archbishop of Mainz; to Lullus, bishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 788; XCVI, 824. 2. Thirty-one diplomas: the Capitulary of Soissons, A.D. 744; the Capitulary of Verberie, A.D. 753; the double Capitulary of Verne; the Capitulary of Compiègne; the Aquitanian Capitulary; concerning the property of the Church of St. Martin; for the monastery of Murbach; for the fairs of St. Denis; for the monastery of St. Denis; for the monastery of Nantua; for the monastery of Honau; for the abbey of Murbach; for the abbey of Prüm; etc., XCVI, 1501 ff.

PIRMINIUS (St.), abbot, A.D. 757. *Scarapsus*, on the individual canonical books, LXXXIX, 1030.

PIUS I (St.), pope, A.D. 147. 1. Decrees that Easter should be celebrated on Sunday. 2. Letter addressed to the Italians, CXXX, 112 ff.

PLACIDIA GALLA, daughter of Theodosius, A.D. 450. Two letters: to Theodosius, concerning the preservation of the Catholic faith; to Augusta Pulcheria, concerning the Second Council of Ephesus, LIV, 860, 864.

PLACIDUS, prior of the monastery of Nonantola, later bishop of an unknown see, A.D. 1119. Book on the Honor of the Church, CLXIII, 613.

PLACIDUS, monk and deacon of Monte Cassino, date uncertain. Supplement to the Distinguished Men of the Monastery of Monte Cassino, CLXXIII, 1049.

POLEMEUS SILVIUS ANNAEUS. See ANNAEUS.

POLYCARP (St.), bishop and martyr of Smyrna, A.D. 167. Fragments of responses, LXVIII, 359.

POMERIUS JULIANUS. See JULIANUS.

POMPEIUS, prefect of the empire, A.D. 519. Letter to Hormisdas concerning perfidy cast down and peace made with the Eastern Church, LXIII, 451.

PONTIANUS, pope, A.D. 230. 1. Decrees. 2. Letter on brotherly love and avoiding evils, CXXX, 142.

PONTIANUS, African bishop, A.D. 540. Letter to Emperor Justinian on the Three Chapters, LXVII, 996.

PONTIUS (St.), deacon of Carthage, A.D. 257. On the life and passion of St. Cyprian, bishop and martyr of Carthage, III, 1478.

PONTIUS, count of Toulouse, about A.D. 1060. Charter concerning the subjection of the abbey of Moissac to Cluny, CLIX, 955.

PONTIUS, abbot of St. Rufus, A.D. 1124. Letter to the abbot of Chaumousey concerning daily fasting, continual silence, abstinence from wine, and the woollen garments of the canons of the monastery of Chaumousey, CLXIII, 1478.

PONTIUS, abbot of Cluny, A.D. 1125. 1. Statutes of Abbot Pontius. 2. Two pious injunctions, CLXVI, 835.

PONTIUS, bishop of Clermont, about 1170. Letter to Maurice, bishop of Paris, and Stephen, abbot of St. Evurtius, concerning the baptism of one of his diocesan flock, CCXI, 312.

PONTIUS, abbot of Vézelay, twelfth century. Letter to Suger on behalf of the widow of Robert the physician, once his friend, and her deceased son, CLXXXVI, 1418.

POPPO, archbishop of Trier, A.D. 1045. Letter to Pope Benedict IX, seeking the canonization of St. Simeon, recluse at Trier, CXLI, 1398, 1368.

POPPO, bishop of Metz, A.D. 1103. 1. Two diplomas: for the abbey of St. Vincent; concerning the rights of the advocates of Amel. 2. Three letters to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLV, 1650, 1656; CLXII, 650, 653, 665.

PORPHYRIUS OPTATIANUS. See OPTATIANUS.

POSSESSOR, African bishop, sixth century. Letter of Pope Hormisdas concerning the book of Bishop Faustus, LXIII, 489.

POSSIDIUS, bishop of Calama, A.D. 630. One book on the life of St. Augustine and a catalogue of the works of the same St. Augustine, L, 408; XXXII, 33.

POTAMIUS, bishop of Lisbon, A.D. 366. 1. Two treatises: on Lazarus; on the martyrdom of Isaiah the prophet. 2. Letter to Athanasius, attacked by the Arians after they had subscribed at the Council of Rimini, VIII, 1409.

PRIMASIUS, bishop of Hadrumetum, A.D. 555. 1. Commentaries on the Epistles of St. Paul. 2. Five books of Commentaries on the Apocalypse of Blessed John, LXVIII, 408.

PRISCIAN, grammarian, about A.D. 525. On the Art of Grammar, CXI, 614.

PROSPER, African, about A.D. 429. Letter to Augustine concerning the Pelagian heresy, XXXIII, 1002.

PROSPER (St.) OF AQUITAINE, A.D. 450. 1. Two letters: to Augustine, concerning the remnants of the Pelagian heresy growing in Gaul and the complaints of such people against the doctrine of predestination and grace; letter to Rufinus concerning grace and free will. 2. Poem on the Ungrateful, or Pelagians, about 1,000 lines. 3. Epigrams: against a detractor of Augustine; epigram against the same man, or some other detractor of Augustine. 4. Epitaph of the Nestorian and Pelagian heresies. 5. Answers to the chapters of objections raised by calumniating Gauls. 6. Answers to the chapters of Vincentian objections. 7. Answers to excerpts of the Genoese. 8. Book entitled *Authorities of the Bishops of the Apostolic See of Former Times, on the Grace of God and the Freedom of the Will*. 9. Book against the *Collator*, that is, in defense of St. Augustine, bishop of Hippo, against the book of the presbyter Cassian entitled *On the Protection of God*. 10. Exposition of Psalms 100 through 150. 11. Book [Col. 0630] of Sentences selected from the works of St. Augustine. 12. One book of epigrams drawn from the sayings of St. Augustine. 13. Complete chronicle divided into two parts: the first from the beginning of the world to the death of Valens, with the notation of consuls from the death of Christ; the second from the death of Emperor Valens to the death of Valentinian III and the capture of Rome by the Vandals. 14. Confession. 15. Poem of a husband to his wife, exhorting her to dedicate herself wholly to God. 16. Poem on Divine Providence. 17. Two books on the calling of all nations. 18. Book on the promises and predictions of God, LI, 64 ff.

PROSPER, converted from Manichaeism, A.D. 530. Profession of the Catholic faith, LXV, 24.

PROTADIUS (St.), archbishop of Besançon, A.D. 624. 1. Praises, or acclamations, copied from an ancient book of letters. 2. Martyrology throughout the cycle of the year, LXXX, 412.

PROTERIUS (St.), bishop of Alexandria, A.D. 454. Letter to St. Leo on the calculation of Easter, LIV, 1084.

PRUDENTIUS, Aurelius, poet, A.D. 405. 1. *Cathemerinon*: twelve hymns—at cockcrow; morning hymn; hymn before food; hymn after food; on the new light of the Paschal Sabbath; before sleep; hymn of those fasting; after fasting; hymn for every hour; at the burial of the dead; etc. 2. *Apotheosis*, 1,085 verses. 3. *Hamartigenia*, 965 verses. 4. *Psychomachia*, 915 verses. 5. *Dittochaeum*: Old Testament, New Testament. 6. Two books against Symmachus. 7. *Peristephanon*: fourteen hymns—in honor of the holy martyrs Hemeterius and Celedonius; Passion of St. Lawrence; in honor of Blessed Eulalia, martyr; in honor of the eighteen martyrs of Saragossa; Passion of St. Vincent, martyr; etc., LXI–LX.

PRUDENTIUS (St.), bishop of Troyes, A.D. 861. 1. Letter to Hincmar and Pardulus concerning double predestination. 2. Book on Predestination against John the Scot, surnamed Eriugena. 3. Covering letter to Venilo, sent through a deputy for the ordination of Aeneas of Paris, since he himself could not be present. 4. Sermon on the life and death of the glorious Virgin Maura. 5. Annals, or the second part of the Annals of St. Bertin, from A.D. 835 to A.D. 861. 6. Florilegium from Holy Scripture. 7. Extracts from the Pontifical of St. Prudentius. 8. Breviary of the Psalter, CXV, 965, 972.

PSEUDO-LIUTPRAND, date uncertain. Book on the Lives of the Roman Pontiffs, CXXIX, 1150.

PUBLICOLA, A.D. 398. Letter to Augustine, XXXIII, 181.

PUBLIUS VICTOR, date uncertain. Description of the City of Rome, XVIII, 436.

PULCHERIA AUGUSTA, A.D. 453. Letter to Pope St. Leo concerning St. Flavian, whose body had been brought to Constantinople for burial in the Basilica of the Apostles, and concerning Anatolius, bishop of Constantinople, whom she says remained in the same faith, LIV, 905.

PULLUS (ROBERT). See ROBERT.

PURCHARDUS, monk of Reichenau, A.D. 1003. Poem on the deeds of Abbot Witigowo, 552 verses, CXXXIX, 352.

PUSTERLA ANGILBERTUS. See ANGILBERTUS.

## Q

QUODVULTDEUS, deacon, A.D. 427. Letter to Augustine, XXXIII, 997.

## R

RABANUS MAURUS, A.D. 856. 1. Two books *On the Praises of the Holy Cross*. 2. Three books *On the Instruction of Clerics*. 3. Book on the Oblation of Children. 4. Four books of Commentaries on Genesis. 5. Book on Computation. 6. Eight books of Commentaries on Matthew. 7. Four books of Commentaries on Exodus. 8. Seven books of Expositions on Leviticus. 9. Four books of Explanations of the Book of Numbers. 10. Four books of Exposition on Deuteronomy. 11. Three books of Commentaries on Joshua. 12. Two books of Commentaries on Judges. 13. Commentary on Ruth. 14. Commentaries on the Four Books of Kings. 15. Commentaries on the Two Books of Chronicles. 16. Exposition of Judith. 17. Exposition of Esther. 18. Three books of Commentaries on the Book of Wisdom. 19. Ten books of Commentaries on Ecclesiasticus. 20. Commentaries on the Books of Maccabees. 21. Homilies: homilies on the principal feasts; likewise seventy on virtues; one hundred and sixty-three homilies on the Gospels and Epistles. 22. Penitential. 23. Twenty books of Commentaries on Ezekiel. 24. Letter: In what degree of generation marriage is lawful. 25. Treatise on marriages of blood-relations, and on the tricks of magicians and false divinations. 26. Treatise on the soul. 27. Martyrology. 28. Canonical answers to certain questions of Reginbald, chorepiscopus. [Col. 0631] 29. On chorepiscopi. 30. Twenty-two books *On the Universe*. 31. Extract from Priscian’s Art of Grammar. 32. Exposition of Solomon’s Proverbs. 33. Commentaries on Jeremiah. 34. Explanations of the Epistles of Blessed Paul. 35. Allegories on Holy Scripture. 36. Commentaries on certain canticles. 37. Book on sacred orders, divine sacraments, and priestly vestments. 38. Three books on ecclesiastical discipline. 39. Three books on not seeing God, purity of heart, and the manner of penance. 40. Three books on vices and virtues and satisfaction for sins. 41. Book of Penitents, addressed to Otgar. 42. Short work on the Passion of the Lord. 43. On the life of Blessed Mary Magdalene and of her sister St. Martha. 44. Commentaries on the Rule of St. Benedict. 45. Eight letters: to Reginbald, chorepiscopus of Mainz; to Heribald, bishop of Auxerre; to Egil, abbot of Prüm, concerning the body and blood of the Lord against Ratpert; to Hincmar of Reims; to Noting, with the book *On the Predestination of God*; to Count Heberard; to Louis, king of Germany; to Hincmar of Reims concerning Gottschalk. 46. Latin-Barbarian glosses on the parts of the human body. 47. On the invention of languages. 48. Fragment of a Latin-Theodisc glossary. 49. Poems on various subjects, hymns, epitaphs, CVII, CVIII, CIX, CX, CXI, CXII.

RACHIO, bishop of Strasbourg, A.D. 788. Inscription of a codex containing the canons of councils and decrees of pontiffs, XCVI, 1030.

RACHIS, king of the Lombards, A.D. 747. Decree by which he determines the boundaries of certain estates belonging to the monastery of Bobbio, LXXXVII, 1376; privilege of Rachis for the church of Piacenza; privilege for the monastery of Amiata, LXXXVII, 1376, 1406, 1408.

RADBOD (St.), bishop of Utrecht, A.D. 918. 1. Brief Chronicle. 2. Three sermons: on St. Switbert; on the life of the holy virgin of Christ Amalberga; on St. Lebwin. 3. Four poems: to St. Martin; on Christ’s viaticum; for St. Swibert; for St. Lebwin, CXXXII, 538.

RADBOD OF DOL, A.D. 923. Letter to King Athelstan, CXXXII, 720.

RADBOD II, bishop of Tournai and Noyon, A.D. 1098. 1. Life of St. Medard, bishop of Noyon and Tournai. 2. Second Life of St. Godeberta, virgin of Noyon in Belgium. 3. Sermon of Radbod on the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary. 4. Letter to Lambert, bishop of Arras. 5. Three charters: for the church of St. Peter of Cluny; for the restoration of the abbey of St. Martin of Tournai; for the church of St. Mary at Bruges, CL, 1493; CLXII, 656.

RADCHIS, abbot of St. Michael at Lucca, A.D. 728. Diploma by which he appoints as his successor in the same office Waltprand, cleric and son of Duke Walpert, LXXXVII, 1371.

RADEGUND (St.), queen of France, A.D. 587. Testament, or letter to the bishops, mentioning the monastery of girls at Poitiers, LXXII, 651, 680.

RADULFUS ARDENS, of Poitiers, A.D. 1100. Homilies: forty-four for the seasons, thirty-three for saints’ days, CLV, 1293. One hundred and twenty-two homilies on the Sunday Epistles and Gospels, CLV, 1294, 1665.

RADULFUS, lord of Silly, A.D. 1112. Copy of the foundation of the abbey of Savigny in Normandy, CCVII, 1163.

RADULFUS TORTARIUS, monk of Fleury, A.D. 1115. Miracles of St. Benedict, CLX, 1172.

RADULFUS, archbishop of Canterbury, A.D. 1122. Letter to Pope Calixtus, before whom he complains of the injury done to himself and the Church of Canterbury in the consecration of the archbishop of York, CLXIII, 1341, 1481.

RADULFUS, Archbishop of Rheims, 1124. Two letters: to Lambert, bishop of Arras; to Goscelin, dean of Beauvais, CLXIII, 1416; CLXII, 692.

RADULFUS, count of Vermandois, c. 1147. Five letters to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1352, 1355, 1369, 1391, 1403.

RADULFUS, count of Clermont, 1169. Instrument concerning the resignation of the prebend which Peter of Moncy held in the church of Blessed Mary at Paris, CCV, 909.

RADULFUS of Caen, c. 1220. *The Deeds of Tancred in the Jerusalem Expedition*, CLV, 489.

RAGINALDUS, chaplain of Duke William, 1171. Privilege of the church of the Holy Sepulchre situated near Troyes, CLV, 1243.

RAIMBALDUS, archbishop of the church of Arles, 1007. Five diplomas: for the monastery of St. Victor; remission of penances granted at the consecration of the church of St. Mary of Correno, which is endowed; charter for St. Victor; sermon and confirmation of the holy Fathers of the holy Truce of God; for the Victorine monks, CXLIII, 1389.

[Col. 0632] RAINALDUS I, archbishop of Rheims, 1093. Eleven letters: to the clergy of Arras concerning Lambert’s consecration; to Lambert, bishop-elect of Arras, concerning his election; to Pope Urban II concerning Lambert’s election; to the count of Flanders concerning confirmation of Lambert’s election; to Lambert, bishop of Arras, concerning the absolution of certain clerics; to the same, that he should attend the synod convened by Urban in Italy; to the same, that he should be present at the Council of Clermont; to Balderic, concerning the Chronicle of Cambrai; etc., CL, 1381.

RAINALDUS, bishop of Lyons, 1213. Origin of the castle of Majorev in the valley of Meria, CLIII, 936.

RAINALDUS II, archbishop of Rheims, 1137. 1. Two letters: to Robert, archdeacon of Tournai, that he should install monks in the church of Pétin; to the clergy of Arras, concerning the election of a bishop. 2. Eleven diplomas: confirmation of the foundation of St. Josse of the Wood; charter for the foundation of the monastery of Igny; concerning the excommunication and absolution of Guiterius, count of Reste; regular canons established in the abbey of St. Martin of Sparnac; for the monastery of Silincourt; etc., CLXXII, 1340; CLXII, 648; CLXXXIX, 1058.

RAINALDUS of Salmanche, twelfth century. Charter concerning the donation of the place of Ralay, CLXII, 1106.

RAINALDUS of Montfaucon, 1148. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1405.

RAINARDUS (St), fifth abbot of Cîteaux, 1151. 1. Statutes of the general chapter of the Cistercian Order. 2. Letter to Innocent II, CLXXXI, 1724.

RANULFUS of Tours, bishop, twelfth century. Letter to Gilbert Foliot, bishop of London, CXC, 1063.

RADBODUS, archbishop of Trier, ninth century. Letter to Robert, bishop of Metz, on behalf of the priest Gislemar, CXXIX, 1396.

RATEFRIDUS, 748. Foundation of a monastery of nuns and of the hospice of St. Peter at Pistoia, LXXXVII, 1377. Establishment of the monastery of the holy virgins under the title of Saints Peter, Paul, and Anastasius, ibid., 1380.

RATHERIUS, bishop of Verona, 974. 1. Six books of *Preludes*, explaining the duties of persons of every age, sex, and condition; otherwise entitled *Meditations of the Heart* and *The Contestant*, composed between February 935 and August 937. 2. Life of St. Ursmar, bishop and abbot of Lobbes in Belgium. 3. Deliberative conclusion drawn up at Liège, when Ratherius, expelled from the see of Liège, urged that place be yielded to the usurper. 4. *Phrenesis*, a little book written at Mainz in the same dispute concerning Liège. 5. Ratherius’s Confession, or an extract from his dialogue of confession. 6. Exhortation and prayers. 7. Invective against certain persons, and a mournful account of the translation of the body of St. Metrone. 8. Decrees and a little book concerning clerics ordained by Milo, the usurper of his see. 9. Little work on his own fall. 10. Two parts on contempt for the canons. 11. A conjecture concerning a certain quality. 12. Ratherius’s synodal letter to priests and the other orders established outside the city, that is, throughout the whole diocese. 13. On unlawful marriage. 14. On idle speech. 15. Itinerary. 16. Judicial decision, or foundation and endowment of the clerics of the cathedral church of Verona. 17. On clerics rebelling against him. 18. Dispute between Ratherius himself and the clerics. 19. Apologetic Book. 20. Testament. 21. Fourteen letters of Ratherius and others to him: to Patricius, concerning the body and blood of the Lord; to the archbishops Wido and Sobbo; to the bishops Godescalc and Aurelius; to Archbishop Rolbert; to John, supreme pontiff; to all the faithful; to Milo, usurper of the see of Verona; to Empress Adelaide. 22. Eleven sermons: on Lent; at the Lord’s Supper; on Easter; on the octave of Easter; on the Ascension of the Lord; on Pentecost; on Mary and Martha, CXXXVI, 145.

RATPERTUS, a Lombard, 748. Donations made to the Pistoian monastery of St. Bartholomew, LXXXVII, 1428.

RATPERTUS, monk of St. Gall, 890. 1. Book on the fortunes of the monastery of St. Gall. 2. Various poems: on the feast of St. Gall; for the solemn procession through fields and mountains with the relics of St. Gall; on the feast of St. Othmar; for receiving the Eucharist; for welcoming the king; a litany for procession on Sundays; for welcoming the queen; for the descent to the spring; epitaph of Hildegard; concerning a certain chapel, CXXVI, 1056.

RATRAMNUS, monk of Corbie, 868. 1. Two books on God’s predestination, addressed to King Charles the Bald. 2. Book on the Nativity of Christ. 3. On the Body and Blood of the Lord. 4. Four books against the objections of the Greeks who disparage the Roman Church. 5. Letters concerning the Cynocephali (“Dog-Heads”) to the priest Rimbert, CXXI, 9 ff., 1153.

RAURACUS, bishop of Nevers, 650. Letter to St. Desiderius, bishop of Cahors, LXXXVII, 214, 259.

RAVENNIUS, Gallic bishop, c. 454. Synodal letter of Ravennius and other Gallic bishops to Pope St. Leo, concerning his letter to Flavian, which was received in Gaul as a symbol of faith, LIV, 966.

RAYMUNDUS, count of Toulouse, ninth century. Charter for the foundation of the abbey of Vabres, LXXXII, 785.

RAYMUNDUS ARNALLI, monk of St. Victor, eleventh century. Letter to his abbot B., excusing himself for not yet having returned from Italy, and asking that he be permitted to devote himself to the study of law, CLI, 640.

RAYMUNDUS of Curamonta, 1096. Charter by which, as he sets out for Jerusalem, he mortgages certain estates to the monks of Tulle, CLV, 484.

RAYMUNDUS, count of Saint-Gilles, 1103. Diploma concerning the donation to St. Victor of Marseille of half the village of Gibellet, CLV, 484.

RAYMUNDUS of Aguilers, canon of Le Puy, 1100. *History of the Franks Who Captured Jerusalem*, CLV, 592.

RAYMUNDUS, viscount of Cahors, 1101. He embraces monastic life in the monastery of Moissac and grants two churches to Abbot Ansquitil, CLIX, 976.

RAYMUNDUS, count of Galicia, eleventh century. Letter of Raymond, count of Galicia, and Henry, count of Portugal, to Hugh, abbot of Cluny, concerning the friendship entered into between them, CLIX, 944.

RAYMUNDUS, count of Tripoli, 1140. Five privileges: concerning the gift of a house situated near Mount Peregrinus; concerning the liberty which we have in the port of Tripoli . . .; concerning the confirmation of certain houses; concerning all the possessions which we have in the lordship of Tripoli, CLV, 1191 ff.

RAYMUNDUS, duke of Narbonne, count of Toulouse, marquis of Provence, twelfth century. Letter to Louis, king of the Franks, CLV, 1268.

RAYMUNDUS, patriarch of Aquileia, 1278. Statute concerning the purchase of houses for the common life of the canons of Udine, XCIX, 649.

RECCAREDUS, king of the Visigoths, 601. Edict confirming the Council of Toledo, LXXII, 1121.

RECESVINTUS, king of the Goths, 650. Two letters to Braulio, bishop of Zaragoza, LXXX, 685, 686.

REGIMUNDUS, or TRACTEMUNDUS, bishop of Elvira, 973. Letter to Liutprand, deacon of Pavia, and the subdeacon of Toledo, CXXXVI, 968.

REGINO, abbot of Prüm, 915. 1. Chronicle from the Incarnation of the Lord to the year 906. 2. Two books on ecclesiastical disciplines and the Christian religion. 3. On harmonic instruction, CXXXII, 9 ff., 483.

REIMBALDUS, provost of St. John’s at Liège, 1115. Two letters to Wazelin, prior of St. James’s, concerning his little works, CLXII, 750.

REINARDUS, abbot of Reinhausen, 1147. Letter to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1153.

REINERUS, monk of St. Lawrence at Liège, 1188. 1. Three little books on the distinguished writers of his monastery. 2. Commentary on the antiphons beginning with “O” before Christmas. 3. *Mirror of Penance*, or *Life of St. Pelagia*, two books. 4. *The Virgin’s Palm*, or on the life and passion of St. Mary the Cappadocian, two books. 5. *Flower of the Desert*, or on the life of St. Theobald, monk and hermit, two books. 6. Two little books on the conflict of two dukes and the wondrous revelation of souls, and on a captive knight freed through the saving sacrifice. 7. A book on the arrival at Liège from Rome of the relics of St. Lawrence the martyr, together with other poems and epigrams of various kinds. 8. Five little books of *The Boulogne Triumph*. 9. Life of Euraclus, forty-fifth bishop of Liège. 10. Life of Reginard, fiftieth bishop of Liège. 11. Book on the fall of lightning upon the church of his monastery. 12. Little book of thanksgiving to Blessed Lawrence upon the new dedication of his monastery church. 13. Brief account of the burning of the church of St. Lambert at Liège. 14. Three books of *Tears*. 15. Two books on the progress of death. 16. Life of St. Wolbodon, bishop of Liège, CCIV, 9 ff.

REINHARDUS, bishop of Halberstadt, 1007. Two letters to Pope Paschal II, CLXIII, 459, 460.

REMBERTUS (St), bishop of Hamburg, 888. Life of St. Ansgar, archbishop of Hamburg, CXXVI, 1010, 992.

REMIGIUS (St), archbishop of Rheims, 533. 1. Four letters: to Clovis, king of the Franks, concerning the death of his sister Albofledis; to the same, when he was preparing for war against the Goths; to three bishops concerning the priest Claudius, in whose case he complains that he had been disregarded; to Falcon, bishop of Tongeren, because he was usurping jurisdiction in the church of Mouzon. 2. Testament of St. Remigius. 3. Epitaph of King Clovis, LXV, 961.

REMIGIUS, bishop of Strasbourg, 778. Testament, or charter donating the monasteries of Aschovia and Wertha to the church of Strasbourg, XCVI, 1582.

[Col. 0634] REMIGIUS, bishop of Chur, 820. Canons for his diocese, CII, 1094.

REMIGIUS (St), bishop of Lyons, 865. 1. Book on the three letters of venerable bishops: what ought to be thought concerning their sense and assertions according to the rule of Catholic truth. 2. On the universal condemnation through Adam and the special rescue from it, through Christ, of the elect. 3. Little book on steadfastly maintaining the truth of Scripture and faithfully following the authority of the holy orthodox Fathers, CXXI, 985.

REMIGIUS, monk of St. Germanus of Auxerre, of the Order of St. Benedict, 908. 1. Commentary on Genesis. 2. Expositions of the Psalms. 3. Commentary on the Song of Songs. 4. Commentary on the Twelve Minor Prophets. 5. Commentary on the Epistles of St. Paul. 6. Exposition on the celebration of Mass. 7. Treatise on the dedication of a church. 8. Twelve homilies on certain words selected from the Gospel of Matthew. 9. Music, CXXXI, 48 ff.

RENALLUS, master of the see of Barcelona, c. 1080. Verses excerpted from the book of Renallus, master of Barcelona and Girona, on the body of Christ, CXLVII, 600.

REOLUS, bishop of Rheims, 686. Charter by which he grants Abbot Beracharius the village of Gaugia to build a monastery of nuns, LXXXVIII, 1212.

RHETICIUS, bishop of Autun, fourth century. Saying concerning baptism, VI, 46.

RIBODIMONTE (HUGH of). See HUGH.

RICHARDUS, abbot of Fleury, 979. Customs and rights of the church concerning the Rule, CXXXVI, 1302.

RICHARDUS, second count of the Normans, 1027. Charter in which he confirms the donations made by his father Richard to the abbey of St. Michael, CL, 579.

RICHARDUS, archbishop of Bourges, eleventh century. Letters concerning the consecration of the church of Vipply; letters concerning the priestly benefice of the church of Lanat, CXXXII, 475, 478.

RICHARDUS of Dumelles, abbot of Préaux, 1100. 1. Fragments of the commentary of Richard of Dumelles. 2. Letter to St. Anselm of Canterbury dedicating his commentary on Genesis, CLV, 1628.

RICHARDUS, abbot of Préaux, 1117. Prologue to Leviticus, addressed to Anselm, archbishop of Canterbury, CLXVI, 1357.

RICHARDUS, bishop of Albano, twelfth century. Two letters: to Robert, count of Flanders; to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 679, 687.

RICHARDUS, cardinal and archbishop of Narbonne, 1118. 1. Account of the harassments endured by Archbishop Richard at the hands of Aimeric, viscount of Narbonne. 2. Five letters and diplomas: letter to King S. concerning the sentence of excommunication against the people of Pamplona; settlement between Archbishop Richard and Bernard, viscount of Béziers, his kinsman; charter of the agreement entered between Richard, archbishop of Narbonne, and Oliver of Termes; donation made to Bertrand, abbot of Psalmody; charter concerning the right of wreck, CLXII, 1593.

RICHARDUS of Haye, 1154. Charter for the foundation of the abbey of Blanche-Lande, CCVII, 1165.

RICHARDUS, bishop of Coutances, c. 1158. Charter concerning the church of Morsalines, CLXXXIX, 1071.

RICHARDUS, monk of Grandselve, in the diocese of Toulouse, Cistercian Order, 1160. Poem in praise of Clairvaux and of its religious discipline, CLXXXV, 1564.

RICHARDUS, archdeacon of Poitiers, twelfth century. Letter concerning the death of St. Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 1036.

RICHARDUS of St. Victor, regular canon of Paris, 1173. 1. Book on preparing the mind for contemplation, called *Benjamin Minor*. 2. Five books on the grace of contemplation, taking occasion from Moses’ ark and for that reason hitherto called *Benjamin Major*. 3. Treatise on meditating upon the calamities which will occur near the end of the world. 4. Exposition of difficulties arising in the explanation of the Tabernacle of the Covenant. 5. Explanations of certain difficulties of Scripture, addressed to Blessed Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux. 6. Mystical annotations on the Psalms. 7. Exposition of the Canticle of Habakkuk. 8. Explanation of the Song of Songs. 9. How Christ is set as a sign to the peoples. 10. On the vision of Ezekiel. 11. Two books on Emmanuel. 12. Explanation of certain difficult passages of the Apostle. 13. Seven books on the Apocalypse of John. 14. Six books on the Trinity. 15. On the three appropriated persons in the Trinity, to Saint Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux. 16. Book on the Incarnate Word. 17. How the Holy Spirit is the love of the Father and the Son. 18. On the most excellent baptism of Christ. 19. On the mission of the Holy Spirit. 20. On the comparison of Christ to a flower and Mary to a rod. 21. On the sacrifice of David the prophet. 22. On the difference between Abraham’s sacrifice and the sacrifice of Blessed Mary the Virgin. 23. On the twofold Passover. 24. On the destruction of evil and the advancement of good. 25. On the state of the inner person. 26. On the power of binding and loosing. 27. On judicial power in the final and universal judgment. 28. On the spirit of blasphemy. 29. On the degrees of charity. 30. On the four degrees of violent charity. 31. Eleven letters of Richard of St. Victor and others to him. 32. Three books on the instruction of the inner person, taking occasion from Nebuchadnezzar’s dream in Daniel. 33. Treatise of excerpts, containing the origin and classification of the arts, the situation of lands, and a summary of histories, CXCVI, 2 ff.

RICHARDUS, abbot of Bristol, twelfth century. Letter to Ervisius, abbot of St. Victor, concerning the monastery of St. Victor, CXCVI, 1386.
