RICHARDUS, abbot of Sprinchersbach, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 296.

RICHARDUS, archbishop of Canterbury, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Alexander III concerning the abbot of Malmesbury, because he had withdrawn himself from obedience to his bishop, etc., CC, 1456. Letter to the Cistercian monks, commending himself to their prayers on the occasion of his elevation to the archbishopric of Canterbury, CCVII, 302.

RICHARDUS, king of the English, twelfth century. 1. Letter to Pope Clement III concerning the peace made between himself and King Tancred, CCIV, 1506. 2. Letters concerning a donation made to the chapter of Bayeux, CCVII, 1159. Letter to Pope Innocent III, CCXVI, 1000.

RICHERUS, monk of St. Remigius, 999. Four books of *Histories*, CXXXVIII, 9.

RICULFUS, bishop of Soissons, 902. Twenty-one statutes, CXXXI, 14.

RIGOBERTUS, 723. Charter by which he sells to Erkenbold, bishop of Thérouanne, estates in the districts of Thérouanne and Ponthieu, LXXXVIII, 1279.

RIHPALDUS, abbot, ninth century. Donation, CXXIX, 931.

RILINDIS, abbess of Hohenburg, 1169. Fragments, CXCIV, 1537.

RIQUINUS, administrator of Toul, 1111. Charter concerning the cell of Frondon, CLXVI, 849.

RISO, priest and chaplain of Bohemond, prince of Antioch, 1138. Privilege concerning the gift of houses which he possessed at Antioch, together with the orchard pertaining to them, CLV, 1183.

RIVERIA, of Adelaide, twelfth century. Two charters: charters of donation concerning the valley of the Fountain of Ebrald, CLXII, 1104.

ROBERTUS, bishop of Metz, 916. 1. Four diplomas: concerning an exchange between Lodoin, abbot of the monastery of Gorze, and the priest Vuerding; for the monastery of St. Arnulf; for the construction of the church of Dodo’s Court; for a certain William. 2. Nine letters, CXXXII, 528.

ROBERTUS, king of the Franks, 1031. 1. Five letters of Robert and others to him: to Leotheric, archbishop of Sens; to Gauzlin, archbishop of Bourges. 2. Twenty hymns and responsories. 3. Fourteen diplomas: concerning the election of abbots and the church of St. Leodegar at Champeaux; for the monastery of Saint-Maur-des-Fossés; for the monastery of St. Germanus at Auxerre; for the monastery of St. Magloire at Paris; for the monastery of Fécamp; for the foundation of the nunnery of Beaumont near Tours; for the monastery of Corbie; for the monks of Flavigny; for the monks of Cormery; for the restoration of the monastery of Latiniac; for the monastery of Micy; etc., CXLI, 898, 936.

ROBERTUS of Tumbalena, abbot of St. Vigor, 1092. 1. Two books of commentaries on the Song of Songs. 2. Letter to the monks of St. Michael of the Mount concerning a certain epileptic monk converted from fickleness, CL, 1360.

ROBERTUS, monk of St. Remigius in the diocese of Rheims, 1120. Nine books of *History of Jerusalem*, CLV, 668.

ROBERTUS PORCARIUS of Mahumeria, twelfth century. Privilege for the monastery of the Holy Sepulchre, CLV, 1225.

ROBERTUS of Mont, twelfth century. Supplement to Sigebert, CLVI, 1237.

ROBERTUS (St), first abbot of Molesme and founder of the Cistercian Order, 1110. Letters to Duke Odo and to the Cistercian brethren, CLVII, 1256.

ROBERTUS of Arbrissel, founder of the Order of Fontevraud, 1117. 1. Charter of the abbey of Grandmont. 2. Rules of the nuns of Fontevraud, 1117. 3. Two diplomas for all the monasteries, both of men and of nuns, situated in his diocese, concerning a monastery situated in the district of Caen which he grants to Lord Gerard of Salis. 4. Agreement between the monastery of the Holy Sepulchre at Sully and the monastery of Fontevraud, CLXII, 1017.

ROBERTUS PULLUS, cardinal and chancellor, 1153. Seven books of *Sentences*: concerning God and his attributes; the creation of the world, angels, and the first human being; sin; grace; Christ’s Incarnation; the efficacy of Christ’s death; the various circumstances of Christ’s life, death, and resurrection; the sacraments; etc., CLXXXVI, 625.

ROBERTUS, dean of Chartres, twelfth century. Letter to [Col. 0636] Suger concerning Hugh of Breteuil and Ebrard, viscount, CLXXXVI, 1401.

ROBERTUS of Ketton, 1157. Preface to the book of the Law of the Saracens, which they call the *Alcoran*, translated by him, addressed to Lord Peter, abbot of Cluny, CLXXXIX, 658, 1073.

ROBERTUS of Péronne, twelfth century. Letter to Lambert, bishop of Arras, CLXII, 653.

ROBERTUS of Blodo, twelfth century. Gift concerning his customary dues, CLXII, 1116.

ROBERTUS, archdeacon of Oxford, later bishop of Hereford, twelfth century. Letter to Gilbert, bishop of London, CXV, 1019.

ROBERTUS, count of Leicester, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Alexander III, requesting his protection for the monastery of Lyre, CC, 1390.

ROBERTUS of Torigni, abbot of St. Michael’s in Peril of the Sea, 1186. 1. Book on the deeds of Henry I, king of the English. 2. Continuation of Sigebert’s chronicle. 3. Two letters: to Gervase, prior of St. Serenicus; to Roger, abbot of Bec. 4. Treatise on the change of the monastic order. 5. Prologue to an abridgment, according to Augustine, of the exposition of the Apostle’s Epistles, CCII, 1306.

ROBERTUS, abbot of Saint-Germain-des-Prés, c. 1194. Diploma concerning the resignation made to the bishop of Paris by Emelina, a Parisian woman, CCV, 914.

RODERICUS, 1138. Privilege concerning the gift of a certain village called Passerel, with thirty-one *casalia* (smallholdings), CLV, 1180.

RODHMUNDUS, bishop of Autun, tenth century. Letters concerning the chapel of Centissa, granted to two clerics, CXXXII, 472.

RODULFUS, king of Burgundy, 1019. Precept concerning Chavigny, Blénosc, St. Victor, and other chapels; charter concerning St. Blaise at Viculis, CXLII, 1039, 1041.

RODULFUS III, surnamed the Pious, king of the Burgundians, 1032. Three diplomas: for the monastery of St. Andrew at Vienne; to Amizo, archbishop of Tarentaise; for the monastery of Cluny, CLI, 1021.

RODULFUS GLABER, monk of Cluny, 1048. 1. Five books of histories of his own time, from the election of the most powerful Hugh Capet as king to the year 1046. 2. Life of St. William, abbot of Dijon, CXLII, 609.

RODULFUS, abbot of St. Trond, 1138. 1. Deeds of the abbots of St. Trond. 2. Four letters of Rodulfus and others to him: to the monastery of St. Pantaleon; to Duke Waleram; to Stephen, bishop of Metz. 3. Life of Lietbert, bishop of Cambrai. 4. Account of the translation of St. Gereon, one soldier of the Theban Legion, CLXXIII, 12 ff., 434.

RODULFUS, bishop of Bourges, 866. Forty-five chapters concerning faith in the Holy Trinity; the honor and restoration of churches; Mass; ecclesiastical vestments; the life and conduct of priests; hospitality; priests’ preaching; parishioners; tithes to be given by the faithful; the Lord’s Prayer and the Creed; observance of the Lord’s Day; public penance; etc., CXIX, 700.

RODULFUS, monk and disciple of Peter the Venerable, 1154. Ninth Life of Peter the Venerable, abbot of Cluny, CLXXXIX, 15.

ROGERIUS, Italian jurist, 1075. On various prescriptions, CXLVI, 1486.

ROGERIUS, monk of Bec, 1090. Poem on contempt for the world, CL, 1431.

ROGERIUS, bishop of Ramla, 1136. Privilege concerning the gift and grant of the *casalia* of Capharut, Gith, Kefrescilta, and Porphilia, CLV, 1171.

ROGERIUS, king of Sicily, twelfth century. Letter to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1415.

ROGERIUS of Pontigny, monk, c. 1175. Life of St. Thomas, archbishop and martyr of Canterbury, CXC, 56.

ROGERIUS, monk of Crowland, twelfth century. Eighth Life of St. Thomas, archbishop and martyr of Canterbury, CXC, 258.

ROGERIUS, bishop of Worcester, twelfth century. Letter to the chapter of Canterbury, CXC, 1010.

ROGERIUS, formerly prior of St. Abraham’s, twelfth century. Letter to Geoffrey, subprior of St. Barbara’s in Neustria: he congratulates him on what he had written concerning the vision of God and exhorts him to humility, CCV, 851.

ROGERIUS, archbishop of Bourges, 1345. Translation of the body of St. Odilo, CXLII, 1048.

ROGERUS, abbot of Saint-Maur-des-Fossés, 1175. Diploma concerning the resignation made to the bishop of Paris by Garnerius of Domibus, CCV, 908.

ROGERUS, archbishop of York, 1180. Letter [Col. 0637] to Pope Alexander III concerning Gilbert, bishop of London, CC, 1398.

ROGERUS, abbot of St. Evurtius at Orléans, c. 1180. Revelation sent by Roger to the monks of St. Ouen at Rouen concerning the discovery of that same most holy bishop Evurtius, CXCIX, 1125.

ROHINGUS and his wife Bebelina, 726. Charter by which they give Bishop Willibrord the church of Saints Peter and Paul at Antwerp, LXXXIX, 553.

ROLANDUS, subdeacon of the Roman Church, 1182. Letter to Pope Lucius III concerning the affair of the bishopric of St. Andrew’s in Scotland, CCI, 1379.

ROMANUS, pope, 897. Two letters: to Riculfus, bishop of Elne; to the servant-of-God, bishop of Girona, CXXIX, 860.

ROMARICUS, count of Habendum, 620. Charter by which Romaricus founds a monastery of nuns near Habendum Castle, LXXX, 461.

ROMUALDUS (St), abbot and founder of the Camaldolese Order, 1027. Fragment of an exposition of Psalm 68 attributed to St. Romuald, CXL, 1120.

RORICO, bishop of Laon, 961. Constitution concerning the restoration of monks at the monastery of St. Vincent, CXXXIII, 952.

RORICO, monk of Moissac near Cahors, c. 1004. Deeds of the Franks from the origin of that people down to the death of King Clovis I, CXXXIX, 590.

ROTBERTUS, bishop of London, 1045. Charter of Rotbert, CXLI, 1441.

ROTGERIUS, count of Foix, twelfth century. Letter to Hugh of Cluny, to whom he grants the place of St. Saturninus of Pradelac to be formed by monastic institutions, CLIX, 940.

ROTHADUS II, bishop of Soissons, 867. Little book of appeal which he presented to Pope Nicholas after he had already waited six months at Rome, CXIX, 745.

ROTRODUS, archbishop of Rouen, 1181. Four letters: to the king of England; to Pope Alexander; to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 672 ff.; to William, archbishop of Sens, CCVII, 96.

ROUDWALDUS, 865. Donation for the monastery of St. Peter, CXXXVI, 1240.

RUALENUS, prior, twelfth century. Letter to the archbishop of Tours concerning direction, love, and charity, CXCVI, 1618.

RUDOLPHUS I, Augustus Caesar, 1273. Three books of letters, XCVIII, 701 ff.

RUDOLPHUS, scholar and disciple of Rabanus Maurus, ninth century. Life of Blessed Rabanus Maurus, CVII, 40.

RUDOLPHUS, bishop of Liège, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 175.

RUFINUS, priest of Aquileia, 410. 1. Two books on the blessings of the patriarchs. 2. Commentary on the Apostles’ Creed. 3. History of the monks, or book on the lives of the Fathers. 4. Two books of ecclesiastical history. Two books of apologies to St. Jerome. 5. Second apology to Pope Anastasius. Commentary on seventy-five Psalms. Commentary on Hosea, Joel, and Amos. Life of St. Eugenia. Two little books on faith, XXI, 9 ff.

RUFINUS, bishop of an uncertain see, 1056. Two books on the good of peace, CL, 1592.

RUPERTUS, abbot of Deutz, 1135. 1. Forty-two books of commentaries on the works of the Holy Trinity: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, the Book of Judges, the Book of Kings, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, the Four Evangelists, and the works of the Holy Spirit. 2. Commentaries on the Twelve Minor Prophets. 3. Seven books on the Song of Songs, concerning the Incarnation of the Lord. 4. Commentary on Job. 5. Commentary on Ecclesiastes. 6. Thirteen books on the glory and honor of the Son of Man through Matthew. 7. Hymn, or prayer, to the Holy Spirit. 8. On the glorification of the Trinity and the procession of the Holy Spirit. 9. Commentaries on the Gospel of St. John. 10. Commentaries on the Apocalypse. 11. On the victory of the Word of God. 12. Twelve books on the divine offices. 13. On the burning of the town of Deutz. 14. On meditation upon death. 15. Life of St. Heribert, archbishop of Cologne. 16. Passion of St. Eliphius the martyr. 17. On the will of God. 18. On the omnipotence of God. 19. On certain chapters of the Rule of St. Benedict. 20. Debate between a monk and a cleric on whether a monk may preach. 21. Letter on the same matter to Everard, abbot of Brauweiler. 22. On the violation of virginity and whether a defiled woman can be consecrated. 23. *The Ring*, or Dialogue between a Christian and a Jew. 24. On the truly apostolic life. 25. Letter on the reason why the monastic order surpasses the clerical order. 26. Chronicle of St. Lawrence at Liège, CLVII, CLXVIII, CLXLX [as printed], CLXX.

RURICIUS, bishop of Limoges, 480. Sixty-four letters: to Bishop Faustus; to Hesperius; to the priest Nepotianus; to Bishop Bassulus; to Bishop Sidonius; to Bishop Eonius; to Abbot Pomerium; to Bishop Cronopius; to Bishop Eufrasius; to Bishop Caesarius; to Apollinaris; etc., LVIII, 68.

RUSTICUS HELPIDIUS, former illustrious quaestor, 520. 1. Poems on the history of the Old and New Testaments. 2. Poem on the benefits of Christ Jesus, LXII, 543.

RUSTICUS, deacon of the Holy Roman Church, 549. Disputation against the Acephali, LXVII, 1166.

## S

SALOMON, bishop of Constance, 920. Verses to Bishop Dado, approximately 600 verses, CXXXII, 562.

SALONIUS, bishop of Vienne, 453. 1. Mystical exposition of the Proverbs of Solomon. 2. Mystical exposition of Ecclesiastes. 3. Letter to Pope St. Leo, LIII, 1012; LIV, 887.

SALVIANUS (St), priest of Marseille, 496. 1. Eight books on the governance of God. 2. Nine letters: to Eucherius; Agriccius; Socer and Socra; Cattura; Limenius; Aprus and Verus; Eucherius; Salonius. 3. Four books against Avarice, LIII, 9 ff.

SAMSON, priest of Worcester, twelfth century. Letter to Anselm, archbishop of Canterbury, CLIX, 249.

SAMSON, archbishop of Rheims, twelfth century. Three letters: to St. Bernard concerning the condition of the monastery of Mores, in the diocese of Langres, CLXXXII, 693; to Suger, asking him to endeavor to aid him against the burgesses of St. Remigius, CLXXXVI, 1360; to Suger, asking whether he will come to the assembly summoned at Soissons for affairs of the realm, CLXXXVI, 1388.

SAMUEL THE MOROCCAN, a Christian converted from Judaism, 1085. Book on the coming of the Messiah, whom the Jews rashly expect, CXLIX, 334.

SANCIA, queen of Portugal, 1134. Charter in favor of St. Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, CLXXXV, 982.

SAULUS, bishop of Córdoba, 869. Letter to Bishop Alterus, CXXI, 467.

SCARILA, author uncertain, sixth century. Letter to Fulgentius concerning the Incarnation of the Son of God and the author of lowly animals, LXV, 377.

SCOTUS JOANNES, Eriugena, 872. 1. Expositions on St. Dionysius’s *Celestial Hierarchy*. 2. Expositions on St. Dionysius’s *Ecclesiastical Hierarchy*. 3. Expositions, or glosses, on St. Dionysius’s *Mystical Theology*. 4. Homily on the prologue of the Holy Gospel according to John. 5. Three fragments of commentaries on the Holy Gospel according to John. 6. Book on predestination. 7. Five books on the division of nature. 8. Book on the departure and return of the soul to God. 9. Translation of the works of St. Dionysius the Areopagite: *On the Celestial Hierarchy*, *On the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy*, *On the Divine Names*, *Mystical Theology*, and the Letters of St. Dionysius. 10. Translation of St. Maximus’s *Ambigua*. 11. Approximately 800 verses: on Christ crucified; on the Cross; on Easter; praises of Irmintrud, wife of Charles the Bald; on Christ’s resurrection; Christ’s descent into hell and resurrection; on the Incarnate Word; Christ’s triumph over death and the devil; etc. Greek verses. 12. Fourth fragment of commentaries on the Holy Gospel according to John, CXXII, 2 ff.

SCOTTUS MARIANUS. See MARIANUS.

SEBASTIANUS, bishop of Salamanca, ninth century. Chronicle published under the name of Alfonso III, from the time of King Wamba down to the present time of the glorious King García, son of Alfonso, CXXIX, 1112.

SECUNDINUS, Manichaean, 405. Letter to Augustine, XX, 247; XLII, 571.

SECUNDINUS, Irish bishop, 490. Hymn in praise of St. Patrick, still living, LXI, 1081; LIII, 837.

SEDATUS, bishop of Béziers, c. 590. Homily on the Epiphany; two sermons attributed to St. Sedatus, LXXII, 769.

SEDULIUS COELIUS, poet, 392. 1. Easter poem divided into five books, 1,733 hexameter verses. 2. Elegy on Christ, 110 verses. 3. Hymn, “From the region of the rising sun,” 92 verses. 4. Epigram, XIX, 434.

SEDULIUS SCOTUS, 820. 1. Collections on all the Epistles of Blessed Paul. 2. Brief explanation of the distinction between breviaries, chapters, and canons. 3. Introduction to Matthew; brief exposition of the introduction according to Matthew. 4. Introduction to Mark; brief explanation of the introduction according to Mark. 5. Introduction to Luke; brief explanation of the introduction according to Luke. 6. Book on Christian Rulers and the fitting rules by which the commonwealth ought rightly to be governed. [Col. 0639] 7. Explanations of St. Jerome’s prefaces to the Gospels, CIII, 9 ff.

SEHERUS, abbot of Chaumousey, 1118. Two books on the beginnings of the monastery of Chaumousey, of the Order of St. Augustine in the diocese of Toul, CLXII, 1120.

SEIFRIDUS, abbot of the monastery of Tegernsee, 1048. Six letters: to Bishop N., sending two of his brethren and promising his own arrival; to Bishop W., excusing the longer delay in copying his uncertain manuscripts; to Widerad, abbot of Fulda, lamenting the wretched condition of the church of Fulda; to Emperor Henry concerning the monastery of Tegernsee; to Sigefrid, archbishop of Mainz, congratulating him on his return from exile; etc., CXLII, 720.

SERAPION, Egyptian monk, fourth century. Rule for monks, in St. Benedict, abbot of Aniane, CIII, 433.

SERGIUS, date uncertain. Life of St. Macarius the Roman, LXXIII, 416.

SERGIUS I, pope, 700. 1. Letter to Ceolfrid, abbot of the monastery of Saints Peter and Paul at Wearmouth and Jarrow, concerning the sending of the Venerable Bede to Rome. 2. Privilege given by Pope Sergius I to Heron, bishop of Langres, LXXXIX, 9 ff.

SERGIUS, Pope II, A.D. 847. Letter to the bishops beyond the Alps concerning the primacy of Drogo, vicar of the Apostolic See, CVI, 906. Letter to Ansgar, bishop of Hamburg, granting him the pallium and confirming what has already been bestowed upon his church by the faithful of Christ, etc., CXXIX, 997.

SERGIUS, Pope III, A.D. 911. Nine letters and privileges: for the monastery of St. Gall; to Amelius of Uzès, informing him that Pope Formosus had been condemned by him; for the church of Silva Candida; to Adalgar of Hamburg, asserting the rights of the Church of Bremen; for the chapter of Asti, confirming its possessions; to Leopardus, abbot of Nonantola, confirming the monastery’s privileges; for the Church of Vienne, confirming its possessions and privileges; to Hogerius, bishop of Hamburg, sending him the pallium; for the monastery of St. Martin of Tours, CXXXI, 972.

SERGIUS IV, Pope, A.D. 1012. Sixteen letters and diplomas: to Andrew, bishop of Poreč, securing to him possession of the parish of Ravenna and of two castles; to Vedianus, granting him the castle of Scure under the title of emphyteusis; concerning the foundation of the parish church of St. Michael near the monastery of Nonantola in the territory of Modena; concerning the monastery of Cuxa; for the monastery of Ripoll; concerning the monastery of St. Peter of Fernilot; for the monastery of Canigou; concerning the monastery of Arles; for the monastery of Montmajour; for the Church of Bamberg; for the monastery of St. Vincent on the Volturno; for the monastery of Bellilocum, CXXXIX, 1500.

SERVATUS LUPUS. See LUPUS.

SEULFUS, archbishop of Rheims, A.D. 928. Council of Rheims, in which penance was imposed upon those who had taken part in the war of Soissons between Kings Robert and Charles, CXXXII, 1063.

SEVERUS of Majorca, A.D. 418. Letter concerning the Jews, XX, 732.

SEVERUS, rhetorician and poet, fourth century. Bucolic poem on the power of the sign of the Lord’s cross, 132 verses, XIX, 796.

SEVERUS, bishop of Milevis, A.D. 430. Letter to Augustine, professing that he derives the greatest delight and profit from reading Augustine, XXXIII, 418.

SEVERUS, bishop, uncertain year. Letter to the whole Church concerning miracles effected for the conversion of the Jews on the island of Minorca in the presence of the relics of St. Stephen, XLI, 821.

SIBERTUS, monk, A.D. 1124. Letter to Rodulf, abbot of St. Trond, concerning the monastery of St. Pantaleon, CLXXIII, 193.

SIBILLA, abbess of Holy Cross, A.D. 1104. Grant made to the abbey of Fontevraud, CLXII, 1095.

SICARDUS, bishop of Cremona, A.D. 1225. 1. *Mitrale*, or summa on ecclesiastical offices, ten books. 2. Chronicle from the death of Pompey to the year 1221, CCXIII, 9 ff.

SICHELMUS, duke, A.D. 663. Charter concerning the monastery of Bèze, LXXXVIII, 1167.

SICHIMUNDUS, archpriest of Lucca, A.D. 729. Foundation of a hospice in the suburb of the city of Lucca. Donation of certain fiefs to the Church of St. Peter at Lucca, LXXXVII, 1372, 1373.

SIDONIUS, confessor, A.D. 251. Letter to Cyprian, III, 675.

SIDONIUS APOLLINARIS, bishop of the Arverni, A.D. 482. 1. One hundred and forty-seven letters, in nine books: to Constantius; Agricola; Philimatius; Gaudentius; Heronius; Eutropius; Vincentius; Domitius; Syagrius; Petronius; Avitus; Apollinaris; [Col. 0640] Felix; Evodius; Sapaudus; Bishop Lupus; Bishop Leontius; Pope Eleutherius; Bishop Mamertus; etc. 2. Twenty-four poems: Preface to the panegyric delivered before Anthemius Augustus, twice consul; panegyric delivered at Rome by Sidonius before Anthemius Augustus, twice consul; publication of the panegyrics, addressed to Peter; preface to the panegyric delivered before Majorian Augustus; panegyric delivered before Julius Valerius Majorian Augustus; preface to the panegyric delivered at Rome before his father-in-law Avitus Augustus; panegyric delivered before his father-in-law Avitus Augustus; apology addressed to Felix, a man of illustrious rank; epithalamium for Ruricius and Iberia; epigram by which he sought from Emperor Majorian a remedy for his three heads; epithalamium for Polemius and Araneola; poem of thanksgiving addressed to Faustus, bishop of Riez; etc.—about 3,900 verses, LVIII, 435.

SIGEBALDUS, king of the Saxons, A.D. 732. Letter to Boniface, bishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 723.

SIGEBERT, Saint, king of the Franks, A.D. 656. 1. Two letters to St. Desiderius, bishop of Cahors. 2. Four diplomas: concerning the monastery of Cazagonguidin; concerning the monasteries of Stavelot and Malmedy; for the Church of St. Peter at Trier; for the Church of Speyer, LXXX, 302, 260, 264.

SIGEBERT, monk of Gembloux, A.D. 1112. 1. *Chronicles*, with all continuations. 2. Book concerning ecclesiastical writers. 3. Deeds of the abbots of Gembloux. 4. Life of St. Wibert, a monk formerly a layman and founder of the monastery of Gembloux. 5. Life of Theoderic, bishop of Metz. 6. Life of St. Sigebert, king. 7. Life of St. Maclovius, or Machutus, bishop and confessor. 8. Life of St. Theodard, bishop of Maastricht and martyr. 9. Twofold Life of St. Lambert, bishop of Maastricht and martyr at Liège in Belgium. 10. Sermon on St. Lucy. 11. Letter on the distinction of the four seasons, written for the clergy of Trier under the name of the people of Liège. 12. Letter to the people of Liège. 13. On married priests. 14. Reply to Hildebrand’s letter written to Herman of Metz in disparagement of royal authority. 15. Fragment of a rhythmical poem on St. Lucy. 16. Fragment concerning St. Lull, CLX, 9 ff.; LXXXVIII, 304.

SIGEFRID, bishop of Mainz, A.D. 1073. Three letters to Pope Alexander II: concerning King Henry, whom he says he confronted to his face and threatened with excommunication; concerning Charles, bishop-elect of Constance, that he should punish most severely the monstrous murder of Cuno, archbishop of Trier; etc., CXLVI, 1430. Letter to Hildebrand, archdeacon of the Roman Church, CXLVIII, 735. Three letters to Pope Gregory VII, CXLVIII, 736 ff., 1432.

SIGEHARDUS, monk of St. Maximin at Trier, about A.D. 963. On the miracles of St. Maximin, CXXXIII, 965.

SIGIBAUDUS, bishop of Metz, A.D. 708. Charter by which Sigibaud, bishop of Metz, and Count Wolfund exchange estates with one another, LXXXVIII, 1252.

SIGLOARDUS, canon of Rheims, ninth century. Rhythmical poem on the death of Fulk, bishop of Rheims, CXXIX, 1145.

SILVANUS, delegate of the Synod of Lampsacus, A.D. 366. Letter to Pope Liberius, VIII, 1377.

SILVANUS, African bishop, A.D. 410. Two letters to the tribune Marcellinus concerning Donatist bishops, XXXIII, 487, 490.

SILVERIUS, Pope, A.D. 536. Two letters: to Vigilius, the false pope, whom he condemns by a sentence of anathema; and to Amator, whose charity he praises, setting forth the actions taken against himself and discussing the inadmissibility of false witnesses against a bishop, LXVI, 85.

SIMON, count, A.D. 1076. Letter to Hugh, abbot of Cluny, to whom he gives the abbey of St. Arnulf of Crépy, CLIX, 966.

SIMON, prior of Mont-Dieu, twelfth century. Two letters to Pope Alexander concerning the restoration of concord between the king and the archbishop of Canterbury, CC, 1436, 1437.

SIMON, count of Leicester, lord of Montfort, A.D. 1209. Letter to Innocent III concerning the defeat of heretics, CCXVI, 141.

SIMPERT, Saint, abbot of Murbach, A.D. 809. 1. Monastic regulations of Murbach. 2. Encyclical letter. 3. Memorandum to a bishop, XCIX, 746, 738.

SIMPLICIUS, Pope, A.D. 467. Nineteen letters of Pope Simplicius and others addressed to him: to Zeno, bishop of Split, whom he appoints vicar of the Apostolic See; to John, bishop of Ravenna, whom he reproves because he had forcibly ordained Gregory bishop; to Florentius, Equitius, and Severus, bishops, concerning the orders of Gaudentius, bishop of Aufinium, on account of unlawful ordinations performed; to Acacius, bishop of Constantinople, that he should oppose Timothy by every effort, lest the ecumenical council which Timothy was pressing for with the emperor should be held; to the same, concerning observance of the decrees of the Council of Chalcedon; to the priests and archimandrites of Constantinople concerning Timothy, whom they had not admitted to communion; to Emperor Zeno, congratulating him on the recovery of his empire and exhorting him to restore the bishop of Alexandria to his see; etc., LVIII, 32.

SIRICIUS, Saint, Pope, A.D. 398. Six letters and decrees: to Himerius, bishop of Tarragona, on Arians not to be rebaptized; the times and rites for receiving baptism; apostates to be separated from the Church; marriage; rules for penitents; monks and virgins not maintaining their profession; clerical incontinence; the age of candidates for ordination; etc. To Anysius, bishop of Thessalonica, that no one in Illyricum be ordained bishop without Anysius’s consent. To the bishops of Africa concerning the qualifications of candidates for ordination. To various bishops concerning the qualifications of bishops and priests to be ordained; to various bishops against the heretic Jovinian and his associates, who are to be removed from the unity of the Church; etc., XIII, 1116.

SISEBUTHUS, king of the Goths, A.D. 621. 1. Eight letters of Sisebuth and others addressed to him: to Caecilius, bishop of Mentesa, when he had withdrawn into a monastery; to Caesarius, patrician; to Theudilan, upon his conversion from lay dress to monastic life; to Advalvald, king of the Lombards, and to Theodelinda, their queen, concerning the faith of Christ. 2. Life and Passion of St. Desiderius, LXXX, 364.

SIVIARDUS, fifth abbot of Anisole, uncertain year. Life of St. Carilefus, priest and monk, first abbot of Anisole, LXXIV, 1248.

SIXTUS II, Pope, A.D. 258. 1. Two doubtful letters, concerning bishops accused or condemned. 2. Two decrees, concerning appeal, V, 84, 89.

SIXTUS III, Saint, Pope, or Xystus, A.D. 440. Ten letters and decrees of Sixtus III and others addressed to him: letter to Cyril, praising his pious petition against Nestorius’s followers; letter to Cyril on his own ordination, concerning John of Antioch and the other associates of Nestorius; to Cyril of Alexandria after peace had been made between Cyril himself and John; to John of Antioch concerning his return; to Perigenes, bishop of the Corinthians, concerning Anastasius, bishop of Thessalonica, from whose authority he ought not to withdraw himself; etc., L, 571.

SMARAGDUS, abbot, A.D. 820. 1. Collections on the Epistles and Gospels. 2. *Diadem of Monks*. 3. Commentaries on the Rule of St. Benedict. 4. *Royal Way*. 5. Proceedings of the Roman conference recorded by Smaragdus, abbot of St. Michael, CII, 9 ff.

SMARAGDUS, monk of St. Maximin, A.D. 900. Preface to an exposition of the Psalms, CXXIX, 1022.

SMERA J., Polovetsian, A.D. 990. Letter to Vladimir, king of the Rus’, CLI, 1406.

SONNATIUS, Saint, archbishop of Rheims, A.D. 625. Twenty-one statutes, LXXX, 442.

SOPHIA, daughter of Rainfred, twelfth century. Gift concerning Ripes and other places in the diocese of Tours, CLXII, 1105.

SOPHIA, abbess at Kitzingen, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, asking whether she ought to abandon the burden that she bears, CXCVII, 322.

SOPHRONIUS, bishop of Jerusalem, A.D. 640. Life of St. Mary of Egypt, the harlot, LXXIII, 872.

SOTHERUS, Pope, A.D. 177. Decrees concerning the faith. Letter to the bishops of Italy, concerning monks among them touching sacred vessels or consecrated altar-cloths, CXXX, 118.

SOUCELINA, abbess of St. Cyricus, A.D. 1190. Concerning meadows sold on the island of Mere, CCV, 912.

SPECIOSUS, bishop of Florence, A.D. 724. Donation to the church and canons of St. John the Baptist in Florentine territory, LXXXVII, 1402.

SPERAINDEO, abbot, uncertain year. Letter to Alvarus of Córdoba against certain heretics who deny in God the Trinity of persons in unity of substance, and the divinity in Christ, CXV, 960; CXXI, 462.

STEPHEN, Saint, I, Pope and martyr, A.D. 257. Two decretal letters attributed to St. Stephen: to Bishop Hilary, concerning ordinations and ecclesiastical vestments; to all bishops, concerning accusations against priests, the expulsion of bishops, etc., III, 984, 997.

STEPHEN, Saint, abbot, about A.D. 590. Rule for monks, LXVI, 950.

STEPHEN, abbot, A.D. 590. Letter to St. Aunarius, bishop of Auxerre, who had asked him to describe the illustrious deeds of the flourishing lives of Germanus and Amator, LXXII, 769.

STEPHEN II, Pope, A.D. 752. Thirteen letters and decrees: to Pippin, king of the Franks; to the nobles of the Franks; to the Franks; to King Pippin and to Charles and Carloman; to Abbot Fulrad. Revelation of Stephen, attesting that he had been divinely delivered through the aid of St. Dionysius when he was afflicted by a fatal disease in that saint’s monastery; etc., LXXXIX, 960; XCVIII, 100.

[Col. 0642] STEPHEN III, Pope, A.D. 771. Five letters: to Queen Bertrada, consecrated to God, concerning Itherius, the royal envoy, who performed vigorous service in the duchy of Benevento for the interests of the Church; to Queen Bertrada and King Charles concerning Christopher and his son Sergius, who, with Dodo and the other Franks, attempted to kill Pope Stephen; to Kings Charles and Carloman, congratulating them on their reconciliation to brotherly concord and requesting their aid against the Lombards; to the same, that neither of them should take Desiderius’s daughter as wife; etc.; to King Carloman, that he might become his spiritual co-father, LXXXIX, 1236; XCVIII, 245.

STEPHEN IV, Pope, A.D. 817. Bull for the monastery of Farfa, CXXIX, 973; CII, 1072.

STEPHEN V, Pope, A.D. 891. Thirty-two letters, diplomas, and privileges: letter to Emperor Basil, reproving him for defending Photius; to Count Guy; diploma for the monastery of Corbie; letter to the eastern bishops concerning the ordination of Stephen, patriarch of Constantinople; to Leutbert, bishop of Mainz; to Dominic, archbishop of Ravenna; to the clergy and people of Piacenza; to the bishops of the province of Cologne; privilege for the Church of Piacenza; privilege for the monastery of St. Liudger; etc., CXXIX, 786.

STEPHEN VI, Pope, A.D. 897. Three letters and privileges: letter to Arnustus, archbishop of Narbonne, concerning the archbishopric of Narbonne; to Aribert, archbishop of Narbonne, concerning Jews who had obtained authority to possess freehold estates; privilege for the monastery of Vézelay, CXXIX, 854.

STEPHEN, bishop of Liège, A.D. 920. Life of St. Lambert, bishop of Maastricht-on-the-Meuse and martyr, CXXXII, 642.

STEPHEN VII, Pope, A.D. 930. Two letters and privileges: bull for the monastery of St. Vincent on the Volturno; privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Brogne, CXXXII, 1052.

STEPHEN VIII, Pope, A.D. 942. Two letters and privileges: privilege for the monastery of Tolla in the diocese of Piacenza; privilege for the convent of St. Mary of Buxières, CXXXII, 1089.

STEPHEN, bishop of Halberstadt, eleventh century. Letter against schismatics, CXLVIII, 1414.

STEPHEN, Saint, first king of the Hungarians, A.D. 1038. 1. Admonitions to his Son. 2. Laws of St. Stephen. 3. Privilege granted to the proto-abbey of St. Martin in Pannonia, CLI, 1204, 1234.

STEPHEN X, Pope, A.D. 1058. Eight letters and privileges: letter to Gervasius, archbishop of Rheims, promising aid to one who acts steadfastly on behalf of religion; bull concerning the secular clergy, declaring them exempt from the courts and burdens of secular powers; concerning the monastery of St. Peter at Perugia; concerning the canons of Arezzo; for the monastery of St. Prosper of Reggio; to the brethren of the monastery of Cluny; concerning the monastery of Cluny, CXLIII, 866.

STEPHEN, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, A.D. 1068. 1. Council of Tours. 2. Letter to John, bishop of Dol, that he should attend the Roman synod of Nicholas II after Easter. 3. Council of Bordeaux, at which Stephen asserts for the monks of Vendôme the cell of St. Clement of Credon, CXLIII, 1408.

STEPHEN OF CHALMET, monk of the Carthusian monastery of Les Portes, twelfth century. Letter on perseverance in the order, to the novices of St. Sulpice of the Cistercian Order, CLIII, 932.

STEPHEN, abbot of St. James at Liège, A.D. 1110. Extract from the miracles of St. Modoald, CLIV, 1276.

STEPHEN, Saint, third abbot of Cîteaux, A.D. 1133. 1. Critical judgment on certain passages of the Bible. 2. Sermon at the death of his predecessor. 3. Two letters, to King Louis surnamed the Fat and to Pope Honorius. 4. Charter of Charity. 5. Earlier customs of the Cistercian Order. 6. Account of the origin of the monastery and Order of Cîteaux, CLXVI, 1361.

STEPHEN OF BAUGÉ, bishop of Autun, A.D. 1136. 1. Treatise on the sacrament of the altar. 2. Five charters: settlement with Hugh of Gissey through Stephen, bishop of Autun; charter in favor of Ungy; charter for the monastery of St. Benignus at Dijon; for the Cistercians; etc., CLXXII, 1272.

STEPHEN, bishop of Paris, A.D. 1142. 1. Twelve letters of Stephen of Paris and others addressed to him: to Henry, archbishop of Sens; to the archpriests of the diocese of Paris; sentence of excommunication against the killers of Thomas, prior of St. Victor, and their supporters; to Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres, concerning the impious killing of Prior Thomas; letter to the Roman pontiff; etc. 2. Six diplomas and donations: charter for the canons of St. Mary of Paris; charter for the regular canons of St. Victor at Paris; charter concerning the church of St. Dionysius of the Prison; charter concerning the church of Fossatus; charter of foundation of the abbey [Col. 0643] of Meder, CLXXIII, 1400; CLXXIX, 665; CCVII, 1177.

STEPHEN, bishop of Metz, A.D. 1151. Four letters: to Wibald, abbot of Stavelot, concerning the monks of Hasteria; to Theoderic, abbot of Waulsort, concerning a man accused of squandering property, whom he summons before the synod of Metz; to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1346, 1347, 1397, 1431.

STEPHEN, Saint, of Muret, founder and institutor of the Grandmontine Order, A.D. 1192. 1. Book of sayings, or reasons. 2. Rule of St. Stephen, CCIV, 998.

STEPHEN OF LISIAC, fourth prior of Grandmont, A.D. 1161. Sayings and deeds of St. Stephen of Muret, CCIV, 1164.

STEPHEN, king of England, A.D. 1154. Letter to Suger concerning friendship and the benefits shown him at the court of the king of France, CLXXXVI, 1434.

STEPHEN, bishop of Meaux, twelfth century. Letter to Pope Alexander III on behalf of St. Thomas of Canterbury, CC, 1414.

STEPHEN, abbot of St. Geneviève in Paris, later bishop of Tournai, A.D. 1203. 1. Letters divided into three parts: the first containing twenty-eight letters written while he was abbot of St. Evurtius at Orléans, from about 1163 to 1177; the second containing 147 letters written while he was abbot of St. Geneviève in Paris, from 1177 to 1192; the third containing sixty-one letters written from 1192 to 1203. Supplement: thirty-two letters. 2. Certain synodal statutes. 3. Fragment from the office of St. Gerald. 4. Sermon delivered in a synod concerning married priests. 5. Proem to the *Summa on the Decrees*, CCXI, 295.

STEPHEN LANGTON, archbishop of Canterbury, A.D. 1221. Treatise on the translation of Blessed Thomas, CXC, 408.

STRABUS. See WALAFRIDUS.

STURMIUS, Saint, abbot of Fulda, A.D. 776. 1. Order of the office in the house of St. Benedict before Easter. 2. Ancient customs of monasteries of the Order of St. Benedict, LXXXIX, 1257.

SUAVIUS, abbot of St. Sever at the head of Gascony, A.D. 1107. 1. Nineteen statutes for the town of St. Sever, CLVII, 476. 2. Letter to Pope Paschal, CLXIII, 461.

SUGER, abbot of St. Denis, A.D. 1152. 1. Book concerning the deeds performed during his administration, in which many matters pertaining to the history of Louis the Fat and Louis the Younger are recorded. 2. Little book concerning the consecration of the church of St. Denis and the translation of the bodies of St. Denis and his companions. 3. Life of King Louis VI, called the Fat. 4. Lessons for the anniversary of King Louis. 5. One hundred and eighty-seven letters of Suger—to Pope Eugenius III, King Louis VII, and other leading men of France—and of these persons to Suger, composed concerning grave affairs while he administered the realm. 6. Testament of Abbot Suger. 7. Ten constitutions, CLXXXVI, 1152.

SULCARDUS, monk of Westminster, about A.D. 1100. Little book concerning the foundation of Westminster Abbey, CLV, 1633.

SULPICIUS SEVERUS, A.D. 303. 1. *Sacred History*, two books, from the creation of the world to his own time. 2. One book on the life of Blessed Martin. 3. Three letters: to Eusebius, priest, against those jealous of Blessed Martin’s virtues; to Aurelius, deacon, concerning the death and appearance of Blessed Martin; to his mother-in-law Bassula, on how Blessed Martin passed from this life into immortality. 4. Three Dialogues. In the appendix, seven letters: to his sister Claudia concerning the Last Judgment; to the same concerning virginity; to St. Paulinus, bishop, sending a cook fit to prepare food for monks; etc., XX, 80; LXXIII, 814. 5. Poems attributed to Sulpicius Severus, LXXIV, 672.

SULPICIUS, Saint, surnamed the Pious, bishop of Bourges, A.D. 640. Three letters: to Desiderius, bishop of the city of Cahors; to Verus, bishop of the city of Rodez; to Pope Desiderius, LXXX, 574.

SYLVESTER, Saint, Pope, A.D. 333. 1. Two fragments against the Jews, VIII, 814. 2. Decree of St. Sylvester, ibid., 819. 3. Two letters to the Synod of Nicaea, ibid., 823. 4. Roman council held under Pope Sylvester, ibid., 825. 5. Letter concerning *formatae* to be received from the bishop of Vienne, VIII, 848.

SYLVESTER (GERBERT), Pope II, A.D. 1003. 1. Little book on the division of numbers. 2. On geometry. 3. Letter to Adelbold concerning the reason for the difference of areas in an equilateral triangle. 4. Letter to Constantine, monk of Fleury, concerning the construction of a sphere. 5. Little book on the *rationale* and the use of reason. 6. Sermon on the instruction of bishops. 7. Little book on the body and blood of the Lord. 8. Gerbert’s profession of faith. 9. Extracts from the Council of Mouzon. 10. Council of Ravenna. 11. Roman Council. 12. Two hundred and six letters written before his elevation to the supreme pontificate; fifteen papal letters and decrees. 13. Five poems, CXXXIX, 57.

[Col. 0644] SYLVIUS ANNAEUS POMPEIUS. See ANNAEUS.

SYMMACHUS AURELIUS, prefect of the city, A.D. 384. Ten books of letters, XVIII, 141.

SYMMACHUS, Pope, A.D. 514. Twelve letters and decrees: to Aeonius, bishop of Arles, concerning his controversy with the bishop of Vienne; to Liberius, patrician, concerning the elected bishop of Aquileia; to Avitus, bishop of Vienne, concerning his case, which had neither been heard nor judged; to Maximinus of Padua, whose virtues are described; to Caesarius, bishop of Arles, answering his consultations; to Easterners, who request that he bring help to the Eastern churches afflicted by schism and receive them into communion—his answer to them; to the bishops of Gaul, concerning the Churches of Vienne and Arles; apologetic writings against the notorious pamphlet of Emperor Anastasius, which attacked the pontiff because he had pronounced a sentence of excommunication against him; to the confessors, bishops deported to Sardinia and other islands; to Theodore of Laureacum, granting him the use of the pallium; copy of a constitution repealing the law of King Odoacer, which conflicted with ecclesiastical liberty in the election of the pope, and concerning the preservation of Church property; decree concerning one who violates his spiritual and penitential daughter, LXII, 40, 80.

SYMPERT, Saint. See SIMPERT.

SYMPHOSIUS AMALARIUS, priest of Metz and chorepiscopus, A.D. 836. 1. Rule for canons compiled by Amalarius. 2. Rule for religious women compiled by Amalarius. 3. Four books on ecclesiastical offices, addressed to Emperor Louis the Pious. 4. Book on the order of the Antiphonary. 5. Eclogues on the office of the Mass. 6. Six letters: to Jeremiah, archbishop of Sens, concerning the name Jesus; to Bishop Jonas; to Bishop Rantgarius; to the monk Hetto; to Guntrad, CV, 816.

SYRUS, monk of Cluny, uncertain year. Life of St. Maiolus, abbot of Cluny, CXXXVII, 745.

## T

TAIO, bishop of Zaragoza, A.D. 646. 1. Letter to Eugenius, bishop of Toledo, concerning Pope St. Gregory. 2. Five books of *Sentences*, LXXXVII, 413.

TALESPERIANUS, bishop of Lucca, A.D. 725. Letters by which he grants to the priest Romuald, as a benefice, a small monastery with a hospice, LXXXVII, 1370.

TARASIUS, patriarch of Constantinople, eighth century. Apology addressed to the people of Constantinople, CXXIX, 202.

TARRA, monk, A.D. 600. Letter to King Reccared, LXXX, 20.

TELESPHORUS, Pope, A.D. 134. Decrees of Pope Telesphorus, CXXX, 104.

TERALDUS, tenth century. Letter to Guido, explaining why short verses are joined to antiphons on the feasts of Saints Paul and Lawrence, CXXXVIII, 185.

TERRICUS, grand master of the Templars, A.D. 1187. Two letters: to all the brethren of the Temple concerning the defeat of the Christians; to Henry, king of England, concerning the capture of Jerusalem, CCI, 1408.

TERTULLIAN, priest of Carthage, A.D. 245. 1. *Apology against the Pagans*. 2. Two books *To the Nations*. 3. On the testimony of the soul. 4. To the martyrs. 5. Book on spectacles. 6. Book on idolatry. 7. Book to Scapula. 8. Book on prayer. 9. Book on baptism against Quintilla. 10. Book on penance. 11. Book on patience. 12. Two books to his wife. 13. Two books on women’s dress. 14. Book on prescriptions against heretics. 15. Book on the soldier’s crown. 16. Book on flight in persecution. 17. *Scorpiace*, against the Gnostics. 18. Book against Praxeas. 19. Book against Hermogenes. 20. Five books against Marcion. 21. Book against the Valentinians. 22. Book against the Jews. 23. Book on the soul. 24. Book on the flesh of Christ. 25. Book on the resurrection of the flesh. 26. Book on the veiling of virgins. 27. Book exhorting to chastity. 28. Book on monogamy. 29. Book on fasts. 30. Book on modesty. 31. Book on the cloak, II, 111.

TEULFUS, monk of Morigny, A.D. 1147. Chronicle of Morigny, CLXXX, 132.

TEUTGAUDUS, archbishop of Trier, ninth century. Letter to King Charles the Bald, the bishops, and all others, on behalf of the priest Hegilo, making pilgrimage to the holy places, CXXIX, 1390.

TEUTHPALDUS, citizen of Lucca, A.D. 718. Diploma by which Teuthpald, Dommulus, and other pious citizens of Lucca build in the city of Lucca a sacred church under the name of St. Sylvester together with a hospice, LXXXVII, 1361.

THANGMARUS, priest of Hildesheim, A.D. 1025. Life of St. Bernward, bishop of Hildesheim, CXL, 386.

THEGANBALDUS, A.D. 801. Gift of Theganbald, XCIX, 803.

THEGANUS, chorepiscopus of the Church of Trier, A.D. 843. Life of Emperor Louis, CVI, 401.

[Col. 0645] THEOBALD, count of Chalon, about A.D. 960. Charter by which he confirmed the donation of the monastery of St. Marcellus of Chalon made to Maiolus, abbot of Cluny, CXXXVII, 780.

THEOBALD, count of Champagne, eleventh century. Count Theobald offers his son to be washed by Blessed Hugh in healing waters, CLIX, 943.

THEOBALD OF ÉTAMPES, A.D. 1119. Five letters: to the bishop of Lincoln concerning certain persons wavering in regard to Holy Scripture; to Faritius, abbot of Abingdon, concerning children who died without baptism; to Queen Margaret, offering himself to her; to Philip, a friend, whom he consoles; to Roscelin, cleric of Compiègne, whom he rebukes because he maintained that sons of priests ought not to be admitted to holy orders, CLXIII, 759.

THEOBALD, count of Blois, A.D. 1145. 1. Theobald’s confirmation concerning the gifts of Jobert of La Ferté, CLXXXV, 986. 2. Four letters to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1352, 1365, 1403, 1405. 3. Letter to Pope Alexander III concerning the martyrdom of St. Thomas, CC, 1447.

THEOBALD, archbishop of Canterbury, A.D. 1150. Letters and testament, CLXXXVIII, 1675; CXCIX, 30, 36.

THEODAHAD, king of the Ostrogoths, A.D. 536. Letter to Emperor Justinian, informing him that Amalasuntha had admitted him as partner in the kingdom and asking that he favor his case, LXIX, 797.

THEUDEBALD, king of the Franks, sixth century. Letter to Emperor Justinian, LXXI, 1165.

THEUDEBERT, king of the Franks, sixth century. Letter to Emperor Justinian, LXXI, 1164.

THEODERIC III, king of the Franks, A.D. 674. Seventeen ecclesiastical and monastic enactments: for the abbot of Fontenelle; for the monastery of Anisole; for the Church of Le Mans; for the monastery of Bèze; for Chramlinus, bishop of Embrun; for the monastery of Nobilacum; for the monastery of St. Denis; for the monasteries of Stavelot and Malmedy; for the monastery of Novy; etc., LXXXVII, 1320.

THEODERIC IV, king of the Franks, A.D. 730. Ten diplomas: for the monastery of Saint-Bertin; for the monastery of Anisole; for the Church of Le Mans; for the monastery of St. Denis; for the monastery of Maurus; for the monastery of Honau; for the monastery of St. Denis; for the monastery of Murbach; for the Church of St. Vincent at Paris, LXXXVIII, 1130.

THEODERIC, bishop of Metz, A.D. 984. 1. Epitaph of Count Evrard. 2. Discovery of saints found by Theoderic, bishop of Metz, and translated to the city of Metz, CXXXVII, 360.

THEODERIC, monk of St. Matthias at Trier, A.D. 1010. 1. Little book on the translation of St. Celsus, CLIV, 1234. 2. Life and Passion of Conrad, archbishop, CLIV, 1252.

THEODERIC, bishop of Chartres, eleventh century. Privilege for the monastery of Vendôme, written on the very day of its dedication, CLVII, 290.

THEODERIC, count of Flanders, A.D. 1142. Charter for the monastery of Clairvaux, CLXXXV, 983. He confirms before St. Bernard the customs of the chapter of St. Martin at Ypres, CLXXXV, 1826. Letter to Suger concerning Robert, the king’s brother, CLXXXVI, 1383.

THEODERIC, bishop of Amiens, A.D. 1148. Two letters to Suger, CLXXXVI, 1359, 1362.

THEODERIC, abbot of New Corbie, A.D. 1157. Letter concerning the writing of monastic chronicles, CLXXXIX, 1506.

THEODGAUDUS, primate of Belgic Gaul, A.D. 868. Letter to Hincmar concerning Hilduin, whom he declared unworthy of the pastoral office, CXXI, 381.

THEODGRIMUS, deacon, A.D. 821. Donation to the monastery of St. Saviour, XCIX, 819.

THEODO, Helvetian vendor, A.D. 730. Charter by which he sells to Murbach monastery his share in the district of Hamarisstad, LXXXVIII, 1285.

THEODORET, bishop of Cyrrhus, A.D. 458. 1. Extracts from the five books of Theodoret, XLVIII, 1064, 1068. 2. Letter to Pope St. Leo, commending his zeal against the Manichaeans and his letter to Flavian, and appealing to the Apostolic See; etc., LIV, 746. 3. Ninth book on the lives of the Fathers, called *Philotheus* or *Theophiles*, LXIV, 9.

THEODORIC, king of the Goths, A.D. 526. 1. Four enactments, LXXII, 1111. 2. Five books of letters, LXIX, 504 ff.

THEODORIC, canon of Paderborn, A.D. 1079. Commentary on the Lord’s Prayer, CXLVII, 332.

THEODORIC, monk of St. Ouen, A.D. 1090. Fragments of the metrical Life of St. Ouen, CL, 1188.

THEODORIC, abbot of St. Hubert at Andage, about A.D. 1107. Letter to the people of Liège, CLVII, 488; CLIV, 1428.

THEODORIC, duke of Lorraine, A.D. 1115. Letter [Col. 0646] to Pope Paschal II concerning the cell of Castiniacum, CLXIII, 468.

THEODORIC, monk, uncertain year. Life of St. Hildegard, abbess, CXCVII, 92.

THEODORITUS, bishop of Lignida, sixth century. Letter to Pope Hormisdas, congratulating him upon the union of the Churches, LXIII, 452.

THEODORE OF MOPSUESTIA, A.D. 458. Extracts from Theodore of Mopsuestia, XLVIII, 1052.

THEODORE, Saint, Pope, A.D. 648. Three letters: to Paul, patriarch of Constantinople, against Pyrrhus and his supporters; to the bishops who consecrated Paul patriarch of Constantinople because of Pyrrhus, formerly patriarch; privilege for the monastery of Bobbio, LXXXVII, 72; CXXIX, 578, 581.

THEODORE, Saint, the Studite, A.D. 826. Sermon on St. Bartholomew the Apostle, translated by Anastasius the Librarian, CXXIX, 730.

THEODORE, archbishop of Canterbury, seventh century. 1. *Penitential*, XCIX, 901. 2. Teaching concerning penance, defended against every suspicion of novelty, ibid., 1164.

THEODOSIUS THE GREAT, Augustus, A.D. 398. Constitution against heretics, XI, 1192.—Letter to Philip, prefect of Illyricum, by which the rights of the Church of Constantinople are extended over Illyricum, XX, 769. Letter to the Emperor Honorius concerning the privileges of the Roman bishop throughout Illyricum, XX, 770. Rescript on behalf of the priests Marcellinus and Faustinus, XIII, 109. Selected decrees concerning religion, XIII, 522.

THEODOSIUS II, Augustus, A.D. 450. Three letters: to Emperor Valentinian concerning the Council of Ephesus, which condemned Flavian; to Empress Galla Placidia concerning the same; to Licinia Eudoxia concerning the same, LIV, 876, 877.

THEODOSIUS, bishop of Caesarea in Bithynia, A.D. 662. Disputation between St. Maximus and Theodosius, bishop of Caesarea in Bithynia, CXXIX, 626.

THEODULF, bishop of Orléans, A.D. 821. 1. Chapters for the priests of his diocese. 2. Book on the order of baptism, addressed to Magnus of Sens. 3. On the Holy Spirit. 4. Fragments of several sermons. 5. Poems, seven books: exhortation to judges; verses at the beginning of the Bibles which he had copied; verses composed to be sung by boys on Palm Sunday; to the monks of St. Benedict; verses written in golden letters concerning St. Quentin; at the tomb of St. Nazarius; epitaph of Queen Fastrada; to King Charles; upon the tomb of Pope Hadrian; concerning a little fox flying upon a hen; concerning books which I used to read; concerning the seven liberal arts depicted in a certain painting; concerning a river that dried up; concerning the seven capital vices; etc. 6. *Mirror concerning Holy Scripture*, a small work doubtfully ascribed to Theodulf, CV, 188 ff.

THEOGER, bishop of Metz, A.D. 1119. *Music*, CLXIII, 770.

THEOPHILUS, delegate of the Synod of Lampsacus, A.D. 366. Letter to Pope Liberius, VIII, 1377.

THEOPHILUS, bishop of Alexandria, A.D. 420. Four letters: to Jerome concerning the Origenists; to Epiphanius concerning the same; to the bishops of Palestine and Cyprus, XXII, 755, 756, 758.

THEOPHILUS, uncertain year. Life of St. Macarius the Roman, LXXIII, 416.

THEOPHYLACIUS, archdeacon, A.D. 752. Two letters to Boniface, archbishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 782, 783.

THEOTMARUS, Archbishop of the Church of Juvavum, 905. Letter to Pope John IX, CXXXI, 34.

THEOTUINUS, Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, 1149. Four letters: to Henry, bishop of Minden; to King Henry; and to Thomas, archbishop of Canterbury, CLXXXIX, 1240; CXC, 982, 992.

THEUDOINUS, provost of Châlons, 868. Letter to Almannus, monk of Antivillare, on writing the Life of Saint Memmius, first bishop of Châlons, CXXI, 385.

THEUZO, hermit and monk of Saint Mary of Florence, 1057. Prologue to an exposition of the Rule of Saint Benedict the abbot, CXLIII, 844.

THIEBALDUS, provost of Xanten, 1149. Two letters to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1217, 1278.

THIETMARUS, bishop of Merseburg, 1018. *Chronicle*, seven books, CXXXIX, 1184.

THIETPALDUS, monk of Tegernsee, 1003. Letter to Saint Asebert, bishop of the Prussian Church, on the study of sacred matters, CXXXIX, 374.

THIOFRIDUS, abbot of Echternach, 1108.

1. *Flowers of the Epitaph of the Saints*, four books.
2. Two sermons: on the relics of the saints; on the veneration of the saints.
3. Fragments of a twofold Life of Saint Willibrord, CLVII, 294.

THOMAS, bishop of York, 1100.

1. Epitaph of King William [Col. 0647].
2. Two letters to Lanfranc, archbishop of Canterbury.
3. Letter to the archbishops and bishops established throughout England, concerning the health restored to him by heaven, CLV, 1625; CXLIX, 1271; CL, 518.

THOMAS (Saint), archbishop of Canterbury and martyr, 1170. One hundred and ninety-seven letters: twenty-eight to Pope Alexander; forty-four to cardinals; twenty-one to the people of Canterbury; two to Roger, archbishop of York; six to Conrad, archbishop of Mainz; seventy-four to various bishops and clerics; and twenty-one to kings and laypersons, CXC, 436.

THOMAS, Cistercian abbot, 1200. Commentary on the *Song of Songs*, twelve books, CCVI, 9.

THOMAS, monk of Radolio, 1200. Life of Peter, abbot of Clairvaux, CCIX, 1008.

TICHONIUS, African, 399. Book on the Seven Rules, XVIII, 16.

TIMASIUS, 415. Letter to Augustine concerning the book written to him, *On Nature and Grace*, against Pelagius’s treatise, XXXIII, 741.

TOMELLUS, monk of Hasnon, about 1080. History of the Monastery of Hasnon, CXLVII, 586.

TORTARIUS RADULFUS. See RADULFUS.

TORTHELMUS, bishop, 733. Letter to Boniface, archbishop of Mainz, LXXXIX, 724.

TRIFOLIUS, priest, 523. Letter to the blessed Senator Faustus against John the Scythian monk, LXIII, 534.

TROJANUS, bishop of Saintes, 540. Letter to Eumerius, bishop of Nantes, concerning a boy of whom it was unknown whether he had been baptized, LXVII, 995.

TROMUNDUS, monk of Clairvaux, about 1163. Letter to Abbot Gerard concerning the canonization of Saint Bernard, CLXXXV, 626.

TUDEBODUS, priest of Civray, eleventh century. History of the Journey to Jerusalem, five books, CLV, 764.

TURGOTUS, prior of Durham, about 1100. Life of the Venerable Bede, XC, 53, 60.

TURRIBIUS, bishop of Astorga, 450. Letter to the bishops Idacius and Ceponius concerning the refusal to receive apocryphal writings as authorities of faith, and concerning the sect of the Priscillianists, LIV, 693.

TURSTINUS, archbishop of York, 1132. Letter to William, bishop of Canterbury, CLXXXII, 697.

TUSAREDUS, eighth century. Letter to Ascaricus, XCIX, 1234.

TUTILO (Saint), monk of Saint Gall, 898. Fragment of a poem by Tutilo; verses to be sung in processions at the Nativity of the Lord; verses for Epiphany; verses for the feast of Saint Othmar, for a procession; verses for the reception of a prince, CXXIX, 863; LXXXVII, 51 ff.

## U

UDALRICUS (Saint), bishop of Augsburg, 973.

1. Synodal sermon.
2. Charter of Udalricus for the monastery of Kempten, CXXXV, 1000.

UDALRICUS, abbot of Tegernsee, 1048. Four letters: to Nikerus, bishop of Freising, reporting to him the cleric Raherius, guilty of many crimes; and to G., archpriest of Freising, concerning the same Raherius, CXLI, 1322.

UDALRICUS, monk of Cluny, 1086. *The Earlier Customs of the Monastery of Cluny*, three books, CXLIX, 634.

UDASCALCUS, monk at Saint Ulrich, Augsburg, 1135.

1. Account of the disputes between Hermann and Egino.
2. Poem on Egino’s journey and death.
3. Life of Chounrad, bishop of Constance, CLXX, 836.

UGO RIGAUDI, twelfth century. Hugh’s gift to the nuns of Fontevraud, CLXII, 1114.

ULFILAS, bishop of the Moeso-Goths, fourth century.

1. Surviving fragments of the translation of Holy Scripture into the Gothic language.
2. Gothic grammar.
3. Glossary of the Gothic language, XVIII, 456.

ULGERIUS, bishop of Angers, 1148.

1. Report to Pope Innocent II on behalf of the monastery of Ronceay against the monks of Vendôme.
2. Four letters: to Pope Lucius II concerning Odo, dean of Saint-Martin of Tours; to the same pope concerning Robert, prior of Saint-Cosmas of Tours; to the clergy of Angers concerning the Knights Templar of Jerusalem; and to Abbot Suger of Saint-Denis concerning the abbot of Bourgueil.
3. Testament of Ulgerius, CLXXX, 1642.

ULTIANUS, notary of Liutprand, king of the Lombards, 716. Judgment of Ultianus in the dispute conducted between Talisperianus, bishop of Lucca, and John, bishop of Pistoia, LXXXVII, 1360.

UNALDUS, abbot of Moissac, 1073. Testament of Unaldus concerning tithes redeemed by him from various laypersons, CLIX, 964.

[Col. 0648] UNIBERTUS, archbishop of Lyons, twelfth century. Letter to Suger concerning the conference convened at Chartres to aid the Eastern Church, CLXXXVI, 1411.

URANIUS, priest, 432. Letter to Pacatus concerning the death of Saint Paulinus of Nola, LIII, 859.

URBAN I (Saint), pope and martyr, 222. Decrees concerning communal life and the offerings of the faithful, CXXX, 138.

URBAN II, pope, 1099.

1. Three hundred and four letters and privileges.
2. Three sermons: a sermon after the consecration of the church of Cluny; an address to the consecrated Ivo; addresses delivered at the Council of Clermont concerning the Jerusalem expedition.
3. Epitaph of Simon, count of Crépy, written upon his pyramid, CLI, 284.

URBANUS, bishop of Llandaff, 1119. Petition of Urban against Pope Calixtus II at Rheims, CLXIII, 1338.

URBAN III, pope, 1187. One hundred and forty-seven letters and privileges, CCII, 1329.

URBAN V, pope, 1367. Rescript to Marquard, patriarch of Aquileia, concerning the correction of an abuse in the rendering of judgments, XCIX, 664.

URSACIUS, bishop, 347. Four letters: to Pope Julius, to Athanasius, and to Germinius, X, 647, 649, 718; to Athanasius, XIII, 563.

URSUS, cleric, 722. Foundation of the monastery of nuns of Saint Mary in the city of Lucca, LXXXVII, 1366.

USUARDUS, monk of Saint-Germain, 877. Martyrology for the entire annual cycle, CXXIII–CXXIV.

UTHO, bishop of Strasbourg, 965. Life of Saint Arbogast, bishop of Strasbourg in Germany, CXXXIV, 1001.

## V

VALCANDUS, monk of the monastery of Moyenmoutier in Lorraine, eleventh century.

1. Life of Saint Hidulph, bishop of Trier and founder of Moyenmoutier, CLI, 588.
2. Life of Saint Deodatus, CLI, 584.

VALENS, Arian bishop, 360. Five letters: to Pope Julius; to Athanasius, X, 647, 649; to Germinius, X, 718; to Emperor Constantius, X, 703; and to Athanasius, XIII, 563.

VALENTINIAN I the Elder, 373. Constitution concerning rebaptizers, XI, 1180. Constitution to Pope Damasus concerning priests and the continent, XIII, 576. Letter to Pinianus approving the election of Siricius, bishop of Rome, XIII, 593.

VALENTINIAN III, 452. Constitution concerning the Manichees, LIV, 622. Constitution or letter to Count and Patrician Aetius concerning the ordination of bishops, LIV, 636. Letter to Leo, archbishop of Rome, concerning his election and the holding of a council, LIV, 899. Letter to the Emperor Theodosius concerning the defense of the faith, LIV, 858.

VALENTINUS, cenobite, 419. Letter to Augustine concerning free will and grace, XXXIII, 974.

VALERIANUS, bishop of Cimiez, fifth century.

1. Twenty homilies: on the good of discipline; on the narrow and constricted way; on promises made and not fulfilled; on the insolence of the mouth; on idle words; on mercy; on parasites; on the good of preserving peace; on the good of humility; on the good of martyrdom; on the Maccabees; on Lent.
2. Letter to monks concerning the virtues and order of apostolic teaching, LII, 682.

VALERIANUS, bishop of Brescia, 761. Charter for the Brescia monastery of Saint Saviour and Saint Julia, LXXXVII, 1390.

VALERIUS (Saint), abbot, 656.

1. Minor works: letter concerning the blessed Echeria; on the vain wisdom of the world; to the blessed Donadeus concerning the monk Maximus, who reported to Valerius his own vision of the delights of paradise and the lamentations of the abyss; concerning the monk Bonellus, to whom a revelation of hell was made; on a heavenly revelation; on the penitence of monks; on the kinds of monks; etc.
2. Life of Saint Fructuosus, bishop of Braga, LXXXVII, 418.

VALERIUS PROBUS, grammarian, ninth century. Short work on ancient signs, CXXX, 1179.

VALRAMUS, bishop of Naumburg, 1110. Four letters: to Louis, Landgrave of Thuringia, with a refutation; to the church of Bamberg; a letter concerning the life of Saint Leonard the confessor; and a letter to Saint Anselm concerning the diversity of ceremonies customarily observed by different persons in different ways during the sacrifice of the altar, CLIX, 985.

VANDEMIRIS, 690. Charter for churches, LXXXVIII, 1216.

VASO, bishop of Liège, 1048.

1. Four letters: to John, provost of Liège; to Henry I, king of the Franks; to Roger II, bishop of Châlons; and to Emperor Henry, surnamed the Black.
2. Charter for the collegiate church of Saint Bartholomew at Liège, CXLII, 726.

[Col. 0649] VENANTIUS FORTUNATUS. See FORTUNATUS.

VERANUS, Gallic bishop, 453. Letter to Pope Saint Leo in acknowledgment of his received letter to Flavian, LIV, 887.

VERANUS (Saint), bishop of Lyons, 586. Ruling concerning the chastity of priests, LXXII, 700.

VERUS, bishop of Rodez, 656. Two letters to Saint Desiderius, bishop of Cahors, LXXXVII, 474, 263, 265; LXXX, 445.

VICTOR (Saint), pope and martyr, 189.

1. Decrees concerning Easter and other matters.
2. Letter to the Africans concerning the matters above, CXXX, 122.

VICTOR, African confessor, 258. Two letters to Cyprian, IV, 420, 422.

VICTOR PUBLIUS, fourth century. Description of the city of Rome, XVIII, 437.

VICTOR, bishop of Vita, 481. *On the Vandal Persecution*, five books, LVIII, 126.

VICTOR, *clarissimus* and rhetorician of Marseilles, 426.

1. Three books of commentaries on Genesis, about 1,600 verses.
2. Metrical letter to Abbot Salmon on the depraved morals of his age, LXI, 936.

VICTOR, African bishop, 533. Letter to Fulgentius of Ruspe concerning the sermon of Fastidiosus the Arian, LXV, 372.

VICTOR, bishop of Capua, 550.

1. Interpretation of the Gospel harmonies of Ammonius of Alexandria, LXVIII, 252, 256.
2. Fragment of Victor of Capua concerning the Paschal Cycle, LXVIII, 1097.
3. On the catena on the four Gospels translated into Latin by Victor of Capua, ibid., 360.

VICTOR, bishop of Tunnuna, 556. Chronicle from the year 444 to the year 566, LXVIII, 937.

VICTOR, bishop of Carthage, 646. Greek-written letter to Pope Theodore: his confession of faith concerning the two natures and the two wills in Christ, LXXXVII, 86; LXXX, 636.

VICTOR II, pope, 1057. Twenty pontifical letters and diplomas: for the monastery of Cluny; for the canons of Ferrara; for the church of Bologna; for the monastery of Moliane; to Adalbert, archbishop of Hamburg, granting him the use of the pallium and mitre; for the canons of Saint Mary of Pisa; for the church of Ascoli; for the abbey of Andlau; for the liberty of Ely monastery; for the monastery of Vendôme; for the church of Trier; for the monastery of Saint-Bertin; for the monastery of Monte Cassino; etc., CXLIII, 800.

VICTOR III, pope, 1087.

1. Two letters: to the empress concerning relief from the tribute of the Holy Sepulchre; and to Ursus, bishop of Ravello, concerning the bishopric of Ravello, whose possessions he confirms.
2. Address delivered at the synod of Benevento concerning the condemnation of Guibert and the avoidance of recent schismatics.
3. Three books of *Dialogues*, concerning miracles wrought by divine assistance through Saint Benedict or other monks in the monastery of Monte Cassino, CXLIX, 913.

VICTORINUS, bishop of Poetovio, 303.

1. Fragment on the making of the world.
2. Scholia on the Apocalypse of the blessed John, V, 282.

VICTORINUS MARIUS, 372.

1. Book to Justinus the Manichee, against the two principles of the Manichees and on the true flesh of Christ.
2. On the words of Scripture: “Evening came and morning came, one day.” Whether the day began at evening or in the morning.
3. Book on the generation of the divine Word, addressed to Candidus the Arian.
4. Four books against Arius.
5. On Receiving.
6. Hymns on the Trinity.
7. Two books on Paul’s Epistle to the Galatians.
8. One book on Paul’s Epistle to the Philippians.
9. Two books on Paul’s Epistle to the Ephesians.
10. Book on physical matters, VIII, 994.

VICTORIUS of Le Mans, 460. Letter to the bishops established within the Third Province, LIII, 1014.

VICTRICIUS (Saint), bishop of Rouen, 408. Book on the praise of the saints, XX, 438.

VICTURIUS, bishop of Grenoble, fifth century. Letter to Avitus, bishop of Vienne, concerning a man who married the sister of his deceased wife, LIV, 232.

VIGILA, monk of Albelda, date unknown. Chronicle of Albelda, CXXIX, 1124.

VIGILIUS (Saint), bishop of Trent and martyr, 398. Two letters: to Simplicianus, bishop of Milan, concerning the martyrdom of Saints Sisinnius, Martyrius, and Alexander; and to Saint John Chrysostom concerning the same martyrs, XIII, 544.

VIGILIUS, deacon, 430. Rule for monks commonly called the Eastern Rule, L, 373; CIII, 476.

VIGILIUS, bishop of Tapsus, 518.

1. Five books against Eutyches.
2. Dialogue against the Arians, with Athanasius, Arius, and Probus the judge as speakers.
3. Dialogue against the Arians and Sabellians, etc., with Athanasius, Arius, Sabellius, Photinus, and Probus the judge as speakers.
4. Twelve books on the Trinity, published under the name of Saint Athanasius, bishop of Alexandria.
5. Against the Arian deacon Marivadus [Col. 0650], under the name of Idacius Clarus, *Against Varimadus*.
6. Two books against the Arian Palladius.
7. Treatise on the Nicene faith against the Arians, LXII, 94.

VIGILIUS, pope, 555.

1. Sixteen letters: to Eutherius, answering his consultations; to Caesarius of Arles concerning the incestuous marriage of King Theudebert; to Justinian concerning Anthimus and his heretical colleagues, struck with a sentence of anathema; to Menna, congratulating him that, after the condemnation of heretics, he embraced the four holy universal synods; to Auxanius of Arles, postponing the grant of the pallium he had requested; to the same concerning investigation of the case of Bishop Praetextatus; to the bishops of Gaul concerning Auxanius of Arles, appointed vicar of the Apostolic See; to Aurelianus of Arles, delegating to him his authority in Gaul after Auxanius’s death; to the whole Church, setting forth the reasons for his withdrawal to Saint Euphemia; etc., LXIX, 9 ff.
2. *Constitutum* concerning the Three Chapters, ibid., 67.
3. Decretal letter confirming the Fifth Ecumenical Synod, ibid., 121.
4. *Constitutum* for the condemnation of the Three Chapters, LXIX, 144.

VIGILIUS, bishop of Auxerre, 670. Charter for the monastery of the Blessed Mary founded outside the walls of Auxerre, LXXXVIII, 1193.

VINCENTIUS (Saint) of Lérins, 440. Two *Commonitories* on the antiquity and universality of the Catholic faith against the profane novelties of all heretics, L, 637.

VINDICIANUS, bishop of Cambrai, 680. Letter to Pope John, incorporating his rescript confirming the privileges of the Church of Saint Mary at Arras granted by Vindicianus, LXXXVIII, 1200.

VITALIANUS, pope, 669. Eleven letters: to Paul, archbishop of Crete, concerning the unjust condemnation of the bishop of Lappa; to Vaanus, the emperor’s chamberlain, concerning the same; to George of Syracuse, that he should support John, bishop of Lappa; to King Oswi of Northumbria, who sought his judgment concerning Easter; to Sicilian monks; to the monks of Fleury; to Clovis, king of the Franks; to Theodore, archbishop of Canterbury, concerning the primacy which he affirms belongs to the Church of Canterbury; etc., LXXXVII, 998.

VITALIS ORDERICUS. See ORDERICUS.

VITIGES, king of the Goths, 560. Five letters: to all the Goths, writing that he had been made king by the army according to ancestral custom; to Emperor Justinian concerning Italy’s calamities caused by the wars, seeking peace from the emperor through envoys; to the Master of Offices, that he should induce the emperor to grant peace to Italy; to the bishops, that they should assist the envoys sent to the emperor; etc., LXIX, 819; LXXII, 1117.

VIVENTIOLUS, bishop of Lyons, 540. Two letters: to Avitus of Vienne concerning the feast of Saint Justus; and to the bishops of the province of Lyons, directing them to come to the Council of Epaone, LXVII, 994; LIX, 272.

VIVENTIUS, bishop, 545. Life of Saint Caesarius, bishop of Arles, LXVII, 1002.

VIVIANUS, Premonstratensian, 1130. *Harmony, or Treatise on Free Will and Grace*, CLXVI, 1320.

VIVIANUS, master, twelfth century. Letters to Thomas of Canterbury, CXC, 690 ff. Letter to Pope Alexander concerning what he had done in carrying out the apostolic mandate entrusted to him, CC, 1448.

VOLDARICUS, patriarch of Aquileia, 1180. Statute for celebrating the solemn office of Saint Mary Magdalene in the church of Aquileia, XCIX, 645.

VOLUSIANUS, pagan, 412. Letter to Augustine, proposing to him questions: How could God, who is immeasurable, be enclosed in a virgin’s womb and in the tiny body of an infant? Whether meanwhile he had abandoned the care of the world? etc., XXXIII, 512.

VULFADUS, bishop of Bourges, 875. Pastoral letter to his parish priests and parishioners, CXXI, 1136.

VULGRINUS, archbishop of Bourges, 1130. Two letters in the cause of Innocent II, Roman pontiff, CLXXIX, 44, 45.

## W

WALAFRIDUS STRABUS, monk of Fulda, 849.

1. Ordinary Gloss on the books of the Old Testament.
2. Ordinary Gloss on the books of the New Testament.
3. Exposition of the first twenty psalms.
4. Epitome of Hrabanus’s commentaries on Leviticus.
5. Homily on the beginning of Saint Matthew’s Gospel.
6. Exposition of the Gospels of Mark, Luke, and John.
7. Illustrations of the histories of the New Testament.
8. One book, addressed to Bishop Regnibert, *On the Beginnings and Developments of Ecclesiastical Matters*.
9. On the Destruction of Jerusalem.
10. Life of Saint Gall, abbot in Alemannia.
11. Life of Saint Othmar, abbot of Saint Gall.
12. Life of Saint Blathmac, abbot of Iona and martyr.
13. Metrical Life of Saint Mamas the monk.
14. On the Visions of Wetti, about 1,000 verses.
15. Verses on each feast of the year.
16. Hymn on the Nativity of the Lord.
17. Hymn on the Agaunian [Col. 0651] martyrs.
18. On the Virgin Mary.
19. Verses composed in the palace at Aachen.
20. Poems on various subjects.
21. *Hortulus*, addressed to Grimald, abbot of the monastery of Saint Gall.
22. Metrical Life of Saint Leodegar, bishop and martyr, attributed by some to Walafrid Strabo, CXIII–CXIV.

WALBERTUS, abbot of Esrum in Denmark, about 1178. Diploma for the monks of the Paraclete, CCIX, 752.

WALDRAMMUS, bishop of Strasbourg, 920. Poems of Waldram to Bishop Solomon, CXXXII, 572, 573; LXXXVII, 44.

WALPRANDUS, bishop of Lucca, 739. Testament of Walprand, LXXXVII, 1405.

WALTARIUS, abbot of Saint Lawrence at Liège, 1152. Letter to Abbot Wibald, CLXXXIX, 1416.

WALTERIUS, bishop of Orléans, 867. Chapters promulgated by Walter at the synod held at the estate of Bullen in the second year of his ordination, CXIX, 726.

WALTERIUS, bishop of Sens, 933. Fourteen statutes, CXXXII, 718.

WALTERIUS, bishop of Chalon-sur-Saône, 1120. Seven diplomas. Charter concerning the acquisition from Saveric, count of Chalon, of part of the county of Chalon. Notice of the foundation of Cîteaux. Letters to Robert, bishop of Langres, concerning the reception back into his earlier monastery of Molesme of Robert, formerly abbot of Cîteaux. Letter to Pope Paschal on behalf of the monastery of Cîteaux; etc., CLX, 1160.

WALTERIUS, chamberlain of Corbie, 1148. Letter to Abbot Wibald concerning buildings to be constructed, and expressing the wish that he return to Corbie as soon as possible, CLXXXIX, 1181.

WALTERIUS, archbishop of Rouen, 1198. Letter granting to the chapter of Rouen the tithe of Dieppe and Bouteilles, CCVII, 1156. On certain distributions to be made to the chapter of Rouen, CCVII, 1179.

WALTERUS, bishop of Albano, twelfth century. Letter to Gilbert, bishop of London, CXC, 1017.

WANDALBERTUS, monk of Prüm, 870.

1. Martyrology.
2. On the names, signs, and qualities of the weather of the twelve months.
3. A calendar-clock through the divisions of the twelve months.
4. On the creation of the world according to the sequence of the six days.
5. On the life and miracles of Saint Goar, CXXI, 574.

WANFREDUS of Siena, 731. Donation for the monastery of Saint Eugenius, LXXXVII, 1403.

WARNAHARIUS (Saint), priest of Langres, 615.

1. Acts of the holy twin martyrs Speusippus, Eleusippus, and Meleusippus.
2. Life of Saint Desiderius, LXXX, 186.

WERNERUS, abbot of Saint Blaise in the Black Forest, 1126. *Florilegia of the Holy Fathers*, or extracts from the honeyed teaching of various Fathers—especially Augustine, Jerome, Ambrose, Gregory, Hilary, Chrysostom, Maximus, Origen, Remigius, Cassiodorus, Bede, Alcuin, and other orthodox doctors—on the Gospels for the temporal cycle throughout the year, CLVII, 920.

WERNERUS, bishop of Minden, 1156. Two letters: to Abbot Wibald concerning a man commended to him by Wibald, whom Count Otto had received badly; and to the archbishop of Magdeburg concerning the bishop of Osnabrück, CLXXXIX, 1439, 1444.

WERNERUS DE KIRCHEIM, twelfth century. Letter to Hildegard, CXCVII, 268.

WETBERTUS, priest, 747. Letter to the monks of Glastonbury, LXXXIX, 773.

WETZEL, 1152. Letter to Emperor Frederick, urging him, having shaken off the yoke of the supreme pontiff, to receive the Empire from the Roman Senate and People, CLXXXIX, 1421.

WIBALDUS, abbot of Stavelot and Corbie, 1158. About 440 letters: to Emperor Lothair concerning the calamities inflicted on the monastery of Monte Cassino by Saracens, Northmen, and Lombards; to the monks of Monte Cassino; to King Conrad; to Pope Eugenius III; to Henry, king of the Romans; to his sister Hadwig; to his monks at Corbie; to the chapter of Liège; to the canons of Paderborn; to the monks of Fulda; to the monks of Stavelot; to Cardinal Guy; etc., CLXXXIX, 1076.

WIBERTUS, archdeacon of Toul, 1054. Life of Pope Saint Leo IX, CXLIII, 458.

WIBERTUS, antipope, 1099. Eleven letters and diplomas: concerning the possessions and privileges of the canons of Verona; letters establishing the order of seating among bishops attending a council; concerning the privileges of the Church of Ravenna; to Vratislaus, first duke and afterwards king of Bohemia; synodal letter to the entire clergy ... for the convent of Blessed Peter at Padua; etc., CXLVIII, 826.

WIBOLDUS, bishop of Cambrai, 965. Clerical game, CXXXIV, 1008.

WICARDUS, abbot of Inda near Aachen, [Col. 0652] ninth century. Letter to Frotharius, bishop of Toul, CVI, 872.

WICBERTUS, abbot, 756. Two letters to Lullus, bishop of Mainz, XCVI, 836, 842.

WICBODUS, author unknown, 790. Book of questions on the book of Genesis, from the sayings of the holy Fathers Augustine, Gregory, Jerome, Ambrose, Hilary, Isidore, Eucherius, and Junilius, XCVI, 1102.

WICMANNUS, archbishop of Magdeburg, 1156. Four letters: to Philip, bishop of Osnabrück, concerning the accusations made by Abbot Wibald; to Abbot Wibald concerning Philip, bishop of Osnabrück; to Pope Adrian concerning the bishop of Osnabrück and the abbot of Corbie, CLXXXIX, 1441, 1442, 1446.

WIDEGERNUS, bishop of Strasbourg, 728. Charter for the monastery of Murbach, LXXXVIII, 1281.

WIDERADUS, abbot, 721. Testament of Abbot Widerad, by which he bequeaths many things to the basilicas of Saints Andochius, Regina, and Ferreolus, etc., LXXXVIII, 1268.

## Z
ZACCHAEUS the Christian, c. 420. Three books of *Consultations*: on Christ, the devil, the Jews, the resurrection, the faith of Christians, God’s foreknowledge, the Holy Spirit, the Lord’s Passion, the polygamy of the patriarchs; against the Manichees, the Marcionites and Photinians, the Sabellians, the Patripassians, the Arians, and the Novatians; on monks, Antichrist, etc., XX, 1062.

ZACHARIAS (St), pope, c. 752. 1. Twenty letters: to Boniface, archbishop, concerning bishoprics founded in Germany, the holding of a synod in the kingdom of France, fornicators and men guilty of bloodshed not to be admitted to the priesthood, pagan rites prohibited at Rome, etc.; to Burchard, bishop of Würzburg, concerning the episcopal see founded by Boniface; to the Franks and Gauls concerning the synod which had been held; to Boniface, archbishop, concerning two false prophets discovered in France; to the same concerning baptism not to be repeated when an unskilled priest administers it using defective words, etc. 2. Three decrees, LXXXIX, 892; XCVIII, 80.

ZACHARIAS of Chrysopolis, c. 1152. Four books *On the Harmony of the Evangelists*, CLXXXVI, 12.

ZACHARIAS, bishop of an unknown see, twelfth century. Sermon on St George, CLXXXVI, 620.

ZACHARIAS BENEDICTUS of Vicenza, Carthusian, twelfth century. *On the Origin of the Sacred Carthusian Order*, CLIII, 572.

ZENO (St), bishop of Verona, c. 381. Ninety-three treatises, in two books—on faith; on faith, hope, and charity; on justice; chastity; continence; patience; humility; fear; avarice; circumcision; the spiritual building of the house of God; the threefold kind of sacrifices; the resurrection; Genesis against the Arians; Genesis, or the eternal generation of the Son of God; the Nativity of the Lord; Abraham; Jacob’s sleep; Judah; Job; Susanna; the prophet Jonah; the birthday of St Arcadius; the creation of man; on Isaiah; *Invitation to the Font*; to the Neophytes after baptism; Easter; Daniel—XI, 253.

ZEPHYRINUS, pope, c. 208. One hundred and thirty decrees, CXXX, 126. Letter to the brethren serving throughout Egypt, CXXX, 128.

ZONARAS (John), twelfth century. Preface concerning the Synod held at Carthage, III, 1080, 1083.

ZOSIMUS, pope, c. 417. Sixteen letters and decrees: to the bishops of Gaul concerning the privileges of the Church of Arles; to Aurelius and all bishops established throughout Africa, concerning the case of Caelestius; to Aurelius and the bishops of Africa concerning Ursus and Tuentius, bishops unlawfully ordained there; to the bishops of the provinces of Vienne and of Second Narbonensis, that the metropolitan of Arles should have authority to ordain bishops in their provinces; to Hilary, bishop of [Col. 0655] Narbonne, that he had no right whatever to ordain bishops in First Narbonensis; to Patroclus, bishop of Arles, against the audacity and unlawful ordinations of Proculus; to his legates, concerning appeals by bishops to the priest of the Roman Church; etc., XX, 638.
